Greetings of Christian love to one and all. This past year and a half have been challenging in one way or another for most people. My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing –James 1:2-4.

We trust that no matter what each of you has faced your inner motivation echoes with the words of Apostle Paul, … for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. –Philippians 4:11-13.

As we are already almost halfway through another year, I stop to consider how time keeps disappearing at an ever-increasing rate of speed. For many, the last 16 to 18 months have been quite challenging as the Covid-19 pandemic and its aftereffects continue to wreak havoc with all that used to be considered normal. For us, some of these aftereffects have hindered us from getting this issue of the magazine out in a timely manner. Our apologies. However, things are back on track to be able to get the next issue out within the next several months, thus allowing us to get back onto our normal schedule once more.

I see the pandemic and the resulting aftereffects as quite similar to one big traffic jam. First, many vehicles are all traveling along quite smoothly at the speed limit. Gradually more and more vehicles join the flow, until the highway becomes quite congested. However, things still continue to flow unhindered until suddenly one vehicle brakes sharply and swerves to avoid some debris on the roadway. Immediately, there is a ripple-effect or domino-effect, as each vehicle brakes to avoid hitting the one in front of them that just applied their brakes. I have seen this type of situation create stop-and-go traffic for a mile or more as traffic slows to a crawl, then once each vehicle finally gets past the offending object they can once more accelerate to their previous rate of speed.

With our world’s economies, both local and global, the same thing seemingly has happened, howbeit on a much, much larger scale. First came the shutdowns, both local and national, causing businesses to lose production and sales. Then as businesses reopened and their workers began to get sick, further production was lost. Suddenly, many manufacturers found themselves behind in their inventory reserve, which graduated into being behind in their ability to supply the demand. Since so much of our world’s businesses have developed trade at a global level, there are many products that are not available for sale as manufacturers wait for the “company overseas” to once more have enough supply to meet the global demand. Another problem that has developed more recently is that due to the major imbalance of supply versus demand on a global level, the cost of purchase for many products has skyrocketed awakening fears among some economists of a global crisis due to inflation.

Where does this leave the church? It seems that the “enemy of our souls” has used this global event to cause churches everywhere to struggle on many levels. I have on my bookshelf a book titled Conscience in Crisis, which is about church history. This book specifically examines the struggle of the “peace” churches in colonial America. One of the key points the book focuses on is that the global events of that time period shook the very foundations of their faith and practice. This caused the collective conscience of the churches to face an unprecedented crisis level, which many individuals never overcame. Some gave up the faith, some quit going to church, some walked away from their church and started going to more worldly churches. And the ones that remained, struggled substantially through many issues until they once more were considered stable.

Our Perspective Matters

When I think of the word perspective, the definition I am using is: a particular attitude toward, or way, of regarding something; a point of view. It is like the prescription of the glasses we have in front of our eyes causing us to see things in a distorted manner or with a clear 20/20 view. Or it is like using a filter in your computer or in your vehicle engine, which only lets through that which is pre-determined should be allowed.

So, our perspective is akin to using a filter or a pair of glasses. Our perspective is shaped by many things: the way we were trained as children, the role models we chose to follow during our formative years, the reading material we absorbed, the spiritual mentors we opened our hearts to, and the peers we embraced throughout our lifetime. Also, our perspective determines how we look at situations, how we interact with God, how we view sin and salvation, and how we respond to both friends and enemies.

In our world today, there are many perspectives, all vying for our allegiance. Many are the “special interest” groups clamoring for our support of their cause. There’s race discrimination on both sides of the matter. There are voices crying “foul” in their effort to gain support and an advantage against their opponents regarding voting rights, honesty of the election outcomes, and desired legislative changes to the judicial system and the Constitution. While there have always been multiple sides to an issue, there has usually been an effort to work together for the good of all. However, in the last number of years it seems that numerous issues have become quite divisive to the point of polarizing the people into two camps. The balance of power in government has been swinging back and forth from the one side to the other. This polarization has been causing bitterness and anger to build, in some instances erupting into violence and vandalism. In other instances, it has caused normally level-headed individuals to lose their cool and make “knee-jerk” reactionary decisions which are totally out of character for them.

In the midst of all this chaos and confusion, what is our perspective as the church? Are we remaining steadfast in allowing God and His Word to mold and shape our perspective to be aligned with His perspective? Or have we allowed the pressure of one peer group or another to start pushing us off-course in our walk as strangers and pilgrims?

I have heard reports of some churches in other parts of the world being pushed by their local government to not meet for fellowship and group worship. There are families whose conscience chooses to obey the government in long-term mask wearing and social distancing. Individuals have become discouraged. Families have become isolated. And churches have struggled through one issue after another in their efforts to maintain peace among the brethren.

As I have interacted with people who are not regular church goers, or those who attend a “dying” church, an “older” church, or a “small country” church, there are numerous things I have heard them testify regarding the churches of the conservative, Anabaptist persuasion. These people are awed by the way we help each other both on a regular basis and when tragedy strikes. They can’t comprehend the large size of our weddings and especially our funerals. They don’t understand how our children are mild-mannered and respectful of others.

Let’s take heed and use wisdom as we continue facing the challenges in the days to come. From my limited vantage point, I believe that long-term mask wearing and social distancing that is practiced at the expense of normal worship as we understand the Scriptures to teach, will eventually have a negative ripple effect on us as believers.

Many years ago, as I was involved in learning from the “counseling model”, it was spoken of as quite troubling and detrimental to interpersonal relationships IF someone had a “mask” on (figuratively). As I have evaluated and considered the long-term effect of a person having a “mask” on (literally), I believe it WILL cause as much and more detriment to interpersonal relationships. There is something about visiting with brothers and sisters of the faith when you can see their whole face. Without even realizing it, we read body language and facial expressions, which aids in understanding and conveying thoughts as we communicate with one another. Thus, it is my personal opinion that long-term mask wearing and social distancing by a local church body will eventually degrade the level of spiritual life and fervor to the point of someday that local body will no longer stand out from all the rest of the nominal Christians around them.

May God bless each one. May we not give up the spiritual fight. May we ever keep our eyes fixed on our Father, our Saviour, and our eternal home.

Curvin L Wenger

Christliche Grüße an alle. Das vergangene Jahr und die letzten sechs Monate waren für die meisten Menschen auf die eine oder andere Weise herausfordernd. Meine Brüder, achtet es für lauter Freude, wenn ihr in mancherlei Versuchungen fallt; denn ihr wisst, dass die Bewährung eures Glaubens Geduld bewirkt. Die Geduld aber soll zu einem vollkommenen Werk führen, damit ihr vollkommen und unversehrt seid und es euch an nichts mangelt –Jakobus 1:2-4.

Wir vertrauen darauf, dass eure innere Einstellung, ganz gleich, womit jeder von euch konfrontiert war, den Worten des Apostels Paulus entspricht: … denn ich habe gelernt, mit dem zufrieden zu sein, was ich habe. Ich weiß, wie man sich in bescheidenen Verhältnissen zurechtfindet, und ich weiß auch, wie man Überfluss hat: In jeder Lage und bei allen Dingen bin ich darin unterwiesen, satt zu sein und zu hungern, Überfluss zu haben und Mangel zu leiden. Ich vermag alles durch Christus, der mich stärkt. –Philipper 4:11-13.

Da wir bereits fast die Hälfte eines weiteren Jahres hinter uns haben, halte ich inne und denke darüber nach, wie die Zeit immer schneller zu verfliegen scheint. Für viele waren die letzten 16 bis 18 Monate ziemlich herausfordernd, da die Covid-19-Pandemie und ihre Nachwirkungen weiterhin alles durcheinanderbringen, was früher als normal galt. Bei uns haben einige dieser Nachwirkungen dazu geführt, dass diese Ausgabe der Zeitschrift nicht rechtzeitig erscheinen konnte. Dafür bitten wir um Entschuldigung. Inzwischen sind wir jedoch wieder im Zeitplan und können die nächste Ausgabe in den kommenden Monaten herausbringen, sodass wir wieder zu unserem üblichen Erscheinungsrhythmus zurückkehren können.

Ich sehe die Pandemie und ihre Folgen als etwas, das einem großen Verkehrsstau sehr ähnelt. Zunächst fahren viele Fahrzeuge ganz ungehindert mit der zulässigen Höchstgeschwindigkeit. Nach und nach kommen immer mehr Fahrzeuge hinzu, bis die Autobahn stark überlastet ist. Dennoch fließt der Verkehr weiterhin ungehindert, bis plötzlich ein Fahrzeug scharf bremst und ausweicht, um Trümmern auf der Fahrbahn auszuweichen. Sofort entsteht eine Kettenreaktion oder ein Dominoeffekt, wenn jedes Fahrzeug bremst, um nicht auf das vorausfahrende Fahrzeug aufzufahren, das gerade gebremst hat. Ich habe erlebt, dass solche Situationen auf einer Strecke von einer Meile oder mehr zu Stop-and-go-Verkehr führen: Der Verkehr wird immer langsamer, bis jedes Fahrzeug schließlich an dem Hindernis vorbeigefahren ist und wieder auf seine vorherige Geschwindigkeit beschleunigen kann.

Bei den Volkswirtschaften unserer Welt, sowohl auf lokaler als auch auf globaler Ebene, scheint dasselbe geschehen zu sein, allerdings in einem viel, viel größeren Ausmaß. Zuerst kamen die Stilllegungen, sowohl auf lokaler als auch auf nationaler Ebene, wodurch Unternehmen Produktion und Umsatz verloren. Dann, als die Betriebe wieder öffneten und ihre Beschäftigten zu erkranken begannen, ging weitere Produktion verloren. Plötzlich stellten viele Hersteller fest, dass ihre Lagerbestände unter den erforderlichen Reserven lagen; daraus wurde ein Rückstand bei ihrer Fähigkeit, die Nachfrage zu bedienen. Da ein großer Teil der Unternehmen in unserer Welt den Handel auf globaler Ebene entwickelt hat, sind viele Produkte nicht erhältlich, während die Hersteller darauf warten, dass der „Konzern in Übersee“ wieder über genügend Vorräte verfügt, um die weltweite Nachfrage zu decken. Ein weiteres Problem, das sich in jüngerer Zeit entwickelt hat, besteht darin, dass aufgrund des erheblichen Ungleichgewichts zwischen Angebot und Nachfrage auf globaler Ebene die Anschaffungskosten vieler Produkte geradezu explodiert sind und bei einigen Wirtschaftswissenschaftlern die Sorge vor einer weltweiten Krise infolge der Inflation geweckt haben.

Was bedeutet das für die Gemeinde? Es scheint, dass der „Feind unserer Seelen“ dieses weltweite Ereignis genutzt hat, um Gemeinden überall auf vielerlei Weise in Bedrängnis zu bringen. In meinem Bücherregal steht ein Buch mit dem Titel Conscience in Crisis, das sich mit Kirchengeschichte befasst. Das Buch untersucht insbesondere den Kampf der „Friedenskirchen“ im kolonialen Amerika. Einer der zentralen Punkte des Buches ist, dass die weltweiten Ereignisse jener Zeit die Grundfesten ihres Glaubens und ihrer Glaubenspraxis erschütterten. Dadurch geriet das gemeinsame Gewissen der Gemeinden in eine beispiellose Krise, die viele Einzelne nie überwanden. Manche gaben den Glauben auf, manche hörten auf, zur Kirche zu gehen, manche kehrten ihrer Gemeinde den Rücken und gingen in weltlichere Gemeinden. Und diejenigen, die blieben, kämpften mit erheblichen Schwierigkeiten, bis sie schließlich wieder als gefestigt galten.

Unsere Perspektive ist entscheidend

Wenn ich an das Wort Perspektive denke, verwende ich folgende Definition: eine bestimmte Einstellung zu etwas oder eine bestimmte Art, etwas zu betrachten; ein Standpunkt. Sie ist wie die Sehstärke der Brille, die wir vor den Augen tragen und durch die wir die Dinge verzerrt oder klar und scharf sehen. Oder sie ist wie ein Filter in Ihrem Computer oder im Motor Ihres Fahrzeugs, der nur das durchlässt, was von vornherein zugelassen werden soll.

Unsere Perspektive ist also vergleichbar mit einem Filter oder einer Brille. Sie wird von vielen Dingen geprägt: davon, wie wir als Kinder erzogen wurden, von den Vorbildern, denen wir in unseren prägenden Jahren folgten, von der Lektüre, die wir in uns aufnahmen, von den geistlichen Mentoren, denen wir unser Herz öffneten, und von den Gleichaltrigen und Weggefährten, die wir im Laufe unseres Lebens an uns heranließen. Außerdem bestimmt unsere Perspektive, wie wir Situationen betrachten, wie wir mit Gott umgehen, wie wir Sünde und Erlösung sehen und wie wir sowohl auf Freunde als auch auf Feinde reagieren.

In unserer heutigen Welt gibt es viele Perspektiven, die alle um unsere Treue werben. Zahlreiche „Interessengruppen“ setzen sich lautstark dafür ein, dass wir ihre Anliegen unterstützen. Bei der Frage der Rassendiskriminierung gibt es auf beiden Seiten Vorwürfe. Stimmen rufen „Unrecht!“, um Unterstützung und einen Vorteil gegenüber ihren Gegnern zu gewinnen – in Fragen des Wahlrechts, der Rechtmäßigkeit der Wahlergebnisse und der gewünschten Gesetzesänderungen am Justizsystem und an der Verfassung. Auch wenn es bei einem Thema schon immer mehrere Seiten gab, hat man sich gewöhnlich darum bemüht, zum Wohl aller zusammenzuarbeiten. In den letzten Jahren scheinen jedoch zahlreiche Themen so spaltend geworden zu sein, dass die Menschen in zwei Lager polarisiert werden. Das Kräfteverhältnis in der Regierung schlägt mal zur einen, mal zur anderen Seite aus. Diese Polarisierung lässt Verbitterung und Zorn wachsen und führt in manchen Fällen zu Gewaltausbrüchen und Vandalismus. In anderen Fällen hat sie dazu geführt, dass sonst besonnene Menschen die Beherrschung verlieren und vorschnelle, reflexartige Entscheidungen treffen, die ganz und gar nicht ihrem Wesen entsprechen.

Was ist inmitten all dieses Chaos und dieser Verwirrung unsere Perspektive als Gemeinde? Bleiben wir standhaft dabei, Gott und sein Wort unsere Perspektive formen und gestalten zu lassen, damit sie mit seiner Perspektive übereinstimmt? Oder haben wir zugelassen, dass der Druck der einen oder anderen Gruppe Gleichgesinnter uns auf unserem Weg als Fremdlinge und Pilger vom Kurs abzubringen beginnt?

Ich habe Berichte gehört, dass Gemeinden in anderen Teilen der Welt von ihren örtlichen Regierungen unter Druck gesetzt werden, sich nicht zu Gemeinschaft und gemeinsamem Gottesdienst zu versammeln. Es gibt Familien, deren Gewissen ihnen gebietet, der Regierung zu gehorchen und langfristig Masken zu tragen sowie Abstand zu halten. Einzelne sind entmutigt worden. Familien sind isoliert worden. Und Gemeinden haben sich mit einer Schwierigkeit nach der anderen auseinandersetzen müssen, während sie sich bemühten, den Frieden unter den Brüdern und Schwestern zu bewahren.

Wenn ich mit Menschen gesprochen habe, die nicht regelmäßig in die Kirche gehen oder eine „sterbende“, eine „ältere“ oder eine „kleine Landgemeinde“ besuchen, habe ich von ihnen immer wieder Aussagen über die Gemeinden konservativer täuferischer Prägung gehört. Diese Menschen sind beeindruckt davon, wie wir einander sowohl im Alltag als auch dann helfen, wenn ein Unglück geschieht. Sie können die Größe unserer Hochzeiten und besonders unserer Beerdigungen kaum fassen. Sie verstehen nicht, wie unsere Kinder so sanftmütig und anderen gegenüber respektvoll sein können.

Lasst uns achtsam sein und Weisheit walten lassen, während wir uns auch in den kommenden Tagen den Herausforderungen stellen. Aus meiner begrenzten Sicht glaube ich, dass langfristiges Maskentragen und Abstandhalten, wenn es auf Kosten des normalen Gottesdienstes geschieht, wie wir ihn nach unserem Verständnis der Lehre der Schrift pflegen sollen, letztlich negative Auswirkungen auf uns als Gläubige haben wird.

Vor vielen Jahren, als ich mich mit dem „Beratungsmodell“ auseinandersetzte, wurde es als sehr beunruhigend und schädlich für zwischenmenschliche Beziehungen bezeichnet, WENN jemand (bildlich gesprochen) eine „Maske“ trug. Wenn ich die langfristigen Auswirkungen betrachte und bedenke, dass jemand (buchstäblich) eine „Maske“ trägt, glaube ich, dass dies zwischenmenschlichen Beziehungen ebenso viel und noch mehr Schaden zufügen WIRD. Es ist etwas Besonderes, mit Brüdern und Schwestern im Glauben zusammenzukommen und ihr ganzes Gesicht sehen zu können. Ohne es überhaupt zu bemerken, lesen wir Körpersprache und Gesichtsausdrücke; das hilft uns, Gedanken zu verstehen und zu vermitteln, wenn wir miteinander sprechen. Deshalb bin ich persönlich der Meinung, dass langfristiges Maskentragen und Abstandhalten durch eine örtliche Gemeinde letztlich das geistliche Leben und den Eifer so weit schwächen wird, dass diese Gemeinde eines Tages nicht mehr aus der Masse der nominellen Christen in ihrem Umfeld herausragen wird.

Möge Gott jeden Einzelnen segnen. Mögen wir den geistlichen Kampf nicht aufgeben. Mögen wir unseren Blick stets auf unseren Vater, unseren Retter und unsere ewige Heimat gerichtet halten.

Curvin L Wenger

Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalm 37:4.

Down deep within every person is a desire to be, or to do, something of value. If we, as humans, had no desire to do anything, life would be boring, and we would be nothing more than a robot. We all know that God wants more from us than to be a robot; He wants us to serve Him with our whole heart.

The meaning for the word desire is: to wish or long for; to crave; to want. Wish, want, crave, and covet all mean to have a longing for. Desire stresses the strength of feeling and often implies strong intention or aim.

Isn’t that what God wants from us—a desire with craving and intentional aim? Yes, it is, but this doesn’t happen on its own, nor does it happen automatically. Our desires are so strong that of ourselves we are no match for them; we need something outside of ourselves to be in control. According to the Bible, we must become born again. When we get born again, we become a new creature in Christ with new desires that God puts inside us. The way He does this, is by giving us a new heart.

God allows each of us to choose if we will serve Him or if we will not. He will not force us to yield ourselves to His will, nor will He force us to serve Him. But, if we are truly born again and serve the Lord joyfully and willingly, then He will give us godly desires which we will want to fulfill.

Does the Christian life become like clockwork just because we get a new heart and our desires have been turned towards serving God? I believe the answer is both yes and no. After we are walking with Christ for some time, we discover that Satan wants to change our desires in such a way that we would rather please him (Satan) instead of the Lord. Because of this, we need to be on guard. Satan wants to set spiritual snares for us. One of the ways he does this is by enticing our flesh.

There are good desires and bad desires. Some desires will bring us closer to Christ and some will draw us away. As Jesus walked on this earth, we know that His desire was to do the will of His Father. Out of His desire, He stayed focused on what He needed to do, even when His flesh was weak. There are two examples of this: one was when Jesus was tempted in the desert to make stones into bread, and the other was when He was in the garden praying right before He was crucified.

When we look at the account in the garden, we see that He did not want to take the cup that was before Him. In other words, Jesus desired to not go through the suffering, but praise God, He chose to please His Father. He laid down His flesh, obeyed the will of God, and allowed Himself to be crucified for our sins. Jesus looked at the long-term effect, and poured Himself into what He knew was right, rather than going by His own feelings. However, He did acknowledge His feelings by expressing them to God when He was praying in the garden. It is the same way with us—there are times that we need to be honest about our feelings and express them to God or to someone else. Yet we cannot walk by our feelings because we must act and do what we know is right according to the word of God.

Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23. If Solomon, the wisest man who ever lived says this, then we should take heed to it. The desires of the heart will make a difference on where we will end up in life. As we are fulfilling one of our desires by acting on it…with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength… –Mark 12:30, we actually feed that desire, causing it to develop into an even deeper longing and passion. As we then act on this stronger, passionate desire, we end up feeding that desire even more. Thus, the vicious cycle continues, repeating itself again and again.

Instead of feeding your desire, you can choose to hinder it—by acting against it. If you have a desire that is not good, and you need to change it to a godly desire, you can act against your original desire and do what is right. In so doing it will start to change your bad desire into one that is right. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also –Matthew 6:21; Luke 12:34.

And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth –Luke 12:15. Covetousness is an ungodly desire. Without bringing it into check, it will become a snare. Money is something that we all need, yet it is something that almost everyone at some point in life covets. Every day we spend much of our time working in some way to earn money.

In so doing, our heart’s desires tend to become focused on our work. Instead, we should see our job as a way of doing God’s work by being a light and encouragement to the ones around us. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him –Colossians 3:17.

Here and there we hear a lot about coveting money; however, we don’t hear much about coveting positions that are not lawful for us. It is not wrong to desire leadership in business or whatever it may be. In fact, it is a blessing for others if someone will stand up and provide leadership as a way to bless others. However, it is a wrong desire to want leadership for our own reputation, which is pride. We are all human and we are not perfect, yet we need to rise above our weaknesses and be a blessing. We all know that God gave each of us different gifts. Let’s use those gifts for the kingdom of God.

Sometimes we are trying so hard to fulfill our fleshly comforts that we lose sight of the real purpose that God has put us here. Our flesh stands in the way. It was this way with Achan. Instead of Achan putting his whole focus on the fight against the enemy, he said that, When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them… –Joshua 7:21.

I don’t know what it was like, but I picture there being loud noises and a bloody mess. If that’s the case, what was Achan thinking in the midst of a bloody battle that made him covet? The only thing I can think of, is that Achan’s number one desire was not on God’s will but was on fulfilling his own desires. It’s very sad that there were so many of God’s people killed because of Achan’s sin. If we see that we have a desire that is not godly, then let’s flee from that desire and work towards gaining a desire that is godly.

We see it is important to develop a godly desire that will encourage or lead us closer to God. The most important desire is to truly know God. That would be very close to the greatest commandment—to love the Lord thy God with all thy heart. To love the Lord thy God with all thy heart you obviously also need to have a desire to love Him. However, there are times in our life that we will need to take a specific action or purpose to love God with all our heart. There are many things that God may want us to surrender.

We all know that peer pressure influences our desires. We need brothers and sisters to walk beside us and encourage us in our relationship with Christ. Friends can draw our attention to something other than Christ. That is why we need to be careful who our close friends are. We need to seek out friends who will be upbuilding. A friend that can walk beside us and encourage us in our walk with God, is worth everything. As humans, we can’t always see everything correctly by ourselves. We need others to help us see our blind spots. A close friend who genuinely wants to help us follow God, will help us look at what is right in God’s eyes. Maybe we need to surrender our flesh and get right with God so we can develop desires that are pure and godly.

As we look at the heart’s desires, we see they have a major impact on who we are and who we will become. When our heart desires something, we pursue it with a deep longing. In fact, there are examples in the Bible where God gave people desires to serve Him. And I arose in the night, I and some few men with me; neither told I any man what my God had put in my heart to do at Jerusalem: neither was there any beast with me, save the beast that I rode upon –Nehemiah 2:12. Reading further… And Moses called Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, even every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work to do it –Exodus 36:2.

Remember, the word desire is a deep longing, craving, or wish. If we are wanting a walk with God that is flourishing, then we must have the desires that God has, since His desires will change our life. So they did eat, and were well filled: for he gave them their own desire; They were not estranged from their lust. But while their meat was yet in their mouths, The wrath of God came upon them, and slew the fattest of them, and smote down the chosen men of Israel –Psalm 78:29-31. Even though God led the Israelites into the wilderness, gave them water and manna, and even a place to worship Him, they were still not satisfied and desired other things. The children of Israel were granted their desires, but they ended up needing to pay with their own lives.

Another good example of God giving people their own desires is found in 1 Samuel 8 when the children of Israel wanted a king over them just like all the other nations. And [they] said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations. But the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the LORD. And the LORD said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee: for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them –1 Samuel 8:5-7. Oh Israel, …for he (God) gave them their own desire –Psalm 78:29.

It sounds like the Lord is saying, “Let’s let them have their own way and give them a king.” However, later in the chapter He lists all the bad things that will come with having a king. The Lord also tells Samuel who will rule over the children of Israel. After their king was anointed, they needed to serve him and could no longer serve God only. Consider why God brought them out of Egypt in the first place. Wasn’t it so they could serve the only true God?

Just like the children of Israel, we have seen God’s wonderous works. If we have been born of God’s Spirit, He led us out of our “Egypt”; He showed us the path of life; He brought us out of the miry clay; He set our feet on a solid rock. Still, we as humans tend to covet and long for something that we think is better. We ask God to give us wisdom and that He would provide for our needs, yet down deep inside we beg for God to give us our selfish desires.

We need to surrender every area of our life to God’s control. God knows what is best for us, however, if we insist, He will give us according to our selfish desires.

Remember, this earth is not our home. The end is coming, which is what God has in mind. We don’t know what is best for us, but God does. Let’s have faith and change our desires for that which God wants us to fulfill in this life. Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalms 37:4. And, Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it–Isaiah 58:14

Ha också din glädje i HERREN, så ska han ge dig vad ditt hjärta önskar – Psaltaren 37:4.

Djupt inom varje människa finns en önskan att vara eller göra något av värde. Om vi människor inte hade någon önskan att göra någonting, skulle livet vara tråkigt, och vi skulle inte vara mer än robotar. Vi vet alla att Gud vill mer av oss än att vi ska vara robotar; han vill att vi ska tjäna honom av hela vårt hjärta.

Betydelsen av ordet önskan är: att vilja eller längta efter; att trakta efter; att vilja ha. Att önska, vilja ha, trakta efter och åtrå betyder alla att längta efter något. Önskan betonar känslans styrka och innebär ofta en stark avsikt eller målsättning.

Är det inte det Gud vill av oss – en önskan präglad av längtan och målmedvetenhet? Jo, det är det, men det sker inte av sig självt och inte heller automatiskt. Våra önskningar är så starka att vi inte kan rå på dem på egen hand; vi behöver något utanför oss själva som kan ha kontrollen. Enligt Bibeln måste vi bli födda på nytt. När vi blir födda på nytt blir vi en ny skapelse i Kristus, med nya önskningar som Gud lägger i oss. Det gör han genom att ge oss ett nytt hjärta.

Gud låter var och en av oss välja om vi ska tjäna honom eller inte. Han tvingar oss inte att underkasta oss hans vilja och tvingar oss inte heller att tjäna honom. Men om vi verkligen är födda på nytt och tjänar Herren med glädje och villigt, då ger han oss gudfruktiga önskningar som vi vill uppfylla.

Blir det kristna livet som ett urverk bara för att vi får ett nytt hjärta och våra önskningar har riktats mot att tjäna Gud? Jag tror att svaret är både ja och nej. När vi har vandrat med Kristus en tid upptäcker vi att Satan vill förändra våra önskningar så att vi hellre vill behaga honom (Satan) än Herren. Därför behöver vi vara på vår vakt. Satan vill gillra andliga snaror för oss. Ett sätt han gör det på är genom att locka vårt kött.

Det finns goda och dåliga önskningar. Vissa önskningar för oss närmare Kristus och andra drar oss bort från honom. När Jesus vandrade på jorden vet vi att hans önskan var att göra sin Faders vilja. Denna önskan hjälpte honom att hålla fokus på det han behövde göra, även när hans kött var svagt. Det finns två exempel på detta: det ena var när Jesus frestades i öknen att göra stenar till bröd, och det andra var när han bad i trädgården strax innan han korsfästes.

När vi ser på händelsen i trädgården märker vi att han inte ville ta den bägare som väntade honom. Med andra ord önskade Jesus att slippa genomgå lidandet, men lovad vare Gud, han valde att behaga sin Fader. Han lade sitt kött åt sidan, lydde Guds vilja och lät sig korsfästas för våra synder. Jesus såg till de långsiktiga följderna och gav sig helt åt det han visste var rätt, i stället för att följa sina egna känslor. Han erkände dock sina känslor genom att uttrycka dem för Gud när han bad i trädgården. Så är det också med oss – ibland behöver vi vara ärliga om våra känslor och uttrycka dem inför Gud eller någon annan. Men vi kan inte låta känslorna styra våra steg, för vi måste handla och göra det vi vet är rätt enligt Guds ord.

Bevara ditt hjärta framför allt du bevarar, ty därifrån utgår livet – Ordspråksboken 4:23. Om Salomo, den visaste människa som någonsin levt, säger detta, bör vi ta det till oss. Hjärtats önskningar påverkar var vi kommer att hamna i livet. När vi uppfyller en av våra önskningar genom att handla efter den… av hela din själ, av hela ditt förstånd och av hela din kraft … – Markusevangeliet 12:30, ger vi faktiskt näring åt den önskan och får den att utvecklas till en ännu djupare längtan och passion. När vi sedan handlar efter denna starkare, passionerade önskan ger vi den ännu mer näring. På så sätt fortsätter den onda cirkeln och upprepar sig gång på gång.

I stället för att ge näring åt din önskan kan du välja att motverka den genom att handla emot den. Om du har en önskan som inte är god och behöver förändra den till en gudfruktig önskan, kan du handla emot din ursprungliga önskan och göra det som är rätt. Då börjar din dåliga önskan förändras till en önskan som är rätt. För där din skatt är, där kommer också ditt hjärta att vara – Matteusevangeliet 6:21; Lukasevangeliet 12:34.

Han sade till dem: ”Se till att ni aktar er för all slags girighet, för en människas liv består inte i överflödet av hennes ägodelar” – Lukasevangeliet 12:15. Girighet är en ogudaktig önskan. Om den inte hålls i schack blir den en snara. Vi behöver alla pengar, men nästan alla åtrår dem någon gång i livet. Varje dag ägnar vi mycket av vår tid åt att på något sätt arbeta för att tjäna pengar.

När vi gör det tenderar våra hjärtans önskningar att riktas mot vårt arbete. I stället bör vi se vårt arbete som ett sätt att utföra Guds verk genom att vara ett ljus och en uppmuntran för människorna omkring oss. Och allt vad ni gör i ord eller handling, gör det i Herren Jesu namn och tacka Gud Fadern genom honom – Kolosserbrevet 3:17.

Här och där hör vi mycket om att åtrå pengar, men vi hör inte mycket om att åtrå positioner som vi inte har rätt till. Det är inte fel att önska sig en ledande roll i affärslivet eller inom något annat område. Faktum är att det är en välsignelse för andra om någon träder fram och ger ledarskap för att välsigna dem. Men det är en felaktig önskan att vilja ha en ledande roll för sitt eget anseendes skull; det är högmod. Vi är alla människor och inte fullkomliga, men vi behöver höja oss över våra svagheter och vara till välsignelse. Vi vet alla att Gud har gett var och en av oss olika gåvor. Låt oss använda dessa gåvor för Guds rike.

Ibland försöker vi så hårt att tillfredsställa vårt kötts bekvämlighetsbehov att vi förlorar siktet på det verkliga syfte Gud har satt oss här för. Vårt kött står i vägen. Så var det med Akan. I stället för att helt koncentrera sig på kampen mot fienden sade Akan: ”När jag bland bytet fick se en fin babylonisk mantel, två hundra siklar silver och en guldtacka som vägde femtio siklar, blev jag begärlig efter det och tog det …” – Josua 7:21.

Jag vet inte hur det var, men jag föreställer mig höga ljud och blod överallt. Om det var så, vad tänkte Akan mitt i en blodig strid som fick honom att åtrå bytet? Det enda jag kan tänka mig är att Akans främsta önskan inte gällde Guds vilja utan att uppfylla sina egna önskningar. Det är mycket sorgligt att så många av Guds folk dödades på grund av Akans synd. Om vi ser att vi har en önskan som inte är gudfruktig, låt oss då fly från den önskan och sträva efter att få en gudfruktig önskan.

Vi ser att det är viktigt att utveckla en gudfruktig önskan som uppmuntrar oss eller för oss närmare Gud. Den viktigaste önskan är att verkligen lära känna Gud. Det ligger mycket nära det största budet – att älska Herren din Gud av hela ditt hjärta. För att älska Herren din Gud av hela ditt hjärta behöver du självklart också ha en önskan att älska honom. Men ibland behöver vi i livet fatta ett särskilt beslut eller vidta en bestämd åtgärd för att älska Gud av hela vårt hjärta. Det finns många saker som Gud kan vilja att vi överlåter åt honom.

Vi vet alla att grupptryck påverkar våra önskningar. Vi behöver bröder och systrar som vandrar vid vår sida och uppmuntrar oss i vår relation till Kristus. Vänner kan rikta vår uppmärksamhet mot något annat än Kristus. Därför behöver vi vara noga med vilka som är våra nära vänner. Vi behöver söka oss till vänner som bygger upp. En vän som kan gå vid vår sida och uppmuntra oss i vår vandring med Gud är värd allt. Som människor kan vi inte alltid se allt rätt på egen hand. Vi behöver andra som hjälper oss att se våra blinda fläckar. En nära vän som uppriktigt vill hjälpa oss att följa Gud hjälper oss att se på vad som är rätt i Guds ögon. Kanske behöver vi överlåta vårt kött åt Gud och ställa allt till rätta med honom, så att vi kan utveckla rena och gudfruktiga önskningar.

När vi ser på hjärtats önskningar märker vi att de har stor inverkan på vilka vi är och vilka vi kommer att bli. När vårt hjärta önskar något strävar vi efter det med en djup längtan. Bibeln innehåller faktiskt exempel på att Gud gav människor en önskan att tjäna honom. ”Jag steg upp om natten, jag och några få män som var med mig. Jag hade inte berättat för någon vad min Gud hade lagt i mitt hjärta att göra för Jerusalem. Jag hade inte heller något annat djur med mig än det jag red på” – Nehemja 2:12. Läser vi vidare … ”Mose kallade till sig Besalel och Oholiab och alla andra män med insikt, i vilkas hjärtan HERREN hade lagt vishet, var och en som kände sig manad i sitt hjärta att komma och utföra arbetet” – Andra Moseboken 36:2.

Kom ihåg att ordet önskan betyder en djup längtan, åtrå eller vilja. Om vi vill ha en blomstrande vandring med Gud måste vi ha de önskningar som Gud har, eftersom hans önskningar kommer att förändra våra liv. ”De åt och blev väl mätta, och han gav dem vad de önskade. De blev inte av med sitt begär. Men medan maten ännu var i deras munnar kom Guds vrede över dem, han dödade de kraftigaste bland dem och slog ner Israels utvalda män” – Psaltaren 78:29–31. Trots att Gud ledde israeliterna ut i öknen, gav dem vatten och manna och till och med en plats där de kunde tillbe honom, var de ändå inte nöjda och önskade sig andra saker. Israels barn fick sina önskningar uppfyllda, men det slutade med att de fick betala med sina egna liv.

Ett annat bra exempel på att Gud ger människor vad de önskar finns i Första Samuelsboken 8, där Israels barn ville ha en kung över sig, precis som alla de andra folken. ”De sade till honom: ’Du är gammal, och dina söner vandrar inte på dina vägar. Ge oss nu en kung som kan döma oss, liksom alla andra folk har.’ Men det misshagade Samuel att de sade: ’Ge oss en kung som kan döma oss.’ Samuel bad till HERREN. Då sade HERREN till Samuel: ’Lyssna till folket och allt vad de säger till dig. Det är inte dig de har förkastat, utan mig. De vill inte att jag ska vara kung över dem’” – Första Samuelsboken 8:5–7. O Israel, ”… han (Gud) gav dem vad de önskade – Psaltaren 78:29.”

Det låter som om Herren säger: ”Låt oss låta dem få som de vill och ge dem en kung.” Men senare i kapitlet räknar han upp allt det onda som kommer att följa med att ha en kung. Herren talar också om för Samuel vem som ska härska över Israels barn. När deras kung hade blivit smord behövde de tjäna honom och kunde inte längre tjäna enbart Gud. Tänk på varför Gud först och främst förde dem ut ur Egypten. Var det inte för att de skulle kunna tjäna den ende sanne Guden?

Precis som Israels barn har vi sett Guds underbara verk. Om vi har blivit födda av Guds Ande har han lett oss ut ur vårt ”Egypten”; han har visat oss livets väg; han har fört oss upp ur den djupa leran; han har ställt våra fötter på en fast klippa. Ändå tenderar vi människor att åtrå och längta efter något som vi tror är bättre. Vi ber Gud ge oss vishet och sörja för våra behov, men djupt inom oss ber vi Gud om att ge oss det vi själviskt önskar.

Vi behöver överlåta varje område av vårt liv åt Guds kontroll. Gud vet vad som är bäst för oss, men om vi insisterar kommer han att ge oss det vi själviskt önskar.

Kom ihåg att jorden inte är vårt hem. Slutet kommer, och det är det Gud har i åtanke. Vi vet inte vad som är bäst för oss, men det gör Gud. Låt oss ha tro och förändra våra önskningar så att de gäller det som Gud vill att vi ska fullborda i detta liv. Jag ska låta dig färdas fram över landets höjder och låta dig njuta av arvet efter din far Jakob. HERRENS mun har talat – Jesaja 58:14.

With a God so big, why would one fear?
He controls the sea, the storms that appear.
He knows tomorrow, before it has come.
The hairs of our head, He knows the sum.

Why would one question a God like this?
Why do some doubt, or ask amiss?
“Trust in the Lord” the Scripture has said.
But our own understanding, we lean on instead?

I’m sure it’s confusing, to the all-knowing One.
All the miracles, with a word, they were done!
He looks to and fro in this world today,
For one that will trust, without a delay.

The things of this world are so brilliant and fast.
Do we even need God, maybe old-fashioned at last?!
Enough with the folly, we all know the truth.
We have seen God working, yes, from our youth.

Nothing can replace our almighty God;
To say any different would certainly sound odd.
He’s waiting for the church to trust Him once more.
He stands and knocks; will you open the door?

Not just in a pinch, or when life’s too hard,
But every moment, your fears disregard.
He’s looking for a people once more in our day,
With confidence in God, His power to display.

by Barry Grant

Met zo’n grote God, waarom zou je bang zijn?
Hij beheerst de zee en de stormen die er zijn.
Hij kent morgen al, nog vóór die is gekomen.
Hij kent het aantal haren op ons hoofd, tot de laatste toe.

Waarom zou je aan zo’n God twijfelen?
Waarom twijfelen sommigen of vragen ze verkeerd?
‘Vertrouw op de Heer’, zegt de Schrift.
Maar in plaats daarvan steunen we op ons eigen inzicht?

Ik weet zeker dat het verwarrend is voor de Alwetende.
Alle wonderen werden door één woord verricht!
Hij kijkt vandaag de wereld rond,
op zoek naar iemand die zonder uitstel vertrouwt.

De dingen van deze wereld zijn zo schitterend en snel.
Hebben we God nog wel nodig, misschien is Hij inmiddels ouderwets?!
Genoeg dwaasheid, we kennen allemaal de waarheid.
We hebben God zien werken, ja, al vanaf onze jeugd.

Niets kan onze almachtige God vervangen;
iets anders beweren zou beslist vreemd klinken.
Hij wacht erop dat de kerk Hem weer vertrouwt.
Hij staat aan de deur en klopt; doe jij open?

Niet alleen als het erop aankomt of wanneer het leven te zwaar is,
maar elk moment: laat je angsten varen.
Hij zoekt in onze tijd opnieuw een volk,
dat met vertrouwen op God zijn kracht laat zien.

door Barry Grant

God the Potter is molding me.
What kind of vessel will I be:
To carry, to store, or for a drink?
A lamp, or a plate, or a kitchen sink?

I’m a little bit shallow, I admit,
For I’m focusing on me quite a bit.
But here is a thought,
I’m not the only pot.

About my life
are many others,
A husband, a daughter,
and some brothers.

The Potter’s hand is on them, too,
Making each of us, something new.
Another pot gives me a bump,
And now I have a little lump.

Into another pot I smack,
It seems they now have a crack.
Back to the Potter’s wheel we go,
Until His likeness, again does show.

If what I do, and what I say,
Changes the course of other’s clay,
Then with great care, I must behave,
Lest other’s pots become concave.

Useful pots are God’s desire,
Ones that can withstand the fire.
It’s not just me, and it’s not just you;
God’s working with other vessels too.

by Elizabeth Rust

This poem was inspired by the Scripture passage in Jeremiah 18:1-6.

God die Pottebakker vorm my.
Watter soort pot sal ek wees:
Om te dra, te bêre, of om uit te drink?
’n Lamp, ’n bord, of ’n kombuiswasbak?

Ek is ’n bietjie oppervlakkig, ek erken,
Want ek fokus nogal baie op myself.
Maar hier is ’n gedagte,
Ek is nie die enigste pot nie.

Om my lewe
is daar baie ander,
’n man, ’n dogter,
en ’n paar broers.

Die Pottebakker se hand is ook op hulle,
En maak elkeen van ons iets nuuts.
’n Ander pot stamp teen my,
En nou het ek ’n klein bultjie.

Ek stamp teen ’n ander pot,
Dit lyk of hulle nou ’n kraak het.
Terug na die Pottebakker se wiel gaan ons,
Totdat sy gelykenis weer verskyn.

As wat ek doen en wat ek sê,
Die koers van ander se klei verander,
Dan moet ek my baie versigtig gedra,
Sodat ander se potte nie hol word nie.

God begeer nuttige potte,
Wat die vuur kan weerstaan.
Dit gaan nie net oor my of net oor jou nie;
God werk ook met ander vate.

deur Elizabeth Rust

Hierdie gedig is geïnspireer deur die Skrifgedeelte in Jeremia 18:1-6.

Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalm 37:4.

Down deep within every person is a desire to be, or to do, something of value. If we, as humans, had no desire to do anything, life would be boring, and we would be nothing more than a robot. We all know that God wants more from us than to be a robot; He wants us to serve Him with our whole heart.

The meaning for the word desire is: to wish or long for; to crave; to want. Wish, want, crave, and covet all mean to have a longing for. Desire stresses the strength of feeling and often implies strong intention or aim.

Isn’t that what God wants from us—a desire with craving and intentional aim? Yes, it is, but this doesn’t happen on its own, nor does it happen automatically. Our desires are so strong that of ourselves we are no match for them; we need something outside of ourselves to be in control. According to the Bible, we must become born again. When we get born again, we become a new creature in Christ with new desires that God puts inside us. The way He does this, is by giving us a new heart.

God allows each of us to choose if we will serve Him or if we will not. He will not force us to yield ourselves to His will, nor will He force us to serve Him. But, if we are truly born again and serve the Lord joyfully and willingly, then He will give us godly desires which we will want to fulfill.

Does the Christian life become like clockwork just because we get a new heart and our desires have been turned towards serving God? I believe the answer is both yes and no. After we are walking with Christ for some time, we discover that Satan wants to change our desires in such a way that we would rather please him (Satan) instead of the Lord. Because of this, we need to be on guard. Satan wants to set spiritual snares for us. One of the ways he does this is by enticing our flesh.

There are good desires and bad desires. Some desires will bring us closer to Christ and some will draw us away. As Jesus walked on this earth, we know that His desire was to do the will of His Father. Out of His desire, He stayed focused on what He needed to do, even when His flesh was weak. There are two examples of this: one was when Jesus was tempted in the desert to make stones into bread, and the other was when He was in the garden praying right before He was crucified.

When we look at the account in the garden, we see that He did not want to take the cup that was before Him. In other words, Jesus desired to not go through the suffering, but praise God, He chose to please His Father. He laid down His flesh, obeyed the will of God, and allowed Himself to be crucified for our sins. Jesus looked at the long-term effect, and poured Himself into what He knew was right, rather than going by His own feelings. However, He did acknowledge His feelings by expressing them to God when He was praying in the garden. It is the same way with us—there are times that we need to be honest about our feelings and express them to God or to someone else. Yet we cannot walk by our feelings because we must act and do what we know is right according to the word of God.

Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23. If Solomon, the wisest man who ever lived says this, then we should take heed to it. The desires of the heart will make a difference on where we will end up in life. As we are fulfilling one of our desires by acting on it…with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength… –Mark 12:30, we actually feed that desire, causing it to develop into an even deeper longing and passion. As we then act on this stronger, passionate desire, we end up feeding that desire even more. Thus, the vicious cycle continues, repeating itself again and again.

Instead of feeding your desire, you can choose to hinder it—by acting against it. If you have a desire that is not good, and you need to change it to a godly desire, you can act against your original desire and do what is right. In so doing it will start to change your bad desire into one that is right. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also –Matthew 6:21; Luke 12:34.

And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth –Luke 12:15. Covetousness is an ungodly desire. Without bringing it into check, it will become a snare. Money is something that we all need, yet it is something that almost everyone at some point in life covets. Every day we spend much of our time working in some way to earn money.

In so doing, our heart’s desires tend to become focused on our work. Instead, we should see our job as a way of doing God’s work by being a light and encouragement to the ones around us. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him –Colossians 3:17.

Here and there we hear a lot about coveting money; however, we don’t hear much about coveting positions that are not lawful for us. It is not wrong to desire leadership in business or whatever it may be. In fact, it is a blessing for others if someone will stand up and provide leadership as a way to bless others. However, it is a wrong desire to want leadership for our own reputation, which is pride. We are all human and we are not perfect, yet we need to rise above our weaknesses and be a blessing. We all know that God gave each of us different gifts. Let’s use those gifts for the kingdom of God.

Sometimes we are trying so hard to fulfill our fleshly comforts that we lose sight of the real purpose that God has put us here. Our flesh stands in the way. It was this way with Achan. Instead of Achan putting his whole focus on the fight against the enemy, he said that, When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them… –Joshua 7:21.

I don’t know what it was like, but I picture there being loud noises and a bloody mess. If that’s the case, what was Achan thinking in the midst of a bloody battle that made him covet? The only thing I can think of, is that Achan’s number one desire was not on God’s will but was on fulfilling his own desires. It’s very sad that there were so many of God’s people killed because of Achan’s sin. If we see that we have a desire that is not godly, then let’s flee from that desire and work towards gaining a desire that is godly.

We see it is important to develop a godly desire that will encourage or lead us closer to God. The most important desire is to truly know God. That would be very close to the greatest commandment—to love the Lord thy God with all thy heart. To love the Lord thy God with all thy heart you obviously also need to have a desire to love Him. However, there are times in our life that we will need to take a specific action or purpose to love God with all our heart. There are many things that God may want us to surrender.

We all know that peer pressure influences our desires. We need brothers and sisters to walk beside us and encourage us in our relationship with Christ. Friends can draw our attention to something other than Christ. That is why we need to be careful who our close friends are. We need to seek out friends who will be upbuilding. A friend that can walk beside us and encourage us in our walk with God, is worth everything. As humans, we can’t always see everything correctly by ourselves. We need others to help us see our blind spots. A close friend who genuinely wants to help us follow God, will help us look at what is right in God’s eyes. Maybe we need to surrender our flesh and get right with God so we can develop desires that are pure and godly.

As we look at the heart’s desires, we see they have a major impact on who we are and who we will become. When our heart desires something, we pursue it with a deep longing. In fact, there are examples in the Bible where God gave people desires to serve Him. And I arose in the night, I and some few men with me; neither told I any man what my God had put in my heart to do at Jerusalem: neither was there any beast with me, save the beast that I rode upon –Nehemiah 2:12. Reading further… And Moses called Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, even every one whose heart stirred him up to come unto the work to do it –Exodus 36:2.

Remember, the word desire is a deep longing, craving, or wish. If we are wanting a walk with God that is flourishing, then we must have the desires that God has, since His desires will change our life. So they did eat, and were well filled: for he gave them their own desire; They were not estranged from their lust. But while their meat was yet in their mouths, The wrath of God came upon them, and slew the fattest of them, and smote down the chosen men of Israel –Psalm 78:29-31. Even though God led the Israelites into the wilderness, gave them water and manna, and even a place to worship Him, they were still not satisfied and desired other things. The children of Israel were granted their desires, but they ended up needing to pay with their own lives.

Another good example of God giving people their own desires is found in 1 Samuel 8 when the children of Israel wanted a king over them just like all the other nations. And [they] said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations. But the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the LORD. And the LORD said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee: for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them –1 Samuel 8:5-7. Oh Israel, …for he (God) gave them their own desire –Psalm 78:29.

It sounds like the Lord is saying, “Let’s let them have their own way and give them a king.” However, later in the chapter He lists all the bad things that will come with having a king. The Lord also tells Samuel who will rule over the children of Israel. After their king was anointed, they needed to serve him and could no longer serve God only. Consider why God brought them out of Egypt in the first place. Wasn’t it so they could serve the only true God?

Just like the children of Israel, we have seen God’s wonderous works. If we have been born of God’s Spirit, He led us out of our “Egypt”; He showed us the path of life; He brought us out of the miry clay; He set our feet on a solid rock. Still, we as humans tend to covet and long for something that we think is better. We ask God to give us wisdom and that He would provide for our needs, yet down deep inside we beg for God to give us our selfish desires.

We need to surrender every area of our life to God’s control. God knows what is best for us, however, if we insist, He will give us according to our selfish desires.

Remember, this earth is not our home. The end is coming, which is what God has in mind. We don’t know what is best for us, but God does. Let’s have faith and change our desires for that which God wants us to fulfill in this life. Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart –Psalms 37:4. And, Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it–Isaiah 58:14

Deléitate también en el SEÑOR, y él te concederá los deseos de tu corazón –Salmo 37:4.

En lo más profundo de cada persona hay un deseo de ser o hacer algo valioso. Si nosotros, como seres humanos, no tuviéramos ningún deseo de hacer nada, la vida sería aburrida y no seríamos más que un robot. Todos sabemos que Dios quiere de nosotros más que ser un robot; quiere que le sirvamos de todo corazón.

El significado de la palabra deseo es: querer o anhelar; ansiar; querer. Desear, querer, ansiar y codiciar significan anhelar algo. Deseo enfatiza la intensidad del sentimiento y a menudo implica una intención o un propósito firmes.

¿No es eso lo que Dios quiere de nosotros: un deseo con ansia y propósito intencional? Sí, lo es, pero esto no sucede por sí solo ni ocurre automáticamente. Nuestros deseos son tan fuertes que por nosotros mismos no podemos hacerles frente; necesitamos algo ajeno a nosotros que los controle. Según la Biblia, debemos nacer de nuevo. Cuando nacemos de nuevo, nos convertimos en una nueva criatura en Cristo, con nuevos deseos que Dios pone dentro de nosotros. Lo hace dándonos un corazón nuevo.

Dios permite que cada uno de nosotros elija si le servirá o no. No nos obligará a someternos a su voluntad ni nos obligará a servirle. Pero si verdaderamente hemos nacido de nuevo y servimos al Señor con gozo y de buena voluntad, entonces él nos dará deseos piadosos que querremos cumplir.

¿Se vuelve la vida cristiana algo que funciona como un reloj solo porque recibimos un corazón nuevo y nuestros deseos se han vuelto hacia el servicio a Dios? Creo que la respuesta es sí y no. Después de caminar con Cristo por algún tiempo, descubrimos que Satanás quiere cambiar nuestros deseos de tal manera que prefiramos agradarle a él (Satanás) en vez de al Señor. Por eso, debemos estar alerta. Satanás quiere tendernos trampas espirituales. Una de las maneras en que lo hace es tentando nuestra carne.

Hay buenos deseos y malos deseos. Algunos deseos nos acercarán más a Cristo y otros nos alejarán. Mientras Jesús caminó sobre esta tierra, sabemos que su deseo era hacer la voluntad de su Padre. Debido a ese deseo, mantuvo la atención puesta en lo que debía hacer, aun cuando su carne era débil. Hay dos ejemplos de esto: uno ocurrió cuando Jesús fue tentado en el desierto a convertir piedras en pan, y el otro, cuando estaba en el jardín orando justo antes de ser crucificado.

Al considerar el relato del jardín, vemos que no quería tomar la copa que tenía delante. En otras palabras, Jesús deseaba no pasar por el sufrimiento, pero ¡alabado sea Dios!, eligió agradar a su Padre. Dejó de lado su carne, obedeció la voluntad de Dios y permitió que lo crucificaran por nuestros pecados. Jesús consideró el efecto a largo plazo y se entregó a lo que sabía que era correcto, en lugar de dejarse llevar por sus propios sentimientos. Sin embargo, reconoció sus sentimientos al expresárselos a Dios cuando oraba en el jardín. Lo mismo ocurre con nosotros: hay momentos en que debemos ser sinceros acerca de nuestros sentimientos y expresárselos a Dios o a otra persona. Sin embargo, no podemos guiarnos por nuestros sentimientos, porque debemos actuar y hacer lo que sabemos que es correcto según la palabra de Dios.

Con toda diligencia guarda tu corazón, porque de él brotan las fuentes de la vida –Proverbios 4:23. Si Salomón, el hombre más sabio que jamás haya vivido, dice esto, deberíamos prestarle atención. Los deseos del corazón influirán en el lugar al que lleguemos en la vida. Cuando cumplimos uno de nuestros deseos al actuar conforme a él…con toda tu alma, y con toda tu mente, y con todas tus fuerzas… –Marcos 12:30, en realidad alimentamos ese deseo y hacemos que se convierta en un anhelo y una pasión aún más profundos. Luego, al actuar conforme a ese deseo más intenso y apasionado, terminamos alimentándolo todavía más. Así continúa el círculo vicioso, repitiéndose una y otra vez.

En vez de alimentar tu deseo, puedes optar por frenarlo, actuando en contra de él. Si tienes un deseo que no es bueno y necesitas cambiarlo por un deseo piadoso, puedes actuar en contra de tu deseo original y hacer lo correcto. Al hacerlo, empezarás a cambiar tu mal deseo por uno correcto. Porque donde esté vuestro tesoro, allí estará también vuestro corazón –Mateo 6:21; Lucas 12:34.

Y les dijo: Mirad, y guardaos de toda avaricia, porque la vida del hombre no consiste en la abundancia de los bienes que posee –Lucas 12:15. La avaricia es un deseo impío. Si no la controlamos, se convertirá en una trampa. Todos necesitamos dinero y, sin embargo, casi todo el mundo lo codicia en algún momento de la vida. Cada día dedicamos gran parte de nuestro tiempo a trabajar de alguna manera para ganar dinero.

Al hacerlo, los deseos de nuestro corazón tienden a centrarse en nuestro trabajo. En cambio, deberíamos ver nuestro empleo como una manera de hacer la obra de Dios, siendo luz y ánimo para quienes nos rodean. Y todo lo que hagáis, sea de palabra o de hecho, hacedlo todo en el nombre del Señor Jesús, dando gracias a Dios Padre por medio de él –Colosenses 3:17.

De vez en cuando oímos hablar mucho de codiciar el dinero; sin embargo, no oímos mucho acerca de codiciar puestos que no nos corresponden legítimamente. No está mal desear un puesto de liderazgo en los negocios o en cualquier otro ámbito. De hecho, es una bendición para los demás que alguien dé un paso al frente y ejerza el liderazgo para bendecirlos. Sin embargo, desear el liderazgo para nuestra propia reputación es un deseo equivocado, pues es orgullo. Todos somos humanos y no somos perfectos; aun así, necesitamos superar nuestras debilidades y ser una bendición. Todos sabemos que Dios nos dio dones diferentes a cada uno. Usemos esos dones para el reino de Dios.

A veces nos esforzamos tanto por satisfacer las comodidades de nuestra carne que perdemos de vista el verdadero propósito para el que Dios nos puso aquí. Nuestra carne se interpone. Así ocurrió con Acán. En vez de concentrarse por completo en la lucha contra el enemigo, Acán dijo: Cuando vi entre los despojos un hermoso manto babilónico, doscientos siclos de plata y un lingote de oro que pesaba cincuenta siclos, los codicié y los tomé… –Josué 7:21.

No sé cómo fue, pero me imagino que había ruidos fuertes y una escena sangrienta. Si fue así, ¿qué pensaba Acán en medio de una batalla sangrienta que lo llevó a codiciar? Lo único que se me ocurre es que el deseo principal de Acán no era hacer la voluntad de Dios, sino satisfacer sus propios deseos. Es muy triste que tantos del pueblo de Dios fueran muertos a causa del pecado de Acán. Si vemos que tenemos un deseo que no es piadoso, huyamos de él y esforcémonos por adquirir un deseo piadoso.

Vemos que es importante cultivar un deseo piadoso que nos anime o nos acerque más a Dios. El deseo más importante es conocer verdaderamente a Dios. Eso estaría muy cerca del mandamiento más importante: amar al Señor tu Dios con todo tu corazón. Para amar al Señor tu Dios con todo tu corazón, obviamente también necesitas tener el deseo de amarlo. Sin embargo, hay momentos en nuestra vida en que tendremos que tomar una medida concreta o proponernos amar a Dios con todo nuestro corazón. Hay muchas cosas a las que Dios quizá quiera que renunciemos.

Todos sabemos que la presión de grupo influye en nuestros deseos. Necesitamos hermanos y hermanas que caminen a nuestro lado y nos animen en nuestra relación con Cristo. Los amigos pueden desviar nuestra atención hacia algo que no sea Cristo. Por eso debemos tener cuidado con quiénes son nuestros amigos íntimos. Debemos buscar amigos que nos edifiquen. Un amigo que pueda caminar a nuestro lado y animarnos en nuestro caminar con Dios vale muchísimo. Como seres humanos, no siempre podemos ver todo correctamente por nuestra cuenta. Necesitamos que otros nos ayuden a reconocer nuestros puntos ciegos. Un amigo cercano que realmente quiera ayudarnos a seguir a Dios nos ayudará a considerar lo que es correcto a los ojos de Dios. Quizá tengamos que rendir nuestra carne y ponernos en orden con Dios para poder cultivar deseos puros y piadosos.

Al considerar los deseos del corazón, vemos que tienen un gran impacto en quiénes somos y en quiénes llegaremos a ser. Cuando nuestro corazón desea algo, lo perseguimos con profundo anhelo. De hecho, hay ejemplos en la Biblia en los que Dios dio a las personas deseos de servirle. Y me levanté de noche, yo y unos pocos hombres conmigo; y no declaré a hombre alguno lo que mi Dios había puesto en mi corazón que hiciese en Jerusalén; ni había animal conmigo, excepto aquel en que yo cabalgaba –Nehemías 2:12. Sigamos leyendo… Y llamó Moisés a Bezaleel y a Aholiab, y a todo hombre sabio de corazón, a quien el SEÑOR había dado sabiduría en su corazón, a todo aquel cuyo corazón lo movió a venir a la obra para hacerla –Éxodo 36:2.

Recuerda que la palabra deseo significa un anhelo profundo, un ansia o un querer. Si queremos que nuestro caminar con Dios prospere, debemos tener los deseos que Dios tiene, pues sus deseos cambiarán nuestra vida. Y comieron, y se saciaron bien; pues les dio lo que desearon. No se apartaron de su codicia. Pero mientras su comida estaba aún en sus bocas, vino sobre ellos la ira de Dios, mató a los más robustos de ellos y abatió a los jóvenes de Israel –Salmo 78:29-31. Aunque Dios condujo a los israelitas al desierto, les dio agua y maná, e incluso un lugar donde adorarlo, ellos seguían insatisfechos y deseaban otras cosas. A los hijos de Israel se les concedieron sus deseos, pero acabaron pagando con sus propias vidas.

Otro buen ejemplo de Dios concediendo a las personas sus propios deseos se encuentra en 1 Samuel 8, cuando los hijos de Israel quisieron tener un rey sobre ellos, como todas las demás naciones. Y [ellos] le dijeron: He aquí, tú eres viejo, y tus hijos no andan en tus caminos; ahora, constitúyenos un rey que nos juzgue, como todas las naciones. Pero a Samuel le desagradó que dijeran: Danos un rey que nos juzgue. Y Samuel oró al SEÑOR. Y el SEÑOR dijo a Samuel: Escucha la voz del pueblo en todo lo que te diga, porque no te han rechazado a ti, sino que me han rechazado a mí, para que no reine sobre ellos –1 Samuel 8:5-7. ¡Oh, Israel!, …pues él (Dios) les dio lo que desearon –Salmo 78:29.

Parece que el Señor está diciendo: «Dejemos que se salgan con la suya y démosles un rey». Sin embargo, más adelante en el capítulo enumera todas las cosas malas que vendrán con tener un rey. El Señor también le dice a Samuel quién gobernará sobre los hijos de Israel. Después de que su rey fuera ungido, tuvieron que servirle y ya no podían servir únicamente a Dios. Considera por qué Dios los sacó de Egipto en primer lugar. ¿No fue para que pudieran servir al único Dios verdadero?

Al igual que los hijos de Israel, hemos visto las maravillosas obras de Dios. Si hemos nacido del Espíritu de Dios, él nos sacó de nuestro «Egipto»; nos mostró el camino de la vida; nos sacó del lodo cenagoso; afirmó nuestros pies sobre una roca firme. Sin embargo, nosotros, como seres humanos, tendemos a codiciar y anhelar algo que creemos mejor. Le pedimos a Dios que nos dé sabiduría y provea para nuestras necesidades, pero en lo profundo rogamos a Dios que nos conceda nuestros deseos egoístas.

Necesitamos someter cada aspecto de nuestra vida al control de Dios. Dios sabe qué es lo mejor para nosotros; sin embargo, si insistimos, nos dará conforme a nuestros deseos egoístas.

Recuerda que esta tierra no es nuestro hogar. Se acerca el fin, y eso es lo que Dios tiene en mente. No sabemos qué es lo mejor para nosotros, pero Dios sí. Tengamos fe y cambiemos nuestros deseos por aquello que Dios quiere que cumplamos en esta vida. Deléitate también en el SEÑOR, y él te concederá los deseos de tu corazón –Salmos 37:4. Y, Entonces te deleitarás en el SEÑOR; y yo te haré cabalgar sobre las alturas de la tierra, y te alimentaré con la herencia de Jacob tu padre, porque la boca del SEÑOR lo ha dicho–Isaías 58:14
