Greetings of Christian love to one and all. This past year and a half have been challenging in one way or another for most people. My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing –James 1:2-4.

We trust that no matter what each of you has faced your inner motivation echoes with the words of Apostle Paul, … for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. –Philippians 4:11-13.

As we are already almost halfway through another year, I stop to consider how time keeps disappearing at an ever-increasing rate of speed. For many, the last 16 to 18 months have been quite challenging as the Covid-19 pandemic and its aftereffects continue to wreak havoc with all that used to be considered normal. For us, some of these aftereffects have hindered us from getting this issue of the magazine out in a timely manner. Our apologies. However, things are back on track to be able to get the next issue out within the next several months, thus allowing us to get back onto our normal schedule once more.

I see the pandemic and the resulting aftereffects as quite similar to one big traffic jam. First, many vehicles are all traveling along quite smoothly at the speed limit. Gradually more and more vehicles join the flow, until the highway becomes quite congested. However, things still continue to flow unhindered until suddenly one vehicle brakes sharply and swerves to avoid some debris on the roadway. Immediately, there is a ripple-effect or domino-effect, as each vehicle brakes to avoid hitting the one in front of them that just applied their brakes. I have seen this type of situation create stop-and-go traffic for a mile or more as traffic slows to a crawl, then once each vehicle finally gets past the offending object they can once more accelerate to their previous rate of speed.

With our world’s economies, both local and global, the same thing seemingly has happened, howbeit on a much, much larger scale. First came the shutdowns, both local and national, causing businesses to lose production and sales. Then as businesses reopened and their workers began to get sick, further production was lost. Suddenly, many manufacturers found themselves behind in their inventory reserve, which graduated into being behind in their ability to supply the demand. Since so much of our world’s businesses have developed trade at a global level, there are many products that are not available for sale as manufacturers wait for the “company overseas” to once more have enough supply to meet the global demand. Another problem that has developed more recently is that due to the major imbalance of supply versus demand on a global level, the cost of purchase for many products has skyrocketed awakening fears among some economists of a global crisis due to inflation.

Where does this leave the church? It seems that the “enemy of our souls” has used this global event to cause churches everywhere to struggle on many levels. I have on my bookshelf a book titled Conscience in Crisis, which is about church history. This book specifically examines the struggle of the “peace” churches in colonial America. One of the key points the book focuses on is that the global events of that time period shook the very foundations of their faith and practice. This caused the collective conscience of the churches to face an unprecedented crisis level, which many individuals never overcame. Some gave up the faith, some quit going to church, some walked away from their church and started going to more worldly churches. And the ones that remained, struggled substantially through many issues until they once more were considered stable.

Our Perspective Matters

When I think of the word perspective, the definition I am using is: a particular attitude toward, or way, of regarding something; a point of view. It is like the prescription of the glasses we have in front of our eyes causing us to see things in a distorted manner or with a clear 20/20 view. Or it is like using a filter in your computer or in your vehicle engine, which only lets through that which is pre-determined should be allowed.

So, our perspective is akin to using a filter or a pair of glasses. Our perspective is shaped by many things: the way we were trained as children, the role models we chose to follow during our formative years, the reading material we absorbed, the spiritual mentors we opened our hearts to, and the peers we embraced throughout our lifetime. Also, our perspective determines how we look at situations, how we interact with God, how we view sin and salvation, and how we respond to both friends and enemies.

In our world today, there are many perspectives, all vying for our allegiance. Many are the “special interest” groups clamoring for our support of their cause. There’s race discrimination on both sides of the matter. There are voices crying “foul” in their effort to gain support and an advantage against their opponents regarding voting rights, honesty of the election outcomes, and desired legislative changes to the judicial system and the Constitution. While there have always been multiple sides to an issue, there has usually been an effort to work together for the good of all. However, in the last number of years it seems that numerous issues have become quite divisive to the point of polarizing the people into two camps. The balance of power in government has been swinging back and forth from the one side to the other. This polarization has been causing bitterness and anger to build, in some instances erupting into violence and vandalism. In other instances, it has caused normally level-headed individuals to lose their cool and make “knee-jerk” reactionary decisions which are totally out of character for them.

In the midst of all this chaos and confusion, what is our perspective as the church? Are we remaining steadfast in allowing God and His Word to mold and shape our perspective to be aligned with His perspective? Or have we allowed the pressure of one peer group or another to start pushing us off-course in our walk as strangers and pilgrims?

I have heard reports of some churches in other parts of the world being pushed by their local government to not meet for fellowship and group worship. There are families whose conscience chooses to obey the government in long-term mask wearing and social distancing. Individuals have become discouraged. Families have become isolated. And churches have struggled through one issue after another in their efforts to maintain peace among the brethren.

As I have interacted with people who are not regular church goers, or those who attend a “dying” church, an “older” church, or a “small country” church, there are numerous things I have heard them testify regarding the churches of the conservative, Anabaptist persuasion. These people are awed by the way we help each other both on a regular basis and when tragedy strikes. They can’t comprehend the large size of our weddings and especially our funerals. They don’t understand how our children are mild-mannered and respectful of others.

Let’s take heed and use wisdom as we continue facing the challenges in the days to come. From my limited vantage point, I believe that long-term mask wearing and social distancing that is practiced at the expense of normal worship as we understand the Scriptures to teach, will eventually have a negative ripple effect on us as believers.

Many years ago, as I was involved in learning from the “counseling model”, it was spoken of as quite troubling and detrimental to interpersonal relationships IF someone had a “mask” on (figuratively). As I have evaluated and considered the long-term effect of a person having a “mask” on (literally), I believe it WILL cause as much and more detriment to interpersonal relationships. There is something about visiting with brothers and sisters of the faith when you can see their whole face. Without even realizing it, we read body language and facial expressions, which aids in understanding and conveying thoughts as we communicate with one another. Thus, it is my personal opinion that long-term mask wearing and social distancing by a local church body will eventually degrade the level of spiritual life and fervor to the point of someday that local body will no longer stand out from all the rest of the nominal Christians around them.

May God bless each one. May we not give up the spiritual fight. May we ever keep our eyes fixed on our Father, our Saviour, and our eternal home.

Curvin L Wenger

","section":"From the Editor","subtitle":null,"title":"From the Editor"},"source_context":{"byline":{"authors":[{"location":null,"name":"Curvin L Wenger","role":"Editor"}],"raw":"Curvin L Wenger"}},"target_language":"Italian","terminology_glossary":{},"translation":{"html":"

Un saluto di amore cristiano a tutti. L'ultimo anno e mezzo è stato impegnativo, in un modo o nell'altro, per la maggior parte delle persone. Fratelli miei, considerate una grande gioia quando vi trovate in prove di ogni genere, sapendo che la prova della vostra fede produce perseveranza. E la perseveranza compia pienamente l'opera sua, affinché siate perfetti e completi, senza mancare di nulla –Giacomo 1:2-4.

Confidiamo che, qualunque cosa abbiate affrontato, la motivazione interiore di ciascuno di voi faccia eco alle parole dell'apostolo Paolo: … infatti ho imparato ad accontentarmi dello stato in cui mi trovo. So vivere nella povertà e so vivere nell'abbondanza; in ogni cosa e in ogni circostanza ho imparato a essere saziato e ad avere fame, a essere nell'abbondanza e a essere nella penuria. Io posso ogni cosa in colui che mi fortifica. –Filippesi 4:11-13.

Essendo già quasi a metà di un altro anno, mi fermo a riflettere su come il tempo continui a volare via a una velocità sempre crescente. Per molti, gli ultimi 16-18 mesi sono stati piuttosto impegnativi, poiché la pandemia di Covid-19 e i suoi effetti persistenti continuano a sconvolgere tutto ciò che un tempo era considerato normale. Per noi, alcuni di questi effetti hanno ostacolato la pubblicazione puntuale di questo numero della rivista. Ce ne scusiamo. Tuttavia, le cose sono tornate in carreggiata e potremo pubblicare il prossimo numero nei prossimi mesi, tornando così ancora una volta al nostro normale calendario.

Vedo la pandemia e i suoi effetti conseguenti come qualcosa di molto simile a un enorme ingorgo stradale. All'inizio, molti veicoli viaggiano tutti senza intoppi al limite di velocità. A poco a poco si aggiungono sempre più veicoli, finché l'autostrada diventa molto congestionata. Eppure il traffico continua a scorrere senza ostacoli, finché all'improvviso un veicolo frena bruscamente e sterza per evitare dei detriti sulla carreggiata. Subito si produce un effetto a catena, o domino, perché ogni veicolo frena per evitare di tamponare quello davanti, che ha appena frenato. Ho visto situazioni di questo tipo creare un traffico a singhiozzo per un miglio o più: il traffico rallenta fino quasi a fermarsi, poi, una volta che ogni veicolo ha finalmente superato l'ostacolo, può accelerare di nuovo fino a raggiungere la velocità precedente.

Lo stesso sembra essere accaduto alle economie del nostro mondo, sia locali che globali, ma su una scala molto, molto più ampia. Per primi sono arrivati i blocchi, locali e nazionali, che hanno fatto perdere alle aziende produzione e vendite. Poi, quando le aziende hanno riaperto e i loro lavoratori hanno cominciato ad ammalarsi, si è persa ulteriore produzione. Improvvisamente, molti produttori si sono trovati con scorte inferiori al necessario, e questo ha portato a non riuscire a soddisfare la domanda. Poiché molte aziende del nostro mondo hanno sviluppato scambi commerciali a livello globale, molti prodotti non sono disponibili per la vendita mentre i produttori aspettano che la «società all'estero» disponga di nuovo di una quantità sufficiente per soddisfare la domanda globale. Un altro problema emerso più di recente è che, a causa del grave squilibrio tra offerta e domanda a livello globale, il costo d'acquisto di molti prodotti è salito alle stelle, risvegliando in alcuni economisti timori di una crisi globale dovuta all'inflazione.

Dove lascia tutto questo la chiesa? Sembra che il «nemico delle nostre anime» abbia usato questo evento globale per far sì che le chiese ovunque si trovino in difficoltà su molti fronti. Ho nella mia libreria un libro intitolato Conscience in Crisis, che tratta della storia della chiesa. Questo libro esamina in particolare le difficoltà delle chiese «pacifiste» nell'America coloniale. Uno dei punti chiave su cui si concentra è che gli eventi globali di quel periodo scossero le fondamenta stesse della loro fede e della loro pratica. Ciò fece sì che la coscienza collettiva delle chiese affrontasse una crisi senza precedenti, dalla quale molti individui non si ripresero mai. Alcuni abbandonarono la fede, alcuni smisero di andare in chiesa, altri lasciarono la propria chiesa e cominciarono a frequentare chiese più mondane. E quelli che rimasero affrontarono notevoli difficoltà e molte questioni, finché non furono nuovamente considerati stabili.

La nostra prospettiva è importante

Quando penso alla parola prospettiva, la definizione che uso è: un atteggiamento particolare verso qualcosa, o un modo particolare di considerarla; un punto di vista. È come la prescrizione degli occhiali che abbiamo davanti agli occhi, che ci porta a vedere le cose in modo distorto oppure con una visione nitida da 10/10. Oppure è come usare un filtro nel computer o nel motore del veicolo, che lascia passare soltanto ciò che è stato stabilito in anticipo che debba essere consentito.

La nostra prospettiva, dunque, è simile all'uso di un filtro o di un paio di occhiali. La nostra prospettiva è plasmata da molte cose: il modo in cui siamo stati educati da bambini, i modelli che abbiamo scelto di seguire negli anni della formazione, il materiale di lettura che abbiamo assimilato, i mentori spirituali ai quali abbiamo aperto il cuore e i coetanei che abbiamo accolto nella nostra vita. Inoltre, la nostra prospettiva determina come guardiamo alle situazioni, come interagiamo con Dio, come consideriamo il peccato e la salvezza e come rispondiamo tanto agli amici quanto ai nemici.

Nel mondo di oggi vi sono molte prospettive, tutte in competizione per ottenere la nostra fedeltà. Sono numerosi i gruppi di «interesse particolare» che reclamano il nostro sostegno per la loro causa. La discriminazione razziale esiste da entrambe le parti della questione. Ci sono voci che gridano «ingiustizia» nel tentativo di ottenere sostegno e un vantaggio sui propri avversari riguardo al diritto di voto, alla correttezza dei risultati elettorali e alle modifiche legislative desiderate del sistema giudiziario e della Costituzione. Sebbene una questione abbia sempre avuto più punti di vista, di solito si è cercato di collaborare per il bene di tutti. Tuttavia, negli ultimi anni numerose questioni sembrano essere diventate molto divisive, al punto da polarizzare le persone in due schieramenti. L'equilibrio del potere nel governo oscilla da una parte all'altra. Questa polarizzazione ha fatto crescere amarezza e rabbia, che in alcuni casi sono sfociate in violenza e vandalismo. In altri casi, ha portato persone normalmente equilibrate a perdere la calma e a prendere decisioni reattive, «di pancia», del tutto insolite per loro.

In mezzo a tutto questo caos e a questa confusione, qual è la nostra prospettiva come chiesa? Restiamo saldi nel permettere a Dio e alla sua Parola di plasmare la nostra prospettiva, affinché sia in linea con la sua? Oppure abbiamo permesso che la pressione di un gruppo di coetanei o di un altro cominciasse a farci deviare dal nostro cammino di stranieri e pellegrini?

Ho sentito riferire che alcune chiese in altre parti del mondo sono state spinte dai governi locali a non riunirsi per la comunione fraterna e il culto comunitario. Ci sono famiglie la cui coscienza sceglie di obbedire al governo indossando mascherine e mantenendo il distanziamento sociale a lungo termine. Le persone si sono scoraggiate. Le famiglie si sono isolate. E le chiese hanno affrontato una questione dopo l'altra nel tentativo di mantenere la pace tra i fratelli.

Parlando con persone che non frequentano regolarmente la chiesa, o che frequentano una chiesa «in declino», una chiesa «di persone anziane» o una chiesa «di campagna», ho sentito molte testimonianze riguardo alle chiese di orientamento anabattista conservatore. Queste persone sono sbalordite dal modo in cui ci aiutiamo a vicenda, sia nella vita quotidiana che quando ci colpisce una tragedia. Non riescono a comprendere quanto siano numerosi i partecipanti ai nostri matrimoni e, soprattutto, ai nostri funerali. Non capiscono come i nostri figli siano miti e rispettosi degli altri.

Prestiamo attenzione e usiamo saggezza mentre continuiamo ad affrontare le sfide dei giorni a venire. Dal mio limitato punto di osservazione, credo che indossare mascherine e mantenere il distanziamento sociale a lungo termine, quando ciò avviene a scapito del culto normale secondo ciò che comprendiamo che le Scritture insegnino, avrà infine un effetto negativo a catena su di noi come credenti.

Molti anni fa, quando ero impegnato ad apprendere il «modello di consulenza», si diceva che fosse assai problematico e dannoso per le relazioni interpersonali SE qualcuno portava una «maschera» (in senso figurato). Dopo aver valutato e considerato l'effetto a lungo termine di una persona che porta una «maschera» (letteralmente), credo che causerà danni altrettanto grandi, se non maggiori, alle relazioni interpersonali. C'è qualcosa di speciale nel far visita a fratelli e sorelle nella fede quando si può vedere il loro volto intero. Senza nemmeno rendercene conto, leggiamo il linguaggio del corpo e le espressioni facciali, e questo ci aiuta a comprendere e a trasmettere i pensieri mentre comunichiamo gli uni con gli altri. Pertanto, secondo la mia opinione personale, indossare mascherine e mantenere il distanziamento sociale a lungo termine all'interno di una chiesa locale finirà per ridurre il livello di vita spirituale e di fervore, al punto che un giorno quella comunità locale non si distinguerà più da tutti gli altri cristiani nominali che la circondano.

Che Dio benedica ciascuno. Che non rinunciamo alla lotta spirituale. Che teniamo sempre gli occhi fissi sul nostro Padre, sul nostro Salvatore e sulla nostra dimora eterna.

Curvin L Wenger

With a God so big, why would one fear?
He controls the sea, the storms that appear.
He knows tomorrow, before it has come.
The hairs of our head, He knows the sum.

Why would one question a God like this?
Why do some doubt, or ask amiss?
“Trust in the Lord” the Scripture has said.
But our own understanding, we lean on instead?

I’m sure it’s confusing, to the all-knowing One.
All the miracles, with a word, they were done!
He looks to and fro in this world today,
For one that will trust, without a delay.

The things of this world are so brilliant and fast.
Do we even need God, maybe old-fashioned at last?!
Enough with the folly, we all know the truth.
We have seen God working, yes, from our youth.

Nothing can replace our almighty God;
To say any different would certainly sound odd.
He’s waiting for the church to trust Him once more.
He stands and knocks; will you open the door?

Not just in a pinch, or when life’s too hard,
But every moment, your fears disregard.
He’s looking for a people once more in our day,
With confidence in God, His power to display.

by Barry Grant

Με έναν τόσο μεγάλο Θεό, γιατί να φοβάται κανείς;
Εκείνος κυβερνά τη θάλασσα και τις καταιγίδες που ξεσπούν.
Γνωρίζει το αύριο, πριν ακόμη έρθει.
Ξέρει πόσες είναι οι τρίχες του κεφαλιού μας.

Γιατί να αμφισβητεί κανείς έναν τέτοιο Θεό;
Γιατί κάποιοι αμφιβάλλουν ή ρωτούν λανθασμένα;
«Να εμπιστεύεσαι τον Κύριο», λέει η Γραφή.
Κι όμως, στηριζόμαστε στη δική μας κατανόηση;

Είμαι βέβαιος πως αυτό προκαλεί σύγχυση στον Παντογνώστη.
Όλα τα θαύματα έγιναν με έναν λόγο!
Σήμερα κοιτάζει πέρα δώθε σε όλο τον κόσμο,
αναζητώντας κάποιον που θα εμπιστευτεί χωρίς καθυστέρηση.

Τα πράγματα αυτού του κόσμου είναι τόσο λαμπρά και γρήγορα.
Χρειαζόμαστε άραγε καν τον Θεό, ίσως να είναι πια παλιομοδίτικος;!
Αρκετά με τις ανοησίες, όλοι ξέρουμε την αλήθεια.
Έχουμε δει τον Θεό να ενεργεί, ναι, από τα νιάτα μας.

Τίποτα δεν μπορεί να αντικαταστήσει τον παντοδύναμο Θεό μας·
Το αντίθετο θα ακουγόταν σίγουρα παράξενο.
Περιμένει η εκκλησία να Τον εμπιστευτεί ξανά.
Στέκεται και χτυπά· θα ανοίξεις την πόρτα;

Όχι μόνο σε μια δύσκολη στιγμή ή όταν η ζωή γίνεται πολύ δύσκολη,
αλλά κάθε στιγμή, παραμερίζοντας τους φόβους σου.
Και πάλι στις μέρες μας αναζητά έναν λαό,
που με εμπιστοσύνη στον Θεό θα φανερώσει τη δύναμή Του.

του Barry Grant

God the Potter is molding me.
What kind of vessel will I be:
To carry, to store, or for a drink?
A lamp, or a plate, or a kitchen sink?

I’m a little bit shallow, I admit,
For I’m focusing on me quite a bit.
But here is a thought,
I’m not the only pot.

About my life
are many others,
A husband, a daughter,
and some brothers.

The Potter’s hand is on them, too,
Making each of us, something new.
Another pot gives me a bump,
And now I have a little lump.

Into another pot I smack,
It seems they now have a crack.
Back to the Potter’s wheel we go,
Until His likeness, again does show.

If what I do, and what I say,
Changes the course of other’s clay,
Then with great care, I must behave,
Lest other’s pots become concave.

Useful pots are God’s desire,
Ones that can withstand the fire.
It’s not just me, and it’s not just you;
God’s working with other vessels too.

by Elizabeth Rust

This poem was inspired by the Scripture passage in Jeremiah 18:1-6.

Бог-Гончар меня лепит опять.
Каким сосудом мне стать:
Для ноши, хранения или питья?
Лампой, тарелкой, раковиной — чем быть мне, друзья?

Признаюсь, я немного поверхностна,
Ведь о себе думаю я часто и пристрастно.
Но вот что пришло мне на ум:
Я не один только горшок в миру.

Вокруг моей жизни
немало людей:
муж, дочь,
и братья моей семьи.

Рука Гончара и над ними трудится,
Чтобы каждый из нас новым родился.
Другой горшок толкнёт меня —
И вот на боку моём выпуклость видна.

Я врежусь в другой горшок —
И трещина в нём появится вдруг.
И снова к гончарному кругу идём,
Пока вновь Его образ в нас не найдём.

Если мои слова и дела
меняют чужой глины путь,
То мне надо быть осторожной всегда,
Чтоб другие горшки не вогнуть.

Бог хочет, чтоб сосуды были полезны,
Чтоб выдержать огонь они были способны.
Дело не только во мне и не только в тебе:
Бог трудится и над другими сосудами тоже.

One Sunday morning a little girl, whom we will call Jennika, woke up to the sun shining into her bedroom. She dressed in her Sunday dress just like she did every other Sunday morning. This Sunday morning was quite different, though. While she was sitting at the breakfast table waiting for her mom to fill her plate, her mom’s chest suddenly started hurting very badly. It hurt so badly, she had to go lie on the couch. Jennika felt scared. She didn’t know what was going to happen. About ten minutes later, her dad took her mom to the hospital. Later that afternoon, she and her siblings heard that their mom had suffered a heart attack.

The next Wednesday evening, her dad asked, “Jennika, would you like to go along to the hospital tomorrow to see Mom?”

“Yes!” she beamed.

The next morning after breakfast, her older sister and baby brother went with her and her dad to the hospital. That day she had lots of fun. She enjoyed looking out the window of the waiting room and watching the helicopters take off and land. One time she even saw an ambulance come with its lights and sirens on. That was exciting! One time she almost got lost in the halls, but one of her mom’s nurses saw her and showed her the right room.

That night she was going to spend the night with her mom. She was so excited! She thought sleeping on the chair in her mom’s room would be fun. Her mom was going to ask the nurses for a pillow and some blankets. About fifteen minutes after her dad left, a nurse came in and said she couldn’t spend the night there after all! Her dad needed to come back to pick her up. She was so disappointed! She cried almost the whole way home. That night they dropped off her two-week-old brother at one of the church families to give her older sisters a break from taking care of him.

The next day she had a wonderful surprise. First, her cousins, who lived about three hours away, came to visit. And she found out that her mom was going to come home that day! She helped her siblings decorate the house. Her older sister made two welcome-home signs for inside the house and her older brother made one for out by the driveway.

“Mom is home!” yelled her younger brother when he saw the car pull up outside the house. Jennika and her siblings dashed to the front door. They led their mom to her favorite recliner which was close to the air conditioner that their uncle had just installed that morning.

That evening Jennika snuggled up to her mom. “I’m glad you’re home,” she whispered. “I like it when you’re home.” Because her mom had been gone so long, Jennika learned to be more thankful for her mom.

Jennika is older now and is still very thankful for her mom. Maybe your mom didn’t need to be in the hospital for a week, but you should still be thankful for her. Don’t forget to tell her!

어느 일요일 아침, 여기서는 제니카라고 부를 한 어린 소녀가 햇살이 침실 안으로 비치는 가운데 잠에서 깨어났습니다. 여느 일요일 아침처럼 주일 옷을 입었습니다. 하지만 그 일요일 아침은 평소와는 아주 달랐습니다. 아침 식탁에 앉아 엄마가 접시에 음식을 담아 주기를 기다리던 중, 엄마의 가슴이 갑자기 몹시 아프기 시작했습니다. 통증이 너무 심해 엄마는 소파에 누워야 했습니다. 제니카는 겁이 났습니다. 무슨 일이 일어날지 알 수 없었습니다. 약 10분 뒤, 아빠가 엄마를 병원으로 데려갔습니다. 그날 오후 늦게, 제니카와 형제자매들은 엄마가 심장마비를 겪었다는 소식을 들었습니다.

그다음 수요일 저녁, 아빠가 물었습니다. “제니카, 내일 병원에 엄마를 보러 같이 가고 싶니?”

“네!” 제니카는 활짝 웃으며 대답했습니다.

다음 날 아침 식사를 마친 뒤, 언니와 아기 남동생이 제니카와 아빠와 함께 병원에 갔습니다. 그날 제니카는 아주 즐거운 시간을 보냈습니다. 대기실 창밖을 내다보며 헬리콥터가 이륙하고 착륙하는 모습을 보는 것이 좋았습니다. 한 번은 불을 켜고 사이렌을 울리며 오는 구급차도 보았습니다. 정말 신났습니다! 한 번은 복도에서 길을 잃을 뻔했지만, 엄마를 돌보던 간호사 한 분이 제니카를 보고 올바른 병실로 데려다주었습니다.

그날 밤 제니카는 엄마와 함께 자려고 했습니다. 무척 신이 났습니다! 엄마 병실의 의자에서 자는 일이 재미있을 거라고 생각했습니다. 엄마는 간호사들에게 베개와 담요를 부탁할 참이었습니다. 아빠가 떠난 지 약 15분 뒤, 간호사가 들어와 제니카는 결국 병원에서 잘 수 없다고 말했습니다! 아빠가 제니카를 데리러 다시 와야 했습니다. 제니카는 무척 실망했습니다! 집에 가는 내내 거의 울었습니다. 그날 밤, 언니들이 아기를 돌보는 부담을 덜 수 있도록 생후 2주 된 남동생을 교회 가정 중 한 곳에 맡겼습니다.

다음 날 제니카에게는 아주 기쁜 일이 생겼습니다. 먼저, 세 시간쯤 떨어진 곳에 사는 사촌들이 놀러 왔습니다. 그리고 엄마가 그날 집에 돌아온다는 것도 알게 되었습니다! 제니카는 형제자매들과 함께 집을 꾸몄습니다. 언니는 집 안에 붙일 환영 표지 두 개를 만들었고, 오빠는 진입로 옆에 세울 표지 하나를 만들었습니다.

차가 집 앞에 도착하는 것을 본 남동생이 “엄마가 집에 오셨어!” 하고 소리쳤습니다. 제니카와 형제자매들은 현관문으로 달려갔습니다. 아이들은 엄마를 가장 좋아하는 안락의자로 모셨습니다. 그 의자는 삼촌이 바로 그날 아침 설치해 준 에어컨 가까이에 있었습니다.

그날 저녁 제니카는 엄마에게 바싹 다가가 안겼습니다. “엄마가 집에 와서 기뻐요.” 제니카가 속삭였습니다. “엄마가 집에 계시면 좋아요.” 엄마가 오랫동안 집을 비웠던 덕분에 제니카는 엄마에게 더욱 감사하는 마음을 갖게 되었습니다.

이제 제니카는 자랐지만 여전히 엄마에게 무척 감사하고 있습니다. 여러분의 엄마는 일주일 동안 병원에 계실 필요가 없었을지도 모릅니다. 그래도 엄마에게 감사하는 마음을 가져야 합니다. 엄마에게 감사하다고 말하는 것을 잊지 마세요!

God the Potter is molding me.
What kind of vessel will I be:
To carry, to store, or for a drink?
A lamp, or a plate, or a kitchen sink?

I’m a little bit shallow, I admit,
For I’m focusing on me quite a bit.
But here is a thought,
I’m not the only pot.

About my life
are many others,
A husband, a daughter,
and some brothers.

The Potter’s hand is on them, too,
Making each of us, something new.
Another pot gives me a bump,
And now I have a little lump.

Into another pot I smack,
It seems they now have a crack.
Back to the Potter’s wheel we go,
Until His likeness, again does show.

If what I do, and what I say,
Changes the course of other’s clay,
Then with great care, I must behave,
Lest other’s pots become concave.

Useful pots are God’s desire,
Ones that can withstand the fire.
It’s not just me, and it’s not just you;
God’s working with other vessels too.

by Elizabeth Rust

This poem was inspired by the Scripture passage in Jeremiah 18:1-6.

God de Pottenbakker vormt mij.
Wat voor vat zal ik zijn:
Om iets te dragen, te bewaren of uit te drinken?
Een lamp, een bord of een gootsteen in de keuken?

Ik ben een beetje oppervlakkig, dat geef ik toe,
want ik ben nogal op mezelf gericht.
Maar hier is een gedachte:
ik ben niet de enige pot.

In mijn leven
zijn er vele anderen:
een man, een dochter
en enkele broers.

Ook op hen rust de hand van de Pottenbakker,
die ieder van ons iets nieuws laat worden.
Een andere pot stoot tegen mij aan,
en nu heb ik een klein deukje.

Ik bots tegen een andere pot,
en nu lijkt die een barst te hebben.
Terug naar de schijf van de Pottenbakker gaan we,
tot zijn gelijkenis weer te zien is.

Als wat ik doe en wat ik zeg
de vorm van andermans klei verandert,
moet ik me dus heel zorgvuldig gedragen,
opdat andermans potten niet naar binnen deuken.

God verlangt naar bruikbare potten,
die het vuur kunnen doorstaan.
Het gaat niet alleen om mij, en niet alleen om jou;
God werkt ook aan andere vaten.

door Elizabeth Rust

Dit gedicht is geïnspireerd op de Schriftpassage in Jeremia 18:1-6.

  1. I love Thy kingdom, Lord,
    The house of Thine abode;
    The church our blest Redeemer saved
    With His own precious blood.
    I love Thy church, O God!
    Her walls before Thee stand,
    Dear as the apple of Thine eye,
    And written on Thy hand.
  2. For her my tears shall fall,
    For her my prayers ascend;
    To her my cares and toils be giv’n,
    Till toils and cares shall end.
    Beyond my highest joy
    I prize her heav’nly ways,
    Her sweet communion, solemn vows,
    Her hymns of love and praise.
  3. Jesus, Thou Friend divine,
    Our Savior and our King!
    Thy hand from ev’ry snare and foe
    Shall great deliverance bring.
    Sure as Thy truth shall last,
    To Zion shall be giv’n
    The brightest glories earth can yield,
    And brighter bliss of heav’n.

Her mom was going to ask the nurses for a pillow and some blankets. About fifteen minutes after her dad left, a nurse came in and said she couldn’t spend the night there after all! Her dad needed to come back to pick her up. She was so disappointed! She cried almost the whole way home. That night they dropped off her two-week-old brother at one of the church families to give her older sisters a break from taking care of him.

The next day she had a wonderful surprise. First, her cousins, who lived about three hours away, came to visit. And she found out that her mom was going to come home that day! She helped her siblings decorate the house. Her older sister made two welcome-home signs for inside the house and her older brother made one for out by the driveway.

“Mom is home!” yelled her younger brother when he saw the car pull up outside the house. Jennika and her siblings dashed to the front door. They led their mom to her favorite recliner which was close to the air conditioner that their uncle had just installed that morning.

That evening Jennika snuggled up to her mom. “I’m glad you’re home,” she whispered. “I like it when you’re home.” Because her mom had been gone so long, Jennika learned to be more thankful for her mom.

Jennika is older now and is still very thankful for her mom. Maybe your mom didn’t need to be in the hospital for a week, but you should still be thankful for her. Don’t forget to tell her!

בוקר יום ראשון אחד התעוררה ילדה קטנה, שנקרא לה ג׳ניקה, כשקרני השמש האירו את חדר השינה שלה. היא לבשה את שמלת יום ראשון שלה, בדיוק כפי שעשתה בכל בוקר יום ראשון אחר. אבל בוקר יום ראשון הזה היה שונה מאוד. בזמן שישבה ליד שולחן ארוחת הבוקר וחיכתה שאמא שלה תמלא את הצלחת שלה, התחיל פתאום לכאוב לאמא שלה מאוד בחזה. הכאב היה חזק כל כך שהיא נאלצה ללכת לשכב על הספה. ג׳ניקה פחדה. היא לא ידעה מה עומד לקרות. כעבור כעשר דקות אבא שלה לקח את אמא שלה לבית החולים. מאוחר יותר באותו אחר הצהריים נודע לה ולאחיה ולאחיותיה שאמא שלהם לקתה בהתקף לב.

ביום רביעי בערב שלאחר מכן שאל אבא שלה: ״ג׳ניקה, תרצי להצטרף אליי מחר לבית החולים כדי לבקר את אמא?״

״כן!״ היא אמרה בהתלהבות.

למחרת בבוקר, אחרי ארוחת הבוקר, הצטרפו אליה אחותה הגדולה ואחיה התינוק ונסעו עם אבא שלה לבית החולים. באותו יום היא נהנתה מאוד. היא אהבה להביט מחלון חדר ההמתנה ולצפות במסוקים ממריאים ונוחתים. פעם אחת היא אפילו ראתה אמבולנס מגיע עם אורות מהבהבים וסירנה פועלת. זה היה מרגש! פעם אחת היא כמעט הלכה לאיבוד במסדרונות, אבל אחת האחיות שטיפלו באמא שלה ראתה אותה והראתה לה את החדר הנכון.

באותו לילה היא הייתה אמורה לישון עם אמא שלה. היא כל כך התרגשה! היא חשבה שיהיה כיף לישון על הכיסא בחדר של אמא שלה. אמא שלה עמדה לבקש מהאחיות כרית וכמה שמיכות. כרבע שעה אחרי שאבא שלה הלך, נכנסה אחות ואמרה שבסופו של דבר היא לא יכולה לישון שם! אבא שלה היה צריך לחזור כדי לקחת אותה. היא התאכזבה כל כך! היא בכתה כמעט כל הדרך הביתה. באותו לילה הם השאירו את אחיה בן השבועיים אצל אחת המשפחות מהקהילה, כדי לתת לאחיותיה הגדולות הפוגה מהטיפול בו.

למחרת ציפתה לה הפתעה נפלאה. קודם כול הגיעו לבקר בני הדודים שלה, שגרו במרחק של כשלוש שעות נסיעה. והיא גילתה שאמא שלה חוזרת הביתה באותו יום! היא עזרה לאחיה ולאחיותיה לקשט את הבית. אחותה הגדולה הכינה שני שלטים לקבלת פנים בתוך הבית, ואחיה הגדול הכין שלט אחד ליד שביל הגישה.

״אמא בבית!״ צעק אחיה הקטן כשראה את המכונית מגיעה אל הבית. ג׳ניקה ואחיה ואחיותיה מיהרו אל דלת הכניסה. הם הובילו את אמא שלהם לכורסת הטלוויזיה האהובה עליה, שהייתה קרובה למזגן שדודם התקין באותו בוקר.

באותו ערב ג׳ניקה התכרבלה לצד אמא שלה. ״אני שמחה שחזרת הביתה,״ לחשה. ״אני אוהבת כשאת בבית.״ מכיוון שאמא שלה נעדרה זמן רב כל כך, ג׳ניקה למדה להעריך אותה ולהודות עליה יותר.

ג׳ניקה כבר גדולה יותר, והיא עדיין אסירת תודה מאוד על אמא שלה. אולי אמא שלך לא הייתה צריכה להיות שבוע בבית החולים, אבל בכל זאת כדאי שתהיה אסיר תודה עליה. אל תשכח לומר לה!

Editor’s Note:

Over the last number of years there seems to be a shift occurring on a variety of specific issues for some conservative Anabaptists. This changing of ideas and practice is not happening in a vacuum, rather we are simply following the leader. Once we start researching this matter further, we soon realize that this same migration on issues of faith and practice has been at work for some years now within the greater Evangelical community. Let’s stop and consider whether we are following God’s Word, or man’s influence.

Some Anabaptists are becoming dissatisfied with a traditional structure of church, so they gravitate towards “cell-group church” or “house-church” models. Others react to overbearing and authoritative church leadership from their past and start emphasizing a more democratic function of church. Then there are the folks who are moving away from a “local” church body emphasis to that of focusing more on a “universal” or a “global” church body. Still others don’t have a problem with what is considered “normal” church, instead they are the type that gets tired of the “old-fashioned” and the “boring.” These folks welcome “new ideas” that are presented in present-day books and at various conferences which are held around the country. These conferences are not all intrinsically wrong, nor are they all selling “new” interpretations, yet there are some that bring in “fresh” ideas originating from “outside” sources in the hope that they will bring “new life” to the lack of zeal within the “normal.”

Another area of shift is that of focusing on the Gospels while ignoring specific teachings in the Epistles. Some folks stress that we should “just follow Jesus” while not allowing the teachings of the Apostles to further detail the application of Jesus’ teachings. Others lift up the “Sermon on the Mount,” the “red letter Scriptures,” or walking in the “footsteps of Jesus,” without realizing that a default outcome of this focus tends to leave out specific teachings of the Epistles regarding practical church functioning and Christian living. Some of these include …exhort[ing] one another daily… –Hebrews 3:13, All scripture … is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, [and] for correction… –2 Timothy 3:16, and the fact that we should be careful because Satan and his agents will transform themselves …into the apostles of Christ and present themselves as …an angel of light –2 Corinthians 11:13-14.

Some individuals believe it is wrong for spiritual authorities to “take the oversight thereof,” or to give clear admonition over the pulpit. They shrink back from churches that have ordained leaders, or they don’t like the thought of spiritual authorities in their lives. Others feel their church doesn’t have much to offer so they attend various group events with others of “like precious faith” (who believe as they do), thus developing a disjointed spiritual body of individuals from many various local churches, fellowshipping together at large events. Many times, these believers allow someone outside of their local church fellowship to become their spiritual advisor, thus feeling justified in not giving their loyalty to their church leaders at home. They come to believe that the traditional way of having church the Anabaptist way is “not the way it used to be” or “not according to the early church”. They believe that structured church brings deadness to local bodies, never mind that the Epistles provide clear details on church structure and practice.

Many of these individuals are interacting and fellowshipping so closely with others from various other groups and churches instead of their own home church, that they do not realize they are actually functioning in a very individualistic manner. This manner of being an alone “local” Christian is categorically opposite from the “group spirituality” that our Anabaptist forefathers specifically believed and taught. Another area of misunderstanding in this whole issue, is that there is a very clear difference between the expression of the kingdom now and the kingdom future. Remember that Jesus said, “my kingdom is not of this world,” yet an extreme focus on kingdom this and kingdom that, will by default cause Christians to ignore this Truth, as they try to express the kingdom “on the earth,” and “in the now.”

The full effect of the resurrection and the ascension of Jesus in the life of a believer can never fully be understood without allowing the Epistles to bring more clear application to the Gospels or to the Sermon on the Mount. Simply following the words of Jesus in red ink will never help us know how to be a part of the “power of His resurrection”, or “the fellowship of His sufferings.” For this we need the balance of the rest of the New Testament.

Many of these points will require their own complete article to sort out all the nuances, which we plan to do as the Lord continues to allow time to continue. Considering all this, we felt that this article is a balanced, yet basic introduction to the many issues at stake and we have chosen it based on those thoughts.

Curvin L Wenger

When Jesus blessed Simon Peter for his confident confession that Jesus was the Christ, the Son of the living God –Matthew 16:16, He brought together two overarching New Testament themes: the church and the kingdom—…I will build my church … And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven… –Matthew 16:18-19. Ever since, Christ’s followers have deliberated, with varying opinions, on the meaning and the nature of the kingdom, and its relation to the church.

Jesus began His preaching by declaring that the kingdom of heaven was at hand (see Matthew 4:17). Throughout the Gospels, the kingdom was the unifying theme of His teaching. In fact, Scripture only records two occasions when Christ mentioned the church. The church, on the other hand, is more prominent in the Acts, the Epistles, and the Revelation. Why this difference? Is there some conflict or incompatible tension between what Jesus taught and emphasized, and that of the apostles?

Recent years seem to have brought an increased interest and reference to the kingdom within Evangelical circles as well as conservative Anabaptist circles. Many are using terms such as working for the kingdom, building up the kingdom, growing the kingdom, kingdom service, kingdom finances, and even funding the kingdom. Kingdom Theology has been offered as a course of study, and the expression Kingdom Christian has been coined to demarcate a particular kind of Christian—one who believes and practices Jesus’ teachings. Among many conservative Anabaptist people, kingdom terminology has practically drowned out the language expressed by Eliza Hewitt who wrote, “For Christ and the Church let our voices ring.”

Among the various factors which have nurtured this renewed kingdom emphasis among some Anabaptists, two stand out. Both of these concerns reflect the influence of Christians from without the conservative Anabaptist tradition, yet who profess to be Bible-believing and born-again.

  1. The first is that some people seem to be more concerned about being Biblical than about being Christ-like. We, conservative Anabaptists, can stand on the Bible to formulate all the right doctrines and positions while our lives fall short in reflecting the character and values of Jesus Christ our Lord, the One with whom we claim to be united in a living relationship.
  2. The second matter involves a fixation on the act of getting saved to the neglect of living a saved life; that is, a life of obedient discipleship, particularly to the very teachings of Jesus who we are to follow. While most conservative Anabaptists profess to practice Christ’s teachings, we are not immune to a careless discipleship.

There are individuals within conservative Anabaptism that address these concerns somewhat in the following manner. They say that while Evangelicals believe in the person and work of Christ, they tend to focus on Paul. For all practical purposes, they (Evangelicals) are more concerned about correct Bible interpretations, theological systems, and assenting to correct beliefs than they are with obedient Christian living, particularly regarding the hard teachings of Christ. In contrast, these Anabaptists claim that the kingdom of God, which Jesus inaugurated and was the theme of His teaching, should set the norm for understanding and living the Christian life. Consequently, for them, the Gospels (and the kingdom) then become primary in interpreting the rest of the New Testament.

What do we make of this? While sweeping generalizations don’t do justice to the exceptions and the qualifiers, the concerns are valid, and this critique regarding our Evangelical friends does hold some measure of truth. These things have their roots in the thinking of Augustine (354-430), in the imbalanced Reformation emphasis regarding justification by faith, and in the work of John Calvin. But what about the antidote of focusing mostly on Christ and the kingdom? Certainly, Christ is central to interpreting, not only the New Testament, but actually the entire Bible. And there is value in holding forth those teachings of Christ, which are so often brushed aside, yet are required of any church that would be worthy of His name. However, I would like to offer three points of caution or critique about taking this antidote unreservedly.

Do the Gospels dominate the rest of Scripture?

First, I believe it’s a mistake to assume that the Gospels (the life and teachings of Jesus) should dominate and control the interpretation of the New Testament scriptures. Rather, the New Testament, as it moves through the Gospels, the Acts, the Epistles, and lastly the Revelation, contains a divinely inspired progression of fuller revelation and doctrinal explanation. This is seen when we consider the words of Jesus regarding the coming of the Holy Spirit: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now. Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come –John 16:12-13. Those New Testament books following the Gospels are the anticipated fulfillment of these words. They bring the teachings and work of Christ to full development and understanding.

Christ’s ministry and teaching about the kingdom laid the groundwork, then His death and resurrection placed the foundation on which He would build His church. The Scriptures which follow the Gospels give us greater comprehension about the meaning of Christ’s death on the cross and its relation and effect on us that comes through faith and obedience. It also develops the whole doctrine of the church. So, the entire New Testament fits together in beautiful harmony. Both the Gospels and the Epistles need to be interpreted in reference to each other. The teachings of Christ do not take precedence over the Epistles, rather the Epistles help interpret the Gospels—they give us a more complete understanding and practical application to the principles Christ gave His Disciples.

Does Theology Militate Against Discipleship?

Secondly, we should be careful to not set correct interpretation and correct practice against one another. To say it another way, we should not pit theology against discipleship. To whatever degree some Evangelicals may overemphasize theology at the expense of discipleship, it should not prejudice us into making a whipping boy out of theology. Theology is the study of God and the things of God. We are forming a personal theology when we study God’s Word and compare Scripture with Scripture in our efforts to come to a unified and harmonious understanding of its various parts.

Every Christian has a theology, whether he can express it well or not. Our theology (or doctrinal understanding, if you want to say it that way) is our belief system and the soil out of which our behavior grows. Some theologies are very elementary, others reflect a lifetime of study, most are incomplete, some are inconsistent, others are dogmatic or laced with philosophy, and some are dreadfully wrong. Hopefully, all of us have a growing, and increasingly accurate understanding of God and His Word. This is quite necessary since our theology, which is the sum of our beliefs about God and our understanding of His Word and the Christian life, is what affects our discipleship—our daily walk with God. A good theology undergirds discipleship. A poor theology undermines discipleship.

Are “Kingdom” and “Church” Interchangeable?

Finally, we should think correctly about the kingdom in relation to the church. What is the relationship of the kingdom to the church? The kingdom is not, as contemporary usage would almost have us think, a generic version of, or a substitute word for, the church. Rather, the kingdom has to do with the reign or rule of God. It is both a present reality, having been inaugurated in the person and mission of Jesus, and a future expectation which God will bring to completion at the end of time. The church, while not the kingdom, is composed of those who are in the kingdom; those who, through the work of Christ, have submitted to the rule of God.

While we struggle for the precise word to express the relationship of the kingdom to the church, as a holy, loving, and obedient community of believers, the church is the earthly manifestation of God’s rule—His kingdom. Christ did not say “I will build my kingdom”; rather He said, “I will build my church.” Likewise, Paul did not build kingdom halls; He started churches. It is possible for us to have an idealistic and romantic view of the kingdom that gets separated from the hard work of living on earth with our fellow believers in a local church body. We can elevate the kingdom and diminish the church. We can get enthusiastic about the concept of the kingdom, the teachings of the kingdom, the growth of the kingdom, and conferences about the kingdom, and yet be cynical, critical, and sorry members of our local church.

Do you want to work for the kingdom (see Colossians 4:11)? Then commit yourself wholeheartedly to Christ and His church. That starts with your local church. Love and serve your church. Accept responsibility in it. Be accountable and loyal to your local church. Work for the good and growth of the church—your local church, and beyond.

I love Thy Kingdom, Lord,

Redaktørens merknad:

I løpet av de siste årene ser det ut til å ha skjedd en endring i en rekke konkrete spørsmål blant noen konservative anabaptister. Denne endringen i ideer og praksis skjer ikke i et vakuum; vi følger ganske enkelt lederen. Når vi begynner å undersøke saken nærmere, innser vi snart at den samme dreiningen i spørsmål om tro og praksis har pågått i flere år i det bredere evangelikale miljøet. La oss stanse opp og overveie om vi følger Guds Ord eller menneskers påvirkning.

Noen anabaptister blir misfornøyde med en tradisjonell kirkestruktur og trekkes derfor mot modeller med «cellegrupper» eller «husmenigheter». Andre reagerer på overstyrende og autoritær kirkeledelse fra fortiden og begynner å legge større vekt på en mer demokratisk funksjon i kirken. Så er det dem som beveger seg bort fra vektleggingen av en «lokal» kirke og i stedet retter oppmerksomheten mer mot en «universell» eller «global» kirke. Andre igjen har ikke noe problem med det som regnes som «normal» kirke, men er snarere av den typen som blir lei av det «gammeldagse» og «kjedelige». Disse menneskene tar imot «nye ideer» som presenteres i bøker fra vår tid og på ulike konferanser rundt om i landet. Disse konferansene er ikke alle i seg selv gale, og de selger heller ikke alle «nye» tolkninger, men noen bringer inn «friske» ideer fra «utenforstående» kilder i håp om at de skal gi «nytt liv» til mangelen på iver i det «normale».

Et annet område der det skjer en dreining, er at man fokuserer på evangeliene samtidig som man overser konkrete læresetninger i brevene. Noen hevder at vi «bare skal følge Jesus», men lar ikke apostlenes lære utdype hvordan Jesu lære skal anvendes. Andre løfter fram «Bergprekenen», «skriftstedene med røde bokstaver» eller det å vandre i «Jesu fotspor», uten å innse at en følge av dette fokuset gjerne blir at konkrete læresetninger i brevene om praktisk menighetsliv og kristenliv utelates. Noen av disse er …oppmuntre hverandre daglig… – Hebreerne 3:13, Hele Skriften … er nyttig til undervisning, til overbevisning, [og] til rettledning… – 2. Timoteus 3:16, og det faktum at vi bør være på vakt, for Satan og hans tjenere skal skape seg om …til Kristi apostler og framstille seg som …en lysets engel – 2. Korinter 11:13-14.

Noen mener det er galt at åndelige ledere «har tilsyn med den», eller gir tydelig formaning fra prekestolen. De trekker seg unna menigheter med ordinerte ledere, eller liker ikke tanken på å ha åndelige ledere i livet sitt. Andre føler at menigheten deres ikke har så mye å tilby, og deltar derfor på ulike arrangementer sammen med andre som har «like dyrebar tro» (som tror slik de selv gjør). Slik utvikler det seg et usammenhengende åndelig fellesskap av personer fra mange forskjellige lokale menigheter, som samles til store arrangementer. Ofte lar disse troende noen utenfor fellesskapet i sin lokale menighet bli deres åndelige rådgiver, og føler dermed at de har grunn til ikke å vise troskap mot menighetslederne hjemme. De begynner å tro at den tradisjonelle anabaptistiske måten å være menighet på «ikke er slik den pleide å være» eller «ikke er slik den tidlige kirken var». De mener at en strukturert menighet fører til åndelig død i lokale menigheter, uten å ta hensyn til at brevene gir tydelige detaljer om menighetsstruktur og praksis.

Mange av disse menneskene omgås og har nært fellesskap med andre fra ulike grupper og menigheter i stedet for sin egen hjemmemenighet, uten å innse at de faktisk lever svært individualistisk. Denne måten å være en enslig «lokal» kristen på står i skarp motsetning til den «gruppebaserte åndeligheten» som våre anabaptistiske forfedre uttrykkelig trodde på og lærte. En annen misforståelse i hele denne saken er at det er en svært tydelig forskjell mellom å gi uttrykk for riket nå og riket i framtiden. Husk at Jesus sa: «Mitt rike er ikke av denne verden», men et ensidig fokus på riket ditt og riket datt vil uunngåelig føre til at kristne overser denne sannheten mens de prøver å uttrykke riket «på jorden» og «her og nå».

Hele betydningen av Jesu oppstandelse og himmelfart i den troendes liv kan aldri fullt ut forstås uten at vi lar brevene tydeliggjøre hvordan evangeliene eller Bergprekenen skal anvendes. Det å bare følge Jesu ord med rød skrift vil aldri hjelpe oss å forstå hvordan vi kan få del i «kraften fra hans oppstandelse» eller «fellesskapet med hans lidelser». Til dette trenger vi balansen som resten av Det nye testamentet gir.

Mange av disse punktene krever en egen, fullstendig artikkel for å få fram alle nyansene. Det planlegger vi å gjøre etter hvert som Herren fortsatt gir oss tid. Når vi tar alt dette i betraktning, mener vi at denne artikkelen er en balansert, men grunnleggende innføring i de mange spørsmålene som står på spill, og vi har valgt den ut fra disse betraktningene.

Curvin L Wenger

Da Jesus velsignet Simon Peter for hans frimodige bekjennelse av at Jesus var Kristus, den levende Guds Sønn – Matteus 16:16, knyttet han sammen to overordnede temaer i Det nye testamentet: kirken og riket—…Jeg vil bygge min kirke … Og jeg vil gi deg nøklene til himmelriket… – Matteus 16:18-19. Siden den gang har Kristi etterfølgere drøftet rikets betydning og natur, og dets forhold til kirken, og hatt ulike oppfatninger om dette.

Jesus begynte sin forkynnelse med å erklære at himmelriket var nær (se Matteus 4:17). Gjennom evangeliene var riket det samlende temaet i hans undervisning. Faktisk omtaler Skriften kirken bare ved to anledninger når den gjengir Kristi ord. Kirken er derimot mer framtredende i Apostlenes gjerninger, brevene og Åpenbaringen. Hvorfor denne forskjellen? Er det en konflikt eller en uforenlig spenning mellom det Jesus lærte og la vekt på, og apostlenes lære og vektlegging?

De siste årene ser det ut til å ha blitt større interesse for og flere henvisninger til riket i evangelikale kretser så vel som i konservative anabaptistiske kretser. Mange bruker uttrykk som å arbeide for riket, bygge opp riket, la riket vokse, tjeneste for riket, rikets finanser og til og med finansiering av riket. Riksteologi har blitt tilbudt som et studiekurs, og uttrykket rikeskristen er blitt laget for å betegne en bestemt type kristen – en som tror på og praktiserer Jesu lære. Blant mange konservative anabaptister har språket om riket i praksis overdøvet ordene Eliza Hewitt skrev: «For Kristus og kirken skal våre stemmer lyde.»

Blant de ulike faktorene som har næret denne fornyede vektleggingen av riket hos noen anabaptister, skiller to seg ut. Begge disse bekymringene gjenspeiler påvirkningen fra kristne utenfor den konservative anabaptistiske tradisjonen, som likevel bekjenner seg til å tro på Bibelen og være født på ny.

  1. For det første virker det som om noen er mer opptatt av å være bibelsk enn av å være lik Kristus. Vi konservative anabaptister kan støtte oss på Bibelen for å utforme alle de rette læresetningene og standpunktene, mens livene våre ikke gjenspeiler karakteren og verdiene til Jesus Kristus, vår Herre, han som vi hevder å være forent med i et levende forhold.
  2. Det andre spørsmålet gjelder en ensidig opptatthet av å bli frelst, på bekostning av å leve et frelst liv – det vil si et liv i lydig disippelskap, særlig i lydighet mot Jesu egne læresetninger, han som vi skal følge. Selv om de fleste konservative anabaptister bekjenner at de praktiserer Kristi lære, er vi ikke immune mot et skjødesløst disippelskap.

Det finnes personer innen konservativ anabaptisme som tar opp disse bekymringene omtrent på følgende måte. De sier at selv om evangelikale tror på Kristi person og verk, har de en tendens til å fokusere på Paulus. I praksis er de (evangelikale) mer opptatt av riktige bibeltolkninger, teologiske systemer og å slutte seg til rette trosoppfatninger enn av å leve som lydige kristne, særlig når det gjelder Kristi vanskelige læresetninger. Til forskjell fra dem hevder disse anabaptistene at Guds rike, som Jesus innledet, og som var temaet for hans undervisning, bør være normen for hvordan man forstår og lever det kristne livet. Derfor blir evangeliene (og riket) for dem det primære utgangspunktet for å tolke resten av Det nye testamentet.

Hva skal vi mene om dette? Selv om brede generaliseringer ikke yter unntakene og forbeholdene rettferdighet, er bekymringene berettigede, og denne kritikken av våre evangelikale venner inneholder en viss sannhet. Disse forholdene har røtter i Augustins tenkning (354-430), i reformasjonens ubalanserte vektlegging av rettferdiggjørelse ved tro og i John Calvins verk. Men hva med motgiften det er å fokusere mest på Kristus og riket? Kristus står utvilsomt sentralt når ikke bare Det nye testamentet, men faktisk hele Bibelen, skal tolkes. Og det har verdi å løfte fram Kristi læresetninger, som så ofte blir skjøvet til side, men som enhver menighet må følge for å være verdig hans navn. Jeg vil likevel komme med tre advarsler eller innvendinger mot å ta imot denne motgiften uten forbehold.

Dominerer evangeliene resten av Skriften?

For det første mener jeg det er en feil å anta at evangeliene (Jesu liv og lære) skal dominere og styre tolkningen av skriftene i Det nye testamentet. Snarere inneholder Det nye testamentet, gjennom evangeliene, Apostlenes gjerninger, brevene og til slutt Åpenbaringen, en guddommelig inspirert utvikling mot en fyldigere åpenbaring og læremessig forklaring. Dette ser vi når vi tenker på Jesu ord om Den hellige ånds komme: Ennå har jeg mye å si dere, men dere kan ikke bære det nå. Men når han kommer, sannhetens Ånd, skal han veilede dere til hele sannheten. For han skal ikke tale ut fra seg selv, men tale det han hører, og gjøre kjent for dere det som skal komme – Johannes 16:12-13. Bøkene i Det nye testamentet som følger etter evangeliene, er den forutsagte oppfyllelsen av disse ordene. De fører Kristi lære og verk fram til full utfoldelse og forståelse.

Kristi tjeneste og undervisning om riket la grunnlaget, og deretter la hans død og oppstandelse fundamentet som han skulle bygge sin kirke på. Skriftene som følger etter evangeliene, gir oss større innsikt i betydningen av Kristi død på korset og dens sammenheng med og virkning på oss, som kommer gjennom tro og lydighet. De utvikler også hele læren om kirken. Slik passer hele Det nye testamentet sammen i vakker harmoni. Evangeliene og brevene må begge tolkes i lys av hverandre. Kristi lære går ikke foran brevene; snarere hjelper brevene oss med å tolke evangeliene – de gir oss en mer fullstendig forståelse av prinsippene Kristus ga disiplene sine, og viser hvordan de skal anvendes i praksis.

Motarbeider teologi disippelskap?

For det andre bør vi være varsomme med å sette riktig tolkning opp mot riktig praksis. Sagt på en annen måte bør vi ikke sette teologi opp mot disippelskap. Selv om noen evangelikale kanskje legger for stor vekt på teologi på bekostning av disippelskap, bør ikke det gjøre oss forutinntatte og få oss til å gjøre teologien til syndebukk. Teologi er studiet av Gud og det som hører Gud til. Vi utformer en personlig teologi når vi studerer Guds Ord og sammenligner Skrift med Skrift i forsøket på å komme fram til en enhetlig og harmonisk forståelse av de ulike delene.

Enhver kristen har en teologi, enten han kan uttrykke den godt eller ikke. Teologien vår (eller vår læremessige forståelse, om du heller vil si det slik) er trossystemet vårt og jordsmonnet som atferden vår vokser fram av. Noen teologier er svært elementære, andre gjenspeiler et helt liv med studier, de fleste er ufullstendige, noen er inkonsekvente, andre er dogmatiske eller gjennomsyret av filosofi, og noen er fryktelig gale. Forhåpentligvis vokser vi alle i forståelsen av Gud og hans Ord, og forståelsen blir stadig mer nøyaktig. Dette er helt nødvendig, for teologien vår – summen av det vi tror om Gud og av vår forståelse av hans Ord og det kristne livet – påvirker disippelskapet vårt, vår daglige vandring med Gud. God teologi styrker disippelskapet. Dårlig teologi svekker disippelskapet.

Er «rike» og «kirke» utskiftbare begreper?

Til slutt bør vi ha en riktig forståelse av rikets forhold til kirken. Hva er forholdet mellom riket og kirken? Riket er ikke, slik dagens språkbruk nærmest får oss til å tro, en generell utgave av kirken eller et erstatningsord for kirken. Riket handler snarere om Guds herredømme eller styre. Det er både en nåværende virkelighet, innledet gjennom Jesu person og oppdrag, og en framtidig forventning som Gud vil føre til fullendelse ved tidens ende. Kirken er ikke riket, men den består av dem som er i riket – dem som gjennom Kristi verk har underordnet seg Guds styre.

Selv om vi strever med å finne det nøyaktige ordet for å uttrykke forholdet mellom riket og kirken som et hellig, kjærlig og lydig fellesskap av troende, er kirken den jordiske manifestasjonen av Guds styre – hans rike. Kristus sa ikke: «Jeg vil bygge mitt rike»; han sa: «Jeg vil bygge min kirke.» På samme måte bygde ikke Paulus rikshaller; han grunnla menigheter. Det er mulig å få et idealistisk og romantisk syn på riket som løsriver det fra det harde arbeidet med å leve på jorden sammen med våre medtroende i en lokal menighet. Vi kan opphøye riket og nedvurdere kirken. Vi kan bli begeistret for tanken på riket, rikets lære, rikets vekst og konferanser om riket, og likevel være kyniske, kritiske og dårlige medlemmer av vår lokale menighet.

Vil du arbeide for riket (se Kolosserne 4:11)? Da må du helhjertet forplikte deg til Kristus og hans kirke. Det begynner i din lokale menighet. Elsk og tjen menigheten din. Ta ansvar i den. Vær ansvarlig overfor og trofast mot din lokale menighet. Arbeid for menighetens beste og vekst – din lokale menighet og menigheten videre utover.

Timothy Dwight skrev:*

Jeg elsker ditt rike, Herre,
huset der du bor,
kirken som vår salige Frelser
frelste med sitt dyrebare blod.
Jeg elsker din kirke, o Gud:
Dens murer står for deg,
dyrbar som din øyesten,
inngravert i din hånd.

Det han mente om det nøyaktige forholdet mellom riket og kirken, kan være annerledes enn det jeg mener. Men det jeg gjerne vil at vi skal legge merke til, er at når han tenkte på riket, tenkte han på kirken. Slik bør vi også gjøre! Er ordene hans dine, slik han fortsetter å skrive?

For henne skal mine tårer falle,
for henne stige mine bønner;
til henne skal jeg gi min omsorg og møye,
til møye og omsorg tar slutt.
Høyere enn min største glede
verdsetter jeg hennes himmelske veier,
hennes søte fellesskap, høytidelige løfter,
hennes lovsanger om kjærlighet og pris.

* Se side 32 for hele sangen.

One Sunday morning a little girl, whom we will call Jennika, woke up to the sun shining into her bedroom. She dressed in her Sunday dress just like she did every other Sunday morning. This Sunday morning was quite different, though. While she was sitting at the breakfast table waiting for her mom to fill her plate, her mom’s chest suddenly started hurting very badly. It hurt so badly, she had to go lie on the couch. Jennika felt scared. She didn’t know what was going to happen. About ten minutes later, her dad took her mom to the hospital. Later that afternoon, she and her siblings heard that their mom had suffered a heart attack.

The next Wednesday evening, her dad asked, “Jennika, would you like to go along to the hospital tomorrow to see Mom?”

“Yes!” she beamed.

The next morning after breakfast, her older sister and baby brother went with her and her dad to the hospital. That day she had lots of fun. She enjoyed looking out the window of the waiting room and watching the helicopters take off and land. One time she even saw an ambulance come with its lights and sirens on. That was exciting! One time she almost got lost in the halls, but one of her mom’s nurses saw her and showed her the right room.

That night she was going to spend the night with her mom. She was so excited! She thought sleeping on the chair in her mom’s room would be fun. Her mom was going to ask the nurses for a pillow and some blankets. About fifteen minutes after her dad left, a nurse came in and said she couldn’t spend the night there after all! Her dad needed to come back to pick her up. She was so disappointed! She cried almost the whole way home. That night they dropped off her two-week-old brother at one of the church families to give her older sisters a break from taking care of him.

The next day she had a wonderful surprise. First, her cousins, who lived about three hours away, came to visit. And she found out that her mom was going to come home that day! She helped her siblings decorate the house. Her older sister made two welcome-home signs for inside the house and her older brother made one for out by the driveway.

“Mom is home!” yelled her younger brother when he saw the car pull up outside the house. Jennika and her siblings dashed to the front door. They led their mom to her favorite recliner which was close to the air conditioner that their uncle had just installed that morning.

That evening Jennika snuggled up to her mom. “I’m glad you’re home,” she whispered. “I like it when you’re home.” Because her mom had been gone so long, Jennika learned to be more thankful for her mom.

Jennika is older now and is still very thankful for her mom. Maybe your mom didn’t need to be in the hospital for a week, but you should still be thankful for her. Don’t forget to tell her!

Однажды в воскресное утро маленькая девочка, которую мы назовём Дженникой, проснулась от солнечных лучей, проникавших в её комнату. Она оделась в своё воскресное платье, как и каждое другое воскресное утро. Но это воскресное утро было совсем необычным. Пока она сидела за столом и ждала, когда мама положит ей еду, у мамы вдруг сильно заболела грудь. Боль была такой сильной, что ей пришлось лечь на диван. Дженнике стало страшно. Она не знала, что произойдёт. Примерно через десять минут папа отвёз маму в больницу. Позже в тот день Дженника и её братья и сёстры узнали, что у мамы случился сердечный приступ.

В следующую среду вечером папа спросил: «Дженника, хочешь завтра поехать со мной в больницу навестить маму?»

«Да!» — обрадовалась она.

На следующее утро после завтрака её старшая сестра и младший братишка поехали вместе с ней и папой в больницу. В тот день она отлично провела время. Ей нравилось смотреть из окна комнаты ожидания, как вертолёты взлетают и приземляются. Однажды она даже увидела, как приехала машина скорой помощи с включёнными мигалками и сиреной. Как здорово! Однажды она чуть не заблудилась в коридорах, но одна из маминых медсестёр увидела её и показала, куда идти.

В ту ночь она собиралась остаться у мамы. Она была так рада! Ей казалось, что будет весело спать на стуле в маминой палате. Мама собиралась попросить медсестёр принести подушку и одеяла. Примерно через пятнадцать минут после того, как папа ушёл, вошла медсестра и сказала, что Дженнике всё-таки нельзя оставаться на ночь! Папе пришлось вернуться за ней. Она так расстроилась! Почти всю дорогу домой она плакала. В ту ночь они отвезли её двухнедельного братишку к одной из семей из церкви, чтобы старшие сёстры могли отдохнуть от заботы о нём.

На следующий день её ждал чудесный сюрприз. Сначала приехали в гости её двоюродные братья и сёстры, которые жили примерно в трёх часах езды. А ещё она узнала, что мама сегодня вернётся домой! Она помогла братьям и сёстрам украсить дом. Старшая сестра сделала две таблички с приветствием для дома, а старший брат — одну, чтобы поставить у подъездной дорожки.

«Мама приехала!» — закричал младший брат, увидев, как машина подъехала к дому. Дженника и её братья и сёстры бросились к входной двери. Они проводили маму к её любимому креслу-качалке, которое стояло рядом с кондиционером, установленным дядей как раз тем утром.

В тот вечер Дженника прижалась к маме. «Я рада, что ты дома, — прошептала она. — Мне нравится, когда ты дома». Пока мамы долго не было, Дженника научилась больше её ценить.

Теперь Дженника уже подросла и по-прежнему очень благодарна маме. Возможно, твоей маме и не пришлось неделю лежать в больнице, но всё равно будь ей благодарен. Не забудь сказать ей об этом!

God the Potter is molding me.
What kind of vessel will I be:
To carry, to store, or for a drink?
A lamp, or a plate, or a kitchen sink?

I’m a little bit shallow, I admit,
For I’m focusing on me quite a bit.
But here is a thought,
I’m not the only pot.

About my life
are many others,
A husband, a daughter,
and some brothers.

The Potter’s hand is on them, too,
Making each of us, something new.
Another pot gives me a bump,
And now I have a little lump.

Into another pot I smack,
It seems they now have a crack.
Back to the Potter’s wheel we go,
Until His likeness, again does show.

If what I do, and what I say,
Changes the course of other’s clay,
Then with great care, I must behave,
Lest other’s pots become concave.

Useful pots are God’s desire,
Ones that can withstand the fire.
It’s not just me, and it’s not just you;
God’s working with other vessels too.

by Elizabeth Rust

This poem was inspired by the Scripture passage in Jeremiah 18:1-6.

خدا کمھار مجھے ڈھال رہا ہے۔
میں کیسا برتن بنوں گا:
اٹھانے، رکھنے یا پینے کے لیے؟
چراغ، تھالی یا باورچی خانے کا سنک؟

مانتی ہوں، کچھ تنگ نظر ہوں میں،
اپنی ہی فکر میں ہوں میں۔
مگر ایک خیال ہے،
صرف میں ہی برتن نہیں ہوں۔

میری زندگی کے
آس پاس اور بھی ہیں،
شوہر، بیٹی،
اور کچھ بھائی۔

کمھار کا ہاتھ اُن پر بھی ہے،
ہم میں سے ہر ایک کو نیا بنا رہا ہے۔
ایک اور برتن مجھے ٹکر مارتا ہے،
اور اب مجھ میں ذرا سا ابھار آ جاتا ہے۔

میں دوسرے برتن سے ٹکرا جاتی ہوں،
لگتا ہے اُس میں دراڑ پڑ گئی ہے۔
ہم پھر کمھار کے چاک پر لوٹتے ہیں،
یہاں تک کہ اُس کی صورت پھر سے دکھائی دے۔

اگر میرے کام اور میری بات،
دوسروں کی مٹی کا رخ بدلتے ہیں،
تو مجھے بہت احتیاط سے چلنا ہوگا،
کہیں دوسروں کے برتن اندر سے دھنس نہ جائیں۔

خدا کی خواہش ہے کہ برتن کارآمد ہوں،
اور آگ کی تپش سہہ سکیں۔
بات صرف میری نہیں، اور صرف تمہاری بھی نہیں؛
خدا دوسرے برتنوں پر بھی کام کر رہا ہے۔

از الزبتھ رسٹ

یہ نظم یرمیاہ 18:1-6 کے صحیفائی حوالے سے متاثر ہو کر لکھی گئی۔
