Jambo ambalo nimekuwa nikiliona mara kwa mara ninaposoma Neno la Mungu ni kwamba watu wa Mungu wana uhakika. Mfikirie Nuhu. Mungu alipomwambia ajenge safina, hakusita hata kidogo. Kwa miaka 120 iliyofuata alifanya hivyo kwa uhakika. Kisha namfikiria Abrahamu, ambaye kwa uhakika alifanya kila jambo ambalo Mungu alimwomba, hata alipomwomba amtoe dhabihu mwanawe wa pekee. Hatuwezi kuzungumzia uhakika bila kuwataja Kalebu na Yoshua, ambao baada ya kusikia ripoti za mashaka kutoka kwa wenzao wote, walieleza kwa uhakika kile walichopaswa kufanya kuhusu nchi hii mpya ya Kanaani: …Na tupande mara moja, tukaitwae; maana twaweza kushinda hakika –Hesabu 13:30.

Hatuwezi kumsahau Daudi, ambaye alitoka na kumnyamazisha mpingaji mkubwa—Goliathi. Wala hatuwezi kuwasahau Danieli, Gideoni, Ayubu, Ezekieli, Isaya, au Yeremia na yote waliyoyafanya kwa uhakika. Tunapomchunguza kila mmoja wa watu hawa wa imani na wengine wengi, tunaona wazi kwamba walikuwa na uhakika mkubwa sana katika Mungu wao!

Wengine wanaweza kusema kwamba kama Mungu angefanya kazi leo jinsi alivyofanya wakati ule, tungekuwa na uhakika zaidi. Labda kama Mungu angekuwa bado Mungu wa Agano la Kale, mambo yangekuwa rahisi zaidi. Kama angetuongoza vitani, akawaangamiza adui zetu, akayatenganisha bahari, na kusababisha mkate uanguke kutoka mbinguni, basi tungekuwa na uhakika zaidi katika yeye.

Sasa na tuzingatie Agano Jipya. Ni tofauti kabisa. Watu wa Mungu wameamriwa kuacha kila kitu kwa ajili ya Kristo. Wameahidiwa kwamba ulimwengu utawachukia. Wameambiwa kwamba ni vigumu kwa tajiri kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu. Wamehakikishiwa kwamba watabarikiwa wakiteseka, wakiwa maskini, wakiwa na njaa, na wakiomboleza.

Je, watu bado wanaweza kuwa na uhakika katika Mungu anayewaomba watu wake wamfuate katika hali hizi? Ndiyo! Wanafunzi walithibitisha hilo. Walizunguka wakihubiri na kufundisha. Walitafutwa na kupigwa mara kwa mara. Shemasi Stefano alionyesha uhakika mkubwa alipoletwa mbele ya watesi wake, hata walipoanza kumsagia meno na kumpiga kwa mawe. Stefano alionyesha uhakika hadi alipopumua pumzi yake ya mwisho yenye maumivu makali.

Kabla hajawa mtume Paulo, Sauli alikuwa adui wa msalaba, mkuu wa wenye dhambi, na Farisayo kuliko Mafarisayo wote. Alikuwa mtu mashuhuri, aliyefundishwa na walimu bora zaidi. Kisha akakutana na Mungu aliye hai, na kila kitu kikabadilika. Baada ya Paulo kubatizwa, …mara akamhubiri Yesu katika masinagogi, ya kwamba yeye ndiye Mwana wa Mungu –Matendo 9:20. Mstari unaofuata unasema watu walishangaa, kisha katika mstari wa 23, mistari mitano baada ya kubatizwa kwake, inasema kwamba Wayahudi wakafanya shauri la kumwua.

Inahitaji uhakika mkubwa katika Mungu ili kumbadilisha mtu wa namna hiyo, na kumfanya abadili kabisa utii wake mara moja. Kulingana na ushuhuda wake mwenyewe, Paulo alikuwa mwaminifu hadi kifo chake: Kwa maana, mimi sasa namiminwa, na wakati wa kufariki kwangu umefika. Nimevipiga vita vilivyo vizuri, mwendo nimeumaliza, Imani nimeilinda: –2 Timotheo 4:6-7.

Mungu alifanya mambo ya ajabu katika Agano Jipya. Aliwaponya vipofu na kuwafufua wafu. Aliwaachilia wafungwa na kuwapiga watu kwa mauti. Wengine wanaweza kusema ingekuwa rahisi zaidi kuwa na uhakika mkubwa katika Mungu kama bado tungekuwa tunaishi nyakati za Biblia za Agano Jipya, Yesu alipokuwa akitembea na kuzungumza kimwili hapa duniani.

Vipi baada ya Biblia?

Katika kanisa la kwanza, tunaona tena kundi la watu ambao hawakusita; walikuwa na uhakika katika Mungu wao, Mungu ambaye hawakuweza kumwona. Makumi ya maelfu ya watu wa Mungu walisimama kwa ujasiri mbele ya ulimwengu na kutangaza uovu wake, na makumi ya maelfu ya watu wa Mungu waliuawa. Uhakika wa watu hawa haukutiliwa shaka kamwe. Waliitwa wapumbavu kwa kuamini katika “Mungu wasiyemwona”. Walidhihakiwa na kudharauliwa kwa “upumbavu” wao, …tunauawa mchana kutwa… –Zaburi 44:22. Watu walitilia shaka matendo yao, walitilia shaka muundo wao wa kidini, walitilia shaka ujumbe waliouhubiri, walitilia shaka mambo mengi, lakini hawakutilia shaka kamwe uhakika wao. Wakristo hawa walimwamini Mungu wao, na hilo halikuwa na shaka yoyote.

Kwa kushangaza, hawakupendezwa na anasa za maisha haya; hawakujali mambo ya ulimwengu huu, na hata maisha yao wenyewe yalikuwa kitu kidogo cha kuachia kwa ajili ya Mungu wao. Familia zilitenganishwa, nyumba na mashamba vilitaifishwa, makanisa yalichomwa moto, lakini hilo halikuwazuia. Waliishi kwa ajili ya jambo kubwa zaidi, jambo ambalo watu wasiomjua Mungu hawangeweza kulielewa.

Katika kipindi cha kanisa la kwanza na kipindi cha Matengenezo, watu waliongezwa katika Ufalme kwa idadi kubwa. Naam, watoto walikua na kujiunga na kanisa la wazazi wao, lakini pia kulikuwa na umati mkubwa wa waongofu wapya kutoka ulimwenguni. Mtu yeyote angewezaje kumshawishi mtu wa kidunia kujiunga na kundi lililokuwa likitafutwa na kuuawa—kundi lililoteseka kama kanisa la Yesu Kristo lilivyoteseka? Naam, tunajua kwamba wokovu ni wa Bwana, lakini uhakika wa watu wa Mungu ndio uliowafanya wengine wajiulize, na kuwafanya wafikirie kwa makini kuhusu dini hii mpya ya wazushi. Hili lilikuwa kundi la watu ambao wangefurahi kukubali kunyang’anywa mali zao, kufurahi kutoa kila kitu walichokuwa nacho ili kuwasaidia wengine, na kutopinga kukamatwa kwao na wenye mamlaka. Kanisa la kweli la Yesu Kristo lilikuwa kundi la watu ambao sikuzote liliwafanya wengine wajiulize, “Hawa watu ni akina nani?” Waliweka wazi imani yao yote kwa Mungu wao, na jambo hilo halikuwa la kawaida. Walisimama kuitetea kweli ya Mungu haidhuru moto uliwaka kwa ukali kiasi gani, haidhuru maisha yao yalifanywa kuwa ya taabu kiasi gani. Yote hayo yalionyesha uhakika mkubwa, si katika nafsi zao, bali katika Mungu wao.

Tunapolitazama kanisa leo, tunaona nini? Baadhi ya watu wa Mungu wanajitwika misalaba yao, na kuikana dunia na tamaa zake, wengine hawafanyi hivyo. Je, kanisa la leo bado linajulikana kwa kuwa na uhakika katika Mungu wake?

Sisi tunaodai kuwa Wakristo, je, tumepoteza baadhi ya uhakika huu wa kibiblia? Je, bado tunamtumikia Mungu mmoja wa kweli bila kuficha? Je, watu wanatutazama na kusimama kwa mshangao kwa sababu ya uhakika tunaouonyesha katika Mungu wetu? Watu wengi sana leo husema kwamba wao ni Wakristo, lakini huonyesha uhakika mdogo sana katika Mungu. Wanaishi karibu sana na njia za ulimwengu. Badala ya kufurahia mateso, wanafurahia mambo mengi sawa na yale ya ulimwengu. Kila mmoja wetu anahitaji moto wa Mungu uwake ndani kabisa ya mioyo yetu, moto ambao hauwezi kuzimwa.

Uhakika ni sawa na utii. Nimekutana na Wakristo wengi wa siku zetu ambao mababu zao walitoa maisha yao kwa ajili ya Kristo, na babu zao waliongoza kanisa kwa ujasiri, lakini sasa inaonekana kuna kitu kinachokosekana. Ninaposhirikiana na Wakristo wengi wanaomcha Mungu, inaonekana kuna mapambano yanayotawala kuhusu uhakika—uhakika katika Mungu aliye hai, mwenye uwezo wote, ajuaye yote, na aliye kila mahali.

Katika hali ya kutokuwa na uhakika ya ulimwengu wetu wa leo, tunahitaji tena kutangaza kwa ujasiri ujumbe wa injili kama waumini wa kweli walivyofanya zamani. Tunahitaji kuweka wazi mipaka ya kibiblia inayotofautisha mema na mabaya. Tunahitaji kujiondoa katika maeneo haya yote mabaya ya kijivu na kuita dhambi, dhambi. Inaonekana tumepoteza uhakika wa kusema dhidi ya dhambi za siku zetu. Tukitangaza kwa uhakika yale ambayo Mungu ametangaza, baadhi ya watu hawatotupenda. Tunahitaji ndugu wasioogopa kudhihakiwa na walio tayari kuifuata njia isiyopitiwa na wengi.

Kabla tu Bwana wetu hajapaa juu, aliwapa wanafunzi wake ahadi tukufu, …mtapokea nguvu, akiisha kuwajilia juu yenu Roho Mtakatifu; nanyi mtakuwa mashahidi wangu katika Yerusalemu, na katika Uyahudi wote, na Samaria, na hata mwisho wa nchi –Matendo 1:8.

Mtapokea nguvu! Si nguvu kutoka kwa wanadamu, si nguvu kutoka kwa falme za ulimwengu huu, bali nguvu halisi ya kushinda—nguvu inayotoka kwa Roho Mtakatifu pekee! Baada ya kupokea nguvu hii, tunaendelea mbele tukiwa kiumbe kipya, tukitangaza kwa uhakika Injili yenye baraka ya Mkombozi wetu.

Tunahitaji mioyo inayowaka kwa mapenzi ya Mungu na neno la Mungu. Tunahitaji mioyo inayowaka moto!

Siku moja nilikuwa nakula chakula cha mchana wanandoa waliponijia na swali zito, “Kwa nini kanisa linafikiri kwamba linapaswa kututawala?” Baada ya kueleza jinsi wanavyofikiri wanapaswa kuwa na “uhuru katika Kristo”, nilifurahi kujibu maswali yao. Hata hivyo, kulikuwa na ndugu mwingine aliyewekwa rasmi aliyeketi kando yangu. Kwa hiyo niliamua kusubiri, nikitumaini kwamba angeanzisha mazungumzo na wanandoa hao, lakini hakusema lolote. Dakika nyingine arobaini na tano zilipopita, nilijaribu kuwaeleza wanandoa hao jinsi walivyohitaji kujikana wenyewe na kujitiisha kwa kanisa. Na kwamba wakiweka maisha yao chini kikamilifu, wakisalimisha yote, hawangekuwa tena na mapambano hayo kuhusu muundo wa kanisa.

Wanandoa hao walionekana kutiwa moyo na kuwa tayari kujaribu tena. Hata hivyo, mhudumu aliyekuwa kando yangu hakuonekana kufurahishwa sana, kwa hiyo nikamuuliza alifikiria nini. Alisema kwamba miaka mingi iliyopita baba yake alimwambia kwamba alipokuwa kijana alifikiri alikuwa na majibu yote. Alipokuwa mzee, alitambua kwamba hakujua chochote, na kwamba masuala ya kanisa ni magumu mno kuyatatua. Tunahitaji tu kujaribu kuelewana.

Je, hili ndilo jibu, kujifanya tu kwamba hatujui chochote na kutumaini kwamba mwishowe mambo yote yataenda sawa? Ninaelewa kwamba hatuna majibu yote. Kwani, natambua kwamba mara nyingi nina maswali mengi kuliko majibu. Hata hivyo, najua kile ambacho Mungu anataka kwa ajili ya kanisa lake! …Kristo naye alilipenda Kanisa, akajitoa kwa ajili yake; ili makusudi alitakase na kulisafisha kwa maji katika neno; apate kujiletea Kanisa tukufu, lisilo na ila wala kunyanzi wala lo lote kama hayo; bali liwe takatifu lisilo na mawaa –Waefeso 5:25-27.

Kanisa tukufu, lisilo na ila wala kunyanzi wala lo lote kama hayo; bali liwe takatifu lisilo na mawaa! Je, sisi, kama watu wa Mungu, tutasimama tena kwa ajili ya kweli, kuikana dunia, na kama kondoo kujiruhusu kuongozwa kwenda machinjoni? Au tumefanya maisha yetu kuwa ya starehe mno kiasi cha kushindwa kujikana wenyewe; je, tumechagua njia rahisi (pana) na kuikana njia iliyonyooka na nyembamba? Je, tumefanya mkataba wa amani na watumishi wa dhambi? Nikilia ninapoandika, je, nanyi mtalia mnaposoma?

Maana ya neno uhakika ni hisia au ufahamu wa uwezo wa mtu mwenyewe. Watu wengi leo wamechanganya uhakika na kiburi, na wana sababu nzuri ya kufanya hivyo. Watu wengi wenye uhakika hujiamini wao wenyewe, badala ya kuwa na uhakika katika Kristo. Tunaona hali hii ya kujiamini kila mahali. Kuna makocha wa maisha na washauri kote ulimwenguni, wanaowaambia watu wajiamini, na kuwaambia wawe na uhakika ndani yao wenyewe. Mtu anapojiamini, mara nyingi huwa na kiburi. Kumbuka, ulimwengu haukioni kiburi kuwa kibaya. Unaweza kusikia ulimwengu ukijivunia kiburi chake kila mahali unapotazama. Watu hujivunia watoto wao, nchi yao, timu yao ya michezo waipendayo, nyasi zao, na kimsingi kila kitu kizuri maishani mwao. Lazima tukumbuke kwamba kiburi ni dhambi na hakitaingia mbinguni. Ingawa kuwa na uhakika katika nafsi yako mwenyewe au katika vitu ni kiburi, kuwa na uhakika katika Mungu si kiburi!

Si jambo jipya kuchanganya uhakika katika Mungu na kiburi. Eliabu, kaka mkubwa wa Daudi, alimwambia, “Naujua ubishi wako.” Je, Daudi alikuwa na kiburi? La, alikuwa tu na uhakika mkubwa sana katika Mungu wake.

Je, inawezekana kwamba unyenyekevu wa bandia umelinyamazisha kanisa? Je, inawezekana kwamba mbinu hii ya adui ni mojawapo ya silaha za sasa za Shetani dhidi ya Wakristo? Je, inaweza pia kuwa sababu inayofanya kanisa lionekane kuwa linapambana katika sehemu zote za ulimwengu? Namna gani kama wanaume waaminifu wangesimama tena kwa imani katika Mungu wao kwa uhakika mkubwa, na kwa maneno na matendo yao kuuonyesha ulimwengu huu uliochafuliwa na dhambi njia iliyonyooka na nyembamba—kuelekea katika Ufalme wa Mungu?!

Sote lazima tukubali kwamba tunaishi katika ulimwengu uliochanganyikiwa—ulimwengu uliochanganyikiwa kuhusu lipi lililo sawa na lipi lililo baya. Namna gani kama ulimwengu ungeweza kulitazama Kanisa na kupata tena kundi la watu wanaojua hasa wanakokwenda—kanisa lisilo na shaka kuhusu njia iliyo sahihi—kanisa linaloweza kutangaza kwa ujasiri jibu la matatizo ya siku zetu—kanisa ambalo si jingine ila lina uhakika kamili katika MUNGU wao?

Na tuje mbele za Mungu wetu kwa magoti yaliyoinama, mioyo yetu ikiwa imeinama chini, tukionyesha huzuni ya kweli ya kimungu kwa sababu ya kupotea kwetu njia. Na tutafute kwa bidii mapenzi ya Mungu kwa ajili yetu wenyewe, familia zetu, makanisa yetu, na majirani zetu. Na tumwombe Mungu atuonyeshe jinsi tunavyoweza kuwa mifano yake kwa ulimwengu unaotuzunguka. Roho ya Bwana MUNGU i juu yangu; kwa sababu BWANA amenitia mafuta niwahubiri wanyenyekevu habari njema; amenituma ili kuwaganga waliovunjika moyo, kuwatangazia mateka uhuru wao, na hao waliofungwa habari za kufunguliwa kwao; kutangaza mwaka wa BWANA uliokubaliwa, na siku ya kisasi ya Mungu wetu; kuwafariji wote waliao; kuwaagizia hao waliao katika Sayuni wapewe kilemba cha uzuri badala ya majivu, mafuta ya furaha badala ya maombolezo, vazi la sifa badala ya roho nzito; wapate kuitwa miti ya haki, iliyopandwa na BWANA, ili atukuzwe –Isaya 61:1-3.

I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well –Psalm 139:14.

We live in a world full of bacteria and viruses. It is estimated that there are 100 trillion bacteria in the average human body. This is a huge number and one that I can’t wrap my mind around. Normally, these bacteria aren’t toxic until they get out of balance or get to a place where they are not intended to be. God has made us in such a way that our bodies have immune capabilities that are amazing.

Antibody-making cells and T cells float around our blood streams like sentinels, waiting for foreign cells or toxins to appear. A simple activity, like brushing your teeth or getting a scratch on your arm, can release bacteria into your blood stream. If it wasn’t for our God-given immune systems, those bacteria could attach to different tissues and cause serious infections.

It is important that we understand some about our immune system and think about ways in which we can help it function better.

In the Beginning

After He finished, …God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good… –Genesis 1:31. This doesn’t just mean that it looked beautiful, although it did. It also means at that point in time all of Creation was working together. There were no pathogenic bacteria and no harmful viruses. Adam and Eve were created perfectly and did not require antibiotics or probiotics to fight off infections.

Before the Fall, there was no need for an immune system the way we need it today. Most likely, the immune system of that era probably served more like a disposal system, getting rid of cells that needed to be cleaned up.

After the Fall, everything was different. Bacteria and viruses began to be “pathogenic” or disease-causing.

Components of Our Immune Systems

When people think of the immune system, they mostly think of cells that make antibodies. These are a very important part of our bodies’ defenses, but there are also many others.

a. Skin…

Our first line of defense against many infections is our skin. Having our body covered with an intact coating of skin with healthy bacteria on its surface can prevent unhealthy organisms from getting into the tissue underneath the skin and even into the blood stream.

I have seen plenty of severe infections that followed incidents during which the skin was broken. Anything from stepping on a nail to a dog bite can lead to infection.

b. Lymphatic System…

When we think about our circulation, the first thing that comes to mind is the blood system with veins, arteries, and the heart. There is another system, called the lymphatic system, that is charged with carrying infection-fighting blood cells throughout the body and getting rid of toxic materials.

There are little filtration areas along this system called lymph nodes that swell up when dealing with infections. Often when someone has an upper respiratory infection, they will notice that the lymph glands in their neck swell up. This is a sign that the immune system is doing what it is supposed to.

c. Bone Marrow/Spleen…

The bone marrow makes infection-fighting cells. Many of these cells are stored in the spleen which acts as a huge filter for the blood. When the body detects any type of infection, these infection-fighting cells are released into the blood stream and into the lymphatic system to fight off the bacteria or virus which is causing that infection.

Thus, people who are missing their spleen have an increased risk for certain types of infection.

d. Immune Cells…

The “soldiers” of our immune system are: white blood cells, B cells (which make antibodies), and T cells. These are the cells that respond to any invasion of our body.

e. Complement System…

This is a system that many people do not know as much about. This system includes the liver, which makes small proteins that help immune cells perform better and causes antibodies to be more effective. These proteins are floating around in an inactive state until there is a sign of infection, then certain enzymes activate them to be ready to help with an infection-fighting response.

Things that Damage our Immune Systems

There are a number of things that weaken our immune systems and make them less able to respond to infections. In fact, all of these things contribute to stunting our bodies’ defenses.

  1. A poor diet
  2. Bad sleep patterns
  3. Certain medications (particularly steroids)
  4. Poorly controlled diabetes (or any other debilitating illness)

Additionally, high levels of anxiety release stress hormones into the body that can lead to poor immunity.

Attempting to eliminate these things is a start, but we should also make certain to replace them with a healthy lifestyle. Many of the things that make our immune systems stronger are obvious, but that doesn’t mean we are always good at doing these things. We may have developed unhealthy habits or perhaps we were never taught certain healthy lifestyle choices.

Eat the Right Foods

There is no one specific food or juice we can consume that will push us towards a healthy ideal. Rather we need to have a mixture of healthy foods which we eat and unhealthy ones which we limit.

The first thing I think about when it comes to “the right foods,” is antioxidants. Antioxidants are chemicals that bind up damaging molecules in our bodies called “free radicals.” Too many free radicals can lead to all sorts of diseases, including diabetes and cancer. Of course, other parts of our bodies, such as our immune system, don’t function as well in this situation either.

Foods that are high in added nitrates, like cured meats, tend to greatly increase these free radicals and should be avoided.

Eating lots of fruits and vegetables really helps to naturally increase our vitamin levels (particularly Vitamin C). Eating healthy fats (those high in omega-3 fatty acids) and avoiding unhealthy ones (those high in saturated fat) probably also positively impact our ability to fight infection.

Get Adequate (Good) Sleep

Studies have looked at the risk of catching the common cold and found that people who slept less were more likely to catch colds. The cutoff point seemed to be around six hours for adults (it is probably more for teens and children).1

This makes sense since our bodies heal the most when we are sleeping. If you are waking up feeling unrested, it is important to figure out why. Things like simply not sleeping long enough, poor sleep hygiene (such as going to sleep thinking about worries, or working right up until bedtime), and sleep apnea can all cause sleep that is not restorative to our bodies.

God made our bodies with a need to rest, and He made a day for that purpose. If nothing else, this is the message of the Sabbath Day (see Exodus 20:8-11).

Consider Probiotics

In the 1800s, men like Joseph Lister and Louis Pasteur pushed forward the germ theory of disease. They believed that bacteria (at that time they didn’t yet know about viruses) were the causes behind many diseases. This led to Joseph Lister pioneering the sterilization of surgical instruments.

In the years since, we have concluded that not all bacteria are “pathogenic” or disease-causing. Many of the bacteria on our skin and in our digestive tract are good bacteria. These good bacteria aid with digestion and protect us from the pathogenic (or bad) bacteria moving in to cause us problems.

Probiotics are found in yogurt and kefir, plus many other foods. Probiotics can also be taken as supplements via capsules or drops.

One study gave 326 children probiotics or a placebo during the cold season. The children who were receiving the probiotics had significantly fewer respiratory illnesses and fevers during those six months.2

People who include these foods in their diet and take some probiotic supplements tend to be healthier and have stronger immune systems.

Cut Down on Sugar Intake

We know that obesity and uncontrolled diabetes increase the risk of infections, both minor and severe. It seems that when there is too much sugar floating around in the blood stream, it gives bad bacteria the nutrients they need to grow quickly, and it causes immune systems to not function as well.

When white blood cells are surrounded by lots of sugar, they are less able to perform “phagocytosis” (the process of swallowing) and they are less able to prevent the invasion of bad bacteria or viruses.3

We may have difficulty cutting all sugar out of our diet, but limiting it seems to make a big difference with regard to how well our bodies can fight off infection.

Exercise Regularly

It probably goes without saying but waiting until you feel like you have a cold coming on and then rushing out to run three miles is probably not going to be helpful. In fact, it could make you feel a lot worse as you deal with a body that is unused to exercise, which is also dealing with an infection.

The key here is moderation. Extreme high levels of activity, like that of performance athletes preparing for a big race or event, seem to increase the risk of infections. However, moderate levels of exercising 30 minutes per day for five days a week is good advice to follow so we can condition our bodies so we will have healthy hearts as well as other healthy systems to protect us from those unseen outside invaders.

Cut Down on Stress

“Dear God…
Grant me the [grace] to accept the things I cannot change,
[the] courage to change the things [that] I can,
and [the] wisdom to know the difference.”

Chronic elevation of stress hormones is harmful for our bodies. Stress hormones increase blood pressure and pulse rate. They push up blood sugars and tend to increase inflammatory responses in our bodies.4

Basically, stress hormones do all of the necessary things within your body to prepare you if the situation should arise that you would need to run away from serious danger, such as a charging grizzly bear. However, this high of a level of stress hormones isn’t particularly helpful when it comes to dealing with a child’s health problem, or the family’s financial difficulty.

Every one of us has dealt with worry at one time or another. Yet, living in a chronic state of worry is not healthy, nor is it a place where God wants to see His people living. From a Christian standpoint, our goal must be to give these concerns to God. Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you –I Peter 5:7. We don’t need to live with anxiety and all of the negative changes it can inflict on our physical health.

Spend Time Outdoors

When people think of sunlight, they mainly seem to think about Vitamin D.

It is true that Vitamin D is produced when our skin is exposed to sunlight, but sun exposure actually does much more. For example, sunlight seems to get our immune cells functioning in top condition to fight infections. Basically, T cells move much faster and more effectively when they have exposure to sunlight.5 Also, sun exposure increases nitric oxide levels in our bodies. This helps dilate blood vessels, lower blood pressure, and is a heart healthy chemical.

As with all the things I have mentioned, moderation is the key. Overexposure in the hot sun can cause sun stroke, and too much ultraviolet light is damaging to our skin cells, which can lead to burns and even skin cancers.

Targeted Supplements

Supplements can be helpful to fill in the gaps in our diet or places where our bodies are simply not absorbing as much of something as they should.

Vitamin D is one that jumps to my mind as we know that low Vitamin D levels increase the risk of severe infections. Our bodies don’t really know where the Vitamin D comes from. While it is probably best to get this from a combination of food and sun exposure, including supplements of Vitamin D may be helpful for older people or for anyone who has trouble achieving this.6

Zinc has been shown (short term) to reduce duration of colds. I would caution here that it isn’t really meant to be taken every day, but more should be taken at the first symptom of an upper respiratory infection coming on. This isn’t a miracle supplement and in studies it only reduced cold symptom duration by about one day.7

Vitamin C is another thing that many take when they feel colds coming on. Studies seem to indicate that it is well tolerated and effective.8 It is probably best to get most of your Vitamin C from your diet and only to introduce extra Vitamin C when you feel infection symptoms coming on.

There are many other supplements that people take; these are just three of the more common ones.

God made our bodies with multiple different systems. These systems heal injuries, maintain our body, and protect it from a world damaged by the introduction of sin at the Fall of man, in the Garden of Eden. We are indeed fearfully and wonderfully made. These systems work without our even thinking about them.

It is important that we are conscious of ways in which we can help, and not impede, these wonderfully designed cells and structures that prevent damaging organisms from entering our bodies and causing infection. It isn’t that healthy living or being a child of God will prevent us from ever getting sick, but rather that making a conscious decision to follow the right path will improve our body’s function. I believe that if we are healthy, it will make it easier for us to fulfil our mission—to reach the world around us with the Gospel message.

Je te louerai ; car je suis une créature si merveilleuse ; tes œuvres sont admirables, et mon âme le reconnaît bien –Psaume 139:14.

Nous vivons dans un monde rempli de bactéries et de virus. On estime que le corps humain moyen abrite 100 000 milliards de bactéries. C’est un nombre énorme, que je ne parviens pas à me représenter. En temps normal, ces bactéries ne sont pas toxiques, sauf lorsqu’elles se déséquilibrent ou se retrouvent dans un endroit où elles ne sont pas censées être. Dieu nous a créés de telle sorte que nos corps disposent de capacités immunitaires remarquables.

Des cellules productrices d’anticorps et des lymphocytes T circulent dans notre sang comme des sentinelles, à l’affût de cellules étrangères ou de toxines. Une activité banale, comme se brosser les dents ou se faire une égratignure au bras, peut libérer des bactéries dans le sang. Sans le système immunitaire que Dieu nous a donné, ces bactéries pourraient s’attacher à différents tissus et provoquer de graves infections.

Il est important que nous comprenions certains aspects de notre système immunitaire et que nous réfléchissions aux moyens de l’aider à mieux fonctionner.

Au commencement

Après avoir terminé, …Dieu vit tout ce qu’il avait fait, et voici, cela était très bon… –Genèse 1:31. Cela ne signifie pas seulement que tout était beau, même si c’était le cas. Cela signifie aussi qu’à ce moment-là toute la Création fonctionnait en harmonie. Il n’y avait ni bactéries pathogènes ni virus nocifs. Adam et Ève avaient été créés parfaitement et n’avaient pas besoin d’antibiotiques ni de probiotiques pour combattre les infections.

Avant la Chute, le système immunitaire n’était pas nécessaire comme il l’est aujourd’hui. Il est probable que le système immunitaire de cette époque servait plutôt de système d’élimination, se débarrassant des cellules qu’il fallait nettoyer.

Après la Chute, tout a changé. Les bactéries et les virus sont devenus « pathogènes », c’est-à-dire responsables de maladies.

Les composantes de notre système immunitaire

Quand les gens pensent au système immunitaire, ils pensent surtout aux cellules qui produisent des anticorps. Celles-ci constituent une partie très importante des défenses de notre corps, mais il en existe beaucoup d’autres.

a. La peau…

Notre première ligne de défense contre de nombreuses infections est la peau. Le fait que notre corps soit recouvert d’une couche de peau intacte, dont la surface abrite des bactéries bénéfiques, peut empêcher des organismes nocifs de pénétrer dans les tissus sous la peau et même dans le sang.

J’ai vu de nombreuses infections graves survenir à la suite d’incidents au cours desquels la peau avait été percée. Tout, d’un clou dans le pied à une morsure de chien, peut entraîner une infection.

b. Le système lymphatique…

Quand nous pensons à la circulation, la première chose qui nous vient à l’esprit est le système sanguin, avec ses veines, ses artères et le cœur. Il existe un autre système, appelé système lymphatique, qui est chargé de transporter dans tout le corps des cellules sanguines combattant les infections et d’éliminer les substances toxiques.

Le long de ce système se trouvent de petites zones de filtration appelées ganglions lymphatiques, qui enflent lorsqu’ils combattent des infections. Souvent, lorsqu’une personne a une infection des voies respiratoires supérieures, elle remarquera que les ganglions lymphatiques de son cou enflent. C’est le signe que le système immunitaire fait ce qu’il est censé faire.

c. La moelle osseuse et la rate…

La moelle osseuse produit des cellules qui combattent les infections. Beaucoup de ces cellules sont stockées dans la rate, qui agit comme un immense filtre pour le sang. Lorsque le corps détecte une infection, quelle qu’elle soit, ces cellules sont libérées dans le sang et dans le système lymphatique afin de combattre la bactérie ou le virus responsable de cette infection.

Ainsi, les personnes qui n’ont pas de rate présentent un risque accru de certains types d’infection.

d. Les cellules immunitaires…

Les « soldats » de notre système immunitaire sont les globules blancs, les lymphocytes B (qui produisent des anticorps) et les lymphocytes T. Ce sont les cellules qui réagissent à toute invasion de notre corps.

e. Le système du complément…

C’est un système que beaucoup de gens connaissent moins bien. Il comprend le foie, qui produit de petites protéines aidant les cellules immunitaires à mieux fonctionner et rendant les anticorps plus efficaces. Ces protéines circulent à l’état inactif jusqu’à l’apparition d’un signe d’infection ; alors, certaines enzymes les activent afin qu’elles soient prêtes à contribuer à la réponse de l’organisme contre l’infection.

Ce qui nuit à notre système immunitaire

Un certain nombre de facteurs affaiblissent notre système immunitaire et le rendent moins apte à réagir aux infections. En fait, tous ces facteurs contribuent à freiner les défenses de notre corps.

  1. Une mauvaise alimentation
  2. De mauvaises habitudes de sommeil
  3. Certains médicaments (en particulier les stéroïdes)
  4. Un diabète mal maîtrisé (ou toute autre maladie invalidante)

De plus, un niveau élevé d’anxiété libère dans le corps des hormones du stress qui peuvent affaiblir l’immunité.

Essayer d’éliminer ces facteurs est un début, mais nous devrions aussi veiller à les remplacer par un mode de vie sain. Beaucoup de choses qui renforcent notre système immunitaire sont évidentes, mais cela ne signifie pas que nous les faisons toujours bien. Nous avons peut-être pris de mauvaises habitudes, ou peut-être ne nous a-t-on jamais enseigné certains choix de vie sains.

Manger les bons aliments

Il n’existe pas un aliment ou un jus en particulier que nous puissions consommer pour nous rapprocher d’un idéal de santé. Nous devons plutôt manger un mélange d’aliments sains et limiter les aliments malsains.

La première chose à laquelle je pense quand il est question des « bons aliments », ce sont les antioxydants. Les antioxydants sont des substances chimiques qui neutralisent des molécules nocives de notre corps appelées « radicaux libres ». Un excès de radicaux libres peut entraîner toutes sortes de maladies, notamment le diabète et le cancer. Bien sûr, d’autres parties de notre corps, comme notre système immunitaire, fonctionnent elles aussi moins bien dans ces conditions.

Les aliments riches en nitrates ajoutés, comme les viandes salaisonnées, tendent à augmenter considérablement ces radicaux libres et devraient être évités.

Manger beaucoup de fruits et de légumes contribue vraiment à augmenter naturellement nos taux de vitamines (en particulier de vitamine C). Manger des graisses saines (riches en acides gras oméga-3) et éviter les graisses malsaines (riches en graisses saturées) a probablement aussi un effet bénéfique sur notre capacité à combattre les infections.

Bien dormir suffisamment

Des études se sont penchées sur le risque d’attraper un rhume et ont constaté que les personnes qui dormaient moins étaient plus susceptibles d’en attraper un. Le seuil semblait se situer aux alentours de six heures pour les adultes (il est probablement plus élevé pour les adolescents et les enfants).1

Cela est logique, puisque notre corps se répare surtout pendant le sommeil. Si vous vous réveillez sans vous sentir reposé, il est important d’en découvrir la raison. Des facteurs comme le fait de ne pas dormir assez longtemps, une mauvaise hygiène du sommeil (par exemple, se coucher en pensant à ses soucis ou travailler jusqu’à l’heure du coucher) et l’apnée du sommeil peuvent tous rendre le sommeil non réparateur pour notre corps.

Dieu a créé nos corps avec un besoin de repos, et Il a institué un jour à cette fin. Si rien d’autre, c’est là le message du jour du sabbat (voir Exode 20:8-11).

Envisager les probiotiques

Au XIXe siècle, des hommes comme Joseph Lister et Louis Pasteur ont fait avancer la théorie microbienne des maladies. Ils croyaient que les bactéries (à l’époque, ils ne connaissaient pas encore les virus) étaient à l’origine de nombreuses maladies. Cela a conduit Joseph Lister à être un pionnier de la stérilisation des instruments chirurgicaux.

Depuis, nous avons conclu que toutes les bactéries ne sont pas « pathogènes », ou responsables de maladies. Beaucoup des bactéries présentes sur notre peau et dans notre tube digestif sont bénéfiques. Elles facilitent la digestion et nous protègent contre les bactéries pathogènes (ou mauvaises) qui pourraient s’installer et nous causer des problèmes.

On trouve des probiotiques dans le yaourt et le kéfir, ainsi que dans de nombreux autres aliments. On peut également prendre des probiotiques sous forme de compléments, en capsules ou en gouttes.

Une étude a administré des probiotiques ou un placebo à 326 enfants pendant la saison des rhumes. Les enfants qui recevaient des probiotiques ont eu nettement moins de maladies respiratoires et de fièvres au cours de ces six mois.2

Les personnes qui incluent ces aliments dans leur régime alimentaire et prennent des compléments probiotiques tendent à être en meilleure santé et à avoir un système immunitaire plus fort.

Réduire sa consommation de sucre

Nous savons que l’obésité et le diabète mal maîtrisé augmentent le risque d’infections, bénignes comme graves. Il semble que lorsqu’il y a trop de sucre qui circule dans le sang, celui-ci apporte aux mauvaises bactéries les nutriments dont elles ont besoin pour se multiplier rapidement et empêche le système immunitaire de fonctionner aussi bien.

Lorsque les globules blancs sont entourés de beaucoup de sucre, ils sont moins capables d’effectuer la « phagocytose » (le processus qui consiste à engloutir) et moins aptes à empêcher l’invasion de mauvaises bactéries ou de virus.3

Il nous est peut-être difficile de supprimer tout le sucre de notre alimentation, mais le fait d’en limiter la consommation semble faire une grande différence quant à la capacité de notre corps à combattre les infections.

Faire régulièrement de l’exercice

On le sait sans doute, mais attendre de sentir qu’on va attraper un rhume pour sortir en courant faire cinq kilomètres ne sera probablement pas utile. En fait, cela pourrait vous faire vous sentir bien plus mal, car votre corps, qui n’est pas habitué à l’exercice, doit aussi lutter contre une infection.

La clé, ici, est la modération. Des niveaux d’activité extrêmement élevés, comme ceux des athlètes de compétition qui se préparent pour une grande course ou un événement, semblent accroître le risque d’infections. Toutefois, il est conseillé de faire de l’exercice à intensité modérée pendant 30 minutes par jour, cinq jours par semaine, afin de conditionner notre corps et d’avoir un cœur en bonne santé, ainsi que d’autres systèmes sains qui nous protègent contre ces agresseurs invisibles venus de l’extérieur.

Réduire le stress

« Cher Dieu…
Accorde-moi la [grâce] d’accepter les choses que je ne peux changer,
[le] courage de changer les choses [que] je peux,
et [la] sagesse d’en connaître la différence. »

Une élévation chronique des hormones du stress est néfaste pour notre corps. Ces hormones augmentent la pression artérielle et le rythme cardiaque. Elles font monter la glycémie et tendent à accroître les réactions inflammatoires dans notre corps.4

En gros, les hormones du stress font dans votre corps tout ce qu’il faut pour vous préparer à fuir si une situation l’exige, par exemple face à un grizzly qui charge. Toutefois, un niveau aussi élevé d’hormones du stress n’est pas particulièrement utile lorsqu’il s’agit de faire face à un problème de santé d’un enfant ou aux difficultés financières de la famille.

Chacun de nous a connu l’inquiétude à un moment ou à un autre. Pourtant, vivre dans un état d’inquiétude chronique n’est pas bon pour la santé et ce n’est pas non plus là que Dieu veut voir vivre son peuple. Du point de vue chrétien, notre objectif doit être de confier ces préoccupations à Dieu. Déchargez-vous sur lui de tous vos soucis, car lui-même prend soin de vous –I Pierre 5:7. Nous n’avons pas besoin de vivre dans l’anxiété et de subir tous les effets négatifs qu’elle peut avoir sur notre santé physique.

Passer du temps à l’extérieur

Quand les gens pensent à la lumière du soleil, ils semblent surtout penser à la vitamine D.

Il est vrai que la vitamine D est produite lorsque notre peau est exposée à la lumière du soleil, mais l’exposition au soleil fait en réalité bien plus. Par exemple, la lumière du soleil semble permettre à nos cellules immunitaires de fonctionner au mieux pour combattre les infections. En gros, les lymphocytes T se déplacent beaucoup plus rapidement et efficacement lorsqu’ils sont exposés à la lumière du soleil.5 En outre, l’exposition au soleil augmente le taux d’oxyde nitrique dans notre corps. Cela contribue à dilater les vaisseaux sanguins et à faire baisser la tension artérielle ; c’est également une substance bénéfique pour le cœur.

Comme pour toutes les choses que j’ai mentionnées, la clé est la modération. Une exposition excessive au soleil brûlant peut provoquer une insolation, et une trop grande quantité de rayons ultraviolets endommage nos cellules cutanées, ce qui peut entraîner des brûlures et même des cancers de la peau.

Des compléments ciblés

Les compléments peuvent être utiles pour combler les lacunes de notre alimentation ou compenser les cas où notre corps n’absorbe tout simplement pas autant qu’il le devrait d’un élément donné.

La vitamine D est l’une des premières choses qui me viennent à l’esprit, car nous savons que de faibles taux de vitamine D augmentent le risque d’infections graves. Notre corps ne sait pas vraiment d’où vient la vitamine D. S’il vaut probablement mieux en obtenir par une combinaison d’aliments et d’exposition au soleil, la prise de compléments de vitamine D peut être utile aux personnes âgées ou à toute personne qui a du mal à en obtenir suffisamment.6

Le zinc a montré qu’à court terme, il pouvait réduire la durée des rhumes. Je tiens à préciser ici qu’il n’est pas vraiment destiné à être pris tous les jours ; il vaut mieux en prendre davantage dès les premiers symptômes d’une infection des voies respiratoires supérieures. Ce n’est pas un complément miracle et, dans les études, il n’a réduit la durée des symptômes du rhume que d’environ un jour.7

La vitamine C est un autre produit que beaucoup prennent lorsqu’ils sentent qu’un rhume arrive. Les études semblent indiquer qu’elle est bien tolérée et efficace.8 Il vaut probablement mieux obtenir la majeure partie de sa vitamine C par l’alimentation et n’en prendre davantage que lorsque des symptômes d’infection apparaissent.

Les gens prennent beaucoup d’autres compléments ; je n’en ai cité que trois parmi les plus courants.

Dieu a créé nos corps avec plusieurs systèmes différents. Ces systèmes guérissent les blessures, entretiennent notre corps et le protègent d’un monde abîmé par l’introduction du péché lors de la Chute de l’homme, dans le jardin d’Éden. Nous sommes véritablement une créature merveilleuse. Ces systèmes fonctionnent sans même que nous y pensions.

Il est important que nous soyons conscients des moyens d’aider ces cellules et ces structures merveilleusement conçues, et de ne pas entraver leur action lorsqu’elles empêchent des organismes nuisibles de pénétrer dans notre corps et de provoquer des infections. Ce n’est pas qu’un mode de vie sain ou le fait d’être enfant de Dieu nous empêchera de tomber malades, mais plutôt que faire consciemment le choix de suivre la bonne voie améliorera le fonctionnement de notre corps. Je crois que si nous sommes en bonne santé, il nous sera plus facile d’accomplir notre mission : atteindre le monde qui nous entoure avec le message de l’Évangile.

I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well –Psalm 139:14.

We live in a world full of bacteria and viruses. It is estimated that there are 100 trillion bacteria in the average human body. This is a huge number and one that I can’t wrap my mind around. Normally, these bacteria aren’t toxic until they get out of balance or get to a place where they are not intended to be. God has made us in such a way that our bodies have immune capabilities that are amazing.

Antibody-making cells and T cells float around our blood streams like sentinels, waiting for foreign cells or toxins to appear. A simple activity, like brushing your teeth or getting a scratch on your arm, can release bacteria into your blood stream. If it wasn’t for our God-given immune systems, those bacteria could attach to different tissues and cause serious infections.

It is important that we understand some about our immune system and think about ways in which we can help it function better.

In the Beginning

After He finished, …God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good… –Genesis 1:31. This doesn’t just mean that it looked beautiful, although it did. It also means at that point in time all of Creation was working together. There were no pathogenic bacteria and no harmful viruses. Adam and Eve were created perfectly and did not require antibiotics or probiotics to fight off infections.

Before the Fall, there was no need for an immune system the way we need it today. Most likely, the immune system of that era probably served more like a disposal system, getting rid of cells that needed to be cleaned up.

After the Fall, everything was different. Bacteria and viruses began to be “pathogenic” or disease-causing.

Components of Our Immune Systems

When people think of the immune system, they mostly think of cells that make antibodies. These are a very important part of our bodies’ defenses, but there are also many others.

a. Skin…

Our first line of defense against many infections is our skin. Having our body covered with an intact coating of skin with healthy bacteria on its surface can prevent unhealthy organisms from getting into the tissue underneath the skin and even into the blood stream.

I have seen plenty of severe infections that followed incidents during which the skin was broken. Anything from stepping on a nail to a dog bite can lead to infection.

b. Lymphatic System…

When we think about our circulation, the first thing that comes to mind is the blood system with veins, arteries, and the heart. There is another system, called the lymphatic system, that is charged with carrying infection-fighting blood cells throughout the body and getting rid of toxic materials.

There are little filtration areas along this system called lymph nodes that swell up when dealing with infections. Often when someone has an upper respiratory infection, they will notice that the lymph glands in their neck swell up. This is a sign that the immune system is doing what it is supposed to.

c. Bone Marrow/Spleen…

The bone marrow makes infection-fighting cells. Many of these cells are stored in the spleen which acts as a huge filter for the blood. When the body detects any type of infection, these infection-fighting cells are released into the blood stream and into the lymphatic system to fight off the bacteria or virus which is causing that infection.

Thus, people who are missing their spleen have an increased risk for certain types of infection.

d. Immune Cells…

The “soldiers” of our immune system are: white blood cells, B cells (which make antibodies), and T cells. These are the cells that respond to any invasion of our body.

e. Complement System…

This is a system that many people do not know as much about. This system includes the liver, which makes small proteins that help immune cells perform better and causes antibodies to be more effective. These proteins are floating around in an inactive state until there is a sign of infection, then certain enzymes activate them to be ready to help with an infection-fighting response.

Things that Damage our Immune Systems

There are a number of things that weaken our immune systems and make them less able to respond to infections. In fact, all of these things contribute to stunting our bodies’ defenses.

  1. A poor diet
  2. Bad sleep patterns
  3. Certain medications (particularly steroids)
  4. Poorly controlled diabetes (or any other debilitating illness)

Additionally, high levels of anxiety release stress hormones into the body that can lead to poor immunity.

Attempting to eliminate these things is a start, but we should also make certain to replace them with a healthy lifestyle. Many of the things that make our immune systems stronger are obvious, but that doesn’t mean we are always good at doing these things. We may have developed unhealthy habits or perhaps we were never taught certain healthy lifestyle choices.

Eat the Right Foods

There is no one specific food or juice we can consume that will push us towards a healthy ideal. Rather we need to have a mixture of healthy foods which we eat and unhealthy ones which we limit.

The first thing I think about when it comes to “the right foods,” is antioxidants. Antioxidants are chemicals that bind up damaging molecules in our bodies called “free radicals.” Too many free radicals can lead to all sorts of diseases, including diabetes and cancer. Of course, other parts of our bodies, such as our immune system, don’t function as well in this situation either.

Foods that are high in added nitrates, like cured meats, tend to greatly increase these free radicals and should be avoided.

Eating lots of fruits and vegetables really helps to naturally increase our vitamin levels (particularly Vitamin C). Eating healthy fats (those high in omega-3 fatty acids) and avoiding unhealthy ones (those high in saturated fat) probably also positively impact our ability to fight infection.

Get Adequate (Good) Sleep

Studies have looked at the risk of catching the common cold and found that people who slept less were more likely to catch colds. The cutoff point seemed to be around six hours for adults (it is probably more for teens and children).1

This makes sense since our bodies heal the most when we are sleeping. If you are waking up feeling unrested, it is important to figure out why. Things like simply not sleeping long enough, poor sleep hygiene (such as going to sleep thinking about worries, or working right up until bedtime), and sleep apnea can all cause sleep that is not restorative to our bodies.

God made our bodies with a need to rest, and He made a day for that purpose. If nothing else, this is the message of the Sabbath Day (see Exodus 20:8-11).

Consider Probiotics

In the 1800s, men like Joseph Lister and Louis Pasteur pushed forward the germ theory of disease. They believed that bacteria (at that time they didn’t yet know about viruses) were the causes behind many diseases. This led to Joseph Lister pioneering the sterilization of surgical instruments.

In the years since, we have concluded that not all bacteria are “pathogenic” or disease-causing. Many of the bacteria on our skin and in our digestive tract are good bacteria. These good bacteria aid with digestion and protect us from the pathogenic (or bad) bacteria moving in to cause us problems.

Probiotics are found in yogurt and kefir, plus many other foods. Probiotics can also be taken as supplements via capsules or drops.

One study gave 326 children probiotics or a placebo during the cold season. The children who were receiving the probiotics had significantly fewer respiratory illnesses and fevers during those six months.2

People who include these foods in their diet and take some probiotic supplements tend to be healthier and have stronger immune systems.

Cut Down on Sugar Intake

We know that obesity and uncontrolled diabetes increase the risk of infections, both minor and severe. It seems that when there is too much sugar floating around in the blood stream, it gives bad bacteria the nutrients they need to grow quickly, and it causes immune systems to not function as well.

When white blood cells are surrounded by lots of sugar, they are less able to perform “phagocytosis” (the process of swallowing) and they are less able to prevent the invasion of bad bacteria or viruses.3

We may have difficulty cutting all sugar out of our diet, but limiting it seems to make a big difference with regard to how well our bodies can fight off infection.

Exercise Regularly

It probably goes without saying but waiting until you feel like you have a cold coming on and then rushing out to run three miles is probably not going to be helpful. In fact, it could make you feel a lot worse as you deal with a body that is unused to exercise, which is also dealing with an infection.

The key here is moderation. Extreme high levels of activity, like that of performance athletes preparing for a big race or event, seem to increase the risk of infections. However, moderate levels of exercising 30 minutes per day for five days a week is good advice to follow so we can condition our bodies so we will have healthy hearts as well as other healthy systems to protect us from those unseen outside invaders.

Cut Down on Stress

“Dear God…
Grant me the [grace] to accept the things I cannot change,
[the] courage to change the things [that] I can,
and [the] wisdom to know the difference.”

Chronic elevation of stress hormones is harmful for our bodies. Stress hormones increase blood pressure and pulse rate. They push up blood sugars and tend to increase inflammatory responses in our bodies.4

Basically, stress hormones do all of the necessary things within your body to prepare you if the situation should arise that you would need to run away from serious danger, such as a charging grizzly bear. However, this high of a level of stress hormones isn’t particularly helpful when it comes to dealing with a child’s health problem, or the family’s financial difficulty.

Every one of us has dealt with worry at one time or another. Yet, living in a chronic state of worry is not healthy, nor is it a place where God wants to see His people living. From a Christian standpoint, our goal must be to give these concerns to God. Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you –I Peter 5:7. We don’t need to live with anxiety and all of the negative changes it can inflict on our physical health.

Spend Time Outdoors

When people think of sunlight, they mainly seem to think about Vitamin D.

It is true that Vitamin D is produced when our skin is exposed to sunlight, but sun exposure actually does much more. For example, sunlight seems to get our immune cells functioning in top condition to fight infections. Basically, T cells move much faster and more effectively when they have exposure to sunlight.5 Also, sun exposure increases nitric oxide levels in our bodies. This helps dilate blood vessels, lower blood pressure, and is a heart healthy chemical.

As with all the things I have mentioned, moderation is the key. Overexposure in the hot sun can cause sun stroke, and too much ultraviolet light is damaging to our skin cells, which can lead to burns and even skin cancers.

Targeted Supplements

Supplements can be helpful to fill in the gaps in our diet or places where our bodies are simply not absorbing as much of something as they should.

Vitamin D is one that jumps to my mind as we know that low Vitamin D levels increase the risk of severe infections. Our bodies don’t really know where the Vitamin D comes from. While it is probably best to get this from a combination of food and sun exposure, including supplements of Vitamin D may be helpful for older people or for anyone who has trouble achieving this.6

Zinc has been shown (short term) to reduce duration of colds. I would caution here that it isn’t really meant to be taken every day, but more should be taken at the first symptom of an upper respiratory infection coming on. This isn’t a miracle supplement and in studies it only reduced cold symptom duration by about one day.7

Vitamin C is another thing that many take when they feel colds coming on. Studies seem to indicate that it is well tolerated and effective.8 It is probably best to get most of your Vitamin C from your diet and only to introduce extra Vitamin C when you feel infection symptoms coming on.

There are many other supplements that people take; these are just three of the more common ones.

God made our bodies with multiple different systems. These systems heal injuries, maintain our body, and protect it from a world damaged by the introduction of sin at the Fall of man, in the Garden of Eden. We are indeed fearfully and wonderfully made. These systems work without our even thinking about them.

It is important that we are conscious of ways in which we can help, and not impede, these wonderfully designed cells and structures that prevent damaging organisms from entering our bodies and causing infection. It isn’t that healthy living or being a child of God will prevent us from ever getting sick, but rather that making a conscious decision to follow the right path will improve our body’s function. I believe that if we are healthy, it will make it easier for us to fulfil our mission—to reach the world around us with the Gospel message.

Te alabaré; porque de manera asombrosa y maravillosa he sido hecho; maravillosas son tus obras, y mi alma lo sabe muy bien –Salmo 139:14.

Vivimos en un mundo lleno de bacterias y virus. Se calcula que en el cuerpo humano promedio hay 100 billones de bacterias. Es una cifra enorme que no logro ni siquiera imaginar. Normalmente, estas bacterias no son tóxicas, a menos que se desequilibren o lleguen a un lugar donde no deberían estar. Dios nos hizo de tal manera que nuestros cuerpos cuentan con capacidades inmunitarias asombrosas.

Las células que producen anticuerpos y las células T circulan por nuestro torrente sanguíneo como centinelas, a la espera de que aparezcan células extrañas o toxinas. Una actividad sencilla, como cepillarse los dientes o hacerse un rasguño en el brazo, puede liberar bacterias en el torrente sanguíneo. Si no fuera por nuestro sistema inmunitario, que Dios nos ha dado, esas bacterias podrían adherirse a distintos tejidos y causar infecciones graves.

Es importante que comprendamos algo sobre nuestro sistema inmunitario y pensemos en maneras de ayudarlo a funcionar mejor.

En el principio

Después de terminar, …vio Dios todo lo que había hecho, y he aquí que era bueno en gran manera… –Génesis 1:31. Esto no solo significa que se veía hermoso, aunque así era. También significa que en aquel momento toda la Creación funcionaba en armonía. No había bacterias patógenas ni virus dañinos. Adán y Eva fueron creados perfectos y no necesitaban antibióticos ni probióticos para combatir infecciones.

Antes de la Caída, no había necesidad de un sistema inmunitario como el que necesitamos hoy. Lo más probable es que el sistema inmunitario de aquella época cumpliera más bien la función de un sistema de eliminación, deshaciéndose de las células que había que limpiar.

Después de la Caída, todo cambió. Las bacterias y los virus empezaron a ser «patógenos», es decir, causantes de enfermedades.

Componentes de nuestro sistema inmunitario

Cuando las personas piensan en el sistema inmunitario, piensan sobre todo en las células que producen anticuerpos. Estas son una parte muy importante de las defensas de nuestro cuerpo, pero también hay muchas otras.

a. Piel…

Nuestra primera línea de defensa contra muchas infecciones es la piel. Tener el cuerpo cubierto por una capa intacta de piel con bacterias saludables en su superficie puede impedir que organismos dañinos penetren en el tejido debajo de la piel e incluso en el torrente sanguíneo.

He visto muchas infecciones graves que aparecieron después de incidentes en los que se rompió la piel. Cualquier cosa, desde pisar un clavo hasta la mordedura de un perro, puede provocar una infección.

b. Sistema linfático…

Cuando pensamos en nuestra circulación, lo primero que nos viene a la mente es el sistema sanguíneo, con las venas, las arterias y el corazón. Hay otro sistema, llamado sistema linfático, cuya función es transportar por todo el cuerpo células sanguíneas que combaten infecciones y eliminar materiales tóxicos.

A lo largo de este sistema hay pequeñas zonas de filtración llamadas ganglios linfáticos, que se hinchan cuando combaten infecciones. A menudo, cuando alguien tiene una infección de las vías respiratorias superiores, nota que se le hinchan los ganglios linfáticos del cuello. Esto indica que el sistema inmunitario está haciendo lo que debe.

c. Médula ósea/bazo…

La médula ósea produce células que combaten infecciones. Muchas de estas células se almacenan en el bazo, que actúa como un enorme filtro de la sangre. Cuando el cuerpo detecta cualquier tipo de infección, estas células que combaten infecciones se liberan en el torrente sanguíneo y en el sistema linfático para luchar contra la bacteria o el virus que la está causando.

Por eso, las personas a quienes les falta el bazo tienen un mayor riesgo de contraer ciertos tipos de infecciones.

d. Células inmunitarias…

Los «soldados» de nuestro sistema inmunitario son los glóbulos blancos, las células B (que producen anticuerpos) y las células T. Estas son las células que responden a cualquier invasión de nuestro cuerpo.

e. Sistema del complemento…

Muchas personas no conocen demasiado este sistema. Incluye el hígado, que produce pequeñas proteínas que ayudan a las células inmunitarias a funcionar mejor y hacen que los anticuerpos sean más eficaces. Estas proteínas circulan en estado inactivo hasta que aparece una señal de infección; entonces, ciertas enzimas las activan para que estén listas para ayudar en la respuesta contra la infección.

Cosas que dañan nuestro sistema inmunitario

Hay varias cosas que debilitan nuestro sistema inmunitario y reducen su capacidad para responder a las infecciones. De hecho, todas estas cosas contribuyen a frenar el desarrollo de las defensas de nuestro cuerpo.

  1. Una alimentación deficiente
  2. Malos hábitos de sueño
  3. Ciertos medicamentos (en particular, los esteroides)
  4. Diabetes mal controlada (o cualquier otra enfermedad debilitante)

Además, los niveles elevados de ansiedad liberan hormonas del estrés en el cuerpo, lo que puede debilitar la inmunidad.

Intentar eliminar estos factores es un comienzo, pero también debemos asegurarnos de sustituirlos por un estilo de vida saludable. Muchas de las cosas que fortalecen nuestro sistema inmunitario son obvias, pero eso no significa que siempre se nos dé bien hacerlas. Quizás hayamos desarrollado hábitos poco saludables o nunca nos hayan enseñado ciertas opciones de vida saludables.

Coma los alimentos adecuados

No hay un alimento o jugo específico que podamos consumir para alcanzar un ideal de salud. Más bien, necesitamos una combinación de alimentos saludables que comamos y alimentos poco saludables cuyo consumo limitemos.

Lo primero que pienso cuando se trata de «los alimentos adecuados» son los antioxidantes. Los antioxidantes son sustancias químicas que se unen a moléculas dañinas de nuestro cuerpo llamadas «radicales libres». Un exceso de radicales libres puede provocar todo tipo de enfermedades, incluida la diabetes y el cáncer. Por supuesto, en esas circunstancias otras partes de nuestro cuerpo, como el sistema inmunitario, tampoco funcionan tan bien.

Los alimentos con alto contenido de nitratos añadidos, como las carnes curadas, tienden a aumentar mucho estos radicales libres y deben evitarse.

Comer muchas frutas y verduras ayuda mucho a aumentar de manera natural nuestros niveles de vitaminas (en particular, de vitamina C). Consumir grasas saludables (las ricas en ácidos grasos omega-3) y evitar las poco saludables (las ricas en grasas saturadas) probablemente también influye de manera positiva en nuestra capacidad para combatir infecciones.

Duerma lo suficiente y bien

Se han realizado estudios sobre el riesgo de contraer el resfriado común, y se ha observado que las personas que dormían menos tenían más probabilidades de resfriarse. El límite parecía situarse en torno a las seis horas para los adultos (probablemente sea más para los adolescentes y los niños).1

Esto tiene sentido, ya que nuestros cuerpos se curan sobre todo mientras dormimos. Si se despierta sin sentirse descansado, es importante averiguar por qué. Cosas como simplemente no dormir lo suficiente, una mala higiene del sueño (por ejemplo, acostarse pensando en las preocupaciones o trabajar hasta la hora de dormir) y la apnea del sueño pueden hacer que el sueño no sea reparador para nuestro cuerpo.

Dios creó nuestros cuerpos con la necesidad de descansar, y estableció un día para ese propósito. Si no hay otra cosa, este es el mensaje del día de reposo (véase Éxodo 20:8-11).

Considere los probióticos

En el siglo XIX, hombres como Joseph Lister y Louis Pasteur impulsaron la teoría microbiana de las enfermedades. Creían que las bacterias (en aquella época aún no sabían de la existencia de los virus) eran la causa de muchas enfermedades. Esto llevó a Joseph Lister a ser pionero en la esterilización de instrumentos quirúrgicos.

Desde entonces, hemos llegado a la conclusión de que no todas las bacterias son «patógenas», es decir, causantes de enfermedades. Muchas de las bacterias de nuestra piel y nuestro aparato digestivo son buenas. Estas bacterias buenas ayudan a la digestión y nos protegen de las bacterias patógenas (o malas) que llegan y nos causan problemas.

Los probióticos se encuentran en el yogur y el kéfir, además de muchos otros alimentos. También se pueden tomar como suplementos en cápsulas o gotas.

En un estudio, a 326 niños se les administró probióticos o un placebo durante la temporada de resfriados. Los niños que recibieron los probióticos tuvieron significativamente menos enfermedades respiratorias y fiebres durante esos seis meses.2

Las personas que incluyen estos alimentos en su dieta y toman algunos suplementos probióticos tienden a gozar de mejor salud y a tener un sistema inmunitario más fuerte.

Reduzca el consumo de azúcar

Sabemos que la obesidad y la diabetes no controlada aumentan el riesgo de infecciones, tanto leves como graves. Parece que cuando hay demasiado azúcar circulando en el torrente sanguíneo, proporciona a las bacterias dañinas los nutrientes que necesitan para crecer rápidamente y hace que el sistema inmunitario no funcione tan bien.

Cuando los glóbulos blancos están rodeados de mucho azúcar, tienen menos capacidad para realizar la «fagocitosis» (el proceso de engullir) y menos capacidad para impedir la invasión de bacterias o virus dañinos.3

Quizás nos cueste eliminar por completo el azúcar de nuestra dieta, pero limitar su consumo parece marcar una gran diferencia en la capacidad de nuestro cuerpo para combatir las infecciones.

Haga ejercicio con regularidad

Probablemente no haga falta decirlo, pero esperar hasta sentir que se avecina un resfriado y salir corriendo a hacer cinco kilómetros seguramente no será útil. De hecho, podría hacerle sentir mucho peor, pues su cuerpo no está acostumbrado al ejercicio y además está lidiando con una infección.

La clave aquí es la moderación. Los niveles extremadamente altos de actividad, como los de los deportistas de competición que se preparan para una carrera o un evento importante, parecen aumentar el riesgo de infecciones. Sin embargo, es aconsejable hacer ejercicio a un nivel moderado durante 30 minutos al día, cinco días a la semana, para acondicionar nuestro cuerpo y tener un corazón sano, así como otros sistemas saludables que nos protejan de esos invasores externos invisibles.

Reduzca el estrés

«Querido Dios…
Concédeme la [gracia] de aceptar las cosas que no puedo cambiar,
[el] valor para cambiar las cosas [que] sí puedo,
y [la] sabiduría para reconocer la diferencia».

La elevación crónica de las hormonas del estrés es perjudicial para nuestro cuerpo. Las hormonas del estrés aumentan la presión arterial y el pulso. Elevan el nivel de azúcar en la sangre y tienden a aumentar las respuestas inflamatorias de nuestro cuerpo.4

En esencia, las hormonas del estrés hacen dentro del cuerpo todo lo necesario para prepararlo en caso de que se presente una situación en la que usted tenga que huir de un peligro grave, como un oso grizzly que se le abalanza. Sin embargo, un nivel de hormonas del estrés tan elevado no es precisamente útil para lidiar con un problema de salud de un hijo o con dificultades económicas de la familia.

Todos hemos tenido preocupaciones alguna vez. Sin embargo, vivir en un estado de preocupación crónica no es saludable, ni es un estado en el que Dios quiera ver vivir a su pueblo. Desde una perspectiva cristiana, nuestro objetivo debe ser entregar estas preocupaciones a Dios. Echando toda vuestra ansiedad sobre él, porque él tiene cuidado de vosotros –1 Pedro 5:7. No necesitamos vivir con ansiedad y con todos los cambios negativos que esta puede causar en nuestra salud física.

Pase tiempo al aire libre

Cuando las personas piensan en la luz del sol, suelen pensar sobre todo en la vitamina D.

Es cierto que la vitamina D se produce cuando nuestra piel se expone a la luz del sol, pero la exposición al sol hace mucho más. Por ejemplo, parece que la luz del sol hace que nuestras células inmunitarias funcionen en condiciones óptimas para combatir infecciones. En esencia, las células T se mueven mucho más rápido y eficazmente cuando están expuestas a la luz del sol.5 Además, la exposición al sol aumenta los niveles de óxido nítrico en nuestro cuerpo. Esto ayuda a dilatar los vasos sanguíneos, reducir la presión arterial y es una sustancia beneficiosa para el corazón.

Como con todas las cosas que he mencionado, la clave es la moderación. La exposición excesiva al sol caliente puede causar insolación, y demasiada luz ultravioleta daña las células de la piel, lo que puede provocar quemaduras e incluso cánceres de piel.

Suplementos específicos

Los suplementos pueden ser útiles para cubrir las carencias de nuestra dieta o las situaciones en las que nuestro cuerpo simplemente no absorbe tanto de algo como debería.

La vitamina D es una de las primeras que me viene a la mente, ya que sabemos que los niveles bajos de vitamina D aumentan el riesgo de infecciones graves. En realidad, nuestro cuerpo no sabe de dónde procede la vitamina D. Aunque probablemente lo mejor sea obtenerla de una combinación de alimentos y exposición al sol, los suplementos de vitamina D pueden ser útiles para las personas mayores o para cualquiera que tenga dificultades para conseguirlo.6

Se ha demostrado que el zinc reduce (a corto plazo) la duración de los resfriados. En este caso, advertiría que no está pensado para tomarse todos los días, sino que conviene tomar más al primer síntoma de una infección de las vías respiratorias superiores. No es un suplemento milagroso y, según los estudios, solo redujo la duración de los síntomas del resfriado alrededor de un día.7

La vitamina C es otra cosa que muchas personas toman cuando sienten que se acerca un resfriado. Los estudios parecen indicar que se tolera bien y es eficaz.8 Probablemente lo mejor sea obtener la mayor parte de la vitamina C de la dieta y añadir más vitamina C solo cuando empiece a sentir síntomas de infección.

Hay muchos otros suplementos que la gente toma; estos son solo tres de los más comunes.

Dios creó nuestro cuerpo con varios sistemas diferentes. Estos sistemas curan las lesiones, mantienen nuestro cuerpo y lo protegen de un mundo dañado por la introducción del pecado en la Caída del hombre, en el jardín del Edén. En verdad, somos hechos de manera asombrosa y maravillosa. Estos sistemas funcionan sin que siquiera pensemos en ellos.

Es importante que seamos conscientes de las maneras en que podemos ayudar a estas células y estructuras maravillosamente diseñadas, y no obstaculizarlas, pues impiden que organismos dañinos entren en nuestro cuerpo y causen infecciones. No se trata de que llevar una vida saludable o ser hijo de Dios nos impida enfermar alguna vez, sino de que tomar conscientemente la decisión de seguir el camino correcto mejorará el funcionamiento de nuestro cuerpo. Creo que, si gozamos de buena salud, nos será más fácil cumplir nuestra misión: llegar al mundo que nos rodea con el mensaje del Evangelio.

One Sunday morning a little girl, whom we will call Jennika, woke up to the sun shining into her bedroom. She dressed in her Sunday dress just like she did every other Sunday morning. This Sunday morning was quite different, though. While she was sitting at the breakfast table waiting for her mom to fill her plate, her mom’s chest suddenly started hurting very badly. It hurt so badly, she had to go lie on the couch. Jennika felt scared. She didn’t know what was going to happen. About ten minutes later, her dad took her mom to the hospital. Later that afternoon, she and her siblings heard that their mom had suffered a heart attack.

The next Wednesday evening, her dad asked, “Jennika, would you like to go along to the hospital tomorrow to see Mom?”

“Yes!” she beamed.

The next morning after breakfast, her older sister and baby brother went with her and her dad to the hospital. That day she had lots of fun. She enjoyed looking out the window of the waiting room and watching the helicopters take off and land. One time she even saw an ambulance come with its lights and sirens on. That was exciting! One time she almost got lost in the halls, but one of her mom’s nurses saw her and showed her the right room.

That night she was going to spend the night with her mom. She was so excited! She thought sleeping on the chair in her mom’s room would be fun. Her mom was going to ask the nurses for a pillow and some blankets. About fifteen minutes after her dad left, a nurse came in and said she couldn’t spend the night there after all! Her dad needed to come back to pick her up. She was so disappointed! She cried almost the whole way home. That night they dropped off her two-week-old brother at one of the church families to give her older sisters a break from taking care of him.

The next day she had a wonderful surprise. First, her cousins, who lived about three hours away, came to visit. And she found out that her mom was going to come home that day! She helped her siblings decorate the house. Her older sister made two welcome-home signs for inside the house and her older brother made one for out by the driveway.

“Mom is home!” yelled her younger brother when he saw the car pull up outside the house. Jennika and her siblings dashed to the front door. They led their mom to her favorite recliner which was close to the air conditioner that their uncle had just installed that morning.

That evening Jennika snuggled up to her mom. “I’m glad you’re home,” she whispered. “I like it when you’re home.” Because her mom had been gone so long, Jennika learned to be more thankful for her mom.

Jennika is older now and is still very thankful for her mom. Maybe your mom didn’t need to be in the hospital for a week, but you should still be thankful for her. Don’t forget to tell her!

Een Sondagoggend het ’n dogtertjie, wat ons Jennika sal noem, wakker geword terwyl die son by haar slaapkamer inskyn. Sy het haar Sondagrok aangetrek, net soos sy elke ander Sondagoggend gedoen het. Maar hierdie Sondagoggend was heeltemal anders. Terwyl sy by die ontbyttafel gesit en wag het dat haar ma haar bord vol skep, het haar ma se bors skielik baie seer begin kry. Dit was so seer dat sy op die rusbank moes gaan lê. Jennika het bang gevoel. Sy het nie geweet wat gaan gebeur nie. Sowat tien minute later het haar pa haar ma hospitaal toe geneem. Later daardie middag het sy en haar sibbe gehoor dat hulle ma ’n hartaanval gehad het.

Die volgende Woensdagaand het haar pa gevra: “Jennika, wil jy môre saam hospitaal toe gaan om vir Ma te sien?”

“Ja!” het sy stralend geantwoord.

Die volgende oggend ná ontbyt het haar ouer suster en kleinboet saam met haar en haar pa hospitaal toe gegaan. Daardie dag het sy baie pret gehad. Sy het dit geniet om by die venster van die wagkamer uit te kyk en die helikopters dop te hou terwyl hulle opstyg en land. Een keer het sy selfs ’n ambulans met sy ligte aan en sirene wat loei, sien aankom. Dit was opwindend! Een keer het sy amper in die gange verdwaal, maar een van haar ma se verpleegsters het haar gesien en vir haar die regte kamer gewys.

Daardie aand sou sy by haar ma oorslaap. Sy was so opgewonde! Sy het gedink dit sou lekker wees om op die stoel in haar ma se kamer te slaap. Haar ma sou die verpleegsters vir ’n kussing en ’n paar komberse vra. Sowat vyftien minute nadat haar pa vertrek het, het ’n verpleegster ingekom en gesê dat sy tog nie daar kon oorslaap nie! Haar pa moes terugkom om haar te kom haal. Sy was so teleurgesteld! Sy het amper die hele pad huis toe gehuil. Daardie aand het hulle haar twee weke oue boetie by een van die kerkgesinne afgelaai sodat haar ouer susters ’n ruskans kon kry van die sorg vir hom.

Die volgende dag het sy ’n wonderlike verrassing gehad. Eers het haar neefs en niggies, wat sowat drie uur ver gewoon het, kom kuier. En sy het uitgevind dat haar ma daardie dag huis toe sou kom! Sy het haar sibbe gehelp om die huis te versier. Haar ouer suster het twee “Welkom tuis”-plakkate vir binne-in die huis gemaak, en haar ouer broer het een gemaak vir buite, by die oprit.

“Ma is tuis!” het haar jonger broer geskree toe hy die motor buite die huis sien stilhou. Jennika en haar sibbe het na die voordeur gehardloop. Hulle het hulle ma na haar gunsteling-leunstoel geneem, wat naby die lugversorger was wat hulle oom daardie oggend pas geïnstalleer het.

Daardie aand het Jennika styf teen haar ma gekruip. “Ek is bly jy is tuis,” het sy gefluister. “Ek hou daarvan as jy tuis is.” Omdat haar ma so lank weg was, het Jennika geleer om meer dankbaar vir haar ma te wees.

Jennika is nou ouer en is steeds baie dankbaar vir haar ma. Miskien hoef jou ma nie ’n week lank in die hospitaal te wees nie, maar jy behoort steeds dankbaar vir haar te wees. Moenie vergeet om dit vir haar te sê nie!

One Sunday morning a little girl, whom we will call Jennika, woke up to the sun shining into her bedroom. She dressed in her Sunday dress just like she did every other Sunday morning. This Sunday morning was quite different, though. While she was sitting at the breakfast table waiting for her mom to fill her plate, her mom’s chest suddenly started hurting very badly. It hurt so badly, she had to go lie on the couch. Jennika felt scared. She didn’t know what was going to happen. About ten minutes later, her dad took her mom to the hospital. Later that afternoon, she and her siblings heard that their mom had suffered a heart attack.

The next Wednesday evening, her dad asked, “Jennika, would you like to go along to the hospital tomorrow to see Mom?”

“Yes!” she beamed.

The next morning after breakfast, her older sister and baby brother went with her and her dad to the hospital. That day she had lots of fun. She enjoyed looking out the window of the waiting room and watching the helicopters take off and land. One time she even saw an ambulance come with its lights and sirens on. That was exciting! One time she almost got lost in the halls, but one of her mom’s nurses saw her and showed her the right room.

That night she was going to spend the night with her mom. She was so excited! She thought sleeping on the chair in her mom’s room would be fun. Her mom was going to ask the nurses for a pillow and some blankets. About fifteen minutes after her dad left, a nurse came in and said she couldn’t spend the night there after all! Her dad needed to come back to pick her up. She was so disappointed! She cried almost the whole way home. That night they dropped off her two-week-old brother at one of the church families to give her older sisters a break from taking care of him.

The next day she had a wonderful surprise. First, her cousins, who lived about three hours away, came to visit. And she found out that her mom was going to come home that day! She helped her siblings decorate the house. Her older sister made two welcome-home signs for inside the house and her older brother made one for out by the driveway.

“Mom is home!” yelled her younger brother when he saw the car pull up outside the house. Jennika and her siblings dashed to the front door. They led their mom to her favorite recliner which was close to the air conditioner that their uncle had just installed that morning.

That evening Jennika snuggled up to her mom. “I’m glad you’re home,” she whispered. “I like it when you’re home.” Because her mom had been gone so long, Jennika learned to be more thankful for her mom.

Jennika is older now and is still very thankful for her mom. Maybe your mom didn’t need to be in the hospital for a week, but you should still be thankful for her. Don’t forget to tell her!
