من الأمور التي لاحظتها مرارًا وأنا أقرأ كلمة الله أن شعب الله واثقون. تأملوا نوحًا. حين أمره الله ببناء فلك، لم يتردد. أمضى السنوات المئة والعشرين التالية واثقًا يفعل ذلك بعينه. ثم أفكر في إبراهيم، الذي فعل بثقة كل ما طلبه الله منه، حتى حين طلب منه أن يذبح ابنه الوحيد. ولا يمكننا أن نتحدث عن الثقة دون أن نذكر كالب ويشوع، اللذين، بعد أن سمعا تقارير الشك التي أدلى بها جميع رفاقهما، وصفا بثقة ما ينبغي أن يفعلوه بهذه الأرض الجديدة، أرض كنعان: ...لنصعد حالًا ونمتلكها، لأننا قادرون عليها جدًا –العدد 13:30.

لا يمكننا أن ننسى داود الذي خرج وأسكت المعترض الأكبر—جليات. ولا يمكننا أن ننسى دانيال وجدعون وأيوب وحزقيال وإشعياء وإرميا، وكل ما فعلوه بثقة. ونحن ندرس كل واحد من هؤلاء الرجال المؤمنين وكثيرين غيرهم، نرى بوضوح أن لديهم ثقة عظيمة بإلههم!

قد يقول بعضهم إنه لو عمل الله اليوم بالطريقة نفسها التي عمل بها آنذاك، لكان لدينا مزيد من الثقة. وربما لو ظل الله إله العهد القديم، لكان الأمر أسهل. فلو قادنا إلى المعركة، ودمر أعداءنا، وشق البحار، وأنزل الخبز من السماء، لكانت ثقتنا به أكبر.

والآن لنتأمل العهد الجديد. إنه مختلف تمامًا. يُؤمر شعب الله أن يترك كل شيء من أجل المسيح. ويُوعَدون بأن العالم سيبغضهم. ويقال لهم إنه من العسير على الغني أن يدخل ملكوت الله. ويُؤكَّد لهم أنهم مباركون إن تألموا، وإن كانوا فقراء، أو جياعًا، أو نائحين.

هل يستطيع الناس أن يظلوا واثقين بإله يطلب من شعبه أن يتبعه في مثل هذه الظروف؟ نعم! لقد أثبت التلاميذ ذلك. كانوا يكرزون ويعلّمون. وطوردوا وضُربوا مرارًا. وأظهر استفانوس الشماس ثقة عظيمة حين أُحضر أمام مضطهديه، حتى عندما أخذوا يصرّون بأسنانهم عليه ويرجمونه. وأظهر استفانوس الثقة حتى لفظ آخر أنفاسه المعذبة.

قبل أن يصبح الرسول بولس، كان شاول عدوًا للصليب، ورئيس الخطاة، وفريسيًا ابن فريسيين. كان رجلًا بارزًا، تتلمذ على أيدي أفضل المعلمين. ثم التقى بالله الحي، فتغير كل شيء. بعد أن اعتمد بولس، ...وللوقت جعل يكرز في المجامع بالمسيح أن هذا هو ابن الله –أعمال الرسل 9:20. وتقول الآية التالية إن الناس اندهشوا، ثم في الآية 23، أي بعد خمس آيات من معموديته، تقول إن اليهود تشاوروا ليقتلوه.

إن تغيير رجل كهذا، وجعله يبدل ولاءه بالكامل بين عشية وضحاها، يتطلب ثقة كبيرة بالله. وبحسب شهادته هو، ظل بولس أمينًا حتى موته: فإني الآن أُسكب سكيبًا، ووقت انحلالي قد حضر. قد جاهدت الجهاد الحسن، أكملت السعي، حفظت الإيمان –تيموثاوس الثانية 4:6-7.

صنع الله أمورًا عجيبة في العهد الجديد. شفى العميان وأقام الموتى من جديد. أطلق السجناء وضرب أناسًا بالموت. وقد يقول البعض إن الثقة العظيمة بالله ستكون أيسر لو كنا لا نزال نعيش في الأزمنة الكتابية للعهد الجديد، حين كان يسوع يمشي ويتكلم هنا على الأرض بجسده.

وماذا بعد الكتاب المقدس؟

نرى مرة أخرى في الكنيسة الأولى جماعة من الناس لم يتزعزعوا؛ فقد وثقوا بإلههم الذي لم يستطيعوا أن يروه. وقف عشرات الآلاف من شعب الله أمام العالم بجرأة وأعلنوا شروره، وقُتل عشرات الآلاف من شعب الله. ولم يشك أحد قط في ثقة هؤلاء الناس. ودُعوا حمقى لأنهم آمنوا بـ«إله لم يستطيعوا أن يروه». وسُخر منهم واحتُقروا بسبب «حماقتهم»، و...قُتلنا كل النهار... –المزامير 44:22. شكك الناس في ممارساتهم، وشككوا في بنية جماعتهم الدينية، وشككوا في الرسالة التي كرزوا بها، وشككوا في أمور كثيرة، لكنهم لم يشككوا قط في ثقتهم. لقد آمن هؤلاء المسيحيون بإلههم، ولم يكن في ذلك أي شك.

والغريب أنهم لم يهتموا بملذات هذه الحياة؛ ولم يكترثوا بأمور هذا العالم، بل إن حياتهم ذاتها كانت أمرًا يسيرًا يضحّون به من أجل إلههم. تمزقت عائلات، وصودرت بيوت وأراضٍ، وأُحرقت كنائس، لكن ذلك لم يثنهم ولم يوقفهم. عاشوا من أجل أمر أعظم، أمر لم يستطع الوثنيون فهمه.

خلال زمن الكنيسة الأولى وعصر الإصلاح، انضم أناس إلى الملكوت بأعداد كبيرة. نعم، نشأ أطفال وانضموا إلى كنائس آبائهم، لكن جموعًا غفيرة من المهتدين الجدد جاءت أيضًا من العالم. كيف أمكن إقناع إنسان دنيوي بالانضمام إلى جماعة تُطارد وتُقتل—جماعة تتألم كما تألمت كنيسة يسوع المسيح؟ نعم، نعلم أن الخلاص من الرب، لكن ثقة شعب الله هي التي جعلت الآخرين يتساءلون، وهي التي دفعتهم إلى التفكير جديًا في هذا الدين الجديد الذي يعتنقه الهراطقة. كانت تلك جماعة من الناس تقبل عن طيب خاطر نهب ممتلكاتها، وتفرح ببذل كل ما لديها لمساعدة الآخرين، ولا تقاوم حين تقبض عليها السلطات. كانت كنيسة يسوع المسيح الحقيقية جماعةً تجعل الآخرين يتساءلون دائمًا: «من هؤلاء الناس؟» لقد وضعوا كل إيمانهم بإلههم بوضوح، ولم يكن ذلك أمرًا شائعًا. وقفوا دفاعًا عن حق الله مهما اشتدت نار الأتون، ومهما جعلوا حياتهم بائسة. وكل ذلك أظهر ثقة عظيمة، لا بأنفسهم، بل بإلههم.

حين ننظر إلى الكنيسة اليوم، ماذا نرى؟ بعض شعب الله يحملون صلبانهم وينكرون العالم وشهوته، وآخرون لا يفعلون. فهل ما زالت كنيسة اليوم معروفة بثقتها بإلهها؟

نحن الذين نعترف بأننا مسيحيون، هل فقدنا شيئًا من هذه الثقة الكتابية؟ هل ما زلنا نخدم الإله الواحد الحق بلا لبس؟ هل ينظر إلينا الناس ويقفون مبهوتين أمام الثقة التي نظهرها بإلهنا؟ يقول كثيرون جدًا اليوم إنهم مسيحيون، لكنهم لا يُظهرون إلا القليل من الثقة بالله. إنهم يعيشون قريبًا جدًا من أساليب العالم. فبدلًا من الابتهاج بالاضطهاد، يستمتعون بكثير من الأمور نفسها التي يستمتع بها العالم. يحتاج كل واحد منا إلى نار الله المتقدة عميقًا في قلوبنا، نار لا يمكن إخمادها.

الثقة تعني الطاعة. لقد قابلت كثيرًا من مسيحيي أيامنا هذه كان أسلافهم قد بذلوا حياتهم من أجل المسيح، وكان أجدادهم يقودون الكنيسة بشجاعة، لكن يبدو الآن أن شيئًا ما مفقود. وأنا أتفاعل مع كثير من المسيحيين المتقين لله، يبدو أن هناك صراعًا سائدًا بشأن الثقة—الثقة بإله حي كلي القدرة، كلي العلم، حاضر في كل مكان.

في ظل ما يسود عالمنا اليوم من عدم يقين، علينا أن نعلن رسالة الإنجيل بجرأة من جديد، كما فعل المؤمنون الحقيقيون في الأزمنة الماضية. علينا أن نرسم بوضوح خطوطًا كتابية فاصلة بين الصواب والخطأ. علينا أن نتخلص من كل هذه المناطق الرمادية البغيضة وأن نسمي الخطية خطية. يبدو أننا فقدنا الثقة في المجاهرة ضد خطية عصرنا. إذا أعلنا بثقة ما أعلنه الله، فلن يحبنا بعض الناس. نحتاج إلى إخوة لا يخافون أن يُسخر منهم، ومستعدين لسلوك الطريق الأقل ارتيادًا.

قبيل صعود ربنا إلى العلاء، أعطى تلاميذه وعدًا مجيدًا: ...لكنكم ستنالون قوة متى حل الروح القدس عليكم، وتكونون لي شهودًا في أورشليم وفي كل اليهودية والسامرة وإلى أقصى الأرض –أعمال الرسل 1:8.

ستنـالون قوة! ليست قوة من الناس، ولا من ممالك هذا العالم، بل قوة حقيقية غالبة—قوة لا تأتي إلا من الروح القدس! بعد أن ننال هذه القوة، نمضي إلى الأمام خليقة جديدة، معلنين بثقة إنجيل فادينا المبارك.

نحتاج إلى قلوب تتقد بمشيئة الله وكلمته. نحتاج إلى قلوب ملتهبة!

كنت أتناول الغداء ذات يوم حين اقترب مني زوجان وسألاني سؤالًا جادًا: «لماذا تظن الكنيسة أنها مضطرة إلى السيطرة علينا؟» وبعد أن شرحا كيف يعتقدان أنه ينبغي أن يكونا «حرين في المسيح»، تحمست للإجابة عن أسئلتهما. لكن كان يجلس إلى جانبي أخ آخر مرسوم. فقررت الانتظار، آملًا أن يتحدث إلى الزوجين، لكنه لم يقل شيئًا. وبعد أن مرّت خمس وأربعون دقيقة أخرى، حاولت أن أوضح للزوجين أنهما بحاجة إلى إنكار ذواتهما والخضوع للكنيسة. وأنهما إذا بذلا حياتيهما بالكامل، وإذا سلّما كل شيء، فلن يعودا يعانيان هذا الصراع مع نظام الكنيسة.

بدا الزوجان مشجَّعين ومستعدين لمنح الأمر فرصة أخرى. لكن الخادم الجالس إلى جانبي لم يبدُ راضيًا، فسألته عن رأيه. قال إن أباه أخبره قبل سنوات أنه حين كان شابًا ظن أن لديه كل الإجابات. وبعد أن كبر، أدرك أنه لا يعرف شيئًا، وأن قضايا الكنيسة أعقد من أن تُحل. وعلينا ببساطة أن نحاول التعايش.

أهذه هي الإجابة، أن نتصرف كأننا لا نعرف شيئًا ونأمل أن تسير الأمور كلها على ما يرام في النهاية؟ أفهم أننا لا نملك كل الإجابات. ففي نهاية المطاف، أدرك أن أسئلتي في معظم الأحيان أكثر من إجاباتي. لكنني أعرف ما يريده الله لكنيسته! ...أحب المسيح أيضًا الكنيسة وأسلم نفسه لأجلها، لكي يقدسها مطهرًا إياها بغسل الماء بالكلمة، لكي يحضرها لنفسه كنيسة مجيدة، لا دنس فيها ولا غضن أو شيء من مثل ذلك، بل تكون مقدسة وبلا عيب –أفسس 5:25-27.

كنيسة مجيدة، لا دنس فيها ولا غضن أو شيء من مثل ذلك، بل تكون مقدسة وبلا عيب! فهل نقف نحن، شعب الله، من جديد من أجل الحق، وننكر العالم، ونسمح لأنفسنا كالغنم أن نُساق إلى الذبح؟ أم جعلنا حياتنا مريحة أكثر مما ينبغي لكي ننكر ذواتنا، واخترنا الطريق السهل (الواسع) وأنكرنا الطريق المستقيم والضيق؟ هل عقدنا اتفاق سلام مع خدام الخطية؟ إذا كنت أبكي وأنا أكتب، فهل ستبكون وأنتم تقرأون؟

تعريف كلمة الثقة هو شعور المرء بقدراته أو إدراكه لها. لقد خلط كثيرون اليوم بين الثقة والكبرياء، ولسبب وجيه. فمعظم الواثقين يثقون بأنفسهم بدلًا من أن يثقوا بالمسيح. ونرى هذه الثقة بالنفس في كل مكان حولنا. فهناك مدربو حياة ومستشارون في أنحاء العالم، يحثون الناس على الإيمان بأنفسهم، ويقولون لهم أن يثقوا بأنفسهم. وغالبًا ما يصبح المرء متكبرًا حين يثق بنفسه. تذكروا أن العالم لا يستهجن الكبرياء. يمكنكم أن تسمعوا العالم يتباهى بكبريائه أينما نظرتم. فالناس يفتخرون بأولادهم، وبلادهم، وفريقهم الرياضي المفضل، ومروجهم، وبكل شيء جيد في حياتهم تقريبًا. يجب ألا ننسى أن الكبرياء خطية، ولن يدخل السماء. صحيح أن الثقة بالنفس أو بالأشياء هي كبرياء، أما الثقة بالله فليست كذلك!

ليس الخلط بين الثقة بالله والكبرياء فكرة جديدة. قال أليآب، أخو داود الأكبر، له: «أنا عرفت كبرياءك». هل كان داود متكبرًا؟ لا، بل كان يثق بإلهه ثقة عظيمة.

هل يمكن أن يكون شعور زائف بالتواضع قد أسكت الكنيسة؟ هل يمكن أن تكون هذه الحيلة التي يستخدمها العدو أحد أسلحة الشيطان الحالية ضد المسيحيين؟ وهل يمكن أن يكون هذا أيضًا سبب معاناة الكنيسة في جميع أنحاء العالم؟ ماذا لو خرج الرجال الأمناء من جديد بالإيمان بإلههم وبثقة عظيمة، وأروا هذا العالم الملطخ بالخطية، بأقوالهم وأفعالهم، الطريق المستقيم والضيق—إلى ملكوت الله؟!

علينا جميعًا أن نتفق على أننا نعيش في عالم مرتبك—مرتبك بشأن الصواب والخطأ. ماذا لو استطاع العالم أن ينظر إلى الكنيسة فيجد مرة أخرى جماعة من الناس تعرف تمامًا إلى أين تتجه—كنيسة لا تشك في الطريق الصحيح—كنيسة تستطيع أن تعلن بجرأة جواب مشكلات عصرنا—كنيسة لا تقل عن كونها واثقة تمامًا بإلهها؟

لنتقدم إلى إلهنا ساجدين على ركبنا، مطأطئي القلوب، ومظهرين حزنًا تقويًا صادقًا على ضلالنا. ولنطلب بإخلاص مشيئة الله لأنفسنا، ولعائلاتنا، وكنائسنا، وجيراننا. ولنطلب من الله أن يرينا كيف نكون أمثلة له أمام العالم المحيط بنا. روح السيد الرب عليّ، لأن الرب مسحني لأبشر المساكين، أرسلني لأعصب منكسري القلب، لأنادي للمسبيين بالعتق، وللمأسورين بالإطلاق، لأنادي بسنة الرب المقبولة، وبيوم انتقام لإلهنا، لأعزي كل النائحين، لأجعل لنائحي صهيون، لأعطيهم جمالًا عوضًا عن الرماد، ودهن فرح عوضًا عن النوح، ورداء تسبيح عوضًا عن الروح اليائسة، فيُدعون أشجار البر، غرس الرب للتمجيد –إشعياء 61:1-3.

“How is the new curriculum selling?” Sandra asked, wrapping her hands around her mug of coffee.

“It’s slow,” Abby answered. “I need to do more advertising, but now that the product is finished, I find it difficult to promote.”

“What’s wrong?” Sandra asked. Abby had spent years developing a curriculum for special needs children. Her passion and dedication to the project was amazing, but now her zeal seemed stifled.

“Well,” Abby said slowly. “I feel like my co-worker constantly criticizes me. ‘The cover design is tacky, there is a misspelling on page 11’, I should have said this, this, and this. My project advisor wants me to work on advertising, but every time I move forward, she tells me I did something wrong.”

“Does it feel like jealousy?” Sandra asked.

“I hadn’t thought of that. I’m staying in the background, but that’s not helping. I feel crippled and I don’t know what to do.”

Sandra nodded. “It’s difficult to be the recipient of another person’s jealousy. But it’s worse to be the one who’s jealous. I’ve been there. It’s miserable.”

“How did you work through it?” Abby asked. “You don’t seem like a jealous person now.”

“It was one point in a message,” Sandra answered. “The minister said, ‘If you feel critical toward someone who is rejoicing, likely you are struggling with jealousy.’ I don’t remember anything else he said,” Sandra chucked, “but, I knew he had identified my problem. I often found it hard to be happy for my peers. I didn’t realize jealousy was my root problem.”

“That makes sense,” replied Abby.

“It is harder for jealousy to take root if I face the negative thoughts right away,” Sandra replied. “It’s a battle worth fighting. I am happier when I can ‘rejoice with them that do rejoice,’ like the Bible says to do.”

“Maybe my co-worker is dealing with negative thoughts about the success more that feeling annoyed at me,” mused Abby.

“That’s likely true,” replied Sandra. “Aim to put her fears to rest so that you can work together productively. Don’t react to her behavior.”

Like Sandra, I too, have had critical thoughts when peers shared good news, or I noticed their accomplishments. Unless checked immediately, that tinge of jealousy keeps me from being happy for others.

The Bible describes the brutality of envy and jealousy. Jealousy is as cruel as the grave. (see Song of Solomon 8:6). Envy [is] the rottenness of the bones –Proverbs 14:30. And, Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy? –Proverbs 27:4. Jealousy is extremely subtle. It can be covered with an aura of godliness. Not only does it have the potential to destroy my relationships now, but also those of my children and grandchildren.

Women don’t decide to be jealous. They don’t say, “Today I’m going to be jealous.” Often, it’s hard to pinpoint when jealousy enters the heart, or even if it is there. But if it is hard to be happy for others, maybe it’s time to search our souls. We are prepared to fight against jealousy when we understand how and where jealousy thrives—within the heart of each of us.

Peers Test Our Rejoicing

Generally, we aren’t envious of people that we’re not close to. Women all around the world get married, have babies, or move into a new house, and we scarcely notice. But it’s hard to rejoice when those near us in time, place, age, or reputation enjoy blessings that we wish for. More than once, a jubilant phone call announcing a milestone challenged my resolve to rejoice with a rejoicing friend. God understands the struggle and He leads me to rest and acceptance.

Recognize Jealousy

The definition of jealous is: ‘Feeling or showing envy of someone or their achievements and advantages.’ Jealousy pops up in many ways, such as craving to copy a peer. Jealousy belittles the achievements of another and tries to control the way others think of that person. Jealousy gloats about the distresses and failures of others, while basking in a spiritual bubble. Jealous people keep the rumor mill in full production by feeding it twisted truths.

Safeguard Your Thoughts

Jealousy starts in the mind. Dwelling on a suspicion or envying another person distorts truth. This is dangerous, because what you perceive as a truth, is a lie.

We decide someone is proud because they brought a beautiful dessert to a potluck. Or we think a sister is a negligent homemaker because she visited a woman at a nursing home. Why? We tend to judge others by our own motives. Isn’t it feelings of guilt, self-justification, or envy that cause us to heap a negligent title on someone who is visiting the elderly? We don’t know how long she thought about that visit or how her husband made it possible. Divisive thoughts converted into words wreak havoc among godly women. It causes extra work for church leaders and stunts the growth of a body of believers.

Embrace The Thought: “Life Isn’t Fair”

Sometimes someone will have something you desire. On the flipside, there are times you will have something another woman wishes for. “Life isn’t fair” is a fact of life that we cannot change; we can only adjust our attitude.

There were friends in the same church who each had a daughter of dating age. As life would have it, one daughter dated and married long before the other one began a courtship. The mother of the single girl determined that she would rejoice with her friend and her daughter. As a result, the mothers are still friends, the girls are friends, and it’s likely their children will be friends.

Count Your Own Blessings

Looking at the blessings of others and making comparisons makes it difficult to be happy and satisfied. The Apostle Paul warns of this: …but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise –2 Corinthians 10:12. Happiness will not come to women who neglect to appreciate what they already have. Neither will they happily rejoice with those who rejoice.

Know Who You Are In Christ

Jealousy stems from feelings of fear and insecurity. God created you for His honor and glory. There isn’t a need for competition, rather we ought to be content in knowing who we are in Jesus. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them –Ephesians 2:8-10.

Have Friends, Not Rivals

We might hesitate to admit that we have a rival, but that’s what a friend will become if we aren’t able to celebrate the blessings in her life. Pray for her regularly, asking God to bless her. Letting go of suspicion and doing something nice for her will help dissipate the negative feelings you have developed.

The Scripture is clear about enmity toward our brother (or sister): He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now. He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him. But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes –1 John 2:9-11.

Replace Jealousy With Gratitude And Contentment

Negative thoughts come without invitation, but we can decide if they will stay or leave. Learn to redirect your attention to truth. Philippians gives us an excellent blueprint: Finally, brethren [sisters], whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things –Philippians 4:8.

When we are at peace with God, with ourselves, and with our fellow women, we will be content with our abilities and with the circumstances in which God has placed us. With our focus on God, we will find joy and the power to rejoice with them that rejoice.

«Come sta andando la vendita del nuovo programma didattico?» chiese Sandra, stringendo la tazza di caffè tra le mani.

«A rilento», rispose Abby. «Dovrei fare più pubblicità, ma ora che il prodotto è pronto, faccio fatica a promuoverlo.»

«Che cosa c’è che non va?» chiese Sandra. Abby aveva trascorso anni a sviluppare un programma didattico per bambini con bisogni speciali. La sua passione e dedizione al progetto erano straordinarie, ma ora il suo entusiasmo sembrava soffocato.

«Beh», disse Abby lentamente. «Mi sembra che la mia collega mi critichi continuamente. “Il design della copertina è pacchiano, a pagina 11 c’è un errore di ortografia”; avrei dovuto dire questo, questo e quest’altro. La mia consulente per il progetto vuole che mi occupi della pubblicità, ma ogni volta che faccio un passo avanti, mi dice che ho sbagliato qualcosa.»

«Ti sembra che sia gelosia?» chiese Sandra.

«Non ci avevo pensato. Rimango sullo sfondo, ma questo non aiuta. Mi sento paralizzata e non so cosa fare.»

Sandra annuì. «È difficile essere il bersaglio della gelosia di un’altra persona. Ma è peggio essere quella gelosa. Ci sono passata. È terribile.»

«Come hai fatto a superarla?» chiese Abby. «Adesso non sembri una persona gelosa.»

«Era un punto di un sermone», rispose Sandra. «Il ministro disse: “Se provi un atteggiamento critico verso qualcuno che gioisce, probabilmente stai lottando contro la gelosia”. Non ricordo nient’altro di quello che disse», ridacchiò Sandra, «ma sapevo che aveva individuato il mio problema. Spesso facevo fatica a essere felice per le mie coetanee. Non mi rendevo conto che la gelosia fosse il problema alla radice.»

«Ha senso», rispose Abby.

«È più difficile che la gelosia metta radici se affronto subito i pensieri negativi», rispose Sandra. «È una battaglia che vale la pena combattere. Sono più felice quando riesco a “rallegrarmi con quelli che si rallegrano”, come dice la Bibbia.»

«Forse la mia collega sta lottando con pensieri negativi sul successo, più che sentirsi infastidita da me», rifletté Abby.

«Probabilmente è così», rispose Sandra. «Cerca di dissipare le sue paure, così potrete collaborare in modo produttivo. Non reagire al suo comportamento.»

Come Sandra, anch’io ho avuto pensieri critici quando le mie coetanee condividevano buone notizie o notavo i loro successi. Se non viene contrastata subito, quella punta di gelosia mi impedisce di essere felice per gli altri.

La Bibbia descrive la crudeltà dell’invidia e della gelosia. La gelosia è crudele come il sepolcro (vedi Cantico dei Cantici 8:6). L’invidia [è] la carie delle ossa –Proverbi 14:30. E ancora: L’ira è crudele, e la collera è impetuosa; ma chi può resistere davanti all’invidia? –Proverbi 27:4. La gelosia è estremamente subdola. Può celarsi sotto un’aura di pietà. Non solo può distruggere le mie relazioni di oggi, ma anche quelle dei miei figli e dei miei nipoti.

Le donne non decidono di essere gelose. Non dicono: «Oggi sarò gelosa». Spesso è difficile individuare quando la gelosia entra nel cuore, o persino capire se sia presente. Ma se facciamo fatica a essere felici per gli altri, forse è il momento di esaminare la nostra anima. Siamo pronte a combattere la gelosia quando comprendiamo come e dove essa prospera: nel cuore di ciascuna di noi.

Le coetanee mettono alla prova la nostra capacità di rallegrarci

In genere, non proviamo invidia per le persone con cui non abbiamo un rapporto stretto. Donne di tutto il mondo si sposano, hanno figli o si trasferiscono in una casa nuova, e a malapena ce ne accorgiamo. Ma è difficile rallegrarsi quando persone vicine a noi per età, luogo, periodo della vita o reputazione ricevono benedizioni che desideriamo. Più di una volta, una telefonata gioiosa che annunciava un traguardo ha messo alla prova la mia determinazione a rallegrarmi con un’amica che gioiva. Dio comprende la lotta e mi guida verso il riposo e l’accettazione.

Riconoscere la gelosia

La definizione di geloso è: «Che prova o manifesta invidia per qualcuno, per i suoi successi o vantaggi». La gelosia si manifesta in molti modi, come desiderare di imitare una coetanea. La gelosia sminuisce i successi altrui e cerca di controllare il modo in cui gli altri vedono quella persona. La gelosia si compiace delle sofferenze e dei fallimenti altrui, mentre si crogiola in una bolla spirituale. Le persone gelose tengono in piena attività la macchina dei pettegolezzi, alimentandola con verità distorte.

Custodisci i tuoi pensieri

La gelosia comincia nella mente. Rimuginare su un sospetto o invidiare un’altra persona distorce la verità. È pericoloso, perché ciò che percepisci come vero è una menzogna.

Decidiamo che qualcuno è orgoglioso perché ha portato un bel dolce a una cena condivisa. Oppure pensiamo che una sorella sia una casalinga negligente perché ha fatto visita a una donna in una casa di riposo. Perché? Tendiamo a giudicare gli altri in base alle nostre motivazioni. Non sono forse il senso di colpa, l’autogiustificazione o l’invidia a spingerci ad appiccicare l’etichetta di negligente a chi fa visita agli anziani? Non sappiamo da quanto tempo pensasse a quella visita né come suo marito l’abbia resa possibile. I pensieri divisivi, quando si trasformano in parole, seminano il caos tra donne devote a Dio. Ciò crea lavoro aggiuntivo per i responsabili della chiesa e ostacola la crescita della comunità dei credenti.

Accogli questo pensiero: «La vita non è giusta»

A volte qualcuno avrà qualcosa che desideri. D’altra parte, capiterà che tu abbia qualcosa che un’altra donna desidera. «La vita non è giusta» è una realtà che non possiamo cambiare; possiamo solo modificare il nostro atteggiamento.

C’erano due amiche nella stessa chiesa, ciascuna con una figlia in età da fidanzamento. Come spesso accade nella vita, una delle figlie si fidanzò e si sposò molto prima che l’altra iniziasse a frequentare qualcuno. La madre della ragazza ancora single decise che si sarebbe rallegrata con l’amica e sua figlia. Di conseguenza, le madri sono ancora amiche, le ragazze sono amiche ed è probabile che anche i loro figli saranno amici.

Conta le tue benedizioni

Guardare alle benedizioni altrui e fare paragoni rende difficile essere felici e soddisfatte. L’apostolo Paolo ci mette in guardia: …ma essi, misurandosi secondo la propria misura e paragonandosi fra loro, non hanno giudizio –2 Corinzi 10:12. Le donne che trascurano di apprezzare ciò che già hanno non troveranno la felicità. E non si rallegreranno con chi gioisce.

Sappi chi sei in Cristo

La gelosia nasce da sentimenti di paura e insicurezza. Dio ti ha creata per il suo onore e la sua gloria. Non c’è bisogno di competere; dovremmo invece essere contente di sapere chi siamo in Gesù. Infatti è per grazia che siete stati salvati, mediante la fede; e ciò non viene da voi, è il dono di Dio. Non è in virtù di opere affinché nessuno se ne vanti. Infatti siamo opera sua, essendo stati creati in Cristo Gesù per fare le opere buone, che Dio ha precedentemente preparate affinché le pratichiamo –Efesini 2:8-10.

Amiche, non rivali

Potremmo esitare ad ammettere di avere una rivale, ma un’amica diventerà tale se non siamo capaci di festeggiare le benedizioni che riceve nella sua vita. Prega regolarmente per lei, chiedendo a Dio di benedirla. Lasciare andare i sospetti e fare qualcosa di gentile per lei aiuterà a dissipare i sentimenti negativi che hai sviluppato.

La Scrittura è chiara riguardo all’ostilità verso nostro fratello (o nostra sorella): Chi dice di essere nella luce e odia suo fratello, è ancora nelle tenebre. Chi ama suo fratello rimane nella luce e non c’è in lui nulla che lo faccia inciampare. Ma chi odia suo fratello è nelle tenebre, cammina nelle tenebre e non sa dove va, perché le tenebre gli hanno accecato gli occhi –1 Giovanni 2:9-11.

Sostituisci la gelosia con gratitudine e contentezza

I pensieri negativi arrivano senza invito, ma possiamo decidere se lasciarli restare o mandarli via. Impara a riportare la tua attenzione alla verità. La lettera ai Filippesi ci offre un ottimo modello: Del resto, fratelli [e sorelle], tutte le cose vere, tutte le cose onorevoli, tutte le cose giuste, tutte le cose pure, tutte le cose amabili, tutte le cose di buona fama, quelle in cui è qualche virtù e qualche lode, siano oggetto dei vostri pensieri –Filippesi 4:8.

Quando siamo in pace con Dio, con noi stesse e con le altre donne, saremo contente delle nostre capacità e delle circostanze in cui Dio ci ha poste. Se terremo lo sguardo fisso su Dio, troveremo gioia e la forza di rallegrarci con chi gioisce.

Editor’s Note:

Over the last number of years there seems to be a shift occurring on a variety of specific issues for some conservative Anabaptists. This changing of ideas and practice is not happening in a vacuum, rather we are simply following the leader. Once we start researching this matter further, we soon realize that this same migration on issues of faith and practice has been at work for some years now within the greater Evangelical community. Let’s stop and consider whether we are following God’s Word, or man’s influence.

Some Anabaptists are becoming dissatisfied with a traditional structure of church, so they gravitate towards “cell-group church” or “house-church” models. Others react to overbearing and authoritative church leadership from their past and start emphasizing a more democratic function of church. Then there are the folks who are moving away from a “local” church body emphasis to that of focusing more on a “universal” or a “global” church body. Still others don’t have a problem with what is considered “normal” church, instead they are the type that gets tired of the “old-fashioned” and the “boring.” These folks welcome “new ideas” that are presented in present-day books and at various conferences which are held around the country. These conferences are not all intrinsically wrong, nor are they all selling “new” interpretations, yet there are some that bring in “fresh” ideas originating from “outside” sources in the hope that they will bring “new life” to the lack of zeal within the “normal.”

Another area of shift is that of focusing on the Gospels while ignoring specific teachings in the Epistles. Some folks stress that we should “just follow Jesus” while not allowing the teachings of the Apostles to further detail the application of Jesus’ teachings. Others lift up the “Sermon on the Mount,” the “red letter Scriptures,” or walking in the “footsteps of Jesus,” without realizing that a default outcome of this focus tends to leave out specific teachings of the Epistles regarding practical church functioning and Christian living. Some of these include …exhort[ing] one another daily… –Hebrews 3:13, All scripture … is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, [and] for correction… –2 Timothy 3:16, and the fact that we should be careful because Satan and his agents will transform themselves …into the apostles of Christ and present themselves as …an angel of light –2 Corinthians 11:13-14.

Some individuals believe it is wrong for spiritual authorities to “take the oversight thereof,” or to give clear admonition over the pulpit. They shrink back from churches that have ordained leaders, or they don’t like the thought of spiritual authorities in their lives. Others feel their church doesn’t have much to offer so they attend various group events with others of “like precious faith” (who believe as they do), thus developing a disjointed spiritual body of individuals from many various local churches, fellowshipping together at large events. Many times, these believers allow someone outside of their local church fellowship to become their spiritual advisor, thus feeling justified in not giving their loyalty to their church leaders at home. They come to believe that the traditional way of having church the Anabaptist way is “not the way it used to be” or “not according to the early church”. They believe that structured church brings deadness to local bodies, never mind that the Epistles provide clear details on church structure and practice.

Many of these individuals are interacting and fellowshipping so closely with others from various other groups and churches instead of their own home church, that they do not realize they are actually functioning in a very individualistic manner. This manner of being an alone “local” Christian is categorically opposite from the “group spirituality” that our Anabaptist forefathers specifically believed and taught. Another area of misunderstanding in this whole issue, is that there is a very clear difference between the expression of the kingdom now and the kingdom future. Remember that Jesus said, “my kingdom is not of this world,” yet an extreme focus on kingdom this and kingdom that, will by default cause Christians to ignore this Truth, as they try to express the kingdom “on the earth,” and “in the now.”

The full effect of the resurrection and the ascension of Jesus in the life of a believer can never fully be understood without allowing the Epistles to bring more clear application to the Gospels or to the Sermon on the Mount. Simply following the words of Jesus in red ink will never help us know how to be a part of the “power of His resurrection”, or “the fellowship of His sufferings.” For this we need the balance of the rest of the New Testament.

Many of these points will require their own complete article to sort out all the nuances, which we plan to do as the Lord continues to allow time to continue. Considering all this, we felt that this article is a balanced, yet basic introduction to the many issues at stake and we have chosen it based on those thoughts.

Curvin L Wenger

When Jesus blessed Simon Peter for his confident confession that Jesus was the Christ, the Son of the living God –Matthew 16:16, He brought together two overarching New Testament themes: the church and the kingdom—…I will build my church … And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven… –Matthew 16:18-19. Ever since, Christ’s followers have deliberated, with varying opinions, on the meaning and the nature of the kingdom, and its relation to the church.

Jesus began His preaching by declaring that the kingdom of heaven was at hand (see Matthew 4:17). Throughout the Gospels, the kingdom was the unifying theme of His teaching. In fact, Scripture only records two occasions when Christ mentioned the church. The church, on the other hand, is more prominent in the Acts, the Epistles, and the Revelation. Why this difference? Is there some conflict or incompatible tension between what Jesus taught and emphasized, and that of the apostles?

Recent years seem to have brought an increased interest and reference to the kingdom within Evangelical circles as well as conservative Anabaptist circles. Many are using terms such as working for the kingdom, building up the kingdom, growing the kingdom, kingdom service, kingdom finances, and even funding the kingdom. Kingdom Theology has been offered as a course of study, and the expression Kingdom Christian has been coined to demarcate a particular kind of Christian—one who believes and practices Jesus’ teachings. Among many conservative Anabaptist people, kingdom terminology has practically drowned out the language expressed by Eliza Hewitt who wrote, “For Christ and the Church let our voices ring.”

Among the various factors which have nurtured this renewed kingdom emphasis among some Anabaptists, two stand out. Both of these concerns reflect the influence of Christians from without the conservative Anabaptist tradition, yet who profess to be Bible-believing and born-again.

  1. The first is that some people seem to be more concerned about being Biblical than about being Christ-like. We, conservative Anabaptists, can stand on the Bible to formulate all the right doctrines and positions while our lives fall short in reflecting the character and values of Jesus Christ our Lord, the One with whom we claim to be united in a living relationship.
  2. The second matter involves a fixation on the act of getting saved to the neglect of living a saved life; that is, a life of obedient discipleship, particularly to the very teachings of Jesus who we are to follow. While most conservative Anabaptists profess to practice Christ’s teachings, we are not immune to a careless discipleship.

There are individuals within conservative Anabaptism that address these concerns somewhat in the following manner. They say that while Evangelicals believe in the person and work of Christ, they tend to focus on Paul. For all practical purposes, they (Evangelicals) are more concerned about correct Bible interpretations, theological systems, and assenting to correct beliefs than they are with obedient Christian living, particularly regarding the hard teachings of Christ. In contrast, these Anabaptists claim that the kingdom of God, which Jesus inaugurated and was the theme of His teaching, should set the norm for understanding and living the Christian life. Consequently, for them, the Gospels (and the kingdom) then become primary in interpreting the rest of the New Testament.

What do we make of this? While sweeping generalizations don’t do justice to the exceptions and the qualifiers, the concerns are valid, and this critique regarding our Evangelical friends does hold some measure of truth. These things have their roots in the thinking of Augustine (354-430), in the imbalanced Reformation emphasis regarding justification by faith, and in the work of John Calvin. But what about the antidote of focusing mostly on Christ and the kingdom? Certainly, Christ is central to interpreting, not only the New Testament, but actually the entire Bible. And there is value in holding forth those teachings of Christ, which are so often brushed aside, yet are required of any church that would be worthy of His name. However, I would like to offer three points of caution or critique about taking this antidote unreservedly.

Do the Gospels dominate the rest of Scripture?

First, I believe it’s a mistake to assume that the Gospels (the life and teachings of Jesus) should dominate and control the interpretation of the New Testament scriptures. Rather, the New Testament, as it moves through the Gospels, the Acts, the Epistles, and lastly the Revelation, contains a divinely inspired progression of fuller revelation and doctrinal explanation. This is seen when we consider the words of Jesus regarding the coming of the Holy Spirit: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now. Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come –John 16:12-13. Those New Testament books following the Gospels are the anticipated fulfillment of these words. They bring the teachings and work of Christ to full development and understanding.

Christ’s ministry and teaching about the kingdom laid the groundwork, then His death and resurrection placed the foundation on which He would build His church. The Scriptures which follow the Gospels give us greater comprehension about the meaning of Christ’s death on the cross and its relation and effect on us that comes through faith and obedience. It also develops the whole doctrine of the church. So, the entire New Testament fits together in beautiful harmony. Both the Gospels and the Epistles need to be interpreted in reference to each other. The teachings of Christ do not take precedence over the Epistles, rather the Epistles help interpret the Gospels—they give us a more complete understanding and practical application to the principles Christ gave His Disciples.

Does Theology Militate Against Discipleship?

Secondly, we should be careful to not set correct interpretation and correct practice against one another. To say it another way, we should not pit theology against discipleship. To whatever degree some Evangelicals may overemphasize theology at the expense of discipleship, it should not prejudice us into making a whipping boy out of theology. Theology is the study of God and the things of God. We are forming a personal theology when we study God’s Word and compare Scripture with Scripture in our efforts to come to a unified and harmonious understanding of its various parts.

Every Christian has a theology, whether he can express it well or not. Our theology (or doctrinal understanding, if you want to say it that way) is our belief system and the soil out of which our behavior grows. Some theologies are very elementary, others reflect a lifetime of study, most are incomplete, some are inconsistent, others are dogmatic or laced with philosophy, and some are dreadfully wrong. Hopefully, all of us have a growing, and increasingly accurate understanding of God and His Word. This is quite necessary since our theology, which is the sum of our beliefs about God and our understanding of His Word and the Christian life, is what affects our discipleship—our daily walk with God. A good theology undergirds discipleship. A poor theology undermines discipleship.

Are “Kingdom” and “Church” Interchangeable?

Finally, we should think correctly about the kingdom in relation to the church. What is the relationship of the kingdom to the church? The kingdom is not, as contemporary usage would almost have us think, a generic version of, or a substitute word for, the church. Rather, the kingdom has to do with the reign or rule of God. It is both a present reality, having been inaugurated in the person and mission of Jesus, and a future expectation which God will bring to completion at the end of time. The church, while not the kingdom, is composed of those who are in the kingdom; those who, through the work of Christ, have submitted to the rule of God.

While we struggle for the precise word to express the relationship of the kingdom to the church, as a holy, loving, and obedient community of believers, the church is the earthly manifestation of God’s rule—His kingdom. Christ did not say “I will build my kingdom”; rather He said, “I will build my church.” Likewise, Paul did not build kingdom halls; He started churches. It is possible for us to have an idealistic and romantic view of the kingdom that gets separated from the hard work of living on earth with our fellow believers in a local church body. We can elevate the kingdom and diminish the church. We can get enthusiastic about the concept of the kingdom, the teachings of the kingdom, the growth of the kingdom, and conferences about the kingdom, and yet be cynical, critical, and sorry members of our local church.

Do you want to work for the kingdom (see Colossians 4:11)? Then commit yourself wholeheartedly to Christ and His church. That starts with your local church. Love and serve your church. Accept responsibility in it. Be accountable and loyal to your local church. Work for the good and growth of the church—your local church, and beyond.

Timothy Dwight wrote:*

I love Thy Kingdom, Lord,
The house of Thine abode,
The church our blest Redeemer
Saved with His own precious blood.
I love Thy church, O God:
Her walls before Thee stand,
Dear as the apple of Thine eye,
And graven on Thy hand.

What he was saying about the precise relationship of the kingdom to the church may be different from what I conceive it to be. However, what I would like for us to appreciate is that when he thought of the kingdom, he thought of the church. And so should we! Are his words yours, as he writes on?

For her my tears shall fall,
For her my prayers ascend;
To her my cares and toils be giv’n,
Till toils and cares shall end.
Beyond my highest joy
I prize her heav’nly ways,
Her sweet communion, solemn vows,
Her hymns of love and praise.

Dokezo la Mhariri:

Katika miaka kadhaa iliyopita, inaonekana kuna mabadiliko yanayotokea kuhusu masuala mbalimbali mahususi miongoni mwa baadhi ya Wanabaptisti wa kihafidhina. Mabadiliko haya ya mawazo na matendo hayatokei bila sababu; badala yake, tunamfuata tu kiongozi. Tunapoanza kuchunguza jambo hili kwa undani zaidi, tunatambua upesi kwamba mabadiliko hayo hayo kuhusu masuala ya imani na matendo yamekuwa yakitokea kwa miaka kadhaa sasa ndani ya jumuiya pana ya Kiinjili. Tusimame na kufikiria ikiwa tunafuata Neno la Mungu au ushawishi wa wanadamu.

Baadhi ya Wanabaptisti hawaridhishwi tena na muundo wa jadi wa kanisa, hivyo wanavutiwa na mifumo ya “kanisa la vikundi vidogo” au “kanisa la nyumbani.” Wengine huitikia uongozi wa kanisa uliopita kiasi na wenye mamlaka makubwa walioupitia zamani, kisha wanaanza kusisitiza utendaji wa kanisa ulio wa kidemokrasia zaidi. Halafu kuna wale wanaoachana na msisitizo wa jumuiya ya kanisa “la mahali” na kuanza kuzingatia zaidi jumuiya ya kanisa “la ulimwenguni kote” au “la kimataifa.” Bado wengine hawana tatizo na kanisa linalochukuliwa kuwa “la kawaida”; wao huchoshwa na mambo “ya kizamani” na “ya kuchosha.” Watu hawa hukaribisha “mawazo mapya” yanayowasilishwa katika vitabu vya siku hizi na kwenye mikutano mbalimbali inayofanyika kote nchini. Mikutano hii si mibaya kiasili, wala yote haiuzi tafsiri “mpya”; hata hivyo, mingine huleta mawazo “mapya” kutoka vyanzo vya “nje,” kwa matumaini kwamba yataleta “uhai mpya” katika ukosefu wa bidii uliopo katika “kanisa la kawaida.”

Eneo jingine la mabadiliko ni kulenga Injili huku tukipuuza mafundisho mahususi katika Nyaraka. Baadhi ya watu husisitiza kwamba tunapaswa “kumfuata Yesu tu,” bila kuruhusu mafundisho ya Mitume kufafanua zaidi jinsi ya kuyatumia mafundisho ya Yesu. Wengine husisitiza “Mahubiri ya Mlimani,” “Maandiko yenye maneno ya Yesu yaliyochapwa kwa rangi nyekundu,” au kutembea katika “nyayo za Yesu,” bila kutambua kwamba matokeo ya kawaida ya mtazamo huu ni kuacha nje mafundisho mahususi ya Nyaraka kuhusu utendaji wa kanisa na maisha ya Kikristo. Baadhi ya mafundisho hayo ni pamoja na …kuonyana kila siku… –Waebrania 3:13, Maandiko yote … yanafaa kwa mafundisho, kwa kuwaonya watu, [na] kwa kuwaongoza… –2 Timotheo 3:16, na ukweli kwamba tunapaswa kuwa waangalifu kwa sababu Shetani na mawakala wake watajigeuza …kuwa mitume wa Kristo na kujifanya kuwa …malaika wa nuru –2 Wakorintho 11:13-14.

Baadhi ya watu wanaamini kuwa si sawa kwa viongozi wa kiroho “kulisimamia,” au kutoa maonyo yaliyo wazi kutoka mimbarini. Wanasita kujiunga na makanisa yenye viongozi waliowekwa rasmi, au hawapendi wazo la kuwa na viongozi wa kiroho katika maisha yao. Wengine wanahisi kwamba kanisa lao halina mengi ya kuwapa, kwa hiyo huhudhuria matukio mbalimbali ya vikundi pamoja na wengine wenye “imani ileile yenye thamani” (wanaoamini kama wao), na hivyo kutengeneza jumuiya ya kiroho isiyoungana ya watu kutoka makanisa mengi tofauti ya mahali, wanaoshirikiana katika mikusanyiko mikubwa. Mara nyingi, waumini hawa humruhusu mtu aliye nje ya ushirika wa kanisa lao la mahali awe mshauri wao wa kiroho, na hivyo kujiona wana haki ya kutokuwa waaminifu kwa viongozi wa kanisa lao nyumbani. Wanafikia kuamini kwamba desturi ya jadi ya kuwa kanisa kwa njia ya Wanabaptisti “si kama ilivyokuwa zamani” au “si kulingana na kanisa la kwanza.” Wanaamini kwamba kanisa lenye muundo huleta ufu hali katika jumuiya za mahali, bila kujali kwamba Nyaraka zinatoa maelezo yaliyo wazi kuhusu muundo na utendaji wa kanisa.

Wengi wa watu hawa hushirikiana na kufellowship kwa ukaribu sana na wengine kutoka vikundi na makanisa mengine mbalimbali badala ya kanisa lao la nyumbani, kiasi kwamba hawatambui kuwa kwa kweli wanaishi kwa namna ya ubinafsi mkubwa. Namna hii ya kuwa Mkristo wa “mahali” aliye peke yake ni kinyume kabisa na “hali ya kiroho ya kijumuiya” ambayo mababu zetu Wanabaptisti waliamini na kufundisha mahususi. Kutoelewana kwingine katika suala hili lote ni kwamba kuna tofauti iliyo wazi sana kati ya udhihirisho wa ufalme sasa na ufalme ujao. Kumbukeni kwamba Yesu alisema, “ufalme wangu si wa ulimwengu huu,” lakini msisitizo uliopitiliza kuhusu ufalme hili na lile utawafanya Wakristo, kwa kawaida, kupuuza Ukweli huu wanapojaribu kuudhihirisha ufalme “duniani” na “sasa hivi.”

Matokeo kamili ya ufufuo na kupaa kwa Yesu katika maisha ya mwamini hayawezi kamwe kueleweka kikamilifu bila kuruhusu Nyaraka zifafanue zaidi matumizi ya Injili au ya Mahubiri ya Mlimani. Kufuata tu maneno ya Yesu yaliyochapwa kwa wino mwekundu hakutatusaidia kamwe kujua jinsi ya kuwa sehemu ya “nguvu za kufufuka kwake,” au “ushirika wa mateso yake.” Kwa hili tunahitaji uwiano wa sehemu nyingine ya Agano Jipya.

Mengi ya mambo haya yatahitaji makala kamili ya pekee ili kuchambua tofauti zake zote ndogondogo; tunapanga kufanya hivyo kadiri Bwana atakavyoendelea kutujalia muda. Kwa kuzingatia yote haya, tulihisi kwamba makala hii ni utangulizi wenye uwiano, ingawa wa msingi, kuhusu masuala mengi yaliyo hatarini, nasi tumeichagua kutokana na mawazo hayo.

Curvin L Wenger

Yesu alipomsifu Simoni Petro kwa ungamo lake thabiti kwamba Yesu alikuwa Kristo, Mwana wa Mungu aliye hai –Mathayo 16:16, aliunganisha mada kuu mbili za Agano Jipya: kanisa na ufalme—…Nitalijenga kanisa langu … Nami nitakupa funguo za ufalme wa mbinguni… –Mathayo 16:18-19. Tangu wakati huo, wafuasi wa Kristo wamejadili, wakiwa na maoni mbalimbali, maana na asili ya ufalme, na uhusiano wake na kanisa.

Yesu alianza kuhubiri kwa kutangaza kwamba ufalme wa mbinguni ulikuwa umekaribia (ona Mathayo 4:17). Katika Injili zote, ufalme ulikuwa mada iliyounganisha mafundisho yake. Kwa kweli, Maandiko yanarekodi matukio mawili tu ambapo Kristo alitaja kanisa. Kwa upande mwingine, kanisa linatajwa zaidi katika Matendo, Nyaraka na Ufunuo. Kwa nini tofauti hii? Je, kuna mgongano au mvutano usioweza kupatanishwa kati ya yale ambayo Yesu alifundisha na kusisitiza, na yale ya mitume?

Miaka ya hivi karibuni inaonekana kuleta ongezeko la kupendezwa na kurejelea ufalme katika duru za Kiinjili na pia miongoni mwa Wanabaptisti wa kihafidhina. Wengi wanatumia misemo kama vile kuifanyia kazi ufalme, kuujenga ufalme, kuukuza ufalme, huduma ya ufalme, fedha za ufalme, na hata kufadhili ufalme. Theolojia ya Ufalme imetolewa kama kozi ya masomo, na jina Mkristo wa Ufalme limebuniwa ili kumtofautisha Mkristo wa aina fulani—anayeyaamini na kuyatekeleza mafundisho ya Yesu. Miongoni mwa Wanabaptisti wengi wa kihafidhina, istilahi za ufalme zimekaribia kuzamisha lugha aliyoitumia Eliza Hewitt alipoandika, “Kwa ajili ya Kristo na Kanisa sauti zetu na zisikike.”

Miongoni mwa mambo mbalimbali yaliyochangia kuimarisha upya msisitizo huu wa ufalme miongoni mwa baadhi ya Wanabaptisti, mawili yanajitokeza. Masuala haya yote mawili yanaakisi ushawishi wa Wakristo walio nje ya mapokeo ya Wanabaptisti wa kihafidhina, lakini wanaodai kuamini Biblia na kuzaliwa mara ya pili.

  1. Jambo la kwanza ni kwamba baadhi ya watu wanaonekana kujali zaidi kuwa wa kibiblia kuliko kuwa kama Kristo. Sisi Wanabaptisti wa kihafidhina tunaweza kusimama juu ya Biblia ili kubuni mafundisho na misimamo yote iliyo sahihi, huku maisha yetu yakishindwa kuakisi tabia na maadili ya Yesu Kristo Bwana wetu, Yule ambaye tunadai kuunganishwa naye katika uhusiano hai.
  2. Jambo la pili linahusu kujikita kupita kiasi katika tendo la kuokoka huku tukipuuza kuishi maisha ya mtu aliyeokoka; yaani, maisha ya uanafunzi wa utii, hasa utii kwa mafundisho yenyewe ya Yesu tunayopaswa kumfuata. Ingawa Wanabaptisti wengi wa kihafidhina wanadai kuyatekeleza mafundisho ya Kristo, sisi pia hatuko salama dhidi ya uanafunzi usiojali.

Kuna watu miongoni mwa Wanabaptisti wa kihafidhina wanaozungumzia masuala haya kwa namna inayofanana na hii. Wanasema kwamba ingawa Wainjili wanaamini nafsi na kazi ya Kristo, huwa na mwelekeo wa kumlenga Paulo. Kwa madhumuni yote ya kiutendaji, wao (Wainjili) wanajali zaidi tafsiri sahihi za Biblia, mifumo ya kiteolojia na kukubali imani sahihi kuliko maisha ya Kikristo yenye utii, hasa kuhusu mafundisho magumu ya Kristo. Kinyume chake, Wanabaptisti hawa wanadai kwamba ufalme wa Mungu, ambao Yesu aliuzindua na ambao ulikuwa mada ya mafundisho yake, unapaswa kuweka kiwango cha kuelewa na kuishi maisha ya Kikristo. Kwa hiyo, kwao, Injili (na ufalme) huwa msingi wa kutafsiri sehemu nyingine ya Agano Jipya.

Tuseme nini kuhusu jambo hili? Ingawa kauli za jumla zinazofagia kila kitu hazitendi haki kwa mambo ya kipekee na masharti maalumu, wasiwasi huu ni halali, na ukosoaji huu kuhusu marafiki zetu Wainjili una ukweli kwa kiasi fulani. Mambo haya yana mizizi yake katika mawazo ya Augustino (354-430), katika msisitizo usio na uwiano wa Matengenezo kuhusu kuhesabiwa haki kwa imani, na katika kazi ya John Calvin. Lakini vipi kuhusu tiba ya kulenga hasa Kristo na ufalme? Bila shaka, Kristo ndiye kiini cha kutafsiri si Agano Jipya tu, bali kwa kweli Biblia nzima. Na kuna thamani katika kusisitiza mafundisho hayo ya Kristo, ambayo mara nyingi hupuuzwa, ilhali yanahitajika kwa kanisa lolote linalostahili jina lake. Hata hivyo, ningependa kutoa mambo matatu ya tahadhari au ukosoaji kuhusu kukubali tiba hii bila masharti.

Je, Injili zinatawala sehemu nyingine ya Maandiko?

Kwanza, ninaamini ni kosa kudhani kwamba Injili (maisha na mafundisho ya Yesu) zinapaswa kutawala na kudhibiti tafsiri ya maandiko ya Agano Jipya. Badala yake, Agano Jipya linapoendelea kupitia Injili, Matendo, Nyaraka, na hatimaye Ufunuo, lina mfuatano wa ufunuo unaokamilika zaidi na maelezo ya mafundisho, ulioongozwa na Mungu. Hili linaonekana tunapozingatia maneno ya Yesu kuhusu kuja kwa Roho Mtakatifu: Nina mambo mengi bado ya kuwaambia, lakini sasa hamwezi kuyastahimili. Lakini yeye, Roho wa kweli, atakapokuja, atawaongoza awatie kwenye kweli yote; kwa maana hatanena kwa shauri lake mwenyewe, lakini yote atakayoyasikia atayanena, na mambo yajayo atawapasha habari yake –Yohana 16:12-13. Vitabu hivyo vya Agano Jipya vinavyofuata Injili ndivyo vinavyotimiza maneno haya yaliyotazamiwa. Vinakuza mafundisho na kazi ya Kristo hadi kufikia ukamilifu na uelewa kamili.

Huduma ya Kristo na mafundisho yake kuhusu ufalme viliweka msingi wa awali; kisha kifo na ufufuo wake viliweka msingi ambao juu yake angejenga kanisa lake. Maandiko yanayofuata Injili yanatupa ufahamu mpana zaidi kuhusu maana ya kifo cha Kristo msalabani na uhusiano wake nasi, pamoja na athari zake kwetu zinazopatikana kwa njia ya imani na utii. Pia yanaendeleza fundisho lote la kanisa. Kwa hiyo, Agano Jipya lote linapatana kwa upatano mzuri. Injili na Nyaraka zote zinahitaji kutafsiriwa kwa kurejelea nyingine. Mafundisho ya Kristo hayatangulii Nyaraka; badala yake, Nyaraka husaidia kufasiri Injili—zinatupa uelewa kamili zaidi na matumizi ya vitendo ya kanuni ambazo Kristo aliwapa wanafunzi wake.

Je, Theolojia Inapingana na Uanafunzi?

Pili, tunapaswa kuwa waangalifu tusipinge tafsiri sahihi na utendaji sahihi kana kwamba haviwezi kuwa pamoja. Kwa maneno mengine, hatupaswi kuiweka theolojia kinyume na uanafunzi. Kwa kiwango chochote ambacho baadhi ya Wainjili huenda wakasisitiza theolojia kupita kiasi kwa gharama ya uanafunzi, hilo halipaswi kutushawishi tuifanye theolojia kuwa mbuzi wa kafara. Theolojia ni somo la Mungu na mambo ya Mungu. Tunaunda theolojia yetu binafsi tunapojifunza Neno la Mungu na kulinganisha Maandiko na Maandiko katika jitihada zetu za kupata uelewa mmoja wenye upatano wa sehemu zake mbalimbali.

Kila Mkristo ana theolojia, aweze kuieleza vizuri au la. Theolojia yetu (au uelewa wetu wa mafundisho, ukipenda kusema hivyo) ndiyo mfumo wetu wa imani na udongo ambao tabia yetu hukua kutoka humo. Baadhi ya theolojia ni za msingi sana, nyingine huonyesha maisha yote ya kujifunza; nyingi hazijakamilika, nyingine hazipatani ndani yake, nyingine ni za kushikilia kwa ukaidi au zimechanganywa na falsafa, na nyingine zina makosa makubwa sana. Tunatumaini kwamba sote tunaendelea kukua katika uelewa sahihi zaidi na zaidi wa Mungu na Neno lake. Hili ni muhimu sana kwa kuwa theolojia yetu, ambayo ni jumla ya imani zetu kuhusu Mungu na uelewa wetu wa Neno lake na maisha ya Kikristo, ndiyo inayoathiri uanafunzi wetu—mwenendo wetu wa kila siku pamoja na Mungu. Theolojia nzuri huimarisha uanafunzi. Theolojia dhaifu hudhoofisha uanafunzi.

Je, “Ufalme” na “Kanisa” Ni Maneno Yanayoweza Kubadilishana?

Mwishowe, tunapaswa kufikiri kwa usahihi kuhusu uhusiano wa ufalme na kanisa. Uhusiano wa ufalme na kanisa ni upi? Ufalme sio, kama matumizi ya siku hizi yanavyokaribia kutufanya tuamini, toleo la jumla la kanisa, wala neno mbadala la kanisa. Badala yake, ufalme unahusu utawala wa Mungu. Ni uhalisia uliopo sasa, kwa kuwa ulianzishwa katika nafsi na utume wa Yesu, na pia ni tarajio la wakati ujao ambalo Mungu atalifikisha kwenye utimilifu mwishoni mwa wakati. Kanisa, ingawa si ufalme, linaundwa na wale walio ndani ya ufalme; wale ambao, kwa kazi ya Kristo, wamejisalimisha kwa utawala wa Mungu.

Ingawa tunatafuta neno sahihi la kueleza uhusiano wa ufalme na kanisa kama jumuiya takatifu, yenye upendo na utii ya waumini, kanisa ndilo udhihirisho wa utawala wa Mungu duniani—ufalme wake. Kristo hakusema, “Nitajenga ufalme wangu”; badala yake alisema, “Nitalijenga kanisa langu.” Vivyo hivyo, Paulo hakujenga majumba ya ufalme; alianzisha makanisa. Inawezekana kuwa na mtazamo wa kimawazo na wa kimahaba kuhusu ufalme, unaojitenga na kazi ngumu ya kuishi duniani pamoja na waumini wenzetu ndani ya jumuiya ya kanisa la mahali. Tunaweza kuutukuza ufalme na kulidunisha kanisa. Tunaweza kuchangamkia dhana ya ufalme, mafundisho ya ufalme, ukuaji wa ufalme na mikutano kuhusu ufalme, lakini wakati huohuo kuwa washiriki wenye mashaka, wakosoaji na wa kusikitisha wa kanisa letu la mahali.

Je, unataka kuifanyia kazi ufalme (ona Wakolosai 4:11)? Basi jiweke wakfu kwa moyo wote kwa Kristo na kanisa lake. Hilo huanzia katika kanisa lako la mahali. Lipende na kulitumikia kanisa lako. Kubali wajibu ndani yake. Uwajibike na kuwa mwaminifu kwa kanisa lako la mahali. Fanya kazi kwa ajili ya mema na ukuaji wa kanisa—kanisa lako la mahali, na zaidi yake.

Timothy Dwight aliandika:*

Naupenda Ufalme wako, Bwana,
Makao yako,
Kanisa ambalo Mkombozi wetu
Aliliokoa kwa damu yake ya thamani.
Ee Mungu, nalipenda kanisa lako:
Kuta zake zimesimama mbele zako,
Linapendwa kama mboni ya jicho lako,
Na limechorwa katika mkono wako.

Huenda alichosema kuhusu uhusiano sahihi kati ya ufalme na kanisa ni tofauti na ninavyouelewa. Hata hivyo, ningependa tuthamini kwamba alipofikiria ufalme, alifikiria kanisa. Nasi tunapaswa kufanya vivyo hivyo! Je, maneno yake ni yako pia, anapoendelea kuandika?

Kwa ajili yake machozi yangu yatadondoka,
Maombi yangu yatapaa kwa ajili yake;
Kwake nitatoa taabu na bidii yangu,
Hadi taabu na mahangaiko yatakapokoma.
Zaidi ya furaha yangu kuu
Nazithamini njia zake za mbinguni,
Ushirika wake mtamu, nadhiri zake takatifu,
Nyimbo zake za upendo na sifa.

* Tazama ukurasa wa 32 kwa wimbo mzima.

One Sunday morning a little girl, whom we will call Jennika, woke up to the sun shining into her bedroom. She dressed in her Sunday dress just like she did every other Sunday morning. This Sunday morning was quite different, though. While she was sitting at the breakfast table waiting for her mom to fill her plate, her mom’s chest suddenly started hurting very badly. It hurt so badly, she had to go lie on the couch. Jennika felt scared. She didn’t know what was going to happen. About ten minutes later, her dad took her mom to the hospital. Later that afternoon, she and her siblings heard that their mom had suffered a heart attack.

The next Wednesday evening, her dad asked, “Jennika, would you like to go along to the hospital tomorrow to see Mom?”

“Yes!” she beamed.

The next morning after breakfast, her older sister and baby brother went with her and her dad to the hospital. That day she had lots of fun. She enjoyed looking out the window of the waiting room and watching the helicopters take off and land. One time she even saw an ambulance come with its lights and sirens on. That was exciting! One time she almost got lost in the halls, but one of her mom’s nurses saw her and showed her the right room.

That night she was going to spend the night with her mom. She was so excited! She thought sleeping on the chair in her mom’s room would be fun. Her mom was going to ask the nurses for a pillow and some blankets. About fifteen minutes after her dad left, a nurse came in and said she couldn’t spend the night there after all! Her dad needed to come back to pick her up. She was so disappointed! She cried almost the whole way home. That night they dropped off her two-week-old brother at one of the church families to give her older sisters a break from taking care of him.

The next day she had a wonderful surprise. First, her cousins, who lived about three hours away, came to visit. And she found out that her mom was going to come home that day! She helped her siblings decorate the house. Her older sister made two welcome-home signs for inside the house and her older brother made one for out by the driveway.

“Mom is home!” yelled her younger brother when he saw the car pull up outside the house. Jennika and her siblings dashed to the front door. They led their mom to her favorite recliner which was close to the air conditioner that their uncle had just installed that morning.

That evening Jennika snuggled up to her mom. “I’m glad you’re home,” she whispered. “I like it when you’re home.” Because her mom had been gone so long, Jennika learned to be more thankful for her mom.

Jennika is older now and is still very thankful for her mom. Maybe your mom didn’t need to be in the hospital for a week, but you should still be thankful for her. Don’t forget to tell her!

Op een zondagochtend werd een klein meisje, dat we Jennika zullen noemen, wakker met de zon die haar slaapkamer binnen scheen. Ze trok haar zondagse jurk aan, net als elke andere zondagochtend. Maar deze zondagochtend was heel anders. Terwijl ze aan de ontbijttafel zat te wachten tot haar moeder haar bord zou vullen, begon de borst van haar moeder plotseling heel erg pijn te doen. Het deed zo’n pijn dat ze op de bank moest gaan liggen. Jennika werd bang. Ze wist niet wat er zou gebeuren. Ongeveer tien minuten later bracht haar vader haar moeder naar het ziekenhuis. Later die middag hoorden zij en haar broers en zussen dat hun moeder een hartaanval had gehad.

De volgende woensdagavond vroeg haar vader: ‘Jennika, zou je morgen mee willen naar het ziekenhuis om mama te zien?’

‘Ja!’ zei ze stralend.

De volgende ochtend gingen na het ontbijt haar oudere zus en haar kleine broertje met haar en haar vader mee naar het ziekenhuis. Die dag had ze het erg naar haar zin. Ze keek graag uit het raam van de wachtkamer naar de helikopters die opstegen en landden. Op een keer zag ze zelfs een ambulance aankomen met zwaailichten en sirene aan. Dat was spannend! Een keer verdwaalde ze bijna in de gangen, maar een verpleegkundige van haar moeder zag haar en wees haar de juiste kamer.

Die nacht zou ze bij haar moeder blijven slapen. Ze was zo opgewonden! Ze dacht dat het leuk zou zijn om op de stoel in de kamer van haar moeder te slapen. Haar moeder zou de verpleegkundigen om een kussen en wat dekens vragen. Ongeveer vijftien minuten nadat haar vader was vertrokken, kwam er een verpleegkundige binnen die zei dat ze toch niet mocht blijven slapen! Haar vader moest terugkomen om haar op te halen. Wat was ze teleurgesteld! Ze huilde bijna de hele weg naar huis. Die avond brachten ze haar broertje van twee weken oud naar een gezin uit de kerk, zodat haar oudere zussen even vrij waren van de zorg voor hem.

De volgende dag wachtte haar een geweldige verrassing. Eerst kwamen haar neven en nichten op bezoek, die ongeveer drie uur verderop woonden. En ze kwam erachter dat haar moeder die dag naar huis zou komen! Ze hielp haar broers en zussen het huis te versieren. Haar oudere zus maakte twee welkomstborden voor binnen in huis en haar oudere broer maakte er een voor bij de oprit.

‘Mama is thuis!’ riep haar jongere broer toen hij de auto buiten voor het huis zag stoppen. Jennika en haar broers en zussen renden naar de voordeur. Ze brachten hun moeder naar haar favoriete relaxfauteuil, die vlak bij de airconditioning stond die hun oom die ochtend nog had geïnstalleerd.

Die avond kroop Jennika dicht tegen haar moeder aan. ‘Ik ben blij dat je thuis bent,’ fluisterde ze. ‘Ik vind het fijn als je thuis bent.’ Omdat haar moeder zo lang weg was geweest, leerde Jennika haar moeder meer dankbaar te zijn.

Jennika is nu ouder en is haar moeder nog steeds heel dankbaar. Misschien hoefde jouw moeder niet een week in het ziekenhuis te liggen, maar toch moet je dankbaar voor haar zijn. Vergeet niet haar dat te vertellen!

“How is the new curriculum selling?” Sandra asked, wrapping her hands around her mug of coffee.

“It’s slow,” Abby answered. “I need to do more advertising, but now that the product is finished, I find it difficult to promote.”

“What’s wrong?” Sandra asked. Abby had spent years developing a curriculum for special needs children. Her passion and dedication to the project was amazing, but now her zeal seemed stifled.

“Well,” Abby said slowly. “I feel like my co-worker constantly criticizes me. ‘The cover design is tacky, there is a misspelling on page 11’, I should have said this, this, and this. My project advisor wants me to work on advertising, but every time I move forward, she tells me I did something wrong.”

“Does it feel like jealousy?” Sandra asked.

“I hadn’t thought of that. I’m staying in the background, but that’s not helping. I feel crippled and I don’t know what to do.”

Sandra nodded. “It’s difficult to be the recipient of another person’s jealousy. But it’s worse to be the one who’s jealous. I’ve been there. It’s miserable.”

“How did you work through it?” Abby asked. “You don’t seem like a jealous person now.”

“It was one point in a message,” Sandra answered. “The minister said, ‘If you feel critical toward someone who is rejoicing, likely you are struggling with jealousy.’ I don’t remember anything else he said,” Sandra chucked, “but, I knew he had identified my problem. I often found it hard to be happy for my peers. I didn’t realize jealousy was my root problem.”

“That makes sense,” replied Abby.

“It is harder for jealousy to take root if I face the negative thoughts right away,” Sandra replied. “It’s a battle worth fighting. I am happier when I can ‘rejoice with them that do rejoice,’ like the Bible says to do.”

“Maybe my co-worker is dealing with negative thoughts about the success more that feeling annoyed at me,” mused Abby.

“That’s likely true,” replied Sandra. “Aim to put her fears to rest so that you can work together productively. Don’t react to her behavior.”

Like Sandra, I too, have had critical thoughts when peers shared good news, or I noticed their accomplishments. Unless checked immediately, that tinge of jealousy keeps me from being happy for others.

The Bible describes the brutality of envy and jealousy. Jealousy is as cruel as the grave. (see Song of Solomon 8:6). Envy [is] the rottenness of the bones –Proverbs 14:30. And, Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy? –Proverbs 27:4. Jealousy is extremely subtle. It can be covered with an aura of godliness. Not only does it have the potential to destroy my relationships now, but also those of my children and grandchildren.

Women don’t decide to be jealous. They don’t say, “Today I’m going to be jealous.” Often, it’s hard to pinpoint when jealousy enters the heart, or even if it is there. But if it is hard to be happy for others, maybe it’s time to search our souls. We are prepared to fight against jealousy when we understand how and where jealousy thrives—within the heart of each of us.

Peers Test Our Rejoicing

Generally, we aren’t envious of people that we’re not close to. Women all around the world get married, have babies, or move into a new house, and we scarcely notice. But it’s hard to rejoice when those near us in time, place, age, or reputation enjoy blessings that we wish for. More than once, a jubilant phone call announcing a milestone challenged my resolve to rejoice with a rejoicing friend. God understands the struggle and He leads me to rest and acceptance.

Recognize Jealousy

The definition of jealous is: ‘Feeling or showing envy of someone or their achievements and advantages.’ Jealousy pops up in many ways, such as craving to copy a peer. Jealousy belittles the achievements of another and tries to control the way others think of that person. Jealousy gloats about the distresses and failures of others, while basking in a spiritual bubble. Jealous people keep the rumor mill in full production by feeding it twisted truths.

Safeguard Your Thoughts

Jealousy starts in the mind. Dwelling on a suspicion or envying another person distorts truth. This is dangerous, because what you perceive as a truth, is a lie.

We decide someone is proud because they brought a beautiful dessert to a potluck. Or we think a sister is a negligent homemaker because she visited a woman at a nursing home. Why? We tend to judge others by our own motives. Isn’t it feelings of guilt, self-justification, or envy that cause us to heap a negligent title on someone who is visiting the elderly? We don’t know how long she thought about that visit or how her husband made it possible. Divisive thoughts converted into words wreak havoc among godly women. It causes extra work for church leaders and stunts the growth of a body of believers.

Embrace The Thought: “Life Isn’t Fair”

Sometimes someone will have something you desire. On the flipside, there are times you will have something another woman wishes for. “Life isn’t fair” is a fact of life that we cannot change; we can only adjust our attitude.

There were friends in the same church who each had a daughter of dating age. As life would have it, one daughter dated and married long before the other one began a courtship. The mother of the single girl determined that she would rejoice with her friend and her daughter. As a result, the mothers are still friends, the girls are friends, and it’s likely their children will be friends.

Count Your Own Blessings

Looking at the blessings of others and making comparisons makes it difficult to be happy and satisfied. The Apostle Paul warns of this: …but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise –2 Corinthians 10:12. Happiness will not come to women who neglect to appreciate what they already have. Neither will they happily rejoice with those who rejoice.

Know Who You Are In Christ

Jealousy stems from feelings of fear and insecurity. God created you for His honor and glory. There isn’t a need for competition, rather we ought to be content in knowing who we are in Jesus. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them –Ephesians 2:8-10.

Have Friends, Not Rivals

We might hesitate to admit that we have a rival, but that’s what a friend will become if we aren’t able to celebrate the blessings in her life. Pray for her regularly, asking God to bless her. Letting go of suspicion and doing something nice for her will help dissipate the negative feelings you have developed.

The Scripture is clear about enmity toward our brother (or sister): He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now. He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him. But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes –1 John 2:9-11.

Replace Jealousy With Gratitude And Contentment

Negative thoughts come without invitation, but we can decide if they will stay or leave. Learn to redirect your attention to truth. Philippians gives us an excellent blueprint: Finally, brethren [sisters], whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things –Philippians 4:8.

When we are at peace with God, with ourselves, and with our fellow women, we will be content with our abilities and with the circumstances in which God has placed us. With our focus on God, we will find joy and the power to rejoice with them that rejoice.

“새 교육과정은 잘 팔리고 있나요?” 샌드라는 커피잔을 두 손으로 감싸 쥐며 물었다.

“더디게 진행되고 있어요.” 애비가 대답했다. “광고를 더 해야 하는데, 제품을 완성하고 나니 홍보하기가 어렵네요.”

“무슨 문제라도 있나요?” 샌드라가 물었다. 애비는 특별한 도움이 필요한 아이들을 위한 교육과정을 개발하는 데 여러 해를 보냈다. 그 일에 쏟은 열정과 헌신은 놀라웠지만, 이제 그녀의 열의는 꺾인 듯했다.

“글쎄요.” 애비가 천천히 말했다. “동료가 계속 저를 비판하는 것 같아요. ‘표지 디자인이 촌스럽다, 11쪽에 철자 오류가 있다’고 하고, 제가 이러저러한 말을 했어야 했다면서요. 제 프로젝트 지도자는 광고 작업을 하라고 하는데, 제가 뭔가를 진행할 때마다 잘못한 점을 지적해요.”

“질투처럼 느껴지나요?” 샌드라가 물었다.

“그런 생각은 못 해 봤어요. 저는 뒷전으로 물러나 있는데, 그게 도움이 되지는 않네요. 무력해진 것 같고 무엇을 해야 할지 모르겠어요.”

샌드라가 고개를 끄덕였다. “다른 사람의 질투를 받는 건 힘든 일이죠. 하지만 질투하는 사람이 되는 건 더 괴로워요. 저도 그런 적이 있어요. 정말 비참하죠.”

“어떻게 극복했어요?” 애비가 물었다. “지금은 질투하는 사람처럼 보이지 않아요.”

“설교 중 한 대목이었어요.” 샌드라가 대답했다. “목사님이 이렇게 말씀하셨어요. ‘기뻐하는 사람을 못마땅하게 여기고 비판하고 싶다면, 아마 질투와 씨름하고 있는 것입니다.’” 샌드라는 웃으며 말했다. “그분이 다른 어떤 말씀을 하셨는지는 기억이 안 나지만, 제 문제를 정확히 짚으셨다는 건 알았어요. 또래들이 잘되는 걸 기뻐하기가 어려울 때가 많았거든요. 질투가 제 근본적인 문제라는 걸 깨닫지 못했어요.”

“그럴듯하네요.” 애비가 대답했다.

“부정적인 생각을 바로 마주하면 질투가 뿌리내리기 어려워져요.” 샌드라가 말했다. “그 싸움은 해 볼 가치가 있어요. 성경 말씀처럼 ‘기뻐하는 자들과 함께 기뻐’할 수 있을 때 저는 더 행복하거든요.”

“어쩌면 동료는 저를 성가셔하는 것보다 성공을 두고 부정적인 생각과 씨름하고 있는지도 모르겠네요.” 애비가 곰곰이 말했다.

“그럴 가능성이 크죠.” 샌드라가 대답했다. “그녀의 두려움을 가라앉혀 함께 생산적으로 일할 수 있도록 해 보세요. 그녀의 행동에 반응하지는 말고요.”

샌드라처럼 저도 또래들이 좋은 소식을 나누거나 그들의 성취를 보았을 때 비판적인 생각을 한 적이 있습니다. 그런 생각을 즉시 다스리지 않으면, 그 작은 질투심 때문에 다른 사람을 기뻐하지 못하게 됩니다.

성경은 시기와 질투의 잔혹함을 묘사합니다. 질투는 무덤처럼 잔인합니다. (아가 8:6 참조). 시기는 뼈의 썩음이니라 –잠언 14:30. 또한, 분은 잔인하고 노는 창수 같거니와 투기 앞에야 누가 서리요 –잠언 27:4. 질투는 아주 교묘합니다. 경건함의 아우라로 가려질 수 있습니다. 질투는 지금 나의 관계를 파괴할 가능성이 있을 뿐 아니라, 내 자녀와 손자녀의 관계도 파괴할 수 있습니다.

여성들은 질투하기로 작정하지 않습니다. “오늘은 질투해야지”라고 말하지 않지요. 질투가 언제 마음에 들어오는지, 아니면 마음속에 있기는 한 건지조차 알아차리기 어려울 때가 많습니다. 하지만 다른 사람을 기뻐하기 어렵다면, 어쩌면 우리의 영혼을 살펴볼 때인지도 모릅니다. 질투가 어떻게, 어디서 자라나는지, 곧 우리 각자의 마음속에서 자라난다는 것을 알 때 우리는 질투와 맞서 싸울 준비를 갖추게 됩니다.

또래들은 우리의 기쁨을 시험합니다

일반적으로 우리는 가까운 사이가 아닌 사람들을 시기하지 않습니다. 전 세계의 여성들이 결혼하고, 아기를 낳고, 새집으로 이사하지만 우리는 거의 알아차리지 못합니다. 그러나 시간적·공간적으로 가깝거나 나이 또는 평판이 비슷한 사람들이 우리가 바라는 축복을 누릴 때는 함께 기뻐하기가 어렵습니다. 중요한 일을 알리는 들뜬 전화 한 통이 기뻐하는 친구와 함께 기뻐하겠다는 제 결심을 시험한 적이 한두 번이 아닙니다. 하나님은 그 씨름을 이해하시며, 제가 안식과 수용에 이르도록 이끄십니다.

질투를 알아차리십시오

질투한다는 말의 뜻은 ‘누군가 또는 그 사람의 성취와 이점을 시기하거나 시기심을 드러내는 것’입니다. 질투는 여러 방식으로 드러나는데, 또래를 따라 하고 싶어 하는 것도 그중 하나입니다. 질투는 다른 사람의 성취를 깎아내리고, 다른 이들이 그 사람을 어떻게 생각할지를 통제하려 합니다. 질투는 영적인 거품 속에서 우쭐해하며 다른 사람의 고통과 실패를 기뻐합니다. 질투하는 사람들은 왜곡된 진실을 퍼뜨려 소문이 끊이지 않게 합니다.

생각을 지키십시오

질투는 생각에서 시작됩니다. 의심에 사로잡히거나 다른 사람을 시기하면 진실이 왜곡됩니다. 진실이라고 여기는 것이 거짓이기 때문에 이는 위험합니다.

누군가가 친교 모임에 아름다운 디저트를 가져왔다고 해서 그 사람이 교만하다고 단정합니다. 또는 한 자매가 요양원에 있는 여성을 방문했다는 이유로 살림을 소홀히 하는 사람이라고 생각합니다. 왜 그럴까요? 우리는 자신의 동기를 기준으로 다른 사람을 판단하는 경향이 있습니다. 죄책감이나 자기 정당화, 시기심 때문에 노인을 방문하는 사람에게 ‘살림을 소홀히 한다’는 딱지를 붙이는 것은 아닐까요? 그 자매가 그 방문을 얼마나 오래 생각해 왔는지, 남편이 어떻게 그 일을 가능하게 했는지는 우리는 모릅니다. 분열을 일으키는 생각이 말로 옮겨지면 경건한 여성들 사이에 큰 혼란을 일으킵니다. 교회 지도자들에게 불필요한 일을 더하고 성도 공동체의 성장을 저해합니다.

“인생은 공평하지 않다”는 생각을 받아들이십시오

때로는 누군가가 여러분이 바라는 것을 갖게 됩니다. 반대로 다른 여성이 바라는 것을 여러분이 갖게 될 때도 있습니다. “인생은 공평하지 않다”는 것은 우리가 바꿀 수 없는 삶의 현실입니다. 우리가 할 수 있는 일은 태도를 조정하는 것뿐입니다.

같은 교회에 다니는 친구 두 사람이 있었는데, 둘 다 데이트를 시작할 나이의 딸이 있었습니다. 인생의 흐름에 따라 한 딸은 데이트를 하고 결혼했지만, 다른 딸은 교제를 시작하기도 훨씬 전이었습니다. 미혼인 딸의 어머니는 친구와 그 딸을 기뻐하기로 마음먹었습니다. 그 결과 두 어머니는 여전히 친구이고, 딸들도 친구이며, 그들의 자녀들도 친구가 될 가능성이 큽니다.

자신의 축복을 헤아리십시오

다른 사람의 축복을 바라보며 비교하면 행복하고 만족하기가 어려워집니다. 사도 바울은 이에 대해 경고합니다. 그들이 자기로서 자기를 헤아리고 자기로서 자기를 비교하니 지혜가 없도다 –고린도후서 10:12. 이미 가진 것을 감사히 여기지 않는 여성들에게는 행복이 찾아오지 않을 것입니다. 그런 여성들은 기뻐하는 사람들과 함께 기뻐하지도 못할 것입니다.

그리스도 안에서 자신이 누구인지 아십시오

질투는 두려움과 불안감에서 비롯됩니다. 하나님은 자신의 존귀와 영광을 위해 여러분을 창조하셨습니다. 경쟁할 필요가 없습니다. 오히려 예수님 안에서 자신이 누구인지 알고 만족해야 합니다. 너희가 그 은혜를 인하여 믿음으로 말미암아 구원을 얻었나니 이것이 너희에게서 난 것이 아니요 하나님의 선물이라 행위에서 난 것이 아니니 이는 누구든지 자랑치 못하게 함이니라 우리는 그의 만드신 바라 그리스도 예수 안에서 선한 일을 위하여 지으심을 받은 자니 이 일은 하나님이 전에 예비하사 우리로 그 가운데서 행하게 하려 하심이니라 –에베소서 2:8-10.

경쟁자가 아니라 친구를 두십시오

경쟁자가 있다고 인정하기를 주저할 수도 있지만, 친구의 삶에 있는 축복을 함께 기뻐하지 못한다면 그 친구는 경쟁자가 되고 말 것입니다. 정기적으로 그녀를 위해 기도하며 하나님께서 그녀에게 복을 주시도록 간구하십시오. 의심을 내려놓고 그녀에게 친절을 베풀면 여러분 안에 자라난 부정적인 감정을 가라앉히는 데 도움이 됩니다.

성경은 형제(또는 자매)에 대한 미움에 관해 분명히 말합니다. 빛 가운데 있다 하며 그 형제를 미워하는 자는 지금까지 어두운 가운데 있는 자요 그의 형제를 사랑하는 자는 빛 가운데 거하여 자기 속에 거리낌이 없으나 그의 형제를 미워하는 자는 어두운 가운데 있고 또 어두운 가운데 행하며 갈 곳을 알지 못하나니 이는 어두움이 그의 눈을 멀게 하였음이니라 –요한일서 2:9-11.

질투를 감사와 만족으로 바꾸십시오

부정적인 생각은 초대하지 않아도 찾아오지만, 그것을 붙들어 둘지 떠나보낼지는 우리가 결정할 수 있습니다. 진실에 주의를 돌리는 법을 배우십시오. 빌립보서는 훌륭한 지침을 줍니다. 끝으로 형제들[자매들]아 무엇에든지 참되며 무엇에든지 경건하며 무엇에든지 옳으며 무엇에든지 정결하며 무엇에든지 사랑할 만하며 무엇에든지 칭찬할 만하며 무슨 덕이 있든지 무슨 기림이 있든지 이것들을 생각하라 –빌립보서 4:8.

하나님과 우리 자신, 그리고 동료 여성들과 화평할 때 우리는 자신의 능력과 하나님께서 우리를 두신 형편에 만족하게 됩니다. 하나님께 초점을 맞추면 기쁨을 얻고 기뻐하는 사람들과 함께 기뻐할 힘을 얻게 됩니다.
