Una cosa che ho notato ripetutamente leggendo la Parola di Dio è che il popolo di Dio è fiducioso. Pensiamo a Noè. Quando Dio gli disse di costruire un’arca, non esitò. Per i successivi 120 anni si dedicò proprio a questo con fiducia. Poi penso ad Abramo, che faceva con fiducia tutto ciò che Dio gli chiedeva, anche quando gli chiese di sacrificare il suo unico figlio. Non possiamo parlare di fiducia senza menzionare Caleb e Giosuè, i quali, dopo aver ascoltato i resoconti pieni di dubbi di tutti i loro compagni, descrissero con fiducia ciò che avrebbero dovuto fare con questa nuova terra di Canaan: …Saliamo subito e conquistiamola, perché siamo ben in grado di superarla –Numeri 13:30.

Non possiamo dimenticare Davide, che andò ad affrontare e zittì il grande detrattore: Golia. Né possiamo dimenticare Daniele, Gedeone, Giobbe, Ezechiele, Isaia o Geremia, e tutto ciò che fecero con fiducia. Studiando ciascuno di questi uomini di fede, e molti altri, vediamo chiaramente che avevano grande fiducia nel loro Dio!

Alcuni potrebbero dire che, se Dio operasse oggi nello stesso modo in cui operava allora, avremmo più fiducia. Forse, se Dio fosse ancora un Dio dell’Antico Testamento, sarebbe più facile. Se ci guidasse in battaglia, distruggesse i nostri nemici, aprisse i mari e facesse cadere dal cielo il pane, avremmo più fiducia in Lui.

Consideriamo ora il Nuovo Testamento. È ben diverso. Al popolo di Dio viene comandato di lasciare ogni cosa per amore di Cristo. Gli viene promesso che il mondo lo odierà. Gli viene detto che è difficile per un ricco entrare nel regno di Dio. Gli viene assicurato che sarà beato se soffrirà, se sarà povero, se avrà fame e se farà cordoglio.

Le persone possono ancora avere fiducia in un Dio che chiede al suo popolo di seguirlo in queste circostanze? Sì! I discepoli lo hanno dimostrato. Andavano predicando e insegnando. Furono braccati e percossi più e più volte. Il diacono Stefano dimostrò grande fiducia quando fu condotto davanti ai suoi oppressori, anche quando questi cominciarono a digrignare i denti contro di lui e a lapidarlo. Stefano dimostrò fiducia fino all’ultimo respiro, straziante.

Prima di diventare l’apostolo Paolo, Saulo era nemico della croce, il principale dei peccatori e un fariseo tra i farisei. Era un uomo influente, istruito dai migliori. Poi incontrò il Dio vivente e tutto cambiò. Dopo che Paolo fu battezzato, …subito si mise a predicare nelle sinagoghe che Gesù è il Figlio di Dio –Atti 9:20. Il versetto successivo dice che la gente era stupita; poi, al versetto 23, cinque versetti dopo il suo battesimo, si legge che i Giudei si accordarono per ucciderlo.

Ci vuole molta fiducia in Dio per cambiare un uomo così, per indurlo a cambiare completamente schieramento da un giorno all’altro. Secondo la sua stessa testimonianza, Paolo fu fedele fino alla morte: Quanto a me, io sto per essere offerto in libazione, e il tempo della mia partenza è giunto. Ho combattuto il buon combattimento, ho finito la corsa, ho serbato la fede: –2 Timoteo 4:6-7.

Dio fece cose straordinarie nel Nuovo Testamento. Guarì i ciechi e risuscitò i morti. Liberò i prigionieri e colpì a morte delle persone. Alcuni potrebbero dire che sarebbe più facile avere grande fiducia in Dio se vivessimo ancora nei tempi biblici del Nuovo Testamento, quando Gesù camminava e parlava fisicamente qui sulla terra.

E dopo la Bibbia?

Nella chiesa primitiva vediamo ancora un gruppo di persone che non vacillava; avevano fiducia nel loro Dio, un Dio che non potevano vedere. Decine di migliaia di persone del popolo di Dio si presentarono con coraggio davanti al mondo e ne proclamarono la malvagità, e decine di migliaia di persone del popolo di Dio furono uccise. La fiducia di queste persone non fu mai messa in dubbio. Furono chiamate stolte perché credevano in un «Dio che non potevano vedere». Furono derise e disprezzate per la loro «stoltezza»; furono …uccise tutto il giorno… –Salmo 44:22. La gente metteva in discussione le loro pratiche, la loro struttura religiosa, il messaggio che predicavano e molte altre cose, ma non mise mai in dubbio la loro fiducia. Questi cristiani credevano nel loro Dio, e non c’era alcun dubbio al riguardo.

Stranamente, non erano interessati ai piaceri di questa vita; non si curavano delle cose di questo mondo, e persino la loro stessa vita era un piccolo prezzo da pagare per il loro Dio. Le famiglie venivano smembrate, case e terreni confiscati, le chiese bruciate, ma questo non li fermava. Vivevano per qualcosa di più grande, qualcosa che i pagani non potevano capire.

Durante il periodo della chiesa primitiva e quello della Riforma, moltissime persone furono aggiunte al Regno. Sì, i figli crescevano e si univano alla chiesa dei loro genitori, ma vi erano anche grandi masse di nuovi convertiti provenienti dal mondo. Come si poteva convincere una persona mondana a unirsi a un gruppo braccato e ucciso, un gruppo che soffriva come soffriva la chiesa di Gesù Cristo? Sì, sappiamo che la salvezza viene dal Signore, ma fu la fiducia del popolo di Dio a suscitare la curiosità degli altri, a indurli a prendere seriamente in considerazione questa nuova religione di eretici. Era un gruppo di persone che avrebbe accettato volentieri la spoliazione dei propri beni, sarebbe stato felice di dare tutto ciò che aveva per aiutare gli altri e non avrebbe opposto resistenza alla propria cattura da parte delle autorità. La vera chiesa di Gesù Cristo era un gruppo di persone che suscitava sempre negli altri la domanda: «Chi sono queste persone?». Riponevano chiaramente tutta la loro fede nel loro Dio, cosa tutt’altro che comune. Si battevano per la Verità di Dio, indipendentemente da quanto ardesse il fuoco e da quanto rendessero miserabili le loro vite. Tutto questo dimostrava grande fiducia, non in loro stessi, ma nel loro Dio.

Guardando alla chiesa di oggi, che cosa vediamo? Alcuni del popolo di Dio prendono la loro croce e rinnegano il mondo e le sue concupiscenze, altri no. La chiesa di oggi è ancora nota per la fiducia che ripone nel suo Dio?

Come cristiani professanti, abbiamo perso parte di questa fiducia biblica? Siamo ancora là fuori a servire senza riserve l’unico vero Dio? Le persone ci guardano e restano meravigliate della fiducia che dimostriamo nel nostro Dio? Troppe persone oggi dicono di essere cristiane, ma dimostrano ben poca fiducia in Dio. Vivono in modo assai simile a quello del mondo. Invece di rallegrarsi della persecuzione, si godono molte delle stesse cose di cui si gode il mondo. Ognuno di noi ha bisogno del fuoco di Dio che arde nel profondo del cuore, un fuoco che non può essere estinto.

La fiducia equivale all’ubbidienza. Ho incontrato molti cristiani dei nostri giorni i cui antenati hanno dato la vita per Cristo e i cui nonni guidavano coraggiosamente la chiesa, ma ora sembra che manchi qualcosa. Interagendo con molti cristiani timorati di Dio, mi sembra che vi sia una lotta diffusa con la fiducia: la fiducia in un Dio vivente, onnipotente, onnisciente e onnipresente.

Nell’incertezza del mondo di oggi, dobbiamo proclamare di nuovo con coraggio il messaggio del Vangelo, proprio come fecero i veri credenti in passato. Dobbiamo tracciare con chiarezza linee bibliche nette tra il bene e il male. Dobbiamo liberarci di tutte queste miserabili zone grigie e chiamare il peccato col suo nome. Sembra che abbiamo perso la fiducia necessaria per parlare contro il peccato dei nostri giorni. Se proclamiamo con fiducia ciò che Dio ha dichiarato, ci saranno persone a cui non piaceremo. Abbiamo bisogno di fratelli che non abbiano paura di essere derisi e siano disposti a percorrere la strada meno battuta.

Poco prima che il nostro Signore salisse in cielo, diede ai suoi discepoli una gloriosa promessa: …riceverete potenza quando lo Spirito Santo verrà su voi, e mi sarete testimoni in Gerusalemme, e in tutta la Giudea e Samaria, e fino all’estremità della terra –Atti 1:8.

Riceverete potenza! Non potenza dagli uomini, non potenza dai regni di questo mondo, ma una potenza reale, che vince: una potenza che viene soltanto dallo Spirito Santo! Dopo aver ricevuto questa potenza, andiamo avanti come nuove creature, proclamando con fiducia il benedetto Vangelo del nostro Redentore.

Abbiamo bisogno di cuori che ardano del volere e della parola di Dio. Abbiamo bisogno di cuori in fiamme!

Un giorno stavo pranzando quando una coppia si avvicinò a me con una domanda seria: «Perché la chiesa pensa di doverci controllare?». Dopo che mi ebbero spiegato perché pensavano di dover essere «liberi in Cristo», ero impaziente di rispondere alle loro domande. Tuttavia, accanto a me sedeva un altro fratello ordinato. Decisi quindi di aspettare, sperando che interagisse con la coppia, ma non disse nulla. Dopo altri quarantacinque minuti, cercai di spiegare alla coppia che dovevano rinnegare se stessi e sottomettersi alla chiesa. E che, se avessero deposto interamente la propria vita, se si fossero arresi completamente, non avrebbero più avuto una simile difficoltà con la struttura della chiesa.

La coppia sembrò incoraggiata e pronta a riprovarci. Tuttavia, il ministro accanto a me non sembrava molto contento, così gli chiesi che cosa ne pensasse. Disse che anni prima suo padre gli aveva raccontato che, da giovane, pensava di avere tutte le risposte. Quando era invecchiato, si era reso conto di non sapere nulla e che le questioni della chiesa erano troppo complicate da risolvere. Dovevamo semplicemente cercare di andare d’accordo.

È questa la risposta: comportarci come se non sapessimo nulla e sperare che alla fine tutto si risolva? Capisco che non abbiamo tutte le risposte. Dopo tutto, mi rendo conto che il più delle volte ho più domande che risposte. Tuttavia, so che cosa vuole Dio per la sua chiesa! …Cristo ha amato la chiesa e ha dato se stesso per lei, per santificarla, avendola purificata col lavacro dell’acqua per mezzo della parola, affinché egli stesso si presentasse la chiesa gloriosa, senza macchia, senza ruga o altri simili difetti, ma santa e irreprensibile –Efesini 5:25-27.

Una chiesa gloriosa, senza macchia, senza ruga o alcunché di simile, ma santa e irreprensibile! Noi, popolo di Dio, torneremo a difendere la verità, a rinnegare il mondo e, come pecore, ci lasceremo condurre al macello? Oppure abbiamo reso le nostre vite troppo comode per poter rinnegare noi stessi, abbiamo scelto la via facile (larga) e rinnegato quella stretta e angusta? Abbiamo firmato un accordo di pace con i servitori del peccato? Se piango mentre scrivo, piangerai mentre leggi?

La definizione della parola fiducia è un sentimento o la consapevolezza delle proprie capacità. Oggi molte persone confondono la fiducia con l’orgoglio, e a ragione. La maggior parte delle persone fiduciose ripone fiducia in se stessa, anziché in Cristo. Vediamo questa sicurezza di sé tutt’intorno a noi. In tutto il mondo ci sono life coach e consulenti che dicono alle persone di credere in se stesse, di avere fiducia in se stesse. Quando una persona ha fiducia in se stessa, spesso diventa orgogliosa. Ricordate che il mondo non disprezza l’orgoglio. Ovunque guardiate, sentite il mondo vantarsi del proprio orgoglio. Le persone sono orgogliose dei propri figli, del proprio paese, della propria squadra sportiva preferita, dei propri prati, praticamente di tutto ciò che va bene nella loro vita. Dobbiamo ricordare che l’orgoglio è peccato e non entrerà in cielo. Mentre la fiducia in se stessi o nelle cose è orgoglio, la fiducia in Dio non lo è!

Confondere la fiducia in Dio con l’orgoglio non è un’idea nuova. Eliab, il fratello maggiore di Davide, gli disse: «Conosco il tuo orgoglio». Davide era orgoglioso? No, semplicemente riponeva grande fiducia nel suo Dio.

È possibile che un falso senso di umiltà abbia messo a tacere la chiesa? È possibile che questa tattica del nemico sia una delle armi che Satana usa attualmente contro i cristiani? Potrebbe essere anche il motivo per cui la chiesa sembra attraversare difficoltà in ogni parte del mondo? E se uomini fedeli tornassero a muoversi per fede nel loro Dio con grande fiducia e, con le loro parole e le loro azioni, mostrassero a questo mondo macchiato dal peccato la via stretta e angusta che conduce al Regno di Dio?!

Dobbiamo tutti riconoscere che viviamo in un mondo confuso, confuso su ciò che è giusto e ciò che è sbagliato. E se il mondo potesse guardare alla chiesa e trovare di nuovo un gruppo di persone che sa esattamente dove sta andando, una chiesa che non ha dubbi su quale sia la via giusta, una chiesa che sa proclamare con coraggio la risposta ai problemi dei nostri giorni, una chiesa che non è niente meno che completamente fiduciosa nel suo DIO?

Presentiamoci davanti al nostro Dio in ginocchio, con il cuore umilmente chinato, manifestando un sincero dolore secondo Dio per aver smarrito la strada. Editor’s Note:

Over the last number of years there seems to be a shift occurring on a variety of specific issues for some conservative Anabaptists. This changing of ideas and practice is not happening in a vacuum, rather we are simply following the leader. Once we start researching this matter further, we soon realize that this same migration on issues of faith and practice has been at work for some years now within the greater Evangelical community. Let’s stop and consider whether we are following God’s Word, or man’s influence.

Some Anabaptists are becoming dissatisfied with a traditional structure of church, so they gravitate towards “cell-group church” or “house-church” models. Others react to overbearing and authoritative church leadership from their past and start emphasizing a more democratic function of church. Then there are the folks who are moving away from a “local” church body emphasis to that of focusing more on a “universal” or a “global” church body. Still others don’t have a problem with what is considered “normal” church, instead they are the type that gets tired of the “old-fashioned” and the “boring.” These folks welcome “new ideas” that are presented in present-day books and at various conferences which are held around the country. These conferences are not all intrinsically wrong, nor are they all selling “new” interpretations, yet there are some that bring in “fresh” ideas originating from “outside” sources in the hope that they will bring “new life” to the lack of zeal within the “normal.”

Another area of shift is that of focusing on the Gospels while ignoring specific teachings in the Epistles. Some folks stress that we should “just follow Jesus” while not allowing the teachings of the Apostles to further detail the application of Jesus’ teachings. Others lift up the “Sermon on the Mount,” the “red letter Scriptures,” or walking in the “footsteps of Jesus,” without realizing that a default outcome of this focus tends to leave out specific teachings of the Epistles regarding practical church functioning and Christian living. Some of these include …exhort[ing] one another daily… –Hebrews 3:13, All scripture … is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, [and] for correction… –2 Timothy 3:16, and the fact that we should be careful because Satan and his agents will transform themselves …into the apostles of Christ and present themselves as …an angel of light –2 Corinthians 11:13-14.

Some individuals believe it is wrong for spiritual authorities to “take the oversight thereof,” or to give clear admonition over the pulpit. They shrink back from churches that have ordained leaders, or they don’t like the thought of spiritual authorities in their lives. Others feel their church doesn’t have much to offer so they attend various group events with others of “like precious faith” (who believe as they do), thus developing a disjointed spiritual body of individuals from many various local churches, fellowshipping together at large events. Many times, these believers allow someone outside of their local church fellowship to become their spiritual advisor, thus feeling justified in not giving their loyalty to their church leaders at home. They come to believe that the traditional way of having church the Anabaptist way is “not the way it used to be” or “not according to the early church”. They believe that structured church brings deadness to local bodies, never mind that the Epistles provide clear details on church structure and practice.

Many of these individuals are interacting and fellowshipping so closely with others from various other groups and churches instead of their own home church, that they do not realize they are actually functioning in a very individualistic manner. This manner of being an alone “local” Christian is categorically opposite from the “group spirituality” that our Anabaptist forefathers specifically believed and taught. Another area of misunderstanding in this whole issue, is that there is a very clear difference between the expression of the kingdom now and the kingdom future. Remember that Jesus said, “my kingdom is not of this world,” yet an extreme focus on kingdom this and kingdom that, will by default cause Christians to ignore this Truth, as they try to express the kingdom “on the earth,” and “in the now.”

The full effect of the resurrection and the ascension of Jesus in the life of a believer can never fully be understood without allowing the Epistles to bring more clear application to the Gospels or to the Sermon on the Mount. Simply following the words of Jesus in red ink will never help us know how to be a part of the “power of His resurrection”, or “the fellowship of His sufferings.” For this we need the balance of the rest of the New Testament.

Many of these points will require their own complete article to sort out all the nuances, which we plan to do as the Lord continues to allow time to continue. Considering all this, we felt that this article is a balanced, yet basic introduction to the many issues at stake and we have chosen it based on those thoughts.

Curvin L Wenger

When Jesus blessed Simon Peter for his confident confession that Jesus was the Christ, the Son of the living God –Matthew 16:16, He brought together two overarching New Testament themes: the church and the kingdom—…I will build my church … And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven… –Matthew 16:18-19. Ever since, Christ’s followers have deliberated, with varying opinions, on the meaning and the nature of the kingdom, and its relation to the church.

Jesus began His preaching by declaring that the kingdom of heaven was at hand (see Matthew 4:17). Throughout the Gospels, the kingdom was the unifying theme of His teaching. In fact, Scripture only records two occasions when Christ mentioned the church. The church, on the other hand, is more prominent in the Acts, the Epistles, and the Revelation. Why this difference? Is there some conflict or incompatible tension between what Jesus taught and emphasized, and that of the apostles?

Recent years seem to have brought an increased interest and reference to the kingdom within Evangelical circles as well as conservative Anabaptist circles. Many are using terms such as working for the kingdom, building up the kingdom, growing the kingdom, kingdom service, kingdom finances, and even funding the kingdom. Kingdom Theology has been offered as a course of study, and the expression Kingdom Christian has been coined to demarcate a particular kind of Christian—one who believes and practices Jesus’ teachings. Among many conservative Anabaptist people, kingdom terminology has practically drowned out the language expressed by Eliza Hewitt who wrote, “For Christ and the Church let our voices ring.”

Among the various factors which have nurtured this renewed kingdom emphasis among some Anabaptists, two stand out. Both of these concerns reflect the influence of Christians from without the conservative Anabaptist tradition, yet who profess to be Bible-believing and born-again.

  1. The first is that some people seem to be more concerned about being Biblical than about being Christ-like. We, conservative Anabaptists, can stand on the Bible to formulate all the right doctrines and positions while our lives fall short in reflecting the character and values of Jesus Christ our Lord, the One with whom we claim to be united in a living relationship.
  2. The second matter involves a fixation on the act of getting saved to the neglect of living a saved life; that is, a life of obedient discipleship, particularly to the very teachings of Jesus who we are to follow. While most conservative Anabaptists profess to practice Christ’s teachings, we are not immune to a careless discipleship.

There are individuals within conservative Anabaptism that address these concerns somewhat in the following manner. They say that while Evangelicals believe in the person and work of Christ, they tend to focus on Paul. For all practical purposes, they (Evangelicals) are more concerned about correct Bible interpretations, theological systems, and assenting to correct beliefs than they are with obedient Christian living, particularly regarding the hard teachings of Christ. In contrast, these Anabaptists claim that the kingdom of God, which Jesus inaugurated and was the theme of His teaching, should set the norm for understanding and living the Christian life. Consequently, for them, the Gospels (and the kingdom) then become primary in interpreting the rest of the New Testament.

What do we make of this? While sweeping generalizations don’t do justice to the exceptions and the qualifiers, the concerns are valid, and this critique regarding our Evangelical friends does hold some measure of truth. These things have their roots in the thinking of Augustine (354-430), in the imbalanced Reformation emphasis regarding justification by faith, and in the work of John Calvin. But what about the antidote of focusing mostly on Christ and the kingdom? Certainly, Christ is central to interpreting, not only the New Testament, but actually the entire Bible. And there is value in holding forth those teachings of Christ, which are so often brushed aside, yet are required of any church that would be worthy of His name. However, I would like to offer three points of caution or critique about taking this antidote unreservedly.

Do the Gospels dominate the rest of Scripture?

First, I believe it’s a mistake to assume that the Gospels (the life and teachings of Jesus) should dominate and control the interpretation of the New Testament scriptures. Rather, the New Testament, as it moves through the Gospels, the Acts, the Epistles, and lastly the Revelation, contains a divinely inspired progression of fuller revelation and doctrinal explanation. This is seen when we consider the words of Jesus regarding the coming of the Holy Spirit: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now. Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come –John 16:12-13. Those New Testament books following the Gospels are the anticipated fulfillment of these words. They bring the teachings and work of Christ to full development and understanding.

Christ’s ministry and teaching about the kingdom laid the groundwork, then His death and resurrection placed the foundation on which He would build His church. The Scriptures which follow the Gospels give us greater comprehension about the meaning of Christ’s death on the cross and its relation and effect on us that comes through faith and obedience. It also develops the whole doctrine of the church. So, the entire New Testament fits together in beautiful harmony. Both the Gospels and the Epistles need to be interpreted in reference to each other. The teachings of Christ do not take precedence over the Epistles, rather the Epistles help interpret the Gospels—they give us a more complete understanding and practical application to the principles Christ gave His Disciples.

Does Theology Militate Against Discipleship?

Secondly, we should be careful to not set correct interpretation and correct practice against one another. To say it another way, we should not pit theology against discipleship. To whatever degree some Evangelicals may overemphasize theology at the expense of discipleship, it should not prejudice us into making a whipping boy out of theology. Theology is the study of God and the things of God. We are forming a personal theology when we study God’s Word and compare Scripture with Scripture in our efforts to come to a unified and harmonious understanding of its various parts.

Every Christian has a theology, whether he can express it well or not. Our theology (or doctrinal understanding, if you want to say it that way) is our belief system and the soil out of which our behavior grows. Some theologies are very elementary, others reflect a lifetime of study, most are incomplete, some are inconsistent, others are dogmatic or laced with philosophy, and some are dreadfully wrong. Hopefully, all of us have a growing, and increasingly accurate understanding of God and His Word. This is quite necessary since our theology, which is the sum of our beliefs about God and our understanding of His Word and the Christian life, is what affects our discipleship—our daily walk with God. A good theology undergirds discipleship. A poor theology undermines discipleship.

Are “Kingdom” and “Church” Interchangeable?

Finally, we should think correctly about the kingdom in relation to the church. What is the relationship of the kingdom to the church? The kingdom is not, as contemporary usage would almost have us think, a generic version of, or a substitute word for, the church. Rather, the kingdom has to do with the reign or rule of God. It is both a present reality, having been inaugurated in the person and mission of Jesus, and a future expectation which God will bring to completion at the end of time. The church, while not the kingdom, is composed of those who are in the kingdom; those who, through the work of Christ, have submitted to the rule of God.

While we struggle for the precise word to express the relationship of the kingdom to the church, as a holy, loving, and obedient community of believers, the church is the earthly manifestation of God’s rule—His kingdom. Christ did not say “I will build my kingdom”; rather He said, “I will build my church.” Likewise, Paul did not build kingdom halls; He started churches. It is possible for us to have an idealistic and romantic view of the kingdom that gets separated from the hard work of living on earth with our fellow believers in a local church body. We can elevate the kingdom and diminish the church. We can get enthusiastic about the concept of the kingdom, the teachings of the kingdom, the growth of the kingdom, and conferences about the kingdom, and yet be cynical, critical, and sorry members of our local church.

Do you want to work for the kingdom (see Colossians 4:11)? Then commit yourself wholeheartedly to Christ and His church. That starts with your local church. Love and serve your church. Accept responsibility in it. Be accountable and loyal to your local church. Work for the good and growth of the church—your local church, and beyond.

Timothy Dwight wrote:*

I love Thy Kingdom, Lord,
The house of Thine abode,
The church our blest Redeemer
Saved with His own precious blood.
I love Thy church, O God:
Her walls before Thee stand,
Dear as the apple of Thine eye,
And graven on Thy hand.

What he was saying about the precise relationship of the kingdom to the church may be different from what I conceive it to be. However, what I would like for us to appreciate is that when he thought of the kingdom, he thought of the church. And so should we! Are his words yours, as he writes on?

For her my tears shall fall,
For her my prayers ascend;
To her my cares and toils be giv’n,
Till toils and cares shall end.
Beyond my highest joy
I prize her heav’nly ways,
Her sweet communion, solemn vows,
Her hymns of love and praise.

* See page 32 for the entire song.

De afgelopen jaren lijkt er op allerlei specifieke punten een verschuiving plaats te vinden onder sommige conservatieve anabaptisten. Deze verandering in ideeën en praktijk gebeurt niet in een vacuüm; we volgen eenvoudigweg de leider. Zodra we deze kwestie verder onderzoeken, beseffen we al snel dat dezelfde verschuiving op het gebied van geloof en praktijk al enkele jaren gaande is binnen de bredere evangelische gemeenschap. Laten we stilstaan bij de vraag of we Gods Woord volgen of de invloed van mensen.

Sommige anabaptisten raken ontevreden met een traditionele kerkstructuur en voelen zich daarom aangetrokken tot modellen als de ‘celgroepkerk’ of de ‘huiskerk’. Anderen reageren op de overheersende en autoritaire kerkleiding uit hun verleden en beginnen de nadruk te leggen op een meer democratische manier van functioneren van de kerk. Dan zijn er mensen die de nadruk verleggen van een ‘plaatselijke’ kerkgemeenschap naar een ‘universele’ of ‘wereldwijde’ kerkgemeenschap. Weer anderen hebben geen probleem met wat als een ‘normale’ kerk wordt beschouwd; zij zijn eerder het type dat de ‘ouderwetse’ en ‘saaie’ kerk beu wordt. Deze mensen verwelkomen ‘nieuwe ideeën’ die worden gepresenteerd in hedendaagse boeken en op allerlei conferenties die in het hele land worden gehouden. Deze conferenties zijn niet allemaal per se verkeerd en ze verkopen ook niet allemaal ‘nieuwe’ interpretaties, maar sommige brengen ‘frisse’ ideeën van ‘buitenaf’ binnen, in de hoop dat die ‘nieuw leven’ zullen brengen in het gebrek aan ijver binnen de ‘normale’ kerk.

Een ander gebied waarop een verschuiving zichtbaar is, betreft de nadruk op de Evangeliën, terwijl specifieke leringen in de Brieven worden genegeerd. Sommige mensen benadrukken dat we ‘gewoon Jezus moeten volgen’, zonder de leringen van de apostelen toe te staan de toepassing van Jezus’ leringen nader uiteen te zetten. Anderen verheffen de ‘Bergrede’, de ‘roodgedrukte Schriftgedeelten’ of het wandelen in de ‘voetsporen van Jezus’, zonder te beseffen dat deze nadruk er doorgaans toe leidt dat specifieke leringen uit de Brieven over het praktische functioneren van de kerk en het christelijke leven buiten beschouwing blijven. Enkele voorbeelden hiervan zijn: …vermaant elkaar dagelijks… –Hebreeën 3:13; Heel de Schrift … is nuttig om te onderwijzen, te weerleggen [en] te verbeteren… –2 Timotheüs 3:16; en het feit dat we voorzichtig moeten zijn, omdat Satan en zijn dienaren zich zullen veranderen …in apostelen van Christus en zich zullen voordoen als …een engel van het licht –2 Korintiërs 11:13-14.

Sommige mensen geloven dat het verkeerd is wanneer geestelijke leiders ‘opzicht houden’, of vanaf de preekstoel duidelijke vermaningen geven. Ze deinzen terug voor kerken met aangestelde leiders, of houden niet van het idee dat er geestelijke autoriteiten in hun leven zijn. Anderen vinden dat hun kerk weinig te bieden heeft en wonen daarom allerlei groepsbijeenkomsten bij met anderen van ‘hetzelfde kostbare geloof’ (die geloven zoals zij), waardoor een onsamenhangend geestelijk lichaam ontstaat van mensen uit allerlei plaatselijke kerken die op grote bijeenkomsten samenkomen. Vaak laten deze gelovigen iemand buiten de gemeenschap van hun plaatselijke kerk hun geestelijk raadgever worden, en voelen ze zich zo gerechtvaardigd om hun kerkleiders thuis niet trouw te zijn. Ze gaan geloven dat de traditionele anabaptistische manier van kerk-zijn ‘niet meer is zoals vroeger’ of ‘niet overeenkomt met de vroege kerk’. Ze menen dat een gestructureerde kerk plaatselijke gemeenschappen levenloos maakt, terwijl de Brieven juist duidelijke details geven over de structuur en praktijk van de kerk.

Veel van deze mensen gaan zo nauw om met en onderhouden zo intensief contact met anderen uit allerlei andere groepen en kerken, in plaats van met hun eigen thuisgemeente, dat ze niet beseffen dat ze in feite op een zeer individualistische manier functioneren. Deze manier van een eenzame ‘plaatselijke’ christen zijn, staat lijnrecht tegenover de ‘gemeenschappelijke spiritualiteit’ waarin onze anabaptistische voorouders specifiek geloofden en die ze onderwezen. Een ander misverstand in deze hele kwestie is dat er een heel duidelijk verschil bestaat tussen de uitdrukking van het koninkrijk nu en het koninkrijk in de toekomst. Bedenk dat Jezus zei: ‘Mijn koninkrijk is niet van deze wereld’; een extreme nadruk op het koninkrijk hier en het koninkrijk daar zal christenen echter vanzelf ertoe brengen deze Waarheid te negeren, terwijl ze proberen het koninkrijk ‘op aarde’ en ‘nu’ tot uitdrukking te brengen.

De volle betekenis van de opstanding en hemelvaart van Jezus in het leven van een gelovige kan nooit ten volle worden begrepen zonder toe te staan dat de Brieven de Evangeliën of de Bergrede nader toepassen. Alleen de woorden van Jezus in rode letters volgen, zal ons nooit helpen begrijpen hoe we deel kunnen hebben aan ‘de kracht van Zijn opstanding’ of ‘de gemeenschap aan Zijn lijden’. Daarvoor hebben we het evenwicht nodig van de rest van het Nieuwe Testament.

Veel van deze punten verdienen een eigen volledig artikel om alle nuances uit te werken. Dat zijn we van plan te doen zolang de Heer ons de tijd daarvoor blijft geven. Met dit alles in gedachten vonden we dat dit artikel een evenwichtige, maar elementaire inleiding biedt op de vele kwesties die op het spel staan, en op grond daarvan hebben we het gekozen.

Curvin L Wenger

Toen Jezus Simon Petrus zegende vanwege zijn krachtige belijdenis dat Jezus de Christus, de Zoon van de levende God was –Mattheüs 16:16, bracht Hij twee overkoepelende thema’s van het Nieuwe Testament samen: de kerk en het koninkrijk—…Ik zal Mijn kerk bouwen … En Ik zal u de sleutels van het Koninkrijk der hemelen geven… –Mattheüs 16:18-19. Sindsdien hebben de volgelingen van Christus met uiteenlopende opvattingen nagedacht over de betekenis en aard van het koninkrijk en de relatie ervan tot de kerk.

Jezus begon Zijn prediking met de verklaring dat het Koninkrijk der hemelen nabij was (zie Mattheüs 4:17). In de hele Evangeliën vormde het koninkrijk het verbindende thema van Zijn onderwijs. In feite vermeldt de Schrift slechts twee gelegenheden waarop Christus de kerk noemde. De kerk staat daarentegen meer op de voorgrond in Handelingen, de Brieven en Openbaring. Hoe komt dat? Is er een conflict of onverenigbare spanning tussen wat Jezus onderwees en benadrukte en wat de apostelen onderwezen?

De afgelopen jaren lijkt er in evangelische kringen en onder conservatieve anabaptisten meer belangstelling te zijn ontstaan voor het koninkrijk en verwijzingen ernaar. Velen gebruiken uitdrukkingen als werken voor het koninkrijk, het koninkrijk opbouwen, het koninkrijk laten groeien, dienst aan het koninkrijk, financiën voor het koninkrijk en zelfs het koninkrijk financieren. Koninkrijkstheologie wordt als studieonderwerp aangeboden en de uitdrukking Koninkrijkschristen is bedacht om een bepaald soort christen aan te duiden: iemand die Jezus’ leringen gelooft en in praktijk brengt. Onder veel conservatieve anabaptisten heeft de terminologie van het koninkrijk de taal die Eliza Hewitt gebruikte bijna verdrongen toen ze schreef: ‘Voor Christus en de kerk klinken onze stemmen.’

Van de verschillende factoren die deze hernieuwde nadruk op het koninkrijk onder sommige anabaptisten hebben gevoed, springen er twee uit. Beide zorgen weerspiegelen de invloed van christenen van buiten de conservatieve anabaptistische traditie, die desondanks belijden dat ze de Bijbel geloven en wedergeboren zijn.

  1. De eerste is dat sommige mensen meer bezorgd lijken te zijn om bijbels te zijn dan om op Christus te lijken. Wij, conservatieve anabaptisten, kunnen ons op de Bijbel beroepen om alle juiste leerstellingen en standpunten te formuleren, terwijl ons leven tekortschiet in het weerspiegelen van het karakter en de waarden van Jezus Christus, onze Heer, met Wie we zeggen een levende relatie te hebben.
  2. De tweede kwestie betreft een fixatie op de daad van gered worden, ten koste van een gered leven leiden; dat wil zeggen, een leven van gehoorzaam discipelschap, in het bijzonder gehoorzaamheid aan juist de leringen van Jezus, die we moeten volgen. Hoewel de meeste conservatieve anabaptisten belijden dat ze de leringen van Christus in praktijk brengen, zijn ook wij niet immuun voor achteloos discipelschap.

Sommigen binnen het conservatieve anabaptisme behandelen deze zorgen ongeveer als volgt. Ze zeggen dat evangelischen wel geloven in de persoon en het werk van Christus, maar geneigd zijn zich op Paulus te richten. In de praktijk maken zij (evangelischen) zich meer zorgen over juiste Bijbelinterpretaties, theologische systemen en het instemmen met juiste overtuigingen dan over gehoorzaam christelijk leven, vooral als het gaat om de moeilijke leringen van Christus. Daartegenover beweren deze anabaptisten dat het koninkrijk van God, dat Jezus inluidde en dat het thema van Zijn onderwijs vormde, de norm moet bepalen voor het begrijpen en leiden van het christelijke leven. Daarom worden voor hen de Evangeliën (en het koninkrijk) leidend bij de interpretatie van de rest van het Nieuwe Testament.

Wat moeten we hiervan denken? Hoewel algemene uitspraken geen recht doen aan uitzonderingen en nuanceringen, zijn de zorgen terecht en bevat deze kritiek op onze evangelische vrienden een zekere kern van waarheid. Deze zaken vinden hun oorsprong in het denken van Augustinus (354-430), in de onevenwichtige nadruk van de Reformatie op rechtvaardiging door geloof en in het werk van Johannes Calvijn. Maar hoe zit het met het tegengif van een overwegende nadruk op Christus en het koninkrijk? Christus staat zeker centraal bij de interpretatie, niet alleen van het Nieuwe Testament, maar van de hele Bijbel. En het is waardevol om die leringen van Christus uit te dragen die zo vaak terzijde worden geschoven, maar die vereist zijn van iedere kerk die Zijn naam waardig wil zijn. Toch wil ik drie aandachtspunten of kritische opmerkingen naar voren brengen over het zonder voorbehoud aanvaarden van dit tegengif.

Overheersen de Evangeliën de rest van de Schrift?

Ten eerste geloof ik dat het een vergissing is om aan te nemen dat de Evangeliën (het leven en de leringen van Jezus) de interpretatie van de nieuwtestamentische geschriften zouden moeten overheersen en bepalen. Het Nieuwe Testament bevat juist, terwijl het achtereenvolgens door de Evangeliën, Handelingen, de Brieven en ten slotte Openbaring gaat, een door God geïnspireerde voortgang van steeds vollere openbaring en leerstellige uitleg. Dat blijkt wanneer we nadenken over Jezus’ woorden met betrekking tot de komst van de Heilige Geest: Ik heb u nog veel te zeggen, maar u kunt het nu niet dragen. Maar wanneer Hij komt, de Geest van de waarheid, zal Hij u de weg wijzen in heel de waarheid; want Hij zal niet vanuit Zichzelf spreken, maar wat Hij hoort, zal Hij spreken, en de toekomstige dingen zal Hij u verkondigen –Johannes 16:12-13. De nieuwtestamentische boeken die op de Evangeliën volgen, zijn de verwachte vervulling van deze woorden. Ze werken de leringen en het werk van Christus volledig uit en helpen ons die te begrijpen.

Christus’ dienstwerk en onderwijs over het koninkrijk legden het fundament; vervolgens vormden Zijn dood en opstanding het fundament waarop Hij Zijn kerk zou bouwen. De Schriftgedeelten die op de Evangeliën volgen, geven ons meer inzicht in de betekenis van Christus’ dood aan het kruis en in de relatie en uitwerking ervan op ons, die door geloof en gehoorzaamheid tot stand komt. Ook werken ze de volledige leer over de kerk uit. Zo vormt het hele Nieuwe Testament een prachtige harmonie. Zowel de Evangeliën als de Brieven moeten met verwijzing naar elkaar worden geïnterpreteerd. De leringen van Christus gaan niet boven de Brieven; de Brieven helpen juist de Evangeliën te interpreteren — ze geven ons een vollediger begrip van de beginselen die Christus Zijn discipelen gaf en een praktische toepassing daarvan.

Staat theologie discipelschap in de weg?

Ten tweede moeten we ervoor oppassen de juiste interpretatie en de juiste praktijk niet tegenover elkaar te plaatsen. Anders gezegd: we moeten theologie niet tegenover discipelschap zetten. In welke mate sommige evangelischen theologie misschien overbeklemtonen ten koste van discipelschap, dat mag ons er niet toe brengen theologie tot zondebok te maken. Theologie is de studie van God en de dingen van God. We vormen een persoonlijke theologie wanneer we Gods Woord bestuderen en Schrift met Schrift vergelijken in onze pogingen om tot een samenhangend en harmonieus begrip van de verschillende delen ervan te komen.

Elke christen heeft een theologie, of hij die nu goed onder woorden kan brengen of niet. Onze theologie (of ons leerstellige begrip, als u het zo wilt noemen) is ons geheel van overtuigingen en de bodem waaruit ons gedrag groeit. Sommige theologieën zijn heel elementair, andere weerspiegelen een leven lang studie; de meeste zijn onvolledig, sommige zijn tegenstrijdig, andere zijn dogmatisch of doorspekt met filosofie, en sommige zijn verschrikkelijk verkeerd. Hopelijk groeien we allemaal in ons begrip van God en Zijn Woord en wordt dat begrip steeds nauwkeuriger. Dat is absoluut noodzakelijk, want onze theologie — de som van onze overtuigingen over God en ons begrip van Zijn Woord en het christelijke leven — beïnvloedt ons discipelschap, onze dagelijkse wandel met God. Een goede theologie ondersteunt discipelschap. Een gebrekkige theologie ondermijnt discipelschap.

Zijn ‘koninkrijk’ en ‘kerk’ onderling verwisselbaar?

Ten slotte moeten we op de juiste manier nadenken over de relatie tussen het koninkrijk en de kerk. Wat is de relatie van het koninkrijk tot de kerk? Het koninkrijk is, anders dan het hedendaagse gebruik ons bijna wil doen geloven, niet een algemene versie van de kerk of een vervangend woord voor de kerk. Het koninkrijk heeft veeleer te maken met Gods heerschappij of regering. Het is zowel een huidige werkelijkheid, die is ingeluid in de persoon en zending van Jezus, als een toekomstige verwachting, die God aan het einde van de tijd tot voltooiing zal brengen. De kerk is niet het koninkrijk, maar bestaat uit degenen die in het koninkrijk zijn: zij die zich door het werk van Christus aan Gods heerschappij hebben onderworpen.

Hoewel we zoeken naar het juiste woord om de relatie tussen het koninkrijk en de kerk als een heilige, liefdevolle en gehoorzame gemeenschap van gelovigen uit te drukken, is de kerk de aardse manifestatie van Gods heerschappij — Zijn koninkrijk. Christus zei niet: ‘Ik zal Mijn koninkrijk bouwen’; Hij zei juist: ‘Ik zal Mijn kerk bouwen.’ Evenzo bouwde Paulus geen koninkrijkszalen; hij stichtte kerken. Het is mogelijk dat we een idealistisch en romantisch beeld van het koninkrijk hebben, los van het zware werk van het leven op aarde met onze medegelovigen in een plaatselijke kerkgemeenschap. We kunnen het koninkrijk verheffen en de kerk kleineren. We kunnen enthousiast zijn over het begrip koninkrijk, de leringen van het koninkrijk, de groei van het koninkrijk en conferenties over het koninkrijk, en toch cynische, kritische en slechte leden van onze plaatselijke kerk zijn.

Wilt u voor het koninkrijk werken (zie Kolossenzen 4:11)? Wijd uzelf dan van ganser harte aan Christus en Zijn kerk. Dat begint bij uw plaatselijke kerk. Heb uw kerk lief en dien haar. Neem er verantwoordelijkheid in. Leg verantwoording af en wees trouw aan uw plaatselijke kerk. Werk voor het welzijn en de groei van de kerk — uw plaatselijke kerk en daarbuiten.

Timothy Dwight schreef:*

Ik heb Uw koninkrijk lief, Heer,
de woning waar U verblijft,
de kerk die onze gezegende Verlosser
met Zijn kostbaar bloed heeft gered.
Ik heb Uw kerk lief, o God:
haar muren staan voor U,
dierbaar als Uw oogappel,
in Uw hand gegrift.

Wat hij precies bedoelde met de relatie tussen het koninkrijk en de kerk, kan verschillen van mijn opvatting. Wat ik echter graag wil dat we beseffen, is dat hij bij het koninkrijk aan de kerk dacht. En dat zouden wij ook moeten doen! Zijn deze woorden ook de uwe, wanneer hij verder schrijft?

Voor haar zullen mijn tranen vloeien,
voor haar stijgen mijn gebeden op;
aan haar geef ik mijn zorgen en inspanningen,
totdat zorgen en moeite eindigen.
Boven mijn grootste vreugde
stel ik haar hemelse wegen op prijs,
haar zoete gemeenschap, plechtige geloften,
haar lofzangen van liefde en lof.

* Zie pagina 32 voor het volledige lied.

I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well –Psalm 139:14.

We live in a world full of bacteria and viruses. It is estimated that there are 100 trillion bacteria in the average human body. This is a huge number and one that I can’t wrap my mind around. Normally, these bacteria aren’t toxic until they get out of balance or get to a place where they are not intended to be. God has made us in such a way that our bodies have immune capabilities that are amazing.

Antibody-making cells and T cells float around our blood streams like sentinels, waiting for foreign cells or toxins to appear. A simple activity, like brushing your teeth or getting a scratch on your arm, can release bacteria into your blood stream. If it wasn’t for our God-given immune systems, those bacteria could attach to different tissues and cause serious infections.

It is important that we understand some about our immune system and think about ways in which we can help it function better.

In the Beginning

After He finished, …God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good… –Genesis 1:31. This doesn’t just mean that it looked beautiful, although it did. It also means at that point in time all of Creation was working together. There were no pathogenic bacteria and no harmful viruses. Adam and Eve were created perfectly and did not require antibiotics or probiotics to fight off infections.

Before the Fall, there was no need for an immune system the way we need it today. Most likely, the immune system of that era probably served more like a disposal system, getting rid of cells that needed to be cleaned up.

After the Fall, everything was different. Bacteria and viruses began to be “pathogenic” or disease-causing.

Components of Our Immune Systems

When people think of the immune system, they mostly think of cells that make antibodies. These are a very important part of our bodies’ defenses, but there are also many others.

a. Skin…

Our first line of defense against many infections is our skin. Having our body covered with an intact coating of skin with healthy bacteria on its surface can prevent unhealthy organisms from getting into the tissue underneath the skin and even into the blood stream.

I have seen plenty of severe infections that followed incidents during which the skin was broken. Anything from stepping on a nail to a dog bite can lead to infection.

b. Lymphatic System…

When we think about our circulation, the first thing that comes to mind is the blood system with veins, arteries, and the heart. There is another system, called the lymphatic system, that is charged with carrying infection-fighting blood cells throughout the body and getting rid of toxic materials.

There are little filtration areas along this system called lymph nodes that swell up when dealing with infections. Often when someone has an upper respiratory infection, they will notice that the lymph glands in their neck swell up. This is a sign that the immune system is doing what it is supposed to.

c. Bone Marrow/Spleen…

The bone marrow makes infection-fighting cells. Many of these cells are stored in the spleen which acts as a huge filter for the blood. When the body detects any type of infection, these infection-fighting cells are released into the blood stream and into the lymphatic system to fight off the bacteria or virus which is causing that infection.

Thus, people who are missing their spleen have an increased risk for certain types of infection.

d. Immune Cells…

The “soldiers” of our immune system are: white blood cells, B cells (which make antibodies), and T cells. These are the cells that respond to any invasion of our body.

e. Complement System…

This is a system that many people do not know as much about. This system includes the liver, which makes small proteins that help immune cells perform better and causes antibodies to be more effective. These proteins are floating around in an inactive state until there is a sign of infection, then certain enzymes activate them to be ready to help with an infection-fighting response.

Things that Damage our Immune Systems

There are a number of things that weaken our immune systems and make them less able to respond to infections. In fact, all of these things contribute to stunting our bodies’ defenses.

  1. A poor diet
  2. Bad sleep patterns
  3. Certain medications (particularly steroids)
  4. Poorly controlled diabetes (or any other debilitating illness)

Additionally, high levels of anxiety release stress hormones into the body that can lead to poor immunity.

Attempting to eliminate these things is a start, but we should also make certain to replace them with a healthy lifestyle. Many of the things that make our immune systems stronger are obvious, but that doesn’t mean we are always good at doing these things. We may have developed unhealthy habits or perhaps we were never taught certain healthy lifestyle choices.

Eat the Right Foods

There is no one specific food or juice we can consume that will push us towards a healthy ideal. Rather we need to have a mixture of healthy foods which we eat and unhealthy ones which we limit.

The first thing I think about when it comes to “the right foods,” is antioxidants. Antioxidants are chemicals that bind up damaging molecules in our bodies called “free radicals.” Too many free radicals can lead to all sorts of diseases, including diabetes and cancer. Of course, other parts of our bodies, such as our immune system, don’t function as well in this situation either.

Foods that are high in added nitrates, like cured meats, tend to greatly increase these free radicals and should be avoided.

Eating lots of fruits and vegetables really helps to naturally increase our vitamin levels (particularly Vitamin C). Eating healthy fats (those high in omega-3 fatty acids) and avoiding unhealthy ones (those high in saturated fat) probably also positively impact our ability to fight infection.

Get Adequate (Good) Sleep

Studies have looked at the risk of catching the common cold and found that people who slept less were more likely to catch colds. The cutoff point seemed to be around six hours for adults (it is probably more for teens and children).1

This makes sense since our bodies heal the most when we are sleeping. If you are waking up feeling unrested, it is important to figure out why. Things like simply not sleeping long enough, poor sleep hygiene (such as going to sleep thinking about worries, or working right up until bedtime), and sleep apnea can all cause sleep that is not restorative to our bodies.

God made our bodies with a need to rest, and He made a day for that purpose. If nothing else, this is the message of the Sabbath Day (see Exodus 20:8-11).

Consider Probiotics

In the 1800s, men like Joseph Lister and Louis Pasteur pushed forward the germ theory of disease. They believed that bacteria (at that time they didn’t yet know about viruses) were the causes behind many diseases. This led to Joseph Lister pioneering the sterilization of surgical instruments.

In the years since, we have concluded that not all bacteria are “pathogenic” or disease-causing. Many of the bacteria on our skin and in our digestive tract are good bacteria. These good bacteria aid with digestion and protect us from the pathogenic (or bad) bacteria moving in to cause us problems.

Probiotics are found in yogurt and kefir, plus many other foods. Probiotics can also be taken as supplements via capsules or drops.

One study gave 326 children probiotics or a placebo during the cold season. The children who were receiving the probiotics had significantly fewer respiratory illnesses and fevers during those six months.2

People who include these foods in their diet and take some probiotic supplements tend to be healthier and have stronger immune systems.

Cut Down on Sugar Intake

We know that obesity and uncontrolled diabetes increase the risk of infections, both minor and severe. It seems that when there is too much sugar floating around in the blood stream, it gives bad bacteria the nutrients they need to grow quickly, and it causes immune systems to not function as well.

When white blood cells are surrounded by lots of sugar, they are less able to perform “phagocytosis” (the process of swallowing) and they are less able to prevent the invasion of bad bacteria or viruses.3

We may have difficulty cutting all sugar out of our diet, but limiting it seems to make a big difference with regard to how well our bodies can fight off infection.

Exercise Regularly

It probably goes without saying but waiting until you feel like you have a cold coming on and then rushing out to run three miles is probably not going to be helpful. In fact, it could make you feel a lot worse as you deal with a body that is unused to exercise, which is also dealing with an infection.

The key here is moderation. Extreme high levels of activity, like that of performance athletes preparing for a big race or event, seem to increase the risk of infections. However, moderate levels of exercising 30 minutes per day for five days a week is good advice to follow so we can condition our bodies so we will have healthy hearts as well as other healthy systems to protect us from those unseen outside invaders.

Cut Down on Stress

“Dear God…
Grant me the [grace] to accept the things I cannot change,
[the] courage to change the things [that] I can,
and [the] wisdom to know the difference.”

Chronic elevation of stress hormones is harmful for our bodies. Stress hormones increase blood pressure and pulse rate. They push up blood sugars and tend to increase inflammatory responses in our bodies.4

Basically, stress hormones do all of the necessary things within your body to prepare you if the situation should arise that you would need to run away from serious danger, such as a charging grizzly bear. However, this high of a level of stress hormones isn’t particularly helpful when it comes to dealing with a child’s health problem, or the family’s financial difficulty.

Every one of us has dealt with worry at one time or another. Yet, living in a chronic state of worry is not healthy, nor is it a place where God wants to see His people living. From a Christian standpoint, our goal must be to give these concerns to God. Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you –I Peter 5:7. We don’t need to live with anxiety and all of the negative changes it can inflict on our physical health.

Spend Time Outdoors

When people think of sunlight, they mainly seem to think about Vitamin D.

It is true that Vitamin D is produced when our skin is exposed to sunlight, but sun exposure actually does much more. For example, sunlight seems to get our immune cells functioning in top condition to fight infections. Basically, T cells move much faster and more effectively when they have exposure to sunlight.5 Also, sun exposure increases nitric oxide levels in our bodies. This helps dilate blood vessels, lower blood pressure, and is a heart healthy chemical.

As with all the things I have mentioned, moderation is the key. Overexposure in the hot sun can cause sun stroke, and too much ultraviolet light is damaging to our skin cells, which can lead to burns and even skin cancers.

Targeted Supplements

Supplements can be helpful to fill in the gaps in our diet or places where our bodies are simply not absorbing as much of something as they should.

Vitamin D is one that jumps to my mind as we know that low Vitamin D levels increase the risk of severe infections. Our bodies don’t really know where the Vitamin D comes from. While it is probably best to get this from a combination of food and sun exposure, including supplements of Vitamin D may be helpful for older people or for anyone who has trouble achieving this.6

Zinc has been shown (short term) to reduce duration of colds. I would caution here that it isn’t really meant to be taken every day, but more should be taken at the first symptom of an upper respiratory infection coming on. This isn’t a miracle supplement and in studies it only reduced cold symptom duration by about one day.7

Vitamin C is another thing that many take when they feel colds coming on. Studies seem to indicate that it is well tolerated and effective.8 It is probably best to get most of your Vitamin C from your diet and only to introduce extra Vitamin C when you feel infection symptoms coming on.

There are many other supplements that people take; these are just three of the more common ones.

God made our bodies with multiple different systems. These systems heal injuries, maintain our body, and protect it from a world damaged by the introduction of sin at the Fall of man, in the Garden of Eden. We are indeed fearfully and wonderfully made. These systems work without our even thinking about them.

It is important that we are conscious of ways in which we can help, and not impede, these wonderfully designed cells and structures that prevent damaging organisms from entering our bodies and causing infection. It isn’t that healthy living or being a child of God will prevent us from ever getting sick, but rather that making a conscious decision to follow the right path will improve our body’s function. I believe that if we are healthy, it will make it easier for us to fulfil our mission—to reach the world around us with the Gospel message.

Eu te louvarei, porque fui formado de modo assombroso e maravilhoso; maravilhosas são as tuas obras, e a minha alma o sabe muito bem –Salmo 139:14.

Vivemos num mundo cheio de bactérias e vírus. Estima-se que haja 100 trilhões de bactérias no corpo humano médio. É um número enorme, que não consigo sequer imaginar. Normalmente, essas bactérias não são tóxicas até que se desequilibrem ou cheguem a um lugar onde não deveriam estar. Deus nos fez de tal maneira que nossos corpos têm capacidades imunológicas extraordinárias.

Células produtoras de anticorpos e células T circulam pela corrente sanguínea como sentinelas, à espera do aparecimento de células estranhas ou toxinas. Uma atividade simples, como escovar os dentes ou fazer um arranhão no braço, pode liberar bactérias na corrente sanguínea. Se não fosse pelo nosso sistema imunológico, que nos foi dado por Deus, essas bactérias poderiam se fixar em diferentes tecidos e causar infecções graves.

É importante que entendamos um pouco sobre nosso sistema imunológico e pensemos em maneiras de ajudá-lo a funcionar melhor.

No princípio

Depois de terminar, …Deus viu tudo o que havia feito, e eis que era muito bom… –Gênesis 1:31. Isso não significa apenas que tudo era belo, embora fosse. Significa também que, naquele momento, toda a Criação funcionava em harmonia. Não havia bactérias patogênicas nem vírus nocivos. Adão e Eva foram criados perfeitos e não precisavam de antibióticos ou probióticos para combater infecções.

Antes da Queda, não havia necessidade de um sistema imunológico como o de que precisamos hoje. Muito provavelmente, o sistema imunológico daquela época servia mais como um sistema de descarte, eliminando células que precisavam ser removidas.

Depois da Queda, tudo mudou. As bactérias e os vírus passaram a ser “patogênicos”, ou causadores de doenças.

Componentes do nosso sistema imunológico

Quando as pessoas pensam no sistema imunológico, a maioria pensa nas células que produzem anticorpos. Elas são uma parte muito importante das defesas do nosso corpo, mas há muitas outras também.

a. Pele…

Nossa primeira linha de defesa contra muitas infecções é a pele. Ter o corpo coberto por uma camada íntegra de pele, com bactérias saudáveis em sua superfície, pode impedir que organismos nocivos penetrem no tecido sob a pele e até mesmo na corrente sanguínea.

Já vi muitas infecções graves que ocorreram após incidentes em que a pele foi rompida. Qualquer coisa, desde pisar num prego até ser mordido por um cão, pode levar a uma infecção.

b. Sistema linfático…

Quando pensamos na circulação, a primeira coisa que nos vem à mente é o sistema sanguíneo, com veias, artérias e o coração. Há outro sistema, chamado sistema linfático, cuja função é transportar pelo corpo células sanguíneas que combatem infecções e eliminar materiais tóxicos.

Ao longo desse sistema há pequenas áreas de filtragem, chamadas linfonodos, que incham quando estão lidando com infecções. Muitas vezes, quando alguém tem uma infecção das vias respiratórias superiores, percebe que os linfonodos do pescoço incham. Isso é um sinal de que o sistema imunológico está fazendo o que deve.

c. Medula óssea/baço…

A medula óssea produz células que combatem infecções. Muitas dessas células ficam armazenadas no baço, que funciona como um enorme filtro do sangue. Quando o corpo detecta qualquer tipo de infecção, essas células que combatem infecções são liberadas na corrente sanguínea e no sistema linfático para combater a bactéria ou o vírus que está causando a infecção.

Assim, as pessoas que não têm baço correm maior risco de certos tipos de infecção.

d. Células imunológicas…

Os “soldados” do nosso sistema imunológico são os glóbulos brancos, as células B (que produzem anticorpos) e as células T. São essas células que respondem a qualquer invasão do nosso corpo.

e. Sistema complemento…

Este é um sistema sobre o qual muitas pessoas não sabem muito. Ele inclui o fígado, que produz pequenas proteínas que ajudam as células imunológicas a funcionar melhor e tornam os anticorpos mais eficazes. Essas proteínas circulam em estado inativo até que haja um sinal de infecção; então, certas enzimas as ativam para que estejam prontas a ajudar na resposta de combate à infecção.

Coisas que prejudicam nosso sistema imunológico

Há várias coisas que enfraquecem nosso sistema imunológico e o tornam menos capaz de responder às infecções. Na verdade, todas elas contribuem para atrofiar as defesas do nosso corpo.

  1. Uma alimentação inadequada
  2. Hábitos de sono ruins
  3. Certos medicamentos (em particular, esteroides)
  4. Diabetes mal controlada (ou qualquer outra doença debilitante)

Além disso, níveis elevados de ansiedade liberam hormônios do estresse no corpo, o que pode levar a uma imunidade baixa.

Tentar eliminar essas coisas é um começo, mas também devemos nos certificar de substituí-las por um estilo de vida saudável. Muitas das coisas que fortalecem nosso sistema imunológico são óbvias, mas isso não significa que sempre sejamos bons em praticá-las. Podemos ter desenvolvido hábitos pouco saudáveis ou talvez nunca tenhamos aprendido certas escolhas de estilo de vida saudável.

Coma os alimentos certos

Não existe um alimento ou suco específico que possamos consumir para nos levar a um ideal de saúde. Em vez disso, precisamos combinar alimentos saudáveis, que devemos consumir, com alimentos não saudáveis, cujo consumo devemos limitar.

A primeira coisa em que penso quando se trata de “alimentos certos” são os antioxidantes. Antioxidantes são substâncias químicas que se ligam a moléculas nocivas do nosso corpo, chamadas “radicais livres”. Um excesso de radicais livres pode levar a todo tipo de doença, incluindo diabetes e câncer. É claro que, nessa situação, outras partes do nosso corpo, como o sistema imunológico, também não funcionam tão bem.

Alimentos com alto teor de nitratos adicionados, como carnes curadas, tendem a aumentar bastante esses radicais livres e devem ser evitados.

Comer muitas frutas e verduras realmente ajuda a aumentar naturalmente nossos níveis de vitaminas (em particular, de vitamina C). O consumo de gorduras saudáveis (ricas em ácidos graxos ômega-3) e a redução do consumo de gorduras não saudáveis (ricas em gordura saturada) provavelmente também têm um impacto positivo na nossa capacidade de combater infecções.

Durma o suficiente (e bem)

Estudos analisaram o risco de contrair um resfriado comum e descobriram que as pessoas que dormiam menos tinham maior probabilidade de pegar resfriados. O limite parecia ser de cerca de seis horas para adultos (provavelmente é mais para adolescentes e crianças).1

Isso faz sentido, pois nosso corpo se recupera principalmente enquanto dormimos. Se você acorda sem se sentir descansado, é importante descobrir o motivo. Coisas como simplesmente não dormir o suficiente, ter uma higiene do sono inadequada (por exemplo, ir dormir pensando nas preocupações ou trabalhar até a hora de se deitar) e ter apneia do sono podem fazer com que o sono não seja restaurador para o nosso corpo.

Deus criou nosso corpo com a necessidade de descansar e criou um dia para esse propósito. Se nada mais, essa é a mensagem do Dia de Sábado (ver Êxodo 20:8-11).

Considere os probióticos

No século XIX, homens como Joseph Lister e Louis Pasteur promoveram a teoria microbiana das doenças. Eles acreditavam que as bactérias (naquela época, ainda não sabiam da existência dos vírus) eram a causa de muitas doenças. Isso levou Joseph Lister a ser pioneiro na esterilização de instrumentos cirúrgicos.

Desde então, concluímos que nem todas as bactérias são “patogênicas”, ou causadoras de doenças. Muitas das bactérias que vivem na nossa pele e no nosso trato digestivo são benéficas. Essas bactérias benéficas ajudam na digestão e nos protegem contra bactérias patogênicas (ou nocivas) que, ao se instalarem, podem nos causar problemas.

Os probióticos são encontrados no iogurte e no kefir, além de muitos outros alimentos. Também podem ser tomados como suplementos em cápsulas ou gotas.

Em um estudo, 326 crianças receberam probióticos ou um placebo durante a temporada de resfriados. As crianças que receberam probióticos tiveram significativamente menos doenças respiratórias e febres durante esses seis meses.2

As pessoas que incluem esses alimentos na dieta e tomam alguns suplementos probióticos tendem a ser mais saudáveis e a ter um sistema imunológico mais forte.

Reduza o consumo de açúcar

Sabemos que a obesidade e o diabetes não controlado aumentam o risco de infecções, tanto leves quanto graves. Parece que, quando há açúcar demais circulando na corrente sanguínea, ele fornece às bactérias nocivas os nutrientes de que precisam para crescer rapidamente e faz com que o sistema imunológico não funcione tão bem.

Quando os glóbulos brancos estão cercados por muito açúcar, têm menos capacidade de realizar a “fagocitose” (o processo de engolir) e de impedir a invasão de bactérias ou vírus nocivos.3

Talvez tenhamos dificuldade para eliminar todo o açúcar da nossa alimentação, mas limitá-lo parece fazer uma grande diferença na capacidade do nosso corpo de combater infecções.

Pratique exercícios regularmente

Provavelmente nem é preciso dizer, mas esperar até sentir que está começando a pegar um resfriado e então sair correndo para correr cinco quilômetros provavelmente não vai ajudar. Na verdade, isso pode fazer você se sentir muito pior, enquanto lida com um corpo que não está acostumado a se exercitar e que também está enfrentando uma infecção.

O segredo aqui é a moderação. Níveis extremamente altos de atividade, como os de atletas de alto rendimento que se preparam para uma grande corrida ou competição, parecem aumentar o risco de infecções. No entanto, é aconselhável praticar exercícios em nível moderado, por 30 minutos ao dia, cinco dias por semana, para condicionar o corpo e ter um coração saudável, assim como outros sistemas saudáveis que nos protejam desses invasores externos invisíveis.

Reduza o estresse

“Querido Deus…
Concede-me a [graça] de aceitar as coisas que não posso mudar,
[a] coragem para mudar as coisas [que] posso,
e [a] sabedoria para saber a diferença.”

A elevação crônica dos hormônios do estresse é prejudicial ao nosso corpo. Esses hormônios aumentam a pressão arterial e a frequência cardíaca. Elevam o nível de açúcar no sangue e tendem a aumentar as respostas inflamatórias no nosso corpo.4

Basicamente, os hormônios do estresse fazem tudo o que é necessário no seu corpo para prepará-lo caso surja uma situação em que você precise fugir de um perigo grave, como um urso-pardo atacando. No entanto, um nível tão elevado de hormônios do estresse não é particularmente útil para lidar com um problema de saúde de uma criança ou com uma dificuldade financeira da família.

Todos nós já nos preocupamos em algum momento. No entanto, viver em um estado crônico de preocupação não é saudável, nem é um estado em que Deus deseja ver seu povo vivendo. Do ponto de vista cristão, nosso objetivo deve ser entregar essas preocupações a Deus. Lançando sobre ele toda a vossa ansiedade, porque ele tem cuidado de vós –1 Pedro 5:7. Não precisamos viver com ansiedade e com todas as mudanças negativas que ela pode causar à nossa saúde física.

Passe tempo ao ar livre

Quando as pessoas pensam na luz do sol, geralmente pensam principalmente na vitamina D.

É verdade que a vitamina D é produzida quando nossa pele é exposta à luz do sol, mas a exposição ao sol faz muito mais. Por exemplo, parece que a luz do sol faz com que nossas células imunológicas funcionem em ótimas condições para combater infecções. Basicamente, as células T se movimentam muito mais rápido e com mais eficácia quando expostas à luz do sol.5 Além disso, a exposição ao sol aumenta os níveis de óxido nítrico no nosso corpo. Isso ajuda a dilatar os vasos sanguíneos, baixar a pressão arterial e é uma substância benéfica para o coração.

Como em todas as coisas que mencionei, o segredo é a moderação. A exposição excessiva ao sol forte pode causar insolação, e a luz ultravioleta em excesso danifica as células da pele, o que pode levar a queimaduras e até mesmo ao câncer de pele.

Suplementos específicos

Os suplementos podem ser úteis para preencher lacunas na nossa alimentação ou suprir necessidades que surgem quando nosso corpo simplesmente não absorve determinada substância em quantidade suficiente.

Vitamina D é uma que me vem à mente, pois sabemos que níveis baixos de vitamina D aumentam o risco de infecções graves. Nosso corpo não sabe realmente de onde vem a vitamina D. Embora provavelmente seja melhor obtê-la por meio de uma combinação de alimentos e exposição ao sol, incluir suplementos de vitamina D pode ser útil para pessoas mais velhas ou para qualquer pessoa que tenha dificuldade em obtê-la dessa forma.6

Zinco demonstrou reduzir (a curto prazo) a duração dos resfriados. Eu recomendaria cautela: não é realmente para ser tomado todos os dias; é melhor tomá-lo assim que surgirem os primeiros sintomas de uma infecção das vias respiratórias superiores. Não é um suplemento milagroso e, nos estudos, reduziu a duração dos sintomas do resfriado em apenas cerca de um dia.7

Vitamina C é outra coisa que muitas pessoas tomam quando sentem que estão começando a pegar um resfriado. Os estudos parecem indicar que ela é bem tolerada e eficaz.8 Provavelmente, o melhor é obter a maior parte da vitamina C por meio da alimentação e só acrescentar vitamina C quando você sentir que os sintomas de uma infecção estão começando.

As pessoas tomam muitos outros suplementos; estes são apenas três dos mais comuns.

Deus criou nosso corpo com vários sistemas diferentes. Esses sistemas curam lesões, mantêm nosso corpo e o protegem de um mundo danificado pela introdução do pecado na Queda do homem, no Jardim do Éden. Somos, de fato, formados de modo assombroso e maravilhoso. Esses sistemas funcionam sem que sequer pensemos neles.

É importante estarmos atentos às maneiras de ajudar, e não prejudicar, essas células e estruturas maravilhosamente projetadas, que impedem organismos nocivos de entrar em nosso corpo e causar infecções. Não é que levar uma vida saudável ou ser filho de Deus vá nos impedir de adoecer algum dia; antes, tomar a decisão consciente de seguir o caminho certo melhora o funcionamento do nosso corpo. Acredito que, se tivermos saúde, será mais fácil cumprirmos nossa missão — alcançar o mundo ao nosso redor com a mensagem do Evangelho.

With a God so big, why would one fear?
He controls the sea, the storms that appear.
He knows tomorrow, before it has come.
The hairs of our head, He knows the sum.

Why would one question a God like this?
Why do some doubt, or ask amiss?
“Trust in the Lord” the Scripture has said.
But our own understanding, we lean on instead?

I’m sure it’s confusing, to the all-knowing One.
All the miracles, with a word, they were done!
He looks to and fro in this world today,
For one that will trust, without a delay.

The things of this world are so brilliant and fast.
Do we even need God, maybe old-fashioned at last?!
Enough with the folly, we all know the truth.
We have seen God working, yes, from our youth.

Nothing can replace our almighty God;
To say any different would certainly sound odd.
He’s waiting for the church to trust Him once more.
He stands and knocks; will you open the door?

Not just in a pinch, or when life’s too hard,
But every moment, your fears disregard.
He’s looking for a people once more in our day,
With confidence in God, His power to display.

by Barry Grant

Når Gud er så stor, hvorfor skulle vi da frykte?
Han styrer havet og stormene som bryter løs.
Han kjenner morgendagen før den har kommet.
Han vet hvor mange hår vi har på hodet.

Hvorfor skulle noen tvile på en slik Gud?
Hvorfor tviler noen eller spør feil?
«Stol på Herren», sier Skriften.
Men i stedet støtter vi oss til vår egen forstand?

Jeg er sikker på at det forvirrer Den allvitende.
Alle miraklene ble gjort med ett ord!
Han ser utover verden i dag,
etter én som vil stole på ham uten å nøle.

Det som hører denne verden til, er så strålende og går så fort.
Trenger vi egentlig Gud, kanskje han er gammeldags nå?!
Nok av tåpelighetene, vi vet alle sannheten.
Vi har sett Gud virke, ja, helt fra ungdommen av.

Ingenting kan erstatte vår allmektige Gud;
Å si noe annet ville sannelig høres merkelig ut.
Han venter på at kirken skal stole på ham igjen.
Han står og banker; vil du åpne døren?

Ikke bare når det kniper, eller når livet er for vanskelig,
men hvert øyeblikk: legg frykten til side.
Han leter igjen etter et folk i vår tid,
med tillit til Gud, som viser hans kraft.

av Barry Grant
