«Hvordan går salget av det nye pensumet?» spurte Sandra og la hendene rundt kaffekoppen.

«Det går tregt», svarte Abby. «Jeg må reklamere mer, men nå som produktet er ferdig, synes jeg det er vanskelig å markedsføre det.»

«Hva er galt?» spurte Sandra. Abby hadde brukt flere år på å utvikle et pensum for barn med særskilte behov. Hennes engasjement og hengivenhet for prosjektet var imponerende, men nå virket iveren hennes dempet.

«Vel», sa Abby langsomt. «Jeg føler at kollegaen min stadig kritiserer meg. ‘Omslagsdesignet er smakløst, det er en skrivefeil på side 11’, jeg burde ha sagt ditt og datt. Prosjektveilederen min vil at jeg skal jobbe med markedsføringen, men hver gang jeg går videre, forteller hun meg at jeg har gjort noe galt.»

«Føles det som sjalusi?» spurte Sandra.

«Det hadde jeg ikke tenkt på. Jeg holder meg i bakgrunnen, men det hjelper ikke. Jeg føler meg lammet, og jeg vet ikke hva jeg skal gjøre.»

Sandra nikket. «Det er vanskelig å bli utsatt for en annens sjalusi. Men det er verre å være den som er sjalu. Jeg har vært der. Det er elendig.»

«Hvordan kom du deg gjennom det?» spurte Abby. «Du virker ikke som en sjalu person nå.»

«Det var et poeng i en preken», svarte Sandra. «Predikanten sa: ‘Hvis du kjenner deg kritisk til noen som gleder seg, strever du sannsynligvis med sjalusi.’ Jeg husker ikke noe annet han sa», lo Sandra, «men jeg visste at han hadde satt fingeren på problemet mitt. Jeg syntes ofte det var vanskelig å glede meg på vegne av jevnaldrende. Jeg skjønte ikke at sjalusi var rotproblemet mitt.»

«Det gir mening», svarte Abby.

«Det er vanskeligere for sjalusien å slå rot hvis jeg tar tak i de negative tankene med en gang», svarte Sandra. «Det er en kamp det er verdt å kjempe. Jeg er lykkeligere når jeg kan ‘glede meg med dem som gleder seg’, slik Bibelen sier at vi skal gjøre.»

«Kanskje kollegaen min strever med negative tanker om suksessen mer enn hun er irritert på meg», funderte Abby.

«Det er sannsynligvis riktig», svarte Sandra. «Prøv å berolige henne, slik at dere kan samarbeide på en god måte. Ikke reager på oppførselen hennes.»

Jeg har også, slik Sandra har, hatt kritiske tanker når jevnaldrende har delt gode nyheter, eller når jeg har lagt merke til det de har oppnådd. Hvis jeg ikke tar tak i det med en gang, hindrer denne lille antydningen av sjalusi meg i å glede meg på andres vegne.

Bibelen beskriver misunnelsens og sjalusiens brutalitet. Sjalusi er grusom som dødsriket. (se Høysangen 8:6). Misunnelse [er] råttenskap i benene –Ordspråkene 14:30. Og Vrede er grusom, og sinne er overveldende; men hvem kan stå seg mot misunnelse? –Ordspråkene 27:4. Sjalusi er svært subtil. Den kan skjules bak en aura av gudsfrykt. Den kan ikke bare ødelegge forholdene mine nå, men også forholdene til barna og barnebarna mine.

Kvinner bestemmer seg ikke for å bli sjalu. De sier ikke: «I dag skal jeg være sjalu.» Ofte er det vanskelig å finne ut når sjalusien kommer inn i hjertet, eller om den i det hele tatt er der. Men hvis det er vanskelig å glede seg på andres vegne, er det kanskje på tide å ransake hjertet. Vi er rustet til å kjempe mot sjalusi når vi forstår hvordan og hvor sjalusien trives – i hjertet til hver og en av oss.

Jevnaldrende setter vår evne til å glede oss på prøve

Som regel misunner vi ikke folk vi ikke står nær. Kvinner over hele verden gifter seg, får barn eller flytter inn i et nytt hus, og vi legger knapt merke til det. Men det er vanskelig å glede seg når mennesker som står oss nær i tid, sted, alder eller anseelse, får velsignelser som vi selv ønsker oss. Mer enn én gang har en jublende telefonsamtale med en gladnyhet om en milepæl satt min beslutning om å glede meg sammen med en glad venninne på prøve. Gud forstår kampen, og han leder meg til hvile og aksept.

Gjenkjenn sjalusien

Å være sjalu betyr: «Å føle eller vise misunnelse overfor noen eller det de har oppnådd og de fordelene de har.» Sjalusi viser seg på mange måter, for eksempel ved at man ønsker å etterligne en jevnaldrende. Sjalusi nedvurderer andres prestasjoner og forsøker å kontrollere hva andre tenker om vedkommende. Sjalusi fryder seg over andres lidelser og nederlag, samtidig som den varmer seg i en åndelig boble. Sjalu mennesker holder ryktesirkulasjonen i full gang ved å gi den forvrengte sannheter.

Vokt tankene dine

Sjalusi begynner i sinnet. Å dvele ved en mistanke eller misunne en annen person fordreier sannheten. Dette er farlig, fordi det du oppfatter som sant, er en løgn.

Vi bestemmer oss for at noen er stolt fordi hun tok med en vakker dessert til et felles måltid. Eller vi tenker at en søster forsømmer hjemmet sitt fordi hun besøkte en kvinne på et sykehjem. Hvorfor? Vi har en tendens til å dømme andre ut fra våre egne motiver. Er det ikke skyldfølelse, selvrettferdiggjøring eller misunnelse som får oss til å stemple noen som forsømmelig fordi hun besøker eldre? Vi vet ikke hvor lenge hun hadde tenkt på besøket, eller hvordan mannen hennes gjorde det mulig. Splittende tanker som blir til ord, skaper kaos blant gudfryktige kvinner. De fører til ekstraarbeid for menighetslederne og hemmer veksten i et fellesskap av troende.

Ta til deg tanken: «Livet er ikke rettferdig»

Noen ganger har noen noe du ønsker deg. På den annen side vil du iblant ha noe en annen kvinne ønsker seg. «Livet er ikke rettferdig» er en kjensgjerning vi ikke kan endre; vi kan bare endre holdningen vår.

Det var to venninner i samme menighet, og begge hadde en datter i gifteklar alder. Slik livet gjerne former seg, begynte den ene datteren å date og giftet seg lenge før den andre begynte å være sammen med noen. Moren til den ugifte jenta bestemte seg for at hun ville glede seg sammen med venninnen og datteren hennes. Resultatet er at mødrene fremdeles er venninner, jentene er venninner, og det er sannsynlig at barna deres også vil bli venner.

Tell dine egne velsignelser

Det blir vanskelig å være glad og tilfreds når vi ser på andres velsignelser og sammenligner oss med dem. Apostelen Paulus advarer mot dette: …men når de måler seg med seg selv og sammenligner seg med seg selv, viser de at de mangler forstand –2. Korinter 10:12. Kvinner som ikke setter pris på det de allerede har, blir ikke lykkelige. De vil heller ikke kunne glede seg sammen med dem som gleder seg.

Vit hvem du er i Kristus

Sjalusi springer ut av følelser av frykt og usikkerhet. Gud skapte deg til sin ære og herlighet. Det er ingen grunn til å konkurrere; i stedet bør vi være tilfreds med å vite hvem vi er i Jesus. For av nåde er dere frelst, ved tro. Det er ikke deres eget verk, men Guds gave. Det hviler ikke på gjerninger, for at ingen skal rose seg. For vi er hans verk, skapt i Kristus Jesus til gode gjerninger, som Gud på forhånd har lagt ferdige for at vi skulle vandre i dem –Efeserne 2:8-10.

Ha venner, ikke rivaler

Vi kan nøle med å innrømme at vi har en rival, men det er det en venninne blir hvis vi ikke klarer å feire velsignelsene i livet hennes. Be regelmessig for henne, og be Gud om å velsigne henne. Når du slipper mistankene og gjør noe hyggelig for henne, vil de negative følelsene du har utviklet, avta.

Skriften er tydelig når det gjelder fiendskap mot vår bror (eller søster): Den som sier at han er i lyset, men hater sin bror, er ennå i mørket. Den som elsker sin bror, blir i lyset, og det er ikke noe i ham som fører til fall. Men den som hater sin bror, er i mørket og vandrer i mørket. Han vet ikke hvor han går, for mørket har blindet hans øyne –1. Johannes 2:9-11.

Bytt ut sjalusi med takknemlighet og tilfredshet

Negative tanker kommer uoppfordret, men vi kan bestemme om de skal bli eller gå. Lær deg å rette oppmerksomheten tilbake mot sannheten. Filipperbrevet gir oss en utmerket veiledning: Til slutt, søsken: Alt som er sant, alt som er edelt, rett og rent, alt som er verdt å elske, alt som kan kalles godt, og all god gjerning og alt som er verdt å prise, legg vinn på det! –Filipperne 4:8.

Når vi har fred med Gud, med oss selv og med våre medsøstre, vil vi være tilfreds med evnene våre og omstendighetene Gud har satt oss i. Når vi har Gud i fokus, vil vi finne glede og kraft til å glede oss sammen med dem som gleder seg.

One Sunday morning a little girl, whom we will call Jennika, woke up to the sun shining into her bedroom. She dressed in her Sunday dress just like she did every other Sunday morning. This Sunday morning was quite different, though. While she was sitting at the breakfast table waiting for her mom to fill her plate, her mom’s chest suddenly started hurting very badly. It hurt so badly, she had to go lie on the couch. Jennika felt scared. She didn’t know what was going to happen. About ten minutes later, her dad took her mom to the hospital. Later that afternoon, she and her siblings heard that their mom had suffered a heart attack.

The next Wednesday evening, her dad asked, “Jennika, would you like to go along to the hospital tomorrow to see Mom?”

“Yes!” she beamed.

The next morning after breakfast, her older sister and baby brother went with her and her dad to the hospital. That day she had lots of fun. She enjoyed looking out the window of the waiting room and watching the helicopters take off and land. One time she even saw an ambulance come with its lights and sirens on. That was exciting! One time she almost got lost in the halls, but one of her mom’s nurses saw her and showed her the right room.

That night she was going to spend the night with her mom. She was so excited! She thought sleeping on the chair in her mom’s room would be fun. Her mom was going to ask the nurses for a pillow and some blankets. About fifteen minutes after her dad left, a nurse came in and said she couldn’t spend the night there after all! Her dad needed to come back to pick her up. She was so disappointed! She cried almost the whole way home. That night they dropped off her two-week-old brother at one of the church families to give her older sisters a break from taking care of him.

The next day she had a wonderful surprise. First, her cousins, who lived about three hours away, came to visit. And she found out that her mom was going to come home that day! She helped her siblings decorate the house. Her older sister made two welcome-home signs for inside the house and her older brother made one for out by the driveway.

“Mom is home!” yelled her younger brother when he saw the car pull up outside the house. Jennika and her siblings dashed to the front door. They led their mom to her favorite recliner which was close to the air conditioner that their uncle had just installed that morning.

That evening Jennika snuggled up to her mom. “I’m glad you’re home,” she whispered. “I like it when you’re home.” Because her mom had been gone so long, Jennika learned to be more thankful for her mom.

Jennika is older now and is still very thankful for her mom. Maybe your mom didn’t need to be in the hospital for a week, but you should still be thankful for her. Don’t forget to tell her!

一个星期天的早晨，一个我们姑且称她为詹妮卡的小女孩醒来时，阳光正照进她的卧室。她穿上星期天的裙子，就像每个星期天早晨一样。不过，这个星期天的早晨却大不相同。她坐在早餐桌旁等妈妈给她盛饭时，妈妈的胸口突然开始剧烈疼痛。疼得太厉害了，她只好躺到沙发上。詹妮卡感到害怕。她不知道接下来会发生什么。大约十分钟后，爸爸送妈妈去了医院。那天下午晚些时候，她和兄弟姐妹听说妈妈心脏病发作了。

接下来的星期三晚上，爸爸问：“詹妮卡，明天你想跟我们一起去医院看妈妈吗？”

“想！”她高兴地说。

第二天早上吃过早餐后，她和爸爸、姐姐以及小弟弟一起去了医院。那天她玩得很开心。她喜欢从候诊室的窗户向外看，观察直升机起飞和降落。有一次，她甚至看见一辆救护车鸣着警笛、闪着灯开了过来。真让人兴奋！有一次她差点在走廊里迷路，幸好妈妈的一位护士看见了她，带她去了正确的病房。

那天晚上，她本来要陪妈妈过夜。她兴奋极了！她觉得睡在妈妈病房里的椅子上一定很好玩。妈妈打算向护士要一个枕头和几条毯子。爸爸离开大约十五分钟后，一位护士进来说，她最终不能在那里过夜了！爸爸得回来接她。她失望极了！回家的路上，她几乎一路都在哭。那天晚上，他们把才两周大的弟弟送到教会的一户人家，让她的姐姐们能歇一歇，不必照顾他。

第二天，她遇到了一个大惊喜。首先，住在大约三小时车程外的表兄弟姐妹来看望他们。她还得知妈妈那天就要回家了！她帮兄弟姐妹们装饰房子。姐姐做了两块“欢迎回家”的牌子，一块放在屋里；哥哥则做了一块，放在车道旁边。

“妈妈回家了！”弟弟看见汽车停在屋外时喊道。詹妮卡和兄弟姐妹们飞奔到前门。他们扶妈妈坐到她最喜欢的躺椅上，椅子就在舅舅那天早上刚装好的空调旁边。

那天晚上，詹妮卡依偎在妈妈身边。“我很高兴你回家了，”她轻声说。“我喜欢你在家的时候。”因为妈妈离开了那么久，詹妮卡学会了更加感激妈妈。

如今詹妮卡长大了，仍然非常感激妈妈。也许你的妈妈不需要住院一个星期，但你仍然应该感激她。别忘了告诉她！

Editor’s Note:

Over the last number of years there seems to be a shift occurring on a variety of specific issues for some conservative Anabaptists. This changing of ideas and practice is not happening in a vacuum, rather we are simply following the leader. Once we start researching this matter further, we soon realize that this same migration on issues of faith and practice has been at work for some years now within the greater Evangelical community. Let’s stop and consider whether we are following God’s Word, or man’s influence.

Some Anabaptists are becoming dissatisfied with a traditional structure of church, so they gravitate towards “cell-group church” or “house-church” models. Others react to overbearing and authoritative church leadership from their past and start emphasizing a more democratic function of church. Then there are the folks who are moving away from a “local” church body emphasis to that of focusing more on a “universal” or a “global” church body. Still others don’t have a problem with what is considered “normal” church, instead they are the type that gets tired of the “old-fashioned” and the “boring.” These folks welcome “new ideas” that are presented in present-day books and at various conferences which are held around the country. These conferences are not all intrinsically wrong, nor are they all selling “new” interpretations, yet there are some that bring in “fresh” ideas originating from “outside” sources in the hope that they will bring “new life” to the lack of zeal within the “normal.”

Another area of shift is that of focusing on the Gospels while ignoring specific teachings in the Epistles. Some folks stress that we should “just follow Jesus” while not allowing the teachings of the Apostles to further detail the application of Jesus’ teachings. Others lift up the “Sermon on the Mount,” the “red letter Scriptures,” or walking in the “footsteps of Jesus,” without realizing that a default outcome of this focus tends to leave out specific teachings of the Epistles regarding practical church functioning and Christian living. Some of these include …exhort[ing] one another daily… –Hebrews 3:13, All scripture … is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, [and] for correction… –2 Timothy 3:16, and the fact that we should be careful because Satan and his agents will transform themselves …into the apostles of Christ and present themselves as …an angel of light –2 Corinthians 11:13-14.

Some individuals believe it is wrong for spiritual authorities to “take the oversight thereof,” or to give clear admonition over the pulpit. They shrink back from churches that have ordained leaders, or they don’t like the thought of spiritual authorities in their lives. Others feel their church doesn’t have much to offer so they attend various group events with others of “like precious faith” (who believe as they do), thus developing a disjointed spiritual body of individuals from many various local churches, fellowshipping together at large events. Many times, these believers allow someone outside of their local church fellowship to become their spiritual advisor, thus feeling justified in not giving their loyalty to their church leaders at home. They come to believe that the traditional way of having church the Anabaptist way is “not the way it used to be” or “not according to the early church”. They believe that structured church brings deadness to local bodies, never mind that the Epistles provide clear details on church structure and practice.

Many of these individuals are interacting and fellowshipping so closely with others from various other groups and churches instead of their own home church, that they do not realize they are actually functioning in a very individualistic manner. This manner of being an alone “local” Christian is categorically opposite from the “group spirituality” that our Anabaptist forefathers specifically believed and taught. Another area of misunderstanding in this whole issue, is that there is a very clear difference between the expression of the kingdom now and the kingdom future. Remember that Jesus said, “my kingdom is not of this world,” yet an extreme focus on kingdom this and kingdom that, will by default cause Christians to ignore this Truth, as they try to express the kingdom “on the earth,” and “in the now.”

The full effect of the resurrection and the ascension of Jesus in the life of a believer can never fully be understood without allowing the Epistles to bring more clear application to the Gospels or to the Sermon on the Mount. Simply following the words of Jesus in red ink will never help us know how to be a part of the “power of His resurrection”, or “the fellowship of His sufferings.” For this we need the balance of the rest of the New Testament.

Many of these points will require their own complete article to sort out all the nuances, which we plan to do as the Lord continues to allow time to continue. Considering all this, we felt that this article is a balanced, yet basic introduction to the many issues at stake and we have chosen it based on those thoughts.

Curvin L Wenger

When Jesus blessed Simon Peter for his confident confession that Jesus was the Christ, the Son of the living God –Matthew 16:16, He brought together two overarching New Testament themes: the church and the kingdom—…I will build my church … And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven… –Matthew 16:18-19. Ever since, Christ’s followers have deliberated, with varying opinions, on the meaning and the nature of the kingdom, and its relation to the church.

Jesus began His preaching by declaring that the kingdom of heaven was at hand (see Matthew 4:17). Throughout the Gospels, the kingdom was the unifying theme of His teaching. In fact, Scripture only records two occasions when Christ mentioned the church. The church, on the other hand, is more prominent in the Acts, the Epistles, and the Revelation. Why this difference? Is there some conflict or incompatible tension between what Jesus taught and emphasized, and that of the apostles?

Recent years seem to have brought an increased interest and reference to the kingdom within Evangelical circles as well as conservative Anabaptist circles. Many are using terms such as working for the kingdom, building up the kingdom, growing the kingdom, kingdom service, kingdom finances, and even funding the kingdom. Kingdom Theology has been offered as a course of study, and the expression Kingdom Christian has been coined to demarcate a particular kind of Christian—one who believes and practices Jesus’ teachings. Among many conservative Anabaptist people, kingdom terminology has practically drowned out the language expressed by Eliza Hewitt who wrote, “For Christ and the Church let our voices ring.”

Among the various factors which have nurtured this renewed kingdom emphasis among some Anabaptists, two stand out. Both of these concerns reflect the influence of Christians from without the conservative Anabaptist tradition, yet who profess to be Bible-believing and born-again.

  1. The first is that some people seem to be more concerned about being Biblical than about being Christ-like. We, conservative Anabaptists, can stand on the Bible to formulate all the right doctrines and positions while our lives fall short in reflecting the character and values of Jesus Christ our Lord, the One with whom we claim to be united in a living relationship.
  2. The second matter involves a fixation on the act of getting saved to the neglect of living a saved life; that is, a life of obedient discipleship, particularly to the very teachings of Jesus who we are to follow. While most conservative Anabaptists profess to practice Christ’s teachings, we are not immune to a careless discipleship.

There are individuals within conservative Anabaptism that address these concerns somewhat in the following manner. They say that while Evangelicals believe in the person and work of Christ, they tend to focus on Paul. For all practical purposes, they (Evangelicals) are more concerned about correct Bible interpretations, theological systems, and assenting to correct beliefs than they are with obedient Christian living, particularly regarding the hard teachings of Christ. In contrast, these Anabaptists claim that the kingdom of God, which Jesus inaugurated and was the theme of His teaching, should set the norm for understanding and living the Christian life. Consequently, for them, the Gospels (and the kingdom) then become primary in interpreting the rest of the New Testament.

What do we make of this? While sweeping generalizations don’t do justice to the exceptions and the qualifiers, the concerns are valid, and this critique regarding our Evangelical friends does hold some measure of truth. These things have their roots in the thinking of Augustine (354-430), in the imbalanced Reformation emphasis regarding justification by faith, and in the work of John Calvin. But what about the antidote of focusing mostly on Christ and the kingdom? Certainly, Christ is central to interpreting, not only the New Testament, but actually the entire Bible. And there is value in holding forth those teachings of Christ, which are so often brushed aside, yet are required of any church that would be worthy of His name. However, I would like to offer three points of caution or critique about taking this antidote unreservedly.

Do the Gospels dominate the rest of Scripture?

First, I believe it’s a mistake to assume that the Gospels (the life and teachings of Jesus) should dominate and control the interpretation of the New Testament scriptures. Rather, the New Testament, as it moves through the Gospels, the Acts, the Epistles, and lastly the Revelation, contains a divinely inspired progression of fuller revelation and doctrinal explanation. This is seen when we consider the words of Jesus regarding the coming of the Holy Spirit: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now. Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come –John 16:12-13. Those New Testament books following the Gospels are the anticipated fulfillment of these words. They bring the teachings and work of Christ to full development and understanding.

Christ’s ministry and teaching about the kingdom laid the groundwork, then His death and resurrection placed the foundation on which He would build His church. The Scriptures which follow the Gospels give us greater comprehension about the meaning of Christ’s death on the cross and its relation and effect on us that comes through faith and obedience. It also develops the whole doctrine of the church. So, the entire New Testament fits together in beautiful harmony. Both the Gospels and the Epistles need to be interpreted in reference to each other. The teachings of Christ do not take precedence over the Epistles, rather the Epistles help interpret the Gospels—they give us a more complete understanding and practical application to the principles Christ gave His Disciples.

Does Theology Militate Against Discipleship?

Secondly, we should be careful to not set correct interpretation and correct practice against one another. To say it another way, we should not pit theology against discipleship. To whatever degree some Evangelicals may overemphasize theology at the expense of discipleship, it should not prejudice us into making a whipping boy out of theology. Theology is the study of God and the things of God. We are forming a personal theology when we study God’s Word and compare Scripture with Scripture in our efforts to come to a unified and harmonious understanding of its various parts.

Every Christian has a theology, whether he can express it well or not. Our theology (or doctrinal understanding, if you want to say it that way) is our belief system and the soil out of which our behavior grows. Some theologies are very elementary, others reflect a lifetime of study, most are incomplete, some are inconsistent, others are dogmatic or laced with philosophy, and some are dreadfully wrong. Hopefully, all of us have a growing, and increasingly accurate understanding of God and His Word. This is quite necessary since our theology, which is the sum of our beliefs about God and our understanding of His Word and the Christian life, is what affects our discipleship—our daily walk with God. A good theology undergirds discipleship. A poor theology undermines discipleship.

Are “Kingdom” and “Church” Interchangeable?

Finally, we should think correctly about the kingdom in relation to the church. What is the relationship of the kingdom to the church? The kingdom is not, as contemporary usage would almost have us think, a generic version of, or a substitute word for, the church. Rather, the kingdom has to do with the reign or rule of God. It is both a present reality, having been inaugurated in the person and mission of Jesus, and a future expectation which God will bring to completion at the end of time. The church, while not the kingdom, is composed of those who are in the kingdom; those who, through the work of Christ, have submitted to the rule of God.

While we struggle for the precise word to express the relationship of the kingdom to the church, as a holy, loving, and obedient community of believers, the church is the earthly manifestation of God’s rule—His kingdom. Christ did not say “I will build my kingdom”; rather He said, “I will build my church.” Likewise, Paul did not build kingdom halls; He started churches. It is possible for us to have an idealistic and romantic view of the kingdom that gets separated from the hard work of living on earth with our fellow believers in a local church body. We can elevate the kingdom and diminish the church. We can get enthusiastic about the concept of the kingdom, the teachings of the kingdom, the growth of the kingdom, and conferences about the kingdom, and yet be cynical, critical, and sorry members of our local church.

Do you want to work for the kingdom (see Colossians 4:11)? Then commit yourself wholeheartedly to Christ and His church. That starts with your local church. Love and serve your church. Accept responsibility in it. Be accountable and loyal to your local church. Work for the good and growth of the church—your local church, and beyond.

Timothy Dwight wrote:*

I love Thy Kingdom, Lord,
The house of Thine abode,
The church our blest Redeemer
Saved with His own precious blood.
I love Thy church, O God:
Her walls before Thee stand,
Dear as the apple of Thine eye,
And graven on Thy hand.

What he was saying about the precise relationship of the kingdom to the church may be different from what I conceive it to be. However, what I would like for us to appreciate is that when he thought of the kingdom, he thought of the church. And so should we! Are his words yours, as he writes on?

For her my tears shall fall,
For her my prayers ascend;
To her my cares and toils be giv’n,
Till toils and cares shall end.
Beyond my highest joy
I prize her heav’nly ways,
Her sweet communion, solemn vows,
Her hymns of love and praise.

* See page 32 for the entire song.

সম্পাদকের কথা:

গত কয়েক বছরে কিছু রক্ষণশীল অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্টদের মধ্যে নানা নির্দিষ্ট বিষয়ে পরিবর্তন ঘটতে দেখা যাচ্ছে। ধারণা ও অনুশীলনের এই পরিবর্তন শূন্যে ঘটছে না; বরং আমরা কেবল নেতার অনুসরণ করছি। বিষয়টি নিয়ে আরও অনুসন্ধান শুরু করলেই আমরা শিগগির বুঝতে পারি যে বিশ্বাস ও অনুশীলনের বিষয়গুলোতে একই ধরনের এই সরে যাওয়া বৃহত্তর ইভানজেলিক্যাল সমাজের ভেতরেও বেশ কয়েক বছর ধরে চলছে। আসুন থেমে বিবেচনা করি—আমরা কি ঈশ্বরের বাক্য অনুসরণ করছি, নাকি মানুষের প্রভাবের বশবর্তী হচ্ছি?

কিছু অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্ট গির্জার ঐতিহ্যগত কাঠামোয় অসন্তুষ্ট হয়ে “সেল-গ্রুপ গির্জা” বা “হাউস-চার্চ” মডেলের দিকে ঝুঁকছেন। অন্যরা অতীতে গির্জার কর্তৃত্বপরায়ণ ও দাপুটে নেতৃত্বের প্রতিক্রিয়ায় গির্জার আরও গণতান্ত্রিক কার্যপ্রণালির ওপর জোর দিতে শুরু করেছেন। আবার কেউ কেউ “স্থানীয়” গির্জার দেহের ওপর জোর দেওয়া থেকে সরে এসে “সর্বজনীন” বা “বিশ্বব্যাপী” গির্জার দেহের দিকে বেশি মনোযোগ দিচ্ছেন। আরও কেউ “স্বাভাবিক” গির্জা নিয়ে সমস্যায় নেই; বরং তাঁরা “সেকেলে” ও “একঘেয়ে” বিষয়গুলোতে ক্লান্ত হয়ে পড়েন। তাঁরা সারা দেশে অনুষ্ঠিত বিভিন্ন সম্মেলনে এবং বর্তমান সময়ের বইয়ে উপস্থাপিত “নতুন ধারণা”কে স্বাগত জানান। এসব সম্মেলন স্বভাবতই সব ভুল নয়, কিংবা সবগুলোই “নতুন” ব্যাখ্যা বিক্রি করছে না; তবু কিছু সম্মেলন “স্বাভাবিক” গির্জার মধ্যে উদ্যমের অভাব দূর করে “নতুন প্রাণ” সঞ্চারের আশায় “বাইরের” উৎস থেকে আসা “সতেজ” ধারণা নিয়ে আসে।

পরিবর্তনের আরেকটি ক্ষেত্র হলো পত্রগুলোতে থাকা নির্দিষ্ট শিক্ষাগুলো উপেক্ষা করে সুসমাচারগুলোর ওপর মনোযোগ দেওয়া। কেউ কেউ জোর দিয়ে বলেন যে আমাদের “শুধু যিশুকে অনুসরণ” করা উচিত; কিন্তু যিশুর শিক্ষার প্রয়োগ আরও বিশদভাবে ব্যাখ্যা করার জন্য প্রেরিতদের শিক্ষাকে তাঁরা স্থান দেন না। অন্যরা “পাহাড়ের উপদেশ,” “লাল অক্ষরে মুদ্রিত শাস্ত্রাংশ,” অথবা “যিশুর পদাঙ্ক অনুসরণ”কে তুলে ধরেন, অথচ বুঝতে পারেন না যে এই মনোযোগের স্বাভাবিক পরিণতিতে গির্জার বাস্তব কার্যপ্রণালি ও খ্রিস্টীয় জীবনযাপন সম্পর্কে পত্রগুলোর নির্দিষ্ট শিক্ষা বাদ পড়ে যায়। এর মধ্যে রয়েছে… প্রতিদিন পরস্পরকে উপদেশ দাও…—ইব্রীয় ৩:১৩; সমস্ত শাস্ত্র… শিক্ষার, তিরস্কারের [এবং] সংশোধনের জন্য উপকারী…—২ তীমথিয় ৩:১৬; এবং এই বিষয়টি যে আমাদের সতর্ক থাকা উচিত, কারণ শয়তান ও তার অনুচরেরা নিজেদের খ্রিস্টের প্রেরিত বলে রূপান্তরিত করবে এবং… দীপ্তিমান দূতের বেশে হাজির হবে—২ করিন্থীয় ১১:১৩-১৪।

কিছু ব্যক্তি মনে করেন, আধ্যাত্মিক কর্তৃপক্ষের “তত্ত্বাবধান গ্রহণ করা” বা মিম্বর থেকে স্পষ্ট ভর্ৎসনা করা ভুল। তাঁরা এমন গির্জা থেকে দূরে থাকেন যেখানে অভিষিক্ত নেতা আছেন, কিংবা নিজেদের জীবনে আধ্যাত্মিক কর্তৃপক্ষের ধারণা তাঁদের ভালো লাগে না। অন্যদের মনে হয়, তাঁদের গির্জার দেওয়ার মতো তেমন কিছু নেই; তাই তাঁরা “একই অমূল্য বিশ্বাসের” (যাঁরা তাঁদের মতো বিশ্বাস করেন) অন্যদের সঙ্গে বিভিন্ন দলীয় অনুষ্ঠানে যোগ দেন। এর ফলে বিভিন্ন স্থানীয় গির্জার ব্যক্তিদের নিয়ে একটি বিচ্ছিন্ন আধ্যাত্মিক দেহ গড়ে ওঠে, যারা বড় বড় অনুষ্ঠানে একত্রে সহভাগিতা করে। প্রায়ই এই বিশ্বাসীরা তাঁদের স্থানীয় গির্জার সহভাগিতার বাইরের কাউকে নিজেদের আধ্যাত্মিক উপদেষ্টা হতে দেন; ফলে তাঁরা নিজেদের ঘরের গির্জার নেতাদের প্রতি আনুগত্য না দেখানোকে ন্যায়সঙ্গত বলে মনে করেন। তাঁরা বিশ্বাস করতে শুরু করেন যে অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্ট পদ্ধতিতে গির্জা করার ঐতিহ্যগত পথ “আগের মতো আর নেই” অথবা “আদি গির্জার রীতি অনুযায়ী নয়।” তাঁদের বিশ্বাস, কাঠামোবদ্ধ গির্জা স্থানীয় গির্জার দেহে প্রাণহীনতা আনে—পত্রগুলোতে গির্জার কাঠামো ও অনুশীলন সম্পর্কে স্পষ্ট বিবরণ দেওয়া আছে, সে কথা তাঁরা উপেক্ষা করেন।

এই ব্যক্তিদের অনেকে নিজেদের ঘরের গির্জার বদলে অন্যান্য গোষ্ঠী ও গির্জার লোকদের সঙ্গে এত ঘনিষ্ঠভাবে মেলামেশা ও সহভাগিতা করেন যে তাঁরা বুঝতেই পারেন না, আসলে তাঁরা অত্যন্ত ব্যক্তিকেন্দ্রিকভাবে চলছেন। একা “স্থানীয়” খ্রিস্টান হয়ে থাকার এই ধরনটি আমাদের অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্ট পূর্বপুরুষেরা বিশেষভাবে যে “গোষ্ঠীগত আধ্যাত্মিকতা” বিশ্বাস ও শিক্ষা দিয়েছিলেন, তার সম্পূর্ণ বিপরীত। এই গোটা বিষয়ে আরেকটি ভুল-বোঝাবুঝি হলো, রাজ্যের বর্তমান প্রকাশ আর ভবিষ্যৎ প্রকাশের মধ্যে অত্যন্ত স্পষ্ট পার্থক্য রয়েছে। মনে রাখবেন, যিশু বলেছিলেন, “আমার রাজ্য এই জগতের নয়”; তবু রাজ্য নিয়ে অতিরিক্ত ব্যস্ততা খ্রিস্টানদের এই সত্য উপেক্ষা করতে বাধ্য করবে, কারণ তারা “পৃথিবীতে” এবং “এখনই” রাজ্য প্রকাশ করার চেষ্টা করে।

বিশ্বাসীর জীবনে যিশুর পুনরুত্থান ও স্বর্গারোহণের পূর্ণ তাৎপর্য কখনোই সম্পূর্ণভাবে বোঝা সম্ভব নয়, যদি না পত্রগুলোকে সুসমাচারগুলো বা পাহাড়ের উপদেশের প্রয়োগ আরও স্পষ্ট করতে দেওয়া হয়। শুধু লাল কালিতে লেখা যিশুর কথাগুলো অনুসরণ করলেই আমরা “তাঁর পুনরুত্থানের শক্তির” বা “তাঁর দুঃখভোগের সহভাগিতার” অংশ কীভাবে হব, তা জানতে পারব না। এ জন্য নতুন নিয়মের বাকি অংশের ভারসাম্য আমাদের প্রয়োজন।

এই বিষয়গুলোর অনেকগুলোতেই সব সূক্ষ্ম দিক পরিষ্কার করতে আলাদা পূর্ণাঙ্গ প্রবন্ধের প্রয়োজন হবে; প্রভু যত দিন সময় দেন, আমরা তা করতে চাই। এসব বিবেচনা করে আমাদের মনে হয়েছে, এই প্রবন্ধটি আলোচ্য বহু বিষয়ের একটি ভারসাম্যপূর্ণ, তবে মৌলিক ভূমিকা; আর সেই বিবেচনাতেই আমরা এটি বেছে নিয়েছি।

কারভিন এল. ওয়েঙ্গার

যিশু যখন সাইমন পিতরকে এই আত্মবিশ্বাসী স্বীকারোক্তির জন্য আশীর্বাদ করেছিলেন যে যিশুই খ্রিস্ট, জীবন্ত ঈশ্বরের পুত্র—মথি ১৬:১৬, তখন তিনি নতুন নিয়মের দুটি ব্যাপক বিষয়কে একত্র করেছিলেন: গির্জা এবং রাজ্য—…আমি আমার গির্জা নির্মাণ করব… আর আমি তোমাকে স্বর্গরাজ্যের চাবিগুলো দেব…—মথি ১৬:১৮-১৯। সেই থেকে খ্রিস্টের অনুসারীরা নানা মত নিয়ে রাজ্যের অর্থ ও প্রকৃতি এবং গির্জার সঙ্গে এর সম্পর্ক নিয়ে আলোচনা করে এসেছেন।

যিশু তাঁর প্রচার শুরু করেছিলেন এই ঘোষণা দিয়ে যে স্বর্গরাজ্য সন্নিকটে (দেখুন মথি ৪:১৭)। সুসমাচারগুলো জুড়ে তাঁর শিক্ষার ঐক্যবদ্ধকারী বিষয় ছিল রাজ্য। বস্তুত, শাস্ত্রে মাত্র দুটি উপলক্ষে খ্রিস্টের গির্জার উল্লেখ নথিবদ্ধ হয়েছে। অন্যদিকে, প্রেরিত, পত্রসমূহ ও প্রকাশিত বাক্যে গির্জার কথা আরও বেশি করে এসেছে। এই পার্থক্য কেন? যিশু যা শিখিয়েছেন ও গুরুত্ব দিয়েছেন, তার সঙ্গে প্রেরিতদের শিক্ষার কি কোনো বিরোধ বা অসংগত টানাপোড়েন আছে?

সাম্প্রতিক বছরগুলোতে ইভানজেলিক্যাল মহল এবং রক্ষণশীল অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্ট মহল—উভয়ের মধ্যেই রাজ্য নিয়ে আগ্রহ ও উল্লেখ বেড়েছে বলে মনে হয়। অনেকে রাজ্যের জন্য কাজ করা, রাজ্যকে গড়ে তোলা, রাজ্যের বৃদ্ধি ঘটানো, রাজ্যের সেবা, রাজ্যের অর্থব্যবস্থা, এমনকি রাজ্যের জন্য অর্থায়নের মতো শব্দ ব্যবহার করছেন। রাজ্য-ধর্মতত্ত্বকে অধ্যয়নের একটি বিষয় হিসেবে উপস্থাপন করা হয়েছে, আর “রাজ্য-খ্রিস্টান” অভিব্যক্তিটি বিশেষ এক ধরনের খ্রিস্টানকে চিহ্নিত করার জন্য চালু হয়েছে—যিনি যিশুর শিক্ষা বিশ্বাস করেন ও পালন করেন। অনেক রক্ষণশীল অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্টের মধ্যে রাজ্য-সংক্রান্ত পরিভাষা কার্যত এলাইজা হিউইটের ভাষাকে ছাপিয়ে গেছে, যিনি লিখেছিলেন, “খ্রিস্ট ও গির্জার জন্য আমাদের কণ্ঠ ধ্বনিত হোক।”

কিছু অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্টের মধ্যে রাজ্যের ওপর এই নবায়িত গুরুত্বকে লালন করেছে এমন নানা কারণের মধ্যে দুটি বিশেষভাবে উল্লেখযোগ্য। এই দুটি উদ্বেগই রক্ষণশীল অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্ট ঐতিহ্যের বাইরের খ্রিস্টানদের প্রভাব প্রতিফলিত করে, যদিও তাঁরা বাইবেলে বিশ্বাসী ও নতুন জন্মপ্রাপ্ত বলে নিজেদের দাবি করেন।

  1. প্রথমত, কিছু মানুষ খ্রিস্টসদৃশ হওয়ার চেয়ে বাইবেলসম্মত হওয়া নিয়ে বেশি উদ্বিগ্ন বলে মনে হয়। আমরা, রক্ষণশীল অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্টরা, সঠিক মতবাদ ও অবস্থান নির্ধারণে বাইবেলের ওপর নির্ভর করতে পারি, অথচ আমাদের জীবন প্রভু যিশু খ্রিস্টের চরিত্র ও মূল্যবোধ প্রতিফলিত করতে ব্যর্থ হতে পারে—সেই যিশুর, যাঁর সঙ্গে জীবন্ত সম্পর্কে যুক্ত আছি বলে আমরা দাবি করি।
  2. দ্বিতীয় বিষয়টি হলো পরিত্রাণ পাওয়ার কাজটির প্রতি এমন এক আসক্তি, যার ফলে পরিত্রাণপ্রাপ্ত জীবন যাপন অবহেলিত হয়; অর্থাৎ, বাধ্যতাপূর্ণ শিষ্যত্বের জীবন, বিশেষত যিশুর সেই শিক্ষাগুলো মেনে চলা, যাঁকে আমাদের অনুসরণ করতে হবে। যদিও অধিকাংশ রক্ষণশীল অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্ট খ্রিস্টের শিক্ষা পালন করার দাবি করেন, অসতর্ক শিষ্যত্বের ঝুঁকি থেকে আমরা মুক্ত নই।

রক্ষণশীল অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্টদের মধ্যে কিছু ব্যক্তি নিম্নরূপে এই উদ্বেগগুলোর কথা বলেন। তাঁদের বক্তব্য, ইভানজেলিক্যালরা খ্রিস্টের ব্যক্তি ও কাজকে বিশ্বাস করলেও, তাঁরা পৌলের ওপর বেশি মনোযোগ দিতে ঝোঁকেন। বাস্তবিক অর্থে, তাঁরা (ইভানজেলিক্যালরা) সঠিক বাইবেল ব্যাখ্যা, ধর্মতাত্ত্বিক ব্যবস্থা এবং সঠিক বিশ্বাসে সম্মতি দেওয়া নিয়ে বেশি উদ্বিগ্ন; বাধ্যতাপূর্ণ খ্রিস্টীয় জীবনযাপন নিয়ে ততটা নন—বিশেষত খ্রিস্টের কঠিন শিক্ষাগুলোর ক্ষেত্রে। বিপরীতে, এই অ্যানাব্যাপ্টিস্টদের দাবি, ঈশ্বরের রাজ্য—যা যিশু সূচনা করেছিলেন এবং যা তাঁর শিক্ষার মূল বিষয় ছিল—খ্রিস্টীয় জীবন বোঝা ও যাপন করার মানদণ্ড হওয়া উচিত। ফলে তাঁদের কাছে সুসমাচারগুলো (এবং রাজ্য) নতুন নিয়মের বাকি অংশ ব্যাখ্যা করার ক্ষেত্রে প্রধান হয়ে ওঠে।

এ বিষয়ে আমরা কী ভাবব? ব্যাপক সাধারণীকরণ ব্যতিক্রম ও শর্তসাপেক্ষ বিষয়গুলোর প্রতি সুবিচার করে না, তবে উদ্বেগগুলো যথার্থ; আর আমাদের ইভানজেলিক্যাল বন্ধুদের সম্পর্কে এই সমালোচনায় কিছুটা সত্য রয়েছে। এসবের শিকড় রয়েছে অগাস্টিনের (৩৫৪-৪৩০) চিন্তাধারায়, বিশ্বাসের দ্বারা ধার্মিক প্রতিপন্ন হওয়ার বিষয়ে সংস্কার আন্দোলনের ভারসাম্যহীন জোরে, এবং জন ক্যালভিনের কাজে। কিন্তু খ্রিস্ট ও রাজ্যের ওপর প্রধানত মনোযোগ দেওয়ার প্রতিষেধকটির কী হবে? অবশ্যই, শুধু নতুন নিয়ম নয়, সমগ্র বাইবেল ব্যাখ্যার ক্ষেত্রেও খ্রিস্ট কেন্দ্রীয়। আর খ্রিস্টের সেই শিক্ষাগুলো তুলে ধরার মূল্য রয়েছে, যেগুলো প্রায়ই পাশ কাটিয়ে যাওয়া হয়, অথচ তাঁর নামের যোগ্য যে কোনো গির্জার জন্য সেগুলো পালন করা আবশ্যক। তবে এই প্রতিষেধক নিঃশর্তে গ্রহণ করার ব্যাপারে আমি সতর্কতা বা সমালোচনার তিনটি দিক তুলে ধরতে চাই।

সুসমাচারগুলো কি শাস্ত্রের বাকি অংশের ওপর প্রাধান্য পায়?

প্রথমত, আমি মনে করি সুসমাচারগুলোকে (যিশুর জীবন ও শিক্ষা) নতুন নিয়মের শাস্ত্রাংশের ব্যাখ্যাকে প্রাধান্য দিতে ও নিয়ন্ত্রণ করতে হবে—এমন ধারণা করা ভুল। বরং, নতুন নিয়ম সুসমাচার, প্রেরিত, পত্রসমূহ এবং সবশেষে প্রকাশিত বাক্যের মধ্য দিয়ে অগ্রসর হওয়ার সময়, পূর্ণতর প্রত্যাদেশ ও মতবাদগত ব্যাখ্যার ঈশ্বর-অনুপ্রাণিত ধারাবাহিকতা ধারণ করে। পবিত্র আত্মার আগমন সম্পর্কে যিশুর কথাগুলো বিবেচনা করলে এটি দেখা যায়: তোমাদিগকে বলিবার আমার আরও অনেক কথা আছে, কিন্তু এখন তোমরা তাহা সহ্য করিতে পার না। তথাপি তিনি, সত্যের আত্মা, যখন আসিবেন, তখন তিনি তোমাদিগকে সমস্ত সত্যে পথ দেখাইবেন; কারণ তিনি আপনা হইতে কিছু বলিবেন না, কিন্তু যাহা যাহা শুনেন, তাহাই বলিবেন; এবং আগামী ঘটনাও তোমাদিগকে জানাইবেন—যোহন ১৬:১২-১৩। সুসমাচারগুলোর পরের নতুন নিয়মের বইগুলোই এই কথাগুলোর প্রত্যাশিত পরিপূর্ণতা। সেগুলো খ্রিস্টের শিক্ষা ও কাজকে পূর্ণ বিকাশ ও উপলব্ধিতে নিয়ে আসে।

রাজ্য সম্পর্কে খ্রিস্টের পরিচর্যা ও শিক্ষা ভিত্তি স্থাপন করেছিল; তারপর তাঁর মৃত্যু ও পুনরুত্থান সেই ভিত্তি স্থাপন করে, যার ওপর তিনি তাঁর গির্জা নির্মাণ করবেন। সুসমাচারগুলোর পরের শাস্ত্রাংশগুলো খ্রিস্টের ক্রুশে মৃত্যুর অর্থ এবং বিশ্বাস ও বাধ্যতার মাধ্যমে আমাদের সঙ্গে তার সম্পর্ক ও আমাদের ওপর তার প্রভাব সম্পর্কে আরও গভীর উপলব্ধি দেয়। এগুলো গির্জার সমগ্র মতবাদও বিকশিত করে। তাই পুরো নতুন নিয়ম সুন্দর সামঞ্জস্যে একত্রে মেলে। সুসমাচার ও পত্র—উভয়কেই পরস্পরের আলোকে ব্যাখ্যা করতে হবে। খ্রিস্টের শিক্ষাগুলো পত্রের ওপর প্রাধান্য পায় না; বরং পত্রগুলো সুসমাচার ব্যাখ্যা করতে সাহায্য করে—খ্রিস্ট তাঁর শিষ্যদের যে নীতিগুলো দিয়েছিলেন, সেগুলোর আরও পূর্ণাঙ্গ উপলব্ধি ও ব্যবহারিক প্রয়োগ আমাদের দেয়।

ধর্মতত্ত্ব কি শিষ্যত্বের পথে বাধা দেয়?

দ্বিতীয়ত, সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা ও সঠিক অনুশীলনকে একে অপরের বিরুদ্ধে দাঁড় করানো থেকে আমাদের সতর্ক থাকা উচিত। অন্যভাবে বললে, ধর্মতত্ত্বকে শিষ্যত্বের বিরোধী করে তোলা উচিত নয়। কোনো কোনো ইভানজেলিক্যাল শিষ্যত্বের ক্ষতি করে যতখানি ধর্মতত্ত্বের ওপর অতিরিক্ত জোর দিয়ে থাকুন না কেন, তাতে আমাদের ধর্মতত্ত্বকে দোষের পাত্র বানানো উচিত নয়। ধর্মতত্ত্ব হলো ঈশ্বর ও ঈশ্বরের বিষয়গুলোর অধ্যয়ন। ঈশ্বরের বাক্য অধ্যয়ন করে এবং এর বিভিন্ন অংশের ঐক্যবদ্ধ ও সামঞ্জস্যপূর্ণ উপলব্ধিতে পৌঁছানোর চেষ্টায় শাস্ত্রের সঙ্গে শাস্ত্রের তুলনা করে আমরা ব্যক্তিগত ধর্মতত্ত্ব গড়ে তুলি।

প্রত্যেক খ্রিস্টানেরই একটি ধর্মতত্ত্ব আছে, তিনি তা ভালোভাবে প্রকাশ করতে পারেন কি না, তা নির্বিশেষে। আমাদের ধর্মতত্ত্ব (অথবা মতবাদগত উপলব্ধি—এভাবে বলতে চাইলে) হলো আমাদের বিশ্বাসব্যবস্থা, আর সেই মাটি, যেখান থেকে আমাদের আচরণ গড়ে ওঠে। কিছু ধর্মতত্ত্ব খুবই প্রাথমিক; অন্যগুলো আজীবন অধ্যয়নের প্রতিফলন। অধিকাংশই অসম্পূর্ণ, কিছু অসংগত, অন্যগুলো দার্শনিক ধারণায় জড়ানো বা অনমনীয়, আর কিছু ভয়াবহ রকমের ভুল। আশা করি, ঈশ্বর ও তাঁর বাক্য সম্পর্কে আমাদের সবার উপলব্ধি ক্রমবর্ধমান এবং ক্রমেই আরও নির্ভুল হবে। এটি অত্যন্ত প্রয়োজনীয়, কারণ আমাদের ধর্মতত্ত্ব—ঈশ্বর সম্পর্কে আমাদের বিশ্বাস এবং তাঁর বাক্য ও খ্রিস্টীয় জীবন সম্পর্কে আমাদের উপলব্ধির সমষ্টি—আমাদের শিষ্যত্বকে, অর্থাৎ ঈশ্বরের সঙ্গে আমাদের দৈনন্দিন চলাকে প্রভাবিত করে। ভালো ধর্মতত্ত্ব শিষ্যত্বের ভিত্তিকে শক্তিশালী করে। দুর্বল ধর্মতত্ত্ব শিষ্যত্বকে দুর্বল করে।

“রাজ্য” ও “গির্জা” কি পরস্পরবিনিমেয়?

সবশেষে, গির্জার সঙ্গে রাজ্যের সম্পর্ক নিয়ে আমাদের সঠিকভাবে ভাবা উচিত। গির্জার সঙ্গে রাজ্যের সম্পর্ক কী? সমসাময়িক ব্যবহারে প্রায় আমাদের যা ভাবতে বাধ্য করা হয়, রাজ্য তা নয়—গির্জার একটি সাধারণ সংস্করণ বা গির্জার পরিবর্তে ব্যবহৃত শব্দ। বরং, রাজ্যের সম্পর্ক ঈশ্বরের রাজত্ব বা শাসনের সঙ্গে। এটি একই সঙ্গে বর্তমান বাস্তবতা—যিশুর ব্যক্তি ও মিশনের মাধ্যমে সূচিত হয়েছে—এবং ভবিষ্যৎ প্রত্যাশা, যা ঈশ্বর সময়ের শেষে পূর্ণ করবেন। গির্জা রাজ্য না হলেও, যারা রাজ্যের অন্তর্ভুক্ত—যারা খ্রিস্টের কাজের মাধ্যমে ঈশ্বরের শাসনের কাছে আত্মসমর্পণ করেছে—তাদের নিয়েই গঠিত।

পবিত্র, প্রেমময় ও বাধ্যতাপূর্ণ বিশ্বাসী-সমাজ হিসেবে গির্জার সঙ্গে রাজ্যের সম্পর্ক বোঝাতে যথাযথ শব্দ খুঁজতে গিয়ে আমরা সংগ্রাম করলেও, গির্জা পৃথিবীতে ঈশ্বরের শাসনের—তাঁর রাজ্যের—প্রকাশ। খ্রিস্ট বলেননি, “আমি আমার রাজ্য নির্মাণ করব”; বরং তিনি বলেছিলেন, “আমি আমার গির্জা নির্মাণ করব।” একইভাবে, পৌল রাজ্যের উপাসনালয় নির্মাণ করেননি; তিনি গির্জা প্রতিষ্ঠা করেছিলেন। এমন আদর্শবাদী ও রোমান্টিক রাজ্য-ভাবনা আমাদের হতে পারে, যা স্থানীয় গির্জার দেহে সহবিশ্বাসীদের সঙ্গে পৃথিবীতে বসবাসের কঠিন পরিশ্রম থেকে বিচ্ছিন্ন। আমরা রাজ্যকে বড় করে দেখাতে এবং গির্জাকে তুচ্ছ করতে পারি। রাজ্যের ধারণা, রাজ্যের শিক্ষা, রাজ্যের বৃদ্ধি এবং রাজ্য-সংক্রান্ত সম্মেলন নিয়ে আমরা উৎসাহী হতে পারি, অথচ আমাদের স্থানীয় গির্জার প্রতি নিন্দুক, সমালোচনাপ্রবণ এবং দুঃখজনক সদস্য হয়ে থাকতে পারি।

আপনি কি রাজ্যের জন্য কাজ করতে চান (দেখুন কলসীয় ৪:১১)? তাহলে খ্রিস্ট ও তাঁর গির্জার প্রতি সম্পূর্ণ হৃদয়ে অঙ্গীকারবদ্ধ হন। তার শুরু আপনার স্থানীয় গির্জা থেকে। আপনার গির্জাকে ভালোবাসুন ও সেবা করুন। সেখানে দায়িত্ব নিন। আপনার স্থানীয় গির্জার কাছে জবাবদিহি করুন এবং তার প্রতি বিশ্বস্ত থাকুন। গির্জার মঙ্গল ও বৃদ্ধির জন্য কাজ করুন—আপনার স্থানীয় গির্জার, এবং তারও বাইরে।

টিমোথি ডুইট লিখেছিলেন:*

প্রভু, তোমার রাজ্যকে আমি ভালোবাসি,
তোমার বাসস্থানের গৃহকে,
আমাদের ধন্য উদ্ধারকর্তার গির্জাকে,
যাকে তিনি নিজের মূল্যবান রক্তে উদ্ধার করেছেন।
হে ঈশ্বর, তোমার গির্জাকে আমি ভালোবাসি:
তার প্রাচীর তোমার সম্মুখে দাঁড়িয়ে আছে,
তোমার চোখের মণির মতো প্রিয়,
আর তোমার হাতে খোদাই করা।

রাজ্যের সঙ্গে গির্জার সুনির্দিষ্ট সম্পর্ক নিয়ে তাঁর বক্তব্য আমার উপলব্ধি থেকে ভিন্ন হতে পারে। তবে আমি চাই, আমরা যেন এই বিষয়টি উপলব্ধি করি: তিনি যখন রাজ্যের কথা ভাবতেন, তখন গির্জার কথা ভাবতেন। আমাদেরও তাই করা উচিত! তিনি যখন পরের কথাগুলো লেখেন, তাঁর কথাগুলো কি আপনারও কথা?

তার জন্য আমার অশ্রু ঝরবে,
তার জন্য আমার প্রার্থনা ঊর্ধ্বে উঠবে;
তার জন্য আমার যত্ন ও শ্রম নিবেদিত হোক,
যত্ন ও শ্রম শেষ না হওয়া পর্যন্ত।
আমার সর্বোচ্চ আনন্দের চেয়েও
তার স্বর্গীয় পথকে আমি মূল্য দিই,
তার মধুর সহভাগিতা, গম্ভীর অঙ্গীকার,
তার প্রেম ও প্রশংসার স্তবগান।

* সম্পূর্ণ গানটির জন্য ৩২ পৃষ্ঠা দেখুন।

Something that I have noticed repeatedly as I read God’s Word is that God’s people are confident. Consider Noah. When God told him to build an ark, there was no wavering. He spent the next 120 years confidently doing just that. Then I think of Abraham confidently doing whatever God asked of him, even when He asked him to sacrifice his only son. We cannot speak of confidence without mentioning Caleb and Joshua, who after hearing all their comrades give their doubting reports, confidently described what they should do with this new land of Canaan: …Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it –Numbers 13:30.

We cannot forget about David who went out and silenced the large naysayer—Goliath. Nor can we forget Daniel, Gideon, Job, Ezekiel, Isaiah, or Jeremiah and all that they did with confidence. As we study each of these men of faith and many others, we clearly see that they had a great amount of confidence in their God!

Some might say that if God worked the same way today as He did back then, we would be more confident. Maybe if God were still an Old Testament God, it would be easier. If He led us into battle, destroyed our enemies, parted seas, and caused bread to fall from heaven, then we would have more confidence in Him.

Now let us consider the New Testament. It is quite different. God’s people are commanded to leave everything for the sake of Christ. They are promised that the world will hate them. They are told that it is difficult for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. They are guaranteed that they will be blessed if they suffer, if they are poor, if they are hungry, and if they mourn.

Can people still have confidence in a God that asks His people to follow Him under these circumstances? Yes! The disciples proved it. They went about preaching and teaching. They were hunted and beaten repeatedly. The deacon, Stephen, showed great confidence when he was brought before his oppressors, even when they began to gnash their teeth at him, and stone him. Stephen showed confidence until he took his last agonizing breath.

Before he became the apostle Paul, Saul was an enemy of the cross, the chiefest of sinners, and a Pharisee of the Pharisees. He was a prominent man, taught by the best. Then he met the living God, and everything changed. After Paul was baptized, …straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God –Acts 9:20. The next verse says the people were amazed, then in verse 23, five verses after he was baptized, it says that the Jews took counsel to kill him.

It takes a lot of confidence in God to change a man like that, to cause him to, overnight, completely change allegiance. According to his own testimony, Paul was faithful until his death: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: –2 Timothy 4:6-7.

God did amazing things in the New Testament. He healed the blind and raised the dead to life again. He released prisoners and struck people dead. Some may say it would be easier to have great confidence in God if we were still living in the New Testament Bible times when Jesus physically walked and talked here on this earth.

What about after the Bible?

In the early church, we again see a group of people that did not waver; they had confidence in their God, a God they could not see. Tens of thousands of God’s people stood boldly before the world and proclaimed its wickedness, and tens of thousands of God’s people were killed. The confidence of these people was never questioned. They were called fools, for believing in a “God they could not see”. They were mocked and scorned for their ‘foolishness’, they were …killed all the day long… –Psalm 44:22. People questioned their practices, they questioned their religious structure, they questioned the message they preached, they questioned many things, but they never questioned their confidence. These Christians believed in their God, of that there was no doubt.

Strangely, they were not interested in the pleasures of this life; they did not care about the things of this world, and even their very lives were a small thing to give up for their God. Families were torn apart, houses and lands were confiscated, churches were burned, but it did not faze stop them. They lived for something greater, something the heathen could not understand.

Through the time of the early church and the time of the Reformation, people were added to the Kingdom in great numbers. Yes, children did grow up and join their parents’ church, but there were also great masses of new converts from the world. How could anyone convince a worldly person to join a group that was hunted and killed—a group that suffered like the church of Jesus Christ suffered? Yes, we know that salvation is of the Lord, but it was the confidence of God’s people that caused others to wonder, that caused them to seriously consider this new religion of heretics. This was a group of people that would gladly accept the spoiling of their goods, be happy to give all they had to help others, and not resist their capture by the authorities. The true church of Jesus Christ was a group of people that always caused others to wonder, “Who are these people?” They clearly put all their faith in their God, and that was not a common occurrence. They stood up for God’s Truth no matter how hot the fire burned, no matter how miserable their lives were made. It all showed a great confidence, not in themselves, but in their God.

As we look at the church today, what do we see? Some of God’s people are taking up their crosses, and denying the world and the lust thereof, other people are not. Is the church of today still known for being confident in their God?

As professing Christians, have we lost some of this biblical confidence? Are we still out there undeniably serving the one true God? Do people look at us, and stand in awe of the confidence we are displaying in our God? Too many people of today are saying they are Christians, but they demonstrate very little confidence in God. They live quite closely to the ways of the world. Instead of enjoying persecution, they enjoy many of the same things that the world does. Each of us needs the fire of God burning deep within our hearts, a fire that cannot be quenched.

Confidence equals obedience. I have met many Christians of our day whose ancestors gave their lives for Christ, and their grandfathers bravely led the church, but there now seems to be something missing. As I interact with many God-fearing Christians, it seems that there is a prevailing struggle with confidence—a confidence in a living God who is all-powerful, all-knowing, and all-present.

In the uncertainty of our world today, we need to once more boldly proclaim the gospel message just like true believers did in times past. We need to clearly draw distinct biblical lines between right and wrong. We need to rid ourselves of all these wretched gray areas and call sin, sin. It seems that we have lost the confidence to speak out against the sin of our day. If we confidently proclaim what God has declared, there are some people who will not like us. We need brethren that are not afraid to be scoffed at and are willing to take the road less traveled.

Right before our Lord ascended on high, He gave His disciples a glorious promise, …ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth –Acts 1:8.

Ye shall receive power! Not power from men, not power from kingdoms of this world, but real, overcoming power—power that comes only from the Holy Ghost! After we receive this power, we go forward as a new creature, confidently proclaiming the blessed Gospel of our Redeemer.

We need hearts that burn with God’s will and God’s word. We need hearts aflame!

I was eating lunch one day when a couple approached me with a serious question, “Why does the church think it has to control us?” After they explained how they think they should be able to be ‘free in Christ’, I was excited to answer their questions. However, there was another ordained brother sitting beside me. So, I decided to wait, hoping that he would engage the couple, but he said nothing. As another forty-five minutes passed, I tried to explain to the couple how they needed to deny themselves and submit to the church. And that if they laid down their lives fully, if they surrendered all, they would no longer have such a struggle with church structure.

The couple seemed encouraged and ready to give things another try. However, the minister beside me did not seem too pleased, so I asked him what he thought. He said that his father told him years ago that when he was young, he thought he had all the answers. After he got old, he realized he did not know anything, and that church issues are too complicated to solve. We need to just try to get along.

Is this the answer, to just act like we don’t know anything and hope that it all works out in the end? I do understand that we don’t have all the answers. After all, I realize that I have more questions than answers most times. However, I do know what God wants for His church! …Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

A glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish! Will we, as God’s people, once again stand for truth, deny the world, and like sheep allow ourselves to be led to the slaughter? Or have we made our lives too comfortable to deny, have we chosen the easy (broad) way and denied the straight and narrow? Have we signed a peace deal with the servants of sin? If I weep as I write, will you weep as you read?

The definition of the word confidence is a feeling or consciousness of one’s powers. Many people today have confused confidence with pride, and for good reason. Most people that are confident are confident in themselves, instead of being confident in Christ. We see this self-confidence all around us. There are life coaches and counselors all over the globe, telling people to believe in themselves, telling them to be confident in themselves. When one is confident in themselves, they often do become proud. Remember the world does not look down on pride. You can hear the world boast of its pride everywhere you look. People are proud of their children, proud of their country, proud of their favorite sports team, proud of their lawns, proud of basically everything that is good in their lives. We must remember that pride is sin and will not enter heaven. While confidence in one’s self or things is pride, confidence in God is not!

It is not a new concept to confuse confidence in God, with pride. David’s oldest brother Eliab said to him, “I know thy pride”. Was David proud? No, he simply had a great deal of confidence in his God.

Could it be that a false sense of humility has silenced the church? Could it be that this tactic of the enemy is one of Satan’s current weapons against Christians? Could it also be the reason that the Church seems to be struggling in all parts of the world? What if faithful men would once again step out in faith in their God with great confidence and by their words and actions show this sinned-stained world the straight and narrow way—into the Kingdom of God?!

We all must agree, we live in a confused world—one that is confused as to what is right and what is wrong. What if the world could look at the Church and once again find a group of people that know exactly where they are going—a church that has no doubt which way is the right way—a church that can boldly proclaim the answer to the problems of our day—a church that is nothing less than completely confident in their GOD?

Let us come before our God on bended knee, with our hearts bowed low, demonstrating genuine godly sorrow for where we have lost our way. Let us earnestly seek God’s will for ourselves, for our families, for our churches, and for our neighbors. Let us ask God to show us how we can be His examples to the world around us. The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn; To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified –Isaiah 61:1-3.

Algo que tenho observado repetidamente ao ler a Palavra de Deus é que o povo de Deus é confiante. Pense em Noé. Quando Deus lhe disse que construísse uma arca, ele não vacilou. Nos 120 anos seguintes, fez exatamente isso com confiança. Depois, penso em Abraão, que fez com confiança tudo o que Deus lhe pediu, mesmo quando lhe pediu que sacrificasse seu único filho. Não podemos falar de confiança sem mencionar Calebe e Josué, que, depois de ouvirem todos os seus companheiros apresentarem relatos cheios de dúvidas, descreveram com confiança o que deveriam fazer com aquela nova terra de Canaã: …Subamos imediatamente e tomemos posse dela, pois somos bem capazes de vencê-la –Números 13:30.

Não podemos nos esquecer de Davi, que saiu e silenciou o grande opositor — Golias. Tampouco podemos nos esquecer de Daniel, Gideão, Jó, Ezequiel, Isaías ou Jeremias, nem de tudo o que fizeram com confiança. Ao estudarmos cada um desses homens de fé e muitos outros, vemos claramente que tinham grande confiança em seu Deus!

Alguns poderiam dizer que, se Deus agisse hoje da mesma maneira que agia naquela época, teríamos mais confiança. Talvez fosse mais fácil se Deus ainda fosse um Deus do Antigo Testamento. Se Ele nos conduzisse à batalha, destruísse nossos inimigos, abrisse mares e fizesse pão cair do céu, então teríamos mais confiança nele.

Agora, consideremos o Novo Testamento. É bem diferente. Ordena-se ao povo de Deus que deixe tudo por amor a Cristo. Promete-se a esse povo que o mundo o odiará. Diz-se a ele que é difícil para um rico entrar no reino de Deus. Garante-se a ele que será abençoado se sofrer, se for pobre, se tiver fome e se prantear.

As pessoas ainda podem confiar em um Deus que pede ao seu povo que o siga nessas circunstâncias? Sim! Os discípulos provaram que sim. Andavam pregando e ensinando. Foram caçados e espancados repetidas vezes. O diácono Estêvão demonstrou grande confiança quando foi levado diante de seus opressores, mesmo quando começaram a ranger os dentes contra ele e a apedrejá-lo. Estêvão demonstrou confiança até dar seu último e agonizante suspiro.

Antes de se tornar o apóstolo Paulo, Saulo era inimigo da cruz, o maior dos pecadores e fariseu entre os fariseus. Era um homem de destaque, instruído pelos melhores. Então encontrou o Deus vivo, e tudo mudou. Depois de Paulo ser batizado, …imediatamente começou a pregar nas sinagogas que Jesus é o Filho de Deus –Atos 9:20. O versículo seguinte diz que o povo ficou admirado; depois, no versículo 23, cinco versículos após seu batismo, diz que os judeus conspiraram para matá-lo.

É preciso muita confiança em Deus para transformar um homem assim, para levá-lo a mudar completamente de lealdade da noite para o dia. Segundo seu próprio testemunho, Paulo permaneceu fiel até a morte: Quanto a mim, já estou sendo oferecido por libação, e o tempo da minha partida está próximo. Combati o bom combate, terminei a corrida, guardei a fé: –2 Timóteo 4:6-7.

Deus realizou coisas extraordinárias no Novo Testamento. Curou os cegos e ressuscitou os mortos. Libertou prisioneiros e fez pessoas morrerem. Alguns poderiam dizer que seria mais fácil ter grande confiança em Deus se ainda vivêssemos nos tempos bíblicos do Novo Testamento, quando Jesus caminhava e falava fisicamente aqui na terra.

E depois da Bíblia?

Na igreja primitiva, vemos novamente um grupo de pessoas que não vacilava; tinham confiança em seu Deus, um Deus que não podiam ver. Dezenas de milhares de pessoas do povo de Deus se posicionaram corajosamente diante do mundo e proclamaram sua maldade, e dezenas de milhares de pessoas do povo de Deus foram mortas. A confiança dessas pessoas jamais foi questionada. Foram chamadas de tolas por acreditarem em um “Deus que não podiam ver”. Foram zombadas e escarnecidas por sua “tolice”; foram …mortos todo o dia… –Salmos 44:22. As pessoas questionavam suas práticas, questionavam sua estrutura religiosa, questionavam a mensagem que pregavam, questionavam muitas coisas, mas nunca questionavam sua confiança. Esses cristãos acreditavam em seu Deus, disso não havia dúvida.

Curiosamente, não estavam interessados nos prazeres desta vida; não se importavam com as coisas deste mundo, e até mesmo suas próprias vidas eram algo pequeno a renunciar por seu Deus. Famílias foram separadas, casas e terras foram confiscadas, igrejas foram queimadas, mas isso não os deteve. Viviam por algo maior, algo que os pagãos não conseguiam compreender.

Durante o período da igreja primitiva e o da Reforma, muitas pessoas foram acrescentadas ao Reino. Sim, as crianças cresciam e se uniam à igreja de seus pais, mas também havia grandes multidões de novos convertidos vindos do mundo. Como alguém poderia convencer uma pessoa mundana a se juntar a um grupo que era caçado e morto — um grupo que sofria como sofreu a igreja de Jesus Cristo? Sim, sabemos que a salvação vem do Senhor, mas era a confiança do povo de Deus que levava os outros a se admirarem, que os levava a considerar seriamente essa nova religião de hereges. Esse era um grupo de pessoas que aceitava de bom grado o confisco de seus bens, ficava feliz em dar tudo o que tinha para ajudar os outros e não resistia à captura pelas autoridades. A verdadeira igreja de Jesus Cristo era um grupo de pessoas que sempre levava os outros a se perguntarem: “Quem são essas pessoas?” Claramente depositavam toda a sua fé em seu Deus, e isso não era algo comum. Defendiam a Verdade de Deus, não importava quão intensamente ardesse o fogo, nem quão miserável se tornasse sua vida. Tudo isso demonstrava grande confiança, não em si mesmas, mas em seu Deus.

Quando olhamos para a igreja hoje, o que vemos? Algumas pessoas do povo de Deus tomam suas cruzes e negam o mundo e sua concupiscência; outras não. A igreja de hoje ainda é conhecida por confiar em seu Deus?

Como cristãos professos, perdemos parte dessa confiança bíblica? Ainda estamos por aí servindo, de maneira inegável, ao único Deus verdadeiro? As pessoas olham para nós e ficam maravilhadas com a confiança que demonstramos em nosso Deus? Hoje, pessoas demais dizem ser cristãs, mas demonstram muito pouca confiança em Deus. Vivem bem próximas dos caminhos do mundo. Em vez de se alegrarem com a perseguição, desfrutam de muitas das mesmas coisas que o mundo desfruta. Cada um de nós precisa do fogo de Deus ardendo profundamente em nosso coração, um fogo que não pode ser apagado.

Confiança equivale a obediência. Conheci muitos cristãos de nossos dias cujos antepassados deram a vida por Cristo e cujos avôs conduziram corajosamente a igreja, mas agora parece faltar alguma coisa. Ao conviver com muitos cristãos tementes a Deus, parece haver uma luta predominante com a confiança — a confiança em um Deus vivo, todo-poderoso, onisciente e onipresente.

Em meio à incerteza do mundo de hoje, precisamos proclamar novamente com ousadia a mensagem do evangelho, assim como fizeram os verdadeiros crentes no passado. Precisamos traçar claramente distinções bíblicas entre o certo e o errado. Precisamos nos livrar de todas essas terríveis zonas cinzentas e chamar o pecado de pecado. Parece que perdemos a confiança para falar contra o pecado de nossos dias. Se proclamarmos com confiança o que Deus declarou, haverá pessoas que não gostarão de nós. Precisamos de irmãos que não tenham medo de ser ridicularizados e estejam dispostos a seguir o caminho menos percorrido.

Pouco antes de nosso Senhor subir ao alto, deu aos seus discípulos uma promessa gloriosa: …recebereis poder, ao descer sobre vós o Espírito Santo, e sereis minhas testemunhas tanto em Jerusalém como em toda a Judeia e Samaria e até os confins da terra –Atos 1:8.

Recebereis poder! Não poder vindo dos homens, nem poder vindo dos reinos deste mundo, mas poder verdadeiro, poder que vence — poder que vem somente do Espírito Santo! Depois de recebermos esse poder, seguimos adiante como nova criatura, proclamando com confiança o bendito Evangelho de nosso Redentor.

Precisamos de corações que ardam com a vontade e a palavra de Deus. Precisamos de corações em chamas!

Um dia, eu estava almoçando quando um casal se aproximou de mim com uma pergunta séria: “Por que a igreja acha que precisa nos controlar?” Depois que explicaram como achavam que deveriam poder ser “livres em Cristo”, fiquei animado para responder às perguntas deles. No entanto, havia outro irmão ordenado sentado ao meu lado. Por isso, decidi esperar, na esperança de que ele conversasse com o casal, mas ele não disse nada. Depois de mais quarenta e cinco minutos, tentei explicar ao casal que precisava negar a si mesmo e se submeter à igreja. E que, se entregassem plenamente a vida, se rendessem tudo, não teriam mais tanta dificuldade com a estrutura da igreja.

O casal pareceu animado e disposto a tentar novamente. No entanto, o ministro ao meu lado não pareceu muito satisfeito, então perguntei o que achava. Ele disse que seu pai lhe contara, anos antes, que, quando era jovem, achava que tinha todas as respostas. Quando envelheceu, percebeu que não sabia nada e que as questões da igreja eram complicadas demais para resolver. Precisamos simplesmente tentar conviver em harmonia.

Essa é a resposta: simplesmente agir como se não soubéssemos nada e esperar que tudo acabe dando certo? Entendo que não temos todas as respostas. Afinal, percebo que, na maioria das vezes, tenho mais perguntas do que respostas. No entanto, sei o que Deus quer para sua igreja! …Cristo também amou a igreja e a si mesmo se entregou por ela, para a santificar, purificando-a com a lavagem da água, pela palavra, para apresentá-la a si mesmo igreja gloriosa, sem mancha, nem ruga, nem coisa semelhante, mas santa e sem defeito –Efésios 5:25-27.

Uma igreja gloriosa, sem mancha, nem ruga, nem coisa semelhante, mas santa e sem defeito! Nós, como povo de Deus, voltaremos a defender a verdade, a negar o mundo e, como ovelhas, permitir que nos levem ao matadouro? Ou tornamos nossa vida confortável demais para renunciar a ela; escolhemos o caminho fácil (largo) e rejeitamos o caminho estreito? Fizemos um acordo de paz com os servos do pecado? Se choro enquanto escrevo, você chorará enquanto lê?

A definição da palavra confiança é um sentimento ou consciência das próprias capacidades. Hoje, muitas pessoas confundem confiança com orgulho, e com razão. A maioria das pessoas confiantes confia em si mesma, em vez de confiar em Cristo. Vemos essa autoconfiança por toda parte. Há treinadores de vida e conselheiros espalhados pelo mundo todo, dizendo às pessoas que acreditem em si mesmas, dizendo-lhes que confiem em si mesmas. Quando alguém confia em si mesmo, muitas vezes acaba ficando orgulhoso. Lembre-se: o mundo não condena o orgulho. Por onde quer que olhe, você pode ouvir o mundo se vangloriar de seu orgulho. As pessoas se orgulham dos filhos, do país, do time esportivo favorito, dos gramados, basicamente de tudo que há de bom em suas vidas. Devemos nos lembrar de que o orgulho é pecado e não entrará no céu. Embora a confiança em si mesmo ou nas coisas seja orgulho, a confiança em Deus não é!

Não é novidade confundir confiança em Deus com orgulho. Eliabe, o irmão mais velho de Davi, disse-lhe: “Conheço a tua presunção”. Davi era orgulhoso? Não, simplesmente tinha grande confiança em seu Deus.

Será que uma falsa sensação de humildade silenciou a igreja? Será que essa tática do inimigo é uma das armas que Satanás usa atualmente contra os cristãos? Será também essa a razão pela qual a Igreja parece estar passando por dificuldades em todas as partes do mundo? E se homens fiéis voltassem a agir com fé em seu Deus e grande confiança, mostrando, por suas palavras e ações, a este mundo manchado pelo pecado o caminho estreito que conduz ao Reino de Deus?!

Todos devemos concordar: vivemos num mundo confuso — confuso quanto ao que é certo e ao que é errado. E se o mundo pudesse olhar para a Igreja e mais uma vez encontrar um grupo de pessoas que sabe exatamente para onde está indo — uma igreja que não tem dúvidas sobre qual é o caminho certo — uma igreja que pode proclamar corajosamente a resposta para os problemas de nossos dias — uma igreja que é nada menos que completamente confiante em seu DEUS?

Compareçamos diante de nosso Deus de joelhos, com o coração humilhado, demonstrando verdadeiro pesar segundo Deus por termos perdido o rumo. Busquemos sinceramente a vontade de Deus para nós mesmos, para nossas famílias, para nossas igrejas e para nossos vizinhos. Peçamos a Deus que nos mostre como podemos ser seus exemplos para o mundo ao nosso redor. O Espírito do Senhor DEUS está sobre mim, porque o SENHOR me ungiu para pregar boas-novas aos mansos; enviou-me para restaurar os quebrantados de coração, proclamar liberdade aos cativos e abertura de prisão aos presos; para proclamar o ano aceitável do SENHOR e o dia da vingança do nosso Deus; para consolar todos os que pranteiam; para dar aos que pranteiam em Sião uma coroa em vez de cinzas, óleo de alegria em vez de pranto, veste de louvor em vez de espírito angustiado, para que sejam chamados árvores de justiça, plantação do SENHOR, para que ele seja glorificado –Isaías 61:1-3.

{"language_guidance":"Use contemporary Modern Hebrew, not reconstructed biblical Hebrew.","language_tag":"he","source":{"html":"

With a God so big, why would one fear?
He controls the sea, the storms that appear.
He knows tomorrow, before it has come.
The hairs of our head, He knows the sum.

Why would one question a God like this?
Why do some doubt, or ask amiss?
“Trust in the Lord” the Scripture has said.
But our own understanding, we lean on instead?

I’m sure it’s confusing, to the all-knowing One.
All the miracles, with a word, they were done!
He looks to and fro in this world today,
For one that will trust, without a delay.

The things of this world are so brilliant and fast.
Do we even need God, maybe old-fashioned at last?!
Enough with the folly, we all know the truth.
We have seen God working, yes, from our youth.

Nothing can replace our almighty God;
To say any different would certainly sound odd.
He’s waiting for the church to trust Him once more.
He stands and knocks; will you open the door?

Not just in a pinch, or when life’s too hard,
But every moment, your fears disregard.
He’s looking for a people once more in our day,
With confidence in God, His power to display.

by Barry Grant

עם אל גדול כל כך, למה לפחד?
הוא שולט בים ובסערות המשתוללות.
הוא יודע את המחר עוד בטרם יבוא.
הוא יודע את מספר שערות ראשנו.

למה להטיל ספק באל כזה?
למה יש המטילים ספק או שואלים שלא כראוי?
„בטח באדון”, כך נאמר בכתובים.
ובכל זאת, אנו נשענים דווקא על הבנתנו?

אני בטוח שהדבר מבלבל את יודע־הכול.
את כל הניסים חוללו במילה אחת!
הוא מביט אנה ואנה בעולם הזה כיום,
ומחפש מי שיבטח בו בלי להתמהמה.

דברי העולם הזה נוצצים כל כך ומהירים.
האם אנו בכלל זקוקים לאלוהים, אולי הוא כבר מיושן?!
די בשטות הזאת, כולנו יודעים את האמת.
ראינו את אלוהים פועל, כן, עוד מילדותנו.

שום דבר אינו יכול להחליף את אלוהינו הכול־יכול;
לומר אחרת יישמע בוודאי מוזר.
הוא ממתין שהכנסייה תבטח בו שוב.
הוא עומד ודופק; האם תפתחו את הדלת?

לא רק בעת צרה, או כשהחיים קשים מדי,
אלא בכל רגע, הניחו לפחדיכם.
גם בימינו הוא מחפש שוב עם,
שיפגין את כוחו מתוך ביטחון באלוהים.

מאת בארי גרנט

Bei einem so großen Gott, warum sollte man sich fürchten?
Er beherrscht das Meer und die Stürme, die aufziehen.
Er kennt das Morgen, noch ehe es gekommen ist.
Er weiß, wie viele Haare wir auf dem Kopf haben.

Warum sollte man einen solchen Gott hinterfragen?
Warum zweifeln manche oder fragen fehl am Platz?
„Vertraue auf den Herrn“, sagt die Schrift.
Doch stattdessen stützen wir uns auf unseren eigenen Verstand?

Ich bin sicher, für den Allwissenden ist das verwirrend.
All die Wunder geschahen auf ein Wort hin!
Er blickt heute in dieser Welt umher,
auf der Suche nach einem, der ohne Zögern vertraut.

Die Dinge dieser Welt sind so glänzend und schnell.
Brauchen wir Gott überhaupt noch, ist er vielleicht inzwischen altmodisch?!
Schluss mit dem Unsinn, wir alle kennen die Wahrheit.
Wir haben Gottes Wirken gesehen, ja, schon von Jugend an.

Nichts kann unseren allmächtigen Gott ersetzen;
etwas anderes zu behaupten, klänge gewiss seltsam.
Er wartet darauf, dass die Gemeinde ihm wieder vertraut.
Er steht da und klopft; wirst du die Tür öffnen?

Nicht nur in der Klemme oder wenn das Leben zu schwer ist,
sondern jeden Augenblick – lass deine Ängste beiseite.
Er sucht in unseren Tagen wieder ein Volk,
das mit Zuversicht auf Gott vertraut und seine Macht sichtbar macht.

von Barry Grant

{"language_guidance":"Use standard written Korean and a respectful editorial register.","language_tag":"ko","source":{"html":"

God the Potter is molding me.
What kind of vessel will I be:
To carry, to store, or for a drink?
A lamp, or a plate, or a kitchen sink?

I’m a little bit shallow, I admit,
For I’m focusing on me quite a bit.
But here is a thought,
I’m not the only pot.

About my life
are many others,
A husband, a daughter,
and some brothers.

The Potter’s hand is on them, too,
Making each of us, something new.
Another pot gives me a bump,
And now I have a little lump.

Into another pot I smack,
It seems they now have a crack.
Back to the Potter’s wheel we go,
Until His likeness, again does show.

If what I do, and what I say,
Changes the course of other’s clay,
Then with great care, I must behave,
Lest other’s pots become concave.

Useful pots are God’s desire,
Ones that can withstand the fire.
It’s not just me, and it’s not just you;
God’s working with other vessels too.

by Elizabeth Rust

This poem was inspired by the Scripture passage in Jeremiah 18:1-6.

도공이신 하나님께서 나를 빚으시네.
나는 어떤 그릇이 될까:
담아 두는 그릇, 저장하는 그릇, 아니면 마시는 그릇?
등잔일까, 접시일까, 아니면 부엌 싱크대일까?

인정하건대 나는 조금 속이 좁아,
나 자신에게 꽤 마음을 쏟고 있네.
하지만 이런 생각이 드네,
그릇은 나 하나만이 아니네.

내 삶의 곁에는
많은 이들이 있네,
남편과 딸,
그리고 형제들도 있네.

도공의 손길은 그들에게도 닿아,
우리 각자를 새롭게 빚으시네.
다른 그릇이 나를 툭 치면,
이제 내게 작은 혹이 생기네.

내가 또 다른 그릇에 부딪히면,
그 그릇엔 금이 간 듯하네.
우리는 다시 도공의 물레로 돌아가네,
그분을 닮은 모습이 다시 드러날 때까지.

내가 하는 일과 내가 하는 말이
다른 이들의 흙이 나아갈 길을 바꾼다면,
다른 그릇들이 오목하게 찌그러지지 않도록,
나는 크게 조심하며 행동해야 하네.

하나님께서는 쓸모 있는 그릇을 바라시네,
불을 견딜 수 있는 그릇을.
나만의 일도, 너만의 일도 아니네;
하나님께서는 다른 그릇들도 빚고 계시네.

One Sunday morning a little girl, whom we will call Jennika, woke up to the sun shining into her bedroom. She dressed in her Sunday dress just like she did every other Sunday morning. This Sunday morning was quite different, though. While she was sitting at the breakfast table waiting for her mom to fill her plate, her mom’s chest suddenly started hurting very badly. It hurt so badly, she had to go lie on the couch. Jennika felt scared. She didn’t know what was going to happen. About ten minutes later, her dad took her mom to the hospital. Later that afternoon, she and her siblings heard that their mom had suffered a heart attack.

The next Wednesday evening, her dad asked, “Jennika, would you like to go along to the hospital tomorrow to see Mom?”

“Yes!” she beamed.

The next morning after breakfast, her older sister and baby brother went with her and her dad to the hospital. That day she had lots of fun. She enjoyed looking out the window of the waiting room and watching the helicopters take off and land. One time she even saw an ambulance come with its lights and sirens on. That was exciting! One time she almost got lost in the halls, but one of her mom’s nurses saw her and showed her the right room.

That night she was going to spend the night with her mom. She was so excited! She thought sleeping on the chair in her mom’s room would be fun. Her mom was going to ask the nurses for a pillow and some blankets. About fifteen minutes after her dad left, a nurse came in and said she couldn’t spend the night there after all! Her dad needed to come back to pick her up. She was so disappointed! She cried almost the whole way home. That night they dropped off her two-week-old brother at one of the church families to give her older sisters a break from taking care of him.

The next day she had a wonderful surprise. First, her cousins, who lived about three hours away, came to visit. And she found out that her mom was going to come home that day! She helped her siblings decorate the house. Her older sister made two welcome-home signs for inside the house and her older brother made one for out by the driveway.

“Mom is home!” yelled her younger brother when he saw the car pull up outside the house. Jennika and her siblings dashed to the front door. They led their mom to her favorite recliner which was close to the air conditioner that their uncle had just installed that morning.

That evening Jennika snuggled up to her mom. “I’m glad you’re home,” she whispered. “I like it when you’re home.” Because her mom had been gone so long, Jennika learned to be more thankful for her mom.

Jennika is older now and is still very thankful for her mom. Maybe your mom didn’t need to be in the hospital for a week, but you should still be thankful for her. Don’t forget to tell her!

","section":"Children’s Corner","subtitle":null,"title":"Be Thankful"},"source_context":{"byline":{"authors":[{"location":"Glenmont OH","name":"Marian Martin"}],"raw":"by Marian Martin Glenmont OH"}},"target_language":"Spanish","terminology_glossary":{},"translation":{"html":"

Una mañana de domingo, una niña pequeña, a quien llamaremos Jennika, se despertó al ver el sol entrar por la ventana de su dormitorio. Se vistió con su vestido de domingo, como hacía todos los domingos por la mañana. Pero aquel domingo por la mañana fue muy diferente. Mientras estaba sentada a la mesa del desayuno esperando que su mamá le llenara el plato, a su mamá empezó a dolerle mucho el pecho de repente. Le dolía tanto que tuvo que ir a acostarse en el sofá. Jennika sintió miedo. No sabía qué iba a pasar. Unos diez minutos después, su papá llevó a su mamá al hospital. Más tarde, esa tarde, ella y sus hermanos se enteraron de que su mamá había sufrido un ataque al corazón.

El miércoles siguiente por la noche, su papá le preguntó: «Jennika, ¿te gustaría acompañarme mañana al hospital para visitar a mamá?»

«¡Sí!», respondió radiante.

A la mañana siguiente, después del desayuno, su hermana mayor y su hermanito bebé fueron con ella y su papá al hospital. Ese día se divirtió mucho. Le gustaba mirar por la ventana de la sala de espera y observar cómo despegaban y aterrizaban los helicópteros. Una vez incluso vio llegar una ambulancia con las luces encendidas y la sirena sonando. ¡Fue emocionante! Una vez estuvo a punto de perderse en los pasillos, pero una de las enfermeras de su mamá la vio y le indicó cuál era la habitación correcta.

Esa noche iba a pasar la noche con su mamá. ¡Estaba muy emocionada! Pensaba que sería divertido dormir en la silla de la habitación de su mamá. Su mamá iba a pedirles a las enfermeras una almohada y unas mantas. Unos quince minutos después de que su papá se fuera, entró una enfermera y dijo que, después de todo, no podía pasar la noche allí. ¡Su papá tenía que volver para recogerla! ¡Se sintió muy decepcionada! Lloró casi todo el camino de vuelta a casa. Esa noche dejaron a su hermanito de dos semanas con una de las familias de la iglesia, para que sus hermanas mayores descansaran de cuidarlo.

Al día siguiente tuvo una sorpresa maravillosa. Primero, fueron a visitarlos sus primos, que vivían a unas tres horas de distancia. ¡Y se enteró de que su mamá volvería a casa ese mismo día! Ayudó a sus hermanos a decorar la casa. Su hermana mayor hizo dos carteles de bienvenida para poner dentro de la casa, y su hermano mayor hizo uno para colocar junto a la entrada del camino de acceso.

«¡Mamá ya está en casa!», gritó su hermano menor cuando vio que el auto se detenía frente a la casa. Jennika y sus hermanos corrieron hacia la puerta principal. Acompañaron a su mamá hasta su sillón reclinable favorito, que estaba cerca del aire acondicionado que su tío acababa de instalar esa misma mañana.

Esa noche, Jennika se acurrucó junto a su mamá. «Me alegra que estés en casa», susurró. «Me gusta cuando estás en casa». Como su mamá había estado fuera tanto tiempo, Jennika aprendió a estar más agradecida por ella.

Ahora Jennika es mayor y sigue estando muy agradecida por su mamá. Tal vez tu mamá no haya tenido que pasar una semana en el hospital, pero aun así debes estar agradecido por ella. ¡No olvides decírselo!
